teacher.aboutMe:
Hello, my name is Carlo Stanga. I am an illustrator, an architect and a books author.

My story is my Daimon’s story.
As the ancient Greeks used to believe, everyone of us has a Daimon. The Daimon is our real essence, what makes us unique individuals, the real reason why we are on this Earth, our creative talent, in one world, our destiny. 
Not attending to your Daimon, your deepest passion, means to damage your own life. On the contrary, supporting your Daimon makes you closer to happiness, that, not without reason, in ancient greek is called Eudaimonia.
Actually a happy life means attending a work you would have done in any case, just because you like it, even without being paid!

In my story the Daimon showed up very early, when I was 2.
He was a doodler Daimon, making me sketching flying withces and elicopters on every available surface like sheets of paper, tables, walls, the kitchen’s furniture…
At that age I did not speak yet, I was only drawing, so my parents led me to the doctor . “ No worries”, he said, “ he just communicates through drawing, he will begin to speak soon”.In fact a few months later I began to speak, but I never stopped drawing.

At the elementary school, attended between the age of 6 and 10, I was so lucky to have a teacher who understood me and my Daimon, letting him express himself. She was often asking me to create big drawings about the main subjects of the school lessons. So I was usually face-down on a large sheet of paper, as big as a carpet, sketching whimsical scenes about the ancient Romans, rain forest, the french revolution, the solar system and so on. I was drawing with a black felt tip pen and my schoolmates were instructed to color my creations. So most of the time I was sorrownded by my friends, very committed in fill my b&w drawing with beautiful colors, all lying on their stomach, just like me. 
My Daimon had a lot of fun! Soncino, my small medieval town, in northern Italy, collects all the main carachteristics of a city, just as a child could imagine. The citadel, slightly raised on the plain with the Alps in distance, is embraced by large red brick walls that at one point, like an origami, bend in a thousand sides and creates a crenellated fortress, furrowed by drawbridges. 
Medieval, Renaissance and Baroque architecture is not lacking and there is even a fourteenth-century heptagonal tower, unique in Europe, leaning like the tower of Pisa.
Thus, influenced by my small but multifaceted village, palaces, towers and windows began to appear in my childhood drawings as far as the eye could see. However, it was my first trip to a big city that blew my interest in architecture and the urban landscape. I was 8 years old and, with my uncles Anna and Peppo, I visited Rome. I was spellbound. I was struck by everything, both in beauty and in size. I was experiecing everything as a magical adventure. The immense spaces, the noisy streetlife, the sunlight reading the surfaces of ancient walls, things that I had just studied at school and found there, like different walls textures: opus incertum, opus reticulatum, opus mixtum, walls and arches built with immense blocks of stone, fragments of colossal statues, luxuriant fountains. The thing that struck me most in this merry-go-round of emotions was the Pantheon. The emotional impact that the two-thousand-year-old concrete dome with the 9-meter-wide oculus from which rain and sun rays alternated made me decide to be an Architect.
So 10 years later, after the Liceo Classico,the high school, here I am at the Faculty of Architecture at Milan Polytechnic. It is here that the love for the theme grew stronger, while the drawing begins to fluctuate schizophrenically between cold technical design and soft freehand lines. Meanwhile, my Daimon makes me attend the school of comics in via Savona, where the teacher Coca Frigerio, pushing me to deepen the illustration, introduces me to the work of many great Italian illustrators and artists such as Adelchi Galloni and Emanuele Luzzati and above all to the great Bruno Munari in person.
Bruno Munari was a disruptive example, above all for his originality and the sense of freedom that his method and approach had. A perfect Daimon awakener.
In the meantime, it could not be placed in a specific area. A designer? Of course, but also a great illustrator, indeed a conceptual artist, a sculptor of useless machines, origami, dynamic works, a teacher who used an extraordinary method capable of developing creativity, this unknown then as today, a free spirit that preserved intact the creativity of the child, so much so that he was completely at ease with children not yet corrupted by bad teachers. Seeing Bruno Munari working in the creative workshops I collaborated with during my graduation was an experience that instilled in my mind a new way of seeing, more free and nonconformist.
At this point the Daimon was jumping with enthusiasm. It is not for a coincidence that Enthusismos in ancient Greek means: "Having a god inside".

So I started working in parallel as a freelance architect and as an illustrator. Both worked well. However, I was very disturbed and bored by the various bureaucratic aspects that the profession of architect required, moreover, after a few years, the Daimon of the drawing recalcitrated, asking me for more time and commitment in what was obviously my destiny. Just at that time, La Repubblica, the first Italian newspaper, called me for a long collaboration, while the MTA in New York asked me for a large illustration dedicated to the American city subway and at that point I decided to dedicate myself completely to illustration. I therefore quit the profession of architect, but architecture continues to be the protagonist in my designs.
By now my Daimon could express himself freely and my sense of eudaimonia, of satisfaction and completeness, confirmed to me the right choice.
Since then the years dedicated to drawing began, experimenting with methods, colors, techniques up to shaping a very recognizable style that continues to make my Daimon win many international awards such as the Treccani Web Prize in 2016, the American Illustration Award, the Gold Medal from the American magazine Creative Quarterly as well as various Communication Arts "Awards of Excellence".
This is how it happens when you indulge your Daimon and push him to express himself freely. Something magically positive starts, everyone begins to function well and things happen.
One of these things happened on the day when the director of Moleskine Publishing Roberto di Puma called me asking me to propose them my personal project, "whatever you want"he said. My Daimon immediately suggested his dream to me: a series of illustrated books on the most important cities in the world. Today the series collects 3 titles, I am Milan, I am London and I am New York. We are thinking about the next city to give voice to.
So the I am the City series is the activity at the center of my work as an illustrator. Many other initiatives flourish around my books such as lectures and workshops, like  those recently held in New York and exhibitions such as the one at the Africa Center in Manhattan, organized by the Moleskine Foundation, or the personal exhibition at the Bonvini Gallery in Milan inaugurated in 2018.
Meanwhile, the projects continue for many other realities such as the new Futurium Museum in Berlin, the Piccolo Teatro in Milan, the large installation to be created at Malpensa airport on the initiative of MEET-Fondazione Cariplo and other books on architecture and music for the Berlin publisher Raum Italic and Princeton Architectural Press in New York.
Long live the Daimon!

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Nasima Alam. I am a primary school teacher, turned self taught cake artist, specialising in bespoke wedding cake designs.  My cake journey was a very unexpected one, which began in 2015 by pure accident. I’ve always been into art and pursued this up to University level. My artistic interests were also evident in my home interior and design, when I dabbled in property developing. It took a different direction when I began to implement this into cake decorating.

 I’ve always enjoyed baking but to be able to take this to an artistic level was very much up my street.  I began teaching myself new skills and techniques through watching lots of YouTube videos and before I knew it, by 2016 Sweet Drops of Heaven was established as a viable registered business. I  teach cake decorating classes, have my own cake stencil designs and also created a cake decorating product called Sweet Flakes of Heaven.  I’ve been fortunate enough to collaborate with large businesses such as Daniel Wellington and have been featured in many industry cake magazines, such as Satin Ice, Cake Masters, Cake Decoration & Sugar Craft.

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm a self-taught Dutch illustrator with a keen eye for detail and a clean minimal style. I love illustrating because I lose all sense of time when I'm drawing. I can get lost in creating smooth and clean lines or getting a character or pose just right.

In my personal projects I try to tell small (and often melancholic) stories about adventure, youth, love, and heartbreak. They can get quite dark. The narratives usually aren't well defined, but I hope the viewer can still sense them. 

I'm also proud to have collaborated with brands and studios like AKQA, Wired, Ueno, New Scientist, and Mathematic. On the side I run a small print shop from my studio in Amsterdam, lovingly creating beautiful giclée fine art prints.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hola! soy Diego Fernández, nací en Buenos Aires, Argentina, soy docente de Morfología de diseño industrial en la Facultad de Arquitectura, Diseño y Urbanismo, de la Universidad de Buenos Aires desde el año 2003, y trabajo en proyectos de diseño industrial. 
   
   Mi carrera se divide entre la docencia y el desarrollo de proyectos relacionados al diseño industrial, y mis trabajos incluyen desarrollos de mobiliario para hogar y oficina, diseño de material para punto de venta (P.O.P.), arquitectura publicitaria (Stands), packaging, diseño de juguetes, equipos de electro medicina, diseño de golosinas y de matricería para golosinas, algunos desarrollados en empresas como Buró s.a.i.c., Propos s.a., RMB design solutions, T.M. Group, Craverolanis s.a., G.C. Properties s.a., Fabrinco srl, Jotatec s.a., Planeta dulce s.a., Flyline  y otros desarrollados en formato freelance.  

   Entre mis otros intereses están la escultura tradicional, fabricación de muebles, planificación y elaboración de maquetas y prototipos. Actualmente estoy incursionando en la escultura digital, con el objetivo de seguir desarrollando mis herramientas conceptuales y técnicas, porque considero que la formación profesional debe ser constante.

   Mi carrera se divide entre la docencia y el desarrollo de proyectos relacionados al diseño industrial, y mis trabajos incluyen desarrollos de mobiliario para hogar y oficina, diseño de material para punto de venta (P.O.P.), arquitectura publicitaria (Stands), packaging, diseño de juguetes, equipos de electro medicina, diseño de golosinas y de matricería para golosinas, algunos desarrollados en empresas como Buró s.a.i.c., Propos s.a., RMB design solutions, T.M. Group, Craverolanis s.a., G.C. Properties s.a., Fabrinco srl, Jotatec s.a., Planeta dulce s.a., Flyline  y otros desarrollados en formato freelance.  

   Entre mis otros intereses están la escultura tradicional, fabricación de muebles, planificación y elaboración de maquetas y prototipos. Actualmente estoy incursionando en la escultura digital, con el objetivo de seguir desarrollando mis herramientas conceptuales y técnicas, porque considero que la formación profesional debe ser constante.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy Silvia.
Apasionada de las historias y el papel desde pequeña. 
Escuché cientos de historias que me trasladaban en el tiempo. Nantes mi tatarabuelo mapas, libros. El taller de mis bisabuelos de litografía y el de mi abuelo y sus hermanos convertido en linotipia. La familia de papel y tinta a la que pertenezco.
Estudié encuadernación artesanal y artes del libro en el Palacio Real de Madrid para volver a darle uso a ese bastidor de madera traído de Nantes. 
Adoro coser libros, estampar tapas y sobre todo contar historias a través del papel. 
Monté mi propio estudio-taller LIBRACOS en 2008 y desde 2016 me he especializado en libros en dimensión (pop-up)
Trabajo con marcas como Disney, Loewe, Meliá, Bvlgari, Globe- Trotter. Instituciones como el Gobierno Vasco, Ayuntamiento de Madrid, y he tenido la suerte de tener expuesto un pequeño pop-up en el Museo Guggenheim de Bilbao, junto al artista Char-lee Mito. 
Trabajo para producciones audiovisuales, presentaciones especiales y producciones editoriales únicas 
Adoro mi pequeño taller, situado en una antigua carbonería del barrio Imperial de Madrid, donde no paran de florecer proyectos y plantas.

web : libracos.com 
Instagram @libracos_

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm born in 1982 in Tortona (AL), I live and work in Voghera (Italy).
In 2007 i achieved my degree in painting at the Art Academy of Brera (Milan).

i work exclusively with colored pencils, I often represent the flora, fauna and female mystics of Sardinia from the 16th to the 18th centuries
Combining organic shapes and textures with chiaroscuro contrasts of light and shadow, my drawings portray isolated female faces framed by plants and animals. 
My imagery refers to the herbalist traditions and Sardinian folklore of the mystical seductresses who enchant, curse and cure. My body of work is a tribute to the legacy of healing women throughout history. 

my works appeared in books, newspapers and magazines such as The New Yorker, Juxtapoz Magazine, Hi Fructose Magazine, Les Arts Dessines, Arte Mondadori.
With Albin Michel I published the illustrated book "Poucette" (distributed in Spain for Edelvives with the title "Pulgarcita"). I'm preparing an illustrated book in collaboration with Sébastien Perez.

I collaborate with Jonathan LeVine Projects (New Jersey) and Thinkspace Projects (Los Angeles) for America, Gallery Benoni (Copenhagen), Galleria Patricia Armocida (Milan), Galleria Giovanni Bonelli (Milan) for Europe.
I took part in the 54th International Art Exhibition, Biennale di Venezia, Italian Pavilion, curated by Vittorio Sgarbi, Lombardy Regional Pavilion, Palazzo Te, Mantova, "Turn The Page: the first ten years of hi-fructose" at the Virginia Museum of Contemporary Art (Moca) (US), POW! WOW! Hawai'i at the Honolulu Museum of Art School (US), THE NATURE SQUISITE: BEYOND THE BOUNDARIES OF POP at the Stelline Foundation (Milan), The New Vanguard - at The Lancaster Museum of Art and History (MOAH) and IMAGO at the Much Museum in Munich (Germany).
Among my solo shows: “Dear Collapse” Thinkspace Project (Los Angeles), “Monism” Galleri Benoni (Copenhagen), “Il Ricordo è un Consolatore Molesto” Galleria Patricia Armocida (Milan), “Home” Galleria Giovanni Bonelli (Milan), “ Animanera ”Jonathan LeVine Gallery (NY).

teacher.aboutMe:
O estúdio paulistano Marmota vs Milky foi fundado em 2012 por Carlos e Fabi: Artistas visuais, amarelos e formados em Desenho Industrial pela UNESP Bauru. Eles assinam trabalhos de estilo versátil, mas distintos e reconhecíveis pela influência do design gráfico japonês e técnicas vetoriais avançadas.

A dupla colaborou com projetos de publicidade para grandes marcas como Adidas, Burger King, Hyundai, Red Bull e Nike. Eles também participaram da  criação da primeira geração de NFTs on-chain (Metadados e Arte usando arte SVG) para Avastars, expuseram uma arte no evento Urban Nation Berlin e criaram a identidade visual do Pixel Show 2016 e 2017, o maior evento de criatividade da América Latina. 

Os artistas também contribuíram para importantes causas sociais, como o aplicativo Woman Interrupted, Card Heroes (cartões de agradecimento entregues a médicos e enfermeiras na linha de frente para lutar contra Covid -19 escrito por pessoas com doença de Parkinson) e a campanha Save Salla, que ganhou um Grand Prix em Cannes Lions em 2021.

Hoje, eles equilibram seu tempo entre seus dois cursos sobre ilustração vetorial desenvolvidos em parceria com a Domestika com trabalhos autorais que buscam explorar a identidade nipo-brasileira do duo.

teacher.aboutMe:
¡Hola! soy José Bermúdez, Diseñador Industrial en la Ciudad de México y Colombia. Luego de haber vivido en Suecia y trabajado en otros estudios de diseño como Esrawe, decidí abrir mi propia casa / estudio, colaborando con otros diseñadores de todo el mundo para diseñar piezas únicas y ediciones limitadas, inspiradas en la funcionalidad y simpleza del diseño Japonés combinado con la estética Escandinava.

Mi trabajo ha sido publicado en los mejores blogs y revistas de todo el mundo, gracias a esto puedo dar a conocer mas mi trabajo y poder compartirlo con demás diseñadores para entender las distintas filosofías de diseño. 

Mi trabajo ha sido exhibido en varias de las mejores ferias de diseño del mundo entre ellas Milan Design Week, Wanted Design en Nueva York, Design Week Mexico, Feria de arte en Brasil y el Furniture exhibtion en Nybro, Suecia. 

Por más de 5 años he diseñado producto, mobiliario y proyectos de interiorismo. Creo firmemente que el diseño es una herramienta en la cual puedo expresar y crear historias, generando una emoción a mis clientes cuando adquieren uno de mis productos. Me gusta combinar procesos low – tech y piezas hechas a mano por los mejores artesanos, dando valor y calidad a cada producto.

teacher.aboutMe:
Mads Berg is one of the world’s most prominent artists in his genre, whose designs and illustrations cater to an international and prestigious range of clients. His main fields of work are brand Illustrations, key visuals, posters, maps, advertising and editorial illustrations, cover art, murals, map design, icon design, and type design.

His illustration style is celebrated for translating classic poster art into a modern and timeless look.

Mads graduated from the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts in 2001, and since then he has been working independently as an illustrator, occasionally working as a lecturer at design schools. He is often requested to serve in design and illustration award juries for contemporary work. In 2010 he won the "Best Danish Children's Comic" prize and in 2009 he won the Danish Design Prize. His poster art is represented at the Danish National Design Archives at the Design Museum.

CLIENTS INCLUDE: Coca-Cola, Toyota, PlayStation3, Fanta, Orangina, Mersk, Iceland Air, Carlsberg, Lego, Bottega Veneta, SAS, Copenhagen Airport, San Diego Zoo, Oxford University Press, Vanity Fair, The Washington Post, Hansen's, Frank's Originals.

teacher.aboutMe:
Nací en una casa de mil colores en medio de la selva, en las afueras de Medellín, Colombia. Una selva llena de pájaros, árboles gigantes y plantas deslumbrantes. Florecía todos los días del año. Cuando me fui, esa selva se convirtió en mi obsesión y en mi musa.

Soy Catalina Estrada, ilustradora y diseñadora de estampados colombiana. Vivo en Barcelona desde 1999. A través de mis diseños, busco acompañar a las personas con luz, color y optimismo, creando puentes que conecten sus vidas con la energía vibrante de la naturaleza y la cultura latina.

He tenido la suerte de colaborar con marcas como Paul Smith, Coca-Cola, Microsoft, Camper, Nike, Levis, Smart (Mercedes Benz), UNICEF, Amnistía Internacional, y gobiernos como los de Barcelona, Londres y la India.

Me gusta la idea de que mis estampados acompañen a las personas, llenando su entorno de belleza, color y calidez, transformando lo cotidiano en algo especial.

A través de mi trabajo también he podido conectar con causas profundamente hermosas y participar en proyectos sociales tanto en Colombia como en otros lugares del mundo.

Creo en el diseño como una manera de crear puentes que conecten a las personas, para que, juntos, podamos construir cosas maravillosas y generar un cambio positivo en el mundo.

teacher.aboutMe:
Tengo muchos perfiles. El único que realmente está avalado por una cédula profesional es el de "Historiador". Me siento cómoda diciendo soy historiadora porque sí lo soy, hay un título por ahí que lo dice, que lo "certifica". Pero en realidad soy muchas otras cosas, entre ellas, escritora para niños. Ese título no existe en ningún lugar. Quizá alguna universidad del mundo ya lo avaló y sí existe y aún no lo sé. Cuando comencé a escribir decía "soy escritora". Un profesor en la SOGEM me sacó de mi fantasía: "escritores" cuando ya tienen libros publicados. 

Y yo no tenía nada publicado.

Me tocó el internet en donde publicar algo en un blog no calificaba como publicación (por ahí del 2005). Luego eso cambió, los concursos decían sin publicar, ni en internet (por ahí del 2010).

Cuando era niña decía que era Acapulqueña, lo primero que me dio una etiqueta de "ser" fue la tierra que me vio nacer. Pero mis padres son chilangos. Así que de niña me decían "no tienes nada de Acapulco". Pero yo sentía que sí, que nacer en Acapulco tenía un sentido. Desde que cumplí un año he vivido en la ciudad de México, incluso ahora. Siento que nunca podré vivir en otra ciudad. Me inspira mucho vivir en México, pero casi todas mis semblanzas dicen: Acapulco, 1984.

Mi primer acercamiento con la literatura infantil fue en la SOGEM (Sociedad General de Escritores de México), en esta escuela estudié el Diplomado en Creación Literaria y tuve mi primera clase en Literatura Infantil y Juvenil impartida por la escritora Verónica Murguía. Al terminar este diplomado entré a estudiar la carrera de Historia en la Facultad de Filosofía y Letras en la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México. Mientras estudiaba la carrera gané la mención honorífica del concurso Invenciones que organizaba Nostra Ediciones, publiqué mi libro "Checo" en 2010. Es un libro que nace de una clase de historia oral, y una serie de entrevistas a mi abuelo, es mi primer libro para niños pero también mi primer trabajo como historiadora.

Posteriormente hice la maestría en Historia del Arte en la UNAM. En la maestría tuve una estancia académica en Madrid y estuve haciendo investigación de archivo en la Biblioteca Nacional de España. Estas investigaciones me ayudaron para concretar mi tema de tesis pero también para generar una ficción que desembocó, años después, en la beca de Jóvenes Creadores del FONCA, en la disciplina Novela. 

Durante los años de la maestría estuve paralelamente editando y haciendo libros. Primero en un pequeño estudio de gestión cultural que hicieron un par de compañeras de la Facultad llamado Estudio Paraíso. Después entré a trabajar a la Biblioteca Vasconcelos como coordinadora cultural de talleres enfocados en público infantil. Al año de estar en esta Biblioteca me invitaron a editar los libros del Fondo Editorial Tierra Adentro. Finalmente dejé de editar libros para enfocarme en la beca del FONCA. En este momento también estuve escribiendo los libros "Barba Azul" y "La voz de Malintzin". 

Después entré en ese momento de la vida en donde uno debe dedicarse 100% a hacer cosas que le gusta. Y estuve trabajando en una pequeña imprenta risográfica. Ahí, además de editar, me puse a dibujar y diseñar y a aprender de procesos de impresión de manera muy Montesori. Hice mis primeros fanzines e impartí los primeros talleres de edición y escritura.

Me di cuenta que lo que quería hacer no cabía en un solo cajón, que abarcaba varias cosas. Escribir libros y editar libros comenzó a tomar un rumbo que me llevó a imaginar la posibilidad de hacer mi propio sello. A finales de 2016 decidí fundar mi propia editorial: Pitzilein Books. La editorial se enfoca en editar y publicar libros de ilustradores, artistas y escritores que se encuentran en la frontera de los géneros literarios: crónica y ficción, filosofía y literatura, gráfica y literatura infantil. Pero también con la idea de publicar libros con formatos extraños como mapas, enciclopedias y fanzines. En 2018 gané la beca de la Fundación de Arte Contemporáneo JUMEX con el apoyo de publicaciones impresas. Y recientemente, en 2020, obtuve el apoyo de Fomento Editorial de la UNAM para publicar un manual ilustrado de cuidado de gatos.
 
Mi trayectoria como escritora ha sido fundamental para editar y conceptualizar libros. Vivimos una época en donde editores, escritores y artistas comenzamos a borrar las fronteras de hacer y crear libros. Un libro puede nacer de una idea, pero también de un dibujo, o de comenzar a doblar hojas e imaginar otras formas de lectura.

2020 para muchos fue el año de la pandemia, para mí simbolizó lograr concretar muchos proyectos que me emocionan y me gustan. Encerradita aprendí más sobre mí misma. Este curso de Domêstika es producto también de esa otra manera de ver la literatura y los libros para niños.

¡Hola!

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi, I’m Anna and I’m a watercolour artist based in London, UK. I love painting bright and colourful florals and in my spare time. Painting is free and therapeutic to me. When I first started I didn't care about the outcome and explored different techniques, colours and materials until I developed my style. It's still changing, but I have become more confident with my work as I have practiced over the past couple of years. Through this journey, I have taken classes and inspirations from other teachers. I believe it's valuable to share our work and process, as you never know who you may inspire!
With my paintings, I started an Instagram account and Etsy store. I never thought they would achieve what they have so far. I'm so grateful for the support so far and now excited to share more about what I do.

teacher.aboutMe:
Matt Kenney is a professional furniture maker that has written dozens of articles and two books about woodworking. As a child growing up in Florida, he made tree forts and skate ramps, but for the last 20 years he has been making furniture. His passion for the craft led to an editorial job at Fine Woodworking magazine, where he wrote articles, was feature in how-to videos, and co-hosted the popular Shop Talk Live podcast. Starting in Spring 2015, Matt made 52 boxes in 52 weeks. That project became the basis for his first book, 52 Boxes in 52 Weeks (Taunton Press). He left the magazine in 2018 to spend more time with his tools. He’s been making furniture, traveling the US and world to teach, and writing since. Matt constantly strives to improve his craftsmanship and design. The result of his efforts is furniture that is modern but grounded in the best of classic design, able to sit harmoniously alongside a wide range of furniture styles, and built to survive generations of daily use.

Matt’s passion for the craft led him to learn the Japanese art of kumiko, which he incorporates into his furniture and uses to create beautiful decorative wall hangings. His love for kumiko pushed him to share the art with others, so he began to teach it and eventually wrote a book about it: The Art of Kumiko (Blue Hills Press, 2020).  He has taught kumiko both in the United States and internationally, and believes that its popularity is due to its delicate elegance and stunning geometric patterns. Although kumiko appears complex and difficult to make, Matt’s experience has allowed him to develop techniques that make the art approachable to beginners and seasoned woodworkers, and that produce excellent results even the first time you give it a try.

Fotógrafo há 20 anos e Diretor de Cena/Filmmaker há 10.
Começou a carreira como fotojornalista no extinto jornal Notícias Populares (1999), fez parte da equipe que fundou o jornal Valor Econômico (2000) e fundou o coletivo Cia de Foto (2004 ~2014). De 2014 a 2018 trabalhou com sua própria produtora de conteúdo digital, em São Paulo. Desde 2019 vive em Milão (Itália).
Em 2009 começou a trabalhar também como diretor de cena em filmes publicitários e corporativos, além de seus próprios projetos artísticos. Essa data coincide com o lançamento da primeira câmera DSLR com a função video. O sensor fullframe, a portabilidade, qualidade da imagem e a intimidade com o equipamento mudou o pensamento em relação a produção de filmes. Tornou-se possível produzir videos com muita qualidade com a mesma câmera que fotografava.
Nesses anos fez campanhas para clientes de todos os tipos e de todos os tamanhos. Nike, Vivo, Brastemp, Martini, Basico, Converse, entre muitos outros.

I am interested in three dimensional geometric form and my range of unique designs are created through intricate scoring and folding techniques through which I explore how light, colour and geometry interact. 
I have exhibited at the London Design Fair, Marseille (France) and had  solo shows at the Manchester Craft and Design Centre and The Lighthouse in Glasgow.  I have been teaching the art of paper folding for over five years and have taught both privately and with organisations such as the Barbican, the DCA and Cockpit Arts in London. I am regularly commissioned by private clients and interior designers and have made lighting for numerous cafes, restaurants and public venues.

I am now freelance and have previously worked with studios such as It's Nice That, Media Arts Lab, 4creative, 2xElliott, GBH and The Office of Craig Oldham. teacher.aboutMe: Soy escritor y profesor de literatura infantil. A lo largo de los últimos quince años me he dedicado a investigar, analizar y promover los libros para niños, me gusta mucho compartir lo que descubro, por lo que imparto talleres y cursos en distintas instituciones y de manera independiente. He publicado libros infantiles en editoriales como La Cifra y Oink, además participar en distintos proyectos independientes y de auto publicación. También he escrito contenidos audiovisuales dirigidos al público infantil, así como guiones para espectáculos que fusionan la danza y la música con la poesía, buscando despertar el gusto por jugar con la palabra entre las niñas y los niños. Me gusta indagar sobre el mundo en libros científicos, explorar diccionarios y fijarme todo lo que hay a mi alrededor en la vida cotidiana para ver qué hay más allá de lo que podemos ver a simple vista, inspirándome a imaginar y escribir.

teacher.aboutMe:
I am a wool-based fibre artist from the South Coast of England with a love of playful colours and textures. Born without a sense of smell, I believes my sense of complementary colours has been heightened to compensate. I have been lucky enough to have written 2 books, '40 Knots and How to Tie Them' and my next book 'Punch Needle Embroidery for Beginners' which is out in November 2020.

A bit about my weaving practice:
In 2013 I saw a small wooden lap loom on Ebay and not really having a clue what it was, I bought it anyway. I didn’t realise that this would be the start of my love for weaving. Teaching myself with books from the library and anything I could find on the internet I managed to find my own style and am well and truly addicted. Trying to create as much texture in my work and exploring the use of colour I look forward to where this weaving journey will take me.

teacher.aboutMe:
I am a French artist living in Barcelona. I define my self as a mobile illustrator and I register my life in drawings: I filled about 200 sketchbooks during the past 18 years.
I use to sketch on vintage accounting books that I find in flea markets. This yellow paper with red and blue lines remind me the first paintings and observations that bring back the scientist expedition of the XVIIIth century like Cook or Laperouse from unknown civilisations and lands. I secretly want to become one of those explorers.
The economy of medium is also what I appreciate. I'm traveling light and don't need much more than a sketchbook, inkpens, watercolor and my folding stool. The street is my studio. 
Nowadays that most of the people are focused on digital, being unplugged with a simple sketchbook made of second hand paper and inviting the spectator to look through it flipping the pages is magic.

Sketching from direct observation and reporting become my main activity. I already published 30 books about Barcelona, Paris, Berlin, Cuba, Ouessant island (…) and thematic like "art nouveau", "vintage cars" or "planes" after my nomination as an official air and space painter for the french army.

Follow my daily adventures on my instagram:

teacher.aboutMe:
Michael set up Johnson Banks in 1992. His company is known for how they define, then design, brands that make a difference. 

They work with people who want to do big things: tackle hunger; fight for an open internet; address child poverty; raise billions for innovation and education; bring culture and enlightenment to the world; create products that question the norm; shift paradigms and change lives. 

Their projects are as varied as world famous museums, art centres in Philadelphia and Paris and not-for-profits across the world. They rebranded the pioneers of ethical investment, Acumen Fund, and for Mozilla undertook the world’s first truly ‘open’ rebrand. They rebranded Action Against Hunger across 54 countries, worked for the Gates Foundation in Europe and in the UK they are working with the University of Cambridge and Imperial College. Recently they have rebranded Teach First, Duolingo, the UN Climate Change Conference (COP26), the Royal Academy of Music, campaigned for the National History museum and rebranded Jodrell Bank. They are currently working on projects across public health, further education, climate change innovation and cultural outreach.

Johnson himself oversees the strategic and creative output of the company but is just as likely to roll up his sleeves and get involved in the work himself. He is a regular speaker at the world’s design and branding conferences, including multiple appearances at Typo Berlin, Kyoorius Design Yatra in India and Brand New conferences in the USA and Europe. 

He has conducted lecture tours across India and China, been an external examiner at multiple UK design colleges and is a Fellow of Ravensbourne College. He is currently visiting professor at Glasgow School of Art, a visiting tutor at Kingston University and a visiting lecturer at multiple universities including Art Center, SVA, UEA & the University of Cambridge. His online branding course on verbal and visual branding has thousands of students across the globe.

He has written three books, including the transatlantic bestseller 'Branding: In five and a half steps' and his third, 'Now Try Something Weirder' was published in 2019. He has won most of the design world’s key prizes, including seven ‘Yellow’ and one ‘Black’ Pencil from D&AD, and has dozens of designs in the V&A's permanent collection. In 2022 he was inducted into Design Week's Hall of Fame and in 2017 he was awarded D&AD's highest honour, the President’s Award, joining a list of previous recipients that include Terence Conran, Ridley Scott, Wally Olins, Alan Parker and John Hegarty.

teacher.aboutMe:
Swedish manga artist and illustrator with a professional career since 2006. In my 14 years as a professional manga artist, I have made over 1600 pages of manga, most of them published as books or part of comic anthologies. My most well-known works are Mjau! and Sword Princess Amaltea, published in Sweden, USA, Italy, Germany, Portugal and the Czech Republic. 

My works vary in genre from fantasy and action to romance and comedy. I love every part of the manga making process and love teaching the neat tricks I've gathered through the years to other aspiring manga creators. I'm a member of the Swedish manga artist collective Nosebleed Studio and I'm also a co-organizer of the annual comic zine festival Seriefest in Malmö. 

Educated at Serieskolan (Comic Art School) in Malmö, Sweden, where I also worked for many years as a teacher. Have done lectures in comic art at California College of the Arts in San Fransisco, USA, and at ACME in Milan, Italy, among others.

teacher.aboutMe: My name is Karmen Loh, also known as Bearbrickjia and I'm an independent digital illustrator. Art has been part of my life for as long as I can remember. I decided to pursue this passion and joined an art college to study 3D animation back in 2013. After graduating in 2016, I realized that I was more interested in illustration. Luckily, with my illustration portfolio that I had worked on in my free time, I received an opportunity to work in a video game company as a concept artist and got to work on game titles such as "Street Fighter V", ''Steel Circus'' and more! During my time there, I continued working on my own personal projects which are characters and portraits. My artworks have often been described as feminine, fantasy with dreamy vibes. In 2019, I've decided to leave the game industry to work as an independent artist and collaborated with XP-Pen, Clip Studio Paint, MrSuicideSheep and more. In 2022, I created key visual illustrations for Coca-Cola & Costa China. In the same year, I created book cover illustrations for publishers such as HarperCollins, Holiday House Books, Penguin Teen/Penguin Random House and more. In 2024, I had the opportunity to create a key art for the Pokémon Championships 2023-24 in Asia. In the same year, I teamed up with PUBG Mobile and Medibang for a global character design contest—PUBG MOBILE x ARTstreet PDP Classic Theme Design Contest.

Amazink es un estudio de serigrafía manual ubicado en el centro de Madrid. 

A los mandos del estudio esta Noelia Tramullas, ilustradora y maestra de taller, con muchas ganas de contagiar su pasión por la gráfica y más concretamente por la serigrafía en ediciones limitadas. 

Realizo proyectos tanto para artistas e ilustradores como  personales, siempre dejando espacio a la experimentación y tratando de superar los limites de la técnica. 

La finalidad del estudio es hacer llegar la serigrafía manual a mas gente, para ello se imparten cursos a diferentes niveles, monográficos para empresas e incluso eventos con serigrafía en vivo. teacher.aboutMe:
¡Hola! Mi nombre es Laura Elliott, soy artista textil y me dedico al tejido en telar. 
Mi pasión es tejer sobre naturaleza, leyendas e historias mágicas utilizando fibras naturales y telares de diferentes tamaños. Gran parte de mi familia es de origen inglés y danés por lo que el folklore de esas tierras siempre me ha interesado: duendes, hadas, trolls, dragones y más.

Partí tejiendo profesionalmente en 2017, luego de haber estudiado Arte y de haber realizado un diploma especializado en creación textil, donde aprendí a tejer en telar desde cero. Ahí logré obtener todos los conocimientos que necesitaba para saber que quería dedicarme a hacer tapices. Comencé tejiendo obras pequeñas y luego fui atreviéndome a hacer piezas más grandes, y así fui descubriendo técnicas que me llevaron a tejer alfombras y tapices de mayor tamaño utilizando diferentes tipos de telares. 

Ahora estoy trabajando en una serie de tapices medianos y grandes sobre el folklore de las islas británicas en un telar de bajo lizo (o telar de pedales). Si quieres ver mis procesos, te recomiendo seguir mi página de instagram. ¡Nos vemos!

teacher.aboutMe:
Estudié diseño de la comunicación gráfica en la UAM México, antes de graduarme ingrese al despacho de ilustración y diseño Tané, donde encontré la magia de la ilustración infantil, la cual me atrapo desde el inicio.
Trabaje por casi 20 años como coordinador del departamento de arte del Periódico Reforma, ejerciendo como ilustrador y haciendo labor de dirección de arte.
Mi trabajo lo encuentras principalmente en el campo editorial, diseñando carteles, ilustrando libros infantiles, ilustración de revista, periódicos, portadas de libros, animaciones y proyectos personales.
Tengo más de 40 libros ilustrados para diversas editoriales sobresaliendo Santillana (México,España), Diego Pun (España), Findaway (EU), Ediciones Castillo (México), Loqueleo (Mexico, España), Editorial Planeta,  Edelvives, etc
Mis dibujos han aparecido en diversas animaciones para Televisa, proyecto 68 voces y canal mórbido.
Mi trabajo ha sido reconocido en diversas ocasiones, destacando dos veces primer lugar del catálogo de ilustradores infantiles y juveniles (Conaculta, 2006, 2013), dos veces merecedor de mención en el concurso Iberoamérica ilustra ( 2014 y 2020) y ganador del premio "Fundación cuatro gatos" por su álbum ilustrado " Esa mañana" (EU 2017).
Gane tercer lugar en el concurso de cartel "Con nuestro ingenio invitemos a leer" (2007).
Fui encargado de la imagen y conceptualización de la 35 Feria internacional del libro infantil y juvenil (FILIJ) 2015 y de la Feria internacional del cuento Los Silos en dos ocasiones (2010 y 2020)
MI trabajo ha sido expuesto en México, España, Japón, Corea del Sur, Cuba, Francia, Chile y Colombia.
Desde hace más de 20 años he encontrado en la ilustración diversas formas de expresión, siempre he sido un ilustrador inquieto que prueba diversas técnicas tanto tradicionales como digitales, es muy difícil que mantenga un estilo y técnica por mas de un proyecto, pero siempre manteniendo un estilo propio.

teacher.aboutMe:
BRIK chocolate designs and handmake chocolates inspired by surfaces, raw materials and architecture, using natural ingredients, constant development, endless curiosity and a commitment to our planet. Bringing a new meaning to eye candy, BRIK tastes as intriguing as it looks. Our destinctive, aesthetic

Founded in 2020 by designer Kia Utzon-Frank and strategist Raffaella Baruzzo. Kia, who is teaching this course is a London-based Dane and founder of BRIK chocolate, creating genre-defying designs for clients like Wallpaper*, Sir Terence Conran, Harry Styles, Tom Dixon, The Barbican, Boghossian jewellery and Goop. Originally trained as a goldsmith, Kia turned her attention to the world of edibles, crafting cakes that look like marble sculptures, and now intricate, delicious chocolate textures inspired by architectural surfaces. 

Working with chocolate as a material, exploring its possibilities and limits, she has created a new perception of this classic indulgence that sparks surprise, wonder and a continuous development of new ideas. She believes that ideas are to be shared for others and herself to create more ideas. 

Raffaella is the cement that holds BRIK together. Her extensive background in sales, operations and business development has seen her work for the likes of Rococo and Fortnum&Mason. For decades the Italian native has been the architect behind the success of international chocolate, confectionary, tea, coffee and spice companies. Her gaze is firmly fixed on customer experience.

En el 2015, publiqué mi primer obra como autora integral: El Delirio de Ani. Una historieta de 184 páginas a todo color, a través de la Editorial Ivrea Argentina.

Posteriormente en el 2016, dediqué mi tiempo a la exploración y práctica del manga, participando en el certamen internacional: Silent Manga Audition. A su vez fui invitada a Japón, en la prefectura de Fukushima, en pos de fomentar el manga en los niños de la zona.

teacher.aboutMe:
Primeiro músico brasileiro a receber o título de Embaixador Ibero-Americano para a Cultura e a fazer parte da Academia do Oscar, cantor, compositor, arranjador, instrumentista, técnico do The Voice Brasil, do The Voice Kids e artista visual, o esteta intuitivo e gestual Carlinhos Brown é reconhecidamente um dos artistas mais criativos e inovadores da cultura brasileira, com uma trajetória consagrada através de sua atuação musical, social e percussiva, e pela exuberância das suas performances. Ao longo de sua trajetória, o mestre criativo criou a Banda Timbalada, participou da criação da Axé Music, dos Tribalistas, além de mergulhar nas artes visuais e ser o primeiro artista a testar um modelo completamente novo, formando uma experiência tripartite de produção para a distribuição das suas músicas: com foco na revitalização rítmica, Carlinhos Brown criou a escola de formação para músicos no Candeal, estúdio para gravação e os espaços culturais Candyall Guetho Square e Museu du Ritmo.
Entre os diversos prêmios recebidos em toda carreira, destacam-se seis Grammys e um Prêmio Goya, além do troféu entregue em reconhecimento à sua atuação como arte-educador pela ISME - Sociedade Internacional de Educação Musical. Em 2020, três novos álbuns nasceram sob o Selo do artista, a Candyall Music: “Axé Inventions – Àjààlà”, em comemoração aos 35 anos do Axé Music, primeiro álbum voltado inteiramente para o gênero; “Umbalista”, álbum onde Carlinhos interpreta de forma inédita algumas de suas composições consolidadas nas vozes de outros artistas; e o álbum infantil “Paxuá e Paramim em: A floresta dos rios voadores”, reunindo 10 canções com mensagens de preservação do meio ambiente. O ano em que Carlinhos Brown virou até tese de doutorado na Espanha, com sua arte ativista defendida pela artista plástica Durce Coelho, trouxe também três nova composições e promete muito mais chegando adiante: “Teia da Felicidade”, “Louvada Seja Dulce” e “ABOTA”, além da assinatura na trilha do novo espetáculo da talentosa Deborah Colker, intitulado “Cura”.

teacher.aboutMe:
Born and raised in Hokkaido, Japan, I started practicing Shodo at the age of five under the creative supervision of her grandmother, a distinguished GAYU calligrapher. Later I began to take sessions at a Gayu SHODO calligraphy school. This laid a solid foundation not only for my development of the various layers of calligraphy technique and skills but also for the SUMIE technique in calligraphic design.

I work as a freelance artist and a professional calligrapher in U.K./Europe and Japan Since 2000. Besides creating various media of calligraphy works and Neo-Japonism art, my passion for learning and teaching SHODO and the interest in developing the effective method of teaching this beautiful form of art has always been expanding. 

●Since 2002, I give SHODO the art of traditional Japanese calligraphy” lessons based on "one to one" private sessions as well as workshops and group classes . Through my teaching experiences in Japan and Europe with multiple age groups and backgrounds, I developed an original effective yet creative way of teaching SHODO - the Mindfulness-Based-Method. Which I believe works for everyone. I've been teaching with this method since 15 years now.

●I focus on bringing the balance of mind and body together as well as student's individual mindfulness process by specially designed practices. So students can learn little by little how to concentrate on their own Qi (living-energy) flow, conduct and apply it with brush and ink onto the paper.
My lesson is totally tailor suited to individual level/speed/needs and provides the most suitable text for the student's technical development in every lesson and workshops. 
The calligraphy texts are based on seasonal, classics, haiku, tanka, Zen and being prepared for improving sensitive stages of skills, techniques and calligraphy styles.

●My original method and concept of teaching SHODO calligraphy is focused on: 
- mind and body connection
- discovering individual inner quality and peace
- "hands-on" guidance 
- tailor-suited lesson for each individual and needs 
- the middle balance
- "Here and Now" momentum flow 
- the mindfulness process
- distressing the body tension
- breathing awareness
- rising the Qi(energy)flow and awareness 

More info and details:
My SHODO site: 
My Neo-Japonism site: 
ARIGATO

●My inspiration is classical Japanese literature, Ukiyoe & floating world, poetry& classic calligraphy, Japonisme influenced art, Art Nouveau & Art Déco styles, antique Kimono, art of Taisho Romanticism (1910-20's style) and modern art of Japan. As well as everyday life’s living words and letters, living colours, lines, patterns and shapes .

●My passion is to discover a continuity of time and spiritual existence and develop what I refer to as the ’Neo-Japonism’ — a new form of style depicting and conveying the sense of Japanese aesthetics. Specially I am fascinated by a new quality of a co-exisitng spirit and aesthetic as a result of uniting the essence of traditional Japanese art & craftsmanship and various form of Japonisme influenced modern paintings.
I use the new way of fusing my calligraphy and Sumie skills with those forms of art.
And - I just love doing it!

HAPPY PRCTICE!

teacher.aboutMe:
I am Akemi Lucas, a Japanese calligraphy master and also known as the artist 'Koshu'. I was born in Japan and embarked on my journey as a calligrapher at the age of eight, when my mother sent me to calligraphy school to improve my writing and sense of balance, which had been compromised from losing sight in my left eye from cancer. I was very sensitive and empathetic child, feeling emotions from others, which caused many illnesses on top of cancer from a young age. So I have learned how precious life is and also how powerful artworks are showing the artists's lives and emotions, which showed how important the mindset is when I hold my brush.

I was taught under Master Seizan Fujimoto, whose lineage is traced back to a well-known calligrapher of the Meiji period, Meikaku Kusakabe. At the age of 16, I started learning the style of Mr Goseki Nishiwaki through the Bunka Calligraphy association in Tokyo, and over time, I have learnt many diverse styles of calligraphy used by other well-known calligraphers.

At the age of 24, I was qualified as a calligraphy teacher and was given the name of "Koshu" by my master, then set up my own school, teaching calligraphy in Japan. After my English husband's death, I followed his wish and moved to the UK. I managed to re-start  my calligraphy and Sumi painting courses as “Koshu Japanese Art". My distinct style of calligraphy builds on traditional skills and the expression within my sumi paintings further embodies the fusion of the ancient and the modern, the eastern and the western, the before and the after.  I pour my deep love, with my faithful heart into every single stroke and hope that the messages in my artworks reach into people’s hearts and leave an echo for future generations.  

I have held several exhibitions in the UK, Japan, USA, and Georgia, and in 2019, in excess of 40 of her artworks were exhibited at the National Museum in the Capital city of Georgia, hosted by the Japanese Embassy. My workshops, demonstrations and online classes continue to be in high demand all over the world.
I also undertake commissioned work with recent highlights being; the creation of the label for the craft Gin and Liqueurs brand Kokoro, that received a Gold award for design in 2018; creating the artwork for new packaging for the Japanese food brand, Yutaka; I was also commissioned to create artworks for the Rugby World Cup Awards, that were held in Tokyo in 2019; and undertook a major commission for the Aldi, Team GB, Tokyo Olympic 2020 advertising campaign.  In May 2021, I launched my first online sumi painting course with Domestika, and soon after, launched the second course. In 2022, I also reopened my school Dream House in Japan, and will start organising residential courses and day workshops from 2024. My first Sumi painting book will be published in 2024. My artworks and courses have brought a broader appreciation of Japanese art and has introduced my work to a wider international audience.

I teach creative workshops to children, teachers and illustrators at my moveable school L'École de Papier. At the school, I research and reproduce many ancient narrative formats such as shadow theatres, theatre books, leperellos and story boxes.

I have collaborated as an illustrator in the french magazine Marketing and was invited among 3 other female artist to collaborate in a special edition of Le Chocolat des Français x Instagram (2018) which was launched to celebrate International Women's Day.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi! I’m Yulia and I’m a self-taught hand embroidery artist based in Cleveland, Ohio. You can find me on Instagram @mossandfeather. I’ve been embroidering for three years now. I’ve always liked art, like painting and drawing, but it wasn’t until I discovered embroidery that creating art became one of the most important aspects of my life. 

I specialize in thread painting, which is a technique used to create realistic embroidery. It’s a lot like painting on a canvas but using thread instead of paint. Using this technique, you can achieve fine artistic detail, including shading, highlights and smooth color gradients. 

I’ve always been inspired by nature and animals and I love how well thread mimics the look of fur and feathers. It’s really the perfect medium for the type of art I like to create.

teacher.aboutMe:
Contar historias a niños y niñas a través de los libros y otros soportes ha sido uno de mis motores en estos últimos veinte años. El 2002 fundé Amanuta con Constanza Recart, una editorial de libros ilustrados, donde textos e imágenes se complementan en los más de 150 títulos publicados. Desde ficción a libros científicos, desde libros para bebés a libros para jóvenes. Medio ambiente, pueblos originarios, flora, fauna, amistad, emociones, historia y actualidad, son algunos de los temas presentes en Amanuta. Varios de estos títulos han recibido reconocimiento en la Feria del libro de Bolonia y White Ravens entre otros. Soy autora de una docena de libros infantiles.
He asesorado a museos, instituciones y exposiciones en temas de contenidos infantiles, he realizado animaciones con temáticas de pueblos originarios y aplicaciones digitales interactivas. 

Lo manual y lo visual siempre han estado presentes en mi vida: en distintas formas, en distintas etapas, con distinta intensidad. Han sido los textiles los que me han acompañado por muchos años. Hago mis propios textiles, estudio técnicas precolombinas y a sus creadores, busco nuevos soportes y me aventuro en la joyería. Vuelvo al textil y busco materiales nuevos. Encuentro en la naturaleza toda mi fuente de inspiración, y me conecto con mi pasado y con los pueblos que habitaron este territorio que conocían y cuidaban la naturaleza. Me inspiro en artistas textiles que desarrollan este arte en todas sus dimensiones. También me conecto con las mujeres que desde tiempo remotos han contado historias, han sido tejedoras de relatos. Texto y textil se unen en sus tramas, relatos, nudos, hilos y desenlaces. Y cómo texto y textiles comparten sus raíces, ahí conecto mis pasiones, historias contadas con hebras, historias contadas con palabras.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hola! Soy Josefina Mogrovejo, Diseñadora de Imagen y Sonido; Fotógrafa y Directora de Arte. 

Mi trabajo se enfoca en Set Design, lo que también llamamos bodegón y naturaleza muertas. Recorrer mercadillos y casas de amigos en busca del prop ideal se ha vuelto mi especialidad! ;)

Exploro y resignifico objetos, busco combinaciones impensadas y soy una convencida de que podemos trasmitir el mensaje que queremos cuando todos los elementos de una fotografía están cuidadosamente seleccionados.

He trabajado en proyectos de pequeña y gran escala para clientes nacionales e internacionales como Disney, Nesquik, Beefeater, Mc Donalds, Tastemade, Brother, Monoblock, Kasadesign y Filgo, entre otros. 

Soy una fanática de generar mundos a través de distintos elementos, jugar con los colores y también combinar texturas y formas diversas.

Dicto talleres desde hace más de 10 años. Enseñar y transmitir lo que fui aprendiendo en estos años de trabajo es una de mis grandes pasiones.

Seguime en @josefinamvejo ;)

teacher.aboutMe:
With over 15 years of experience as a motion designer, I create bold, dynamic and engaging motion graphics and animations using Adobe After Effects and Cinema 4D. I’ve collaborated with global brands including Rolex, Rolls-Royce, HSBC, Microsoft, Samsung, Sony PlayStation, BT and EE, as well as innovative studios and agencies such as Squint Opera, VML, AKQA and Domestika.
 
My work spans 2D/3D motion design, social-first campaigns and data visualisation, always focused on making complex ideas accessible and visually striking. Alongside commercial work, I’m now expanding into responsible AI and ethics, applying design and storytelling to communicate emerging technologies with clarity and transparency.

In addition, I’ve shared my experience as a TED speaker and teacher, covering topics from design practice to time management and minimalism.
 
Specialities: After Effects, Cinema 4D, Motion Graphics, Animation, Social-First Design, Data Visualisation, Concept Development, Graphic/Digital Design, Ethical Storytelling.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Renata and I am a children's book author and illustrator. 

I grew up in Mexico City, and I've been an avid reader ever since I was a child. Whenever a book I was reading didn't have illustrations, I'd just make them myself. This is how I became interested in illustration as a career. 

I studied Design and Visual Communication at the National Autonomous University of Mexico, and then I moved to the UK to study an MA in Children's Book Illustration at the Cambridge School of Art.

My first picturebook, "The Cherry Thief", was published in 2014 in the UK by Child's Play International, and my second one, "My New Mom & Me", was published by Penguin Random House in 2016 and has been translated to seven languages. My third book, "A casa en tres idiomas", is a YA novel in Spanish, forthcoming by Editorial Porrúa.

As an illustrator, I've worked with many publishers of children's books in Mexico and the US, as well as some animation studios. I love experimenting with visual language, and I consider my work to be very versatile across fields and styles.

Other than drawing and reading, I love cooking, baking, knitting and riding my bike.

teacher.aboutMe:
AOP empezó hace más de tres años como un proyecto diario nacido de la voluntad de acercar el proceso creativo arquitectónico al colectivo imaginativo. Se trata de una herramienta de difusión e inspiración de la representación arquitectónica en forma de collage o render, donde la sensibilidad de los autores es la principal protagonista. 

Nuestra pasión por el mundo de la visualización arquitectónica nos llevó a crear nuestro propio estudio en el que actualmente trabajamos Brenda, arquitecta licenciada por la UPC y Alba, artista visual y profesora de modelado 3d en CIM, UPC, entre otras personas de nuestro equipo como Marta Cendra, Miriam, Andrea...

Así, con la mirada puesta en el detalle y una gran sensibilidad, trabajamos, si es necesario, desde la creación de un modelo 3D hasta la imagen final de un proyecto. 

Creemos que para diseñar, crear, proyectar, materializar y construir arquitectura o interiorismo, es necesario representarla en una imagen visual que además abra el camino a la experimentación durante el diseño.

Al principio empezamos con pequeños proyectos personales, hasta empezar a realizar encargos privados para estudios españoles pero también estudios a nivel internacional. 

Siempre intentando dar a las imágenes que creamos nuestro toque o estilo personal, diferente y pintoresco, que hablen un mismo lenguaje comprensible por todos. Además, procuramos que estas imágenes expliquen una historia y puedan transmitir sentimientos y  emociones a través de ellas.

teacher.aboutMe:
I love comic books. With more than 20 years experience drawing comic books, fanzines and stories with characters such as Judge Dredd, Power Rangers, Starship Troopers and VR Troopers, the narrative possibilities never cease to amaze me. I have drawn graphic novels with Robin Hood, King Arthur, Joan of Arc, the 16th century pirate Grace O’Malley and the graphic novel The Coldest City, written by Antony Johnston, was adapted to film in 2017 as Atomic Blonde, with oscar-winning Charlize Theron.

I have written and published numerous comic book short stories and creator-owned projects, both in the UK and Brazil, such as Project Mega-Ultra, WAR and 10 Lost Days, and also work with book and magazine illustration, plus storyboards for TV and advertising. I was born in England and now live in sunny São Paulo, with my wife and two daughters.

teacher.aboutMe:
Me llamo Helena Palau y soy una fotógrafa y videógrafa afincada en Barcelona. Soy una gran apasionada del mundo audiovisual desde pequeña, lo que me llevó a estudiar Comunicación Audiovisual en la UAB y especializarme en fotografía y vídeo de publicidad. Amante de los viajes, he conseguido que estos formen gran parte de mi línea editorial. He creado contenido para marcas y negocios de más de quince países por todo el mundo. He impartido por cuenta propia cursos de introducción a la fotografía de exteriores y técnicas outdoor por España. 
En mis fotografías y vídeos apuesto por visibilizar causas como la desigualdad social, la lucha por el medio ambiente o el feminismo. Mi trabajo cuenta con el apoyo de grandes marcas como Mapfre, LG España, Miki Travel Asia, L’Oréal o Teva con las que he colaborado en campañas de publicidad. Desde 2018 utilizo mi perfil de Instagram para compartir mis fotografías y experiencias con más de 58.000 seguidores de todo el mundo. Trabajo a diario en esta plataforma con la intención de crear una comunidad sana y más consciente del mundo que nos rodea.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy Estrellita Caracol, ilustradora, artista y autora.

Mi nombre real es Natalia Spadaro, pero todos me conocen por mi seudónimo, que es como elegí firmar mi trabajo.

El dibujo, el collage y los libros forman parte de mi vida desde que tengo memoria, quizás por eso me resulta tan natural utilizar esta técnica como forma de expresión. 

Me formé como diseñadora gráfica en la Universidad de Buenos Aires y si bien mi vida siempre estuvo rodeada de libros, no creía en la posibilidad de dedicarme a la ilustración, hasta que una propuesta inesperada para participar en la revista La Valijita de Billiken me abrió a ese mundo y supe que era lo que quería hacer. 
Comencé a ilustrar desde el oficio y me fui formando de manera autodidacta. Elegí trabajar y especializarme en el collage porque me resulta una técnica lúdica y versátil. Lo siento como un juego. Es inmediato y es como es, cuando se recorta algo ya está, no se puede borrar ni volver atrás, eso me parece maravilloso.

Mi trabajo fue editado por Gerbera Ediciones, Atlántida, Edelvives, MacMillan, Puerto de Palos, Estrada, Treintayseis, Dalúa, y Kalimat Publishing de los Emiratos Árabes.
Fui colaboradora permanente de la revista La Valijita de Billiken desde el 2007 hasta el 2019. Desde el 2016 trabajo en la adaptación de las canciones del Grupo Canticuénticos para convertirlas en libros álbum.

Me apasiona contar historias, hablar de mis sentimientos y pensamientos a través de las imágenes, me parece poderoso y universal. Y si bien la mayor parte de mi trabajo está dedicada a la creación de libros álbum de literatura infantil, no pienso que ilustro para niños, ilustro de acuerdo a la historia que quiero contar y a cómo la quiero contar y pienso que los libros ilustrados se los puede disfrutar a cualquier edad. Leer imágenes también es leer.

Además de hacer libros, dedico gran parte de mi tiempo a visitar escuelas y ferias del libro en Argentina y en otros países de Latinoamérica, donde organizo charlas, shows de collage en vivo, talleres y encuentros de ilustración para grandes y chicos.

Hola, soy diseñador e ilustrador con formación en diseño industrial, estudié en la Universidad Autónoma de México.
He colaborado con agencias y grandes marcas al rededor de todo el mundo, algunas son: Apple, Coca Cola, Autodesk, Miroculus, Volkswagen, ee mobile, Nexus, Cisco, creando personajes para animación, campañas publicitarias, video juegos, art toys, botargas, stands, empaques y máquinas que detectan cáncer. 

En mis creaciones lo más importante es el proceso, saber los usos y posibilidades que tendrá para poder salir de la pantalla y convertirse en: stickers, juguetes, pines, autos de control remoto, impresiones 2d y 3d.

Y lo primordial en mi desarrollo profesional son los proyectos personales, en los que puedo experimentar nuevas técnicas, materiales y flujos de trabajo sin estar atado a un brief o limitantes del cliente.

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm a writer of books, short stories, and a series of creative writing guides. I'm also an artist and a bookbinder. As a writer and teacher, I've created a series of Writing Maps to inspire other writers. Over the past fifteen years, I have edited literary magazines and collections of short stories, and set up small publishing houses, where I design different publications. 

Inspiration is everywhere, and I love sharing my writing journey, my approaches to writing, and my experiments with making books. For over 20 years, I've taught creative writing in colleges, schools, adult education and other settings, and run workshops in art galleries, bookshops, cafés, parks, a cemetery, and a zoo. 

My love for books as objects has led me to becoming a bookbinder and a book artist. Besides writing novels and short stories, I also make zines and photo books.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hola, soy Coralí Lecca Céspedes, ceramista y fundadora de Coraceramics.
Desde que nací estuve rodeada de las arcillas, pigmentos y esmaltes de mi madre, Sonia Céspedes Rossel, ceramista desde hace más de 40 años, cuyo taller siempre estuvo dentro de la casa. Contrario a lo que se imaginaría, mi interés por la cerámica no nació desde pequeña, sino todo lo contrario, mis intereses se inclinaron más hacia la música, la fotografía y lo audiovisual, tal es así que estudié ingeniería de sonido y luego ejercí durante 13 años la edición de video y animación de gráficas, de donde aprendí muchísimas cosas que hoy aplico en el mundo de la cerámica. 
Después de trabajar durante tantos años frente la computadora, tenía muchas ganas de cambiar de rubro y hacer algo con mis manos y no se me pasaba por la mente lo que la vida tenía guardado para mi.
En el año 2014, tras haber estado un año fuera del país, volví a Lima y mi madre, que tenía una tienda de cerámica en una feria anual de diseño, me pidió ayudarla, así que yo acepté feliz. A medida que fueron pasando las semanas, me interesaba más y más, tanto así que le pedí a mi madre ser su alumna en sus clases de cerámica y ella me recibió feliz!
A medida que iba pasando el tiempo, me emocionaba con todo lo que podía crear y sobre todo de lo feliz que me sentía al trabajar con ese material y todas las posibilidades de creación que existían. Fue así como jugando que decidí crear el instagram de @Coraceramics "Aventuras de una aprendiz de la cerámica" que era una bitácora de mis creaciones en clases. A medida que fui aprendiendo a través de las enseñanzas de mi madre, pasé a trabajar para ella y a formar parte del staff de producción de su taller y, en paralelo, tenía mis momentos de creación como Coraceramics.
Un día, me escribió una amiga que estaba abriendo su tienda de plantas a decirme que querían comprarme mis piezas y yo, sorprendida, no lo podía creer! "¿En serio quieren comprarlas?" - "Claro que sí!" - me dijeron y ahí comenzó una aventura que me ha traído hasta aquí, en la que sólo siento un profundo agradecimiento a cada persona y situación que me ha hecho aprender a lo largo de este camino.
Un tiempo después, me independicé como taller y marca y formé mi equipo, que son como mi familia, y fui aprendiendo sobre cómo llevar un emprendimiento y todas las tareas y responsabilidades que eso implica y que hoy lo siento como parte de la construcción de mi sueño en el día a día. 
Quién se imaginaría el camino que se me abriría al poner mis manos sobre la arcilla y que hoy es, en definitiva, el camino de mi vida.

Coraceramics nace del amor a la cerámica, a la familia, de la curiosidad y fascinación que despierta la transformación de un material a una pieza que te acompañará para toda la vida.

Meu nome é Naíma Almeida, sou artista visual, brasileira. Sou movida pela mistura de materiais e processos extremamente artesanais, com soluções digitais e novas possibilidades tecnológicas como realidade aumentada. Gosto de tentar dissolver os limites entre analógico e digital, craft e design. Meus trabalhos geralmente são uma explosão gráfica e colorida e exploram a tridimensionalidade através de camadas. Para isso, uso materiais muito variados, que vão de feltro cortado manualmente até recursos da fabricação digital como corte a laser de acrílico etc.
Trabalhei com clientes como Instagram, Adobe, Washington Post, TimeOut New York, Natura. E tive trabalhos premiados internacionalmente como D&AD (Londres), Clio (New York), Ibero-American Design Biennial (Madrid), Latin America Design Award (Peru).

teacher.aboutMe:
Esta es una pequeña ventana que te acercará a mi mundo, en donde la magia reside en la luz y el color, para conseguir espacios alegres, que producen sensaciones y no dejan indiferente. Estos son los dos pilares fundamentales de mis trabajos y sobre los que voy construyendo el resto de los elementos.
Mi carrera es una constante búsqueda por encontrar la belleza, fijándome en los pequeños detalles que juntos consiguen crear una composición única.

Me confieso una apasionada de las antigüedades, de encontrar esas piezas que brillan a través de su historia, y que no dudo al mezclarlas con los muebles más actuales y sencillos. Es curioso descubrir cómo estas piezas más antiguas, lo que hacen es aportar frescura a los espacios y los convierten en lugares únicos.
Es mi mejor forma de transmitir lo que siento y comunicarme, donde no hay reglas, el color, los estampados y los diferentes materiales, nunca sobran ni se pelean.En resumen aquí podrás encontrar “THE COLOR OF MY LIFE” Todo aquello que me apasiona, que refleja lo que siento, por eso lo quiero compartir y que también consiga emocionarte.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hola! Soy Ignacia Astudillo, decoradora y fundadora de GOLD Interiosimo.  Mi pasión es el diseño de interiores y me dedico a ayudar a las personas a crear espacios únicos. 
Mi propósito es que tu casa te haga sentir feliz y represente tu personalidad; porque tu hogar es tu refugio y me encantaría ayudarte a construirlo.

Siempre fui soñadora y creativa, estudié Diseño de ambientes y objetos en Santiago de Chile y fue ahí donde encontré mi pasión, lo que me impulsó a dar lo mejor de mí.
En 2014 nació mi primer emprendimiento “Ignacia & Felipe”, el proceso fue de mucho aprendizaje y luego de 4 años se disolvió a fines del 2018. 

Fundé GOLD Interiorismo a principios del 2019, un estudio de diseño de interiores que desarrolla proyectos de decoración en Chile. Soy detallista, creo en el trabajo bien hecho, en la dedicación y en la confianza. Tenemos experiencia en el diseño de interiores de proyectos inmobiliarios, departamentos pilotos, espacios comunes, salas de venta, oficinas y especialmente residenciales; como también en asesorías de tendencias y en creación de contenido para marcas como Arauco.

En 2019 participé en la conducción de una web serie llamada “Las cosas cambian, las casas también” de Sodimac, donde tuve la oportunidad de ayudar a familias a diseñar un espacio de su casa y mejorar su forma de vida.  Esto cambió mi perspectiva y comencé a preguntarme cómo podría acercar la decoración que tanto me apasiona a más personas.

teacher.aboutMe: Andrea Chapela (Mexico City, 1990) has a degree in chemistry from the UNAM (National Autonomous University of Mexico) and an MFA in Spanish Creative Writing from the University of Iowa. The four books of her fantasy saga Vâudïz were published between 2008 and 2015 by the publishing house Urano. In 2016, she was awarded a Jóvenes Creadores grant for a science fiction short story collection. In September 2017, she was awarded a grant by the Spanish government to live and work in Madrid’s Residencia de Estudiantes for two years. She is part of the Mexicanx Initiative and attended Clarion West Workshop in 2017. In 2018, she received the Gilberto Owen National Prize for Literature in Mexico for the science fiction short story collection Ansibles, perfiladores y otras máquinas de ingenio [Ansibles, Profilers, and Other Ingenious Machines]. In 2019 she was awarded the Juan José Arreola National Prize for Literature in Mexico for her collection of short stories Un año de servicio a la habitación [One Year of Room Service], published by the Univerisdad de Guadalajara Press. The book is a lyrical essay, published by Tierra Adentro in fall 2019. Her stories have been published in the journals Tierra Adentro, Este País, Samovar and in various anthologies. I'm an artist from Lebanon, known for my use of the Kufic scripts. In the course of my early career as a graphic designer and illustrator, I was invited to assist master calligrapher Samir Sayegh with his work. Through years of close collaboration in his studio, I learned the essence of Kufic, the origin of all Arabic calligraphy, and devoted myself to this art when I moved to London. 
For over a decade, I have studied and revived these disused styles, and developed my own visual language out of them. I teach historical styles such as Manuscript Kufic and Square Kufic in the UK, and aim to create courses for other styles in this diverse tradition. I also work on rediscovering the inks and paints used in calligraphy and illumination during that same period, and authored a book on the subject.
Find me on twitter and instagram as @joumajnouna, and on Patreon.com/majnouna.

teacher.aboutMe:
“I am an inquiring designer who takes her job very seriously, but without taking herself too seriously.”

Giorgia Smiraglia has a multidisciplinary background that ranges from fine arts to graphic design. 
Grew up in an art town in Southern Italy, she has been surrounded by the opulent beauty of Baroque since childhood. This environment fostered her interest in ornaments and the principles that sustain their elegance.
Her creative thinking is driven by two key elements: the chaos of experimentation and logical thinking to find patterns in the chaos. During her career, Giorgia indeed matured an interest in the correlation between mathematics and aesthetics, and the role that logical thinking plays in the design process. She believes that logic and creativity are not antithetical, but rather they are essential to each other to create anything great and meaningful.

After receiving a degree from the Istituto Europeo di Design in Milan, she launched her career working for an American designer who introduced her to the world of patterns. After the experience in Milan, she moved to London where she has been designing patterns for several firms worldwide, ranging from body care products to alcoholic beverages, from luxury hotels and restaurants to fashion firms.

Her portfolio includes clients such as Fila, The Body Shop, Marriott International, Fortnum & Mason, Pernod Ricard, Glenlivet, Glenfiddich, Rothschild, Mondadori.

Her work has been featured in several books and magazines.

Louise Lockhart lives in an old cotton mill in the countryside in England, where she spends her days cutting shapes from paper, creating patterns and pictures. She takes inspiration from folk art, vintage print ephemera and the every day world around her. She likes to use a bold colour palette, making her work instantly recognisable and eye-catching. She works as a freelance illustrator, working on children's books and designs for clients such as Anthropologie, Boden, Heal's and Blue Q.

HaJ’s original comedy screenplay, Angry Black Women that she co-created won 2017’s Just For Laughs “From Set to Screen” competition. The comedy screenplay was also a selection at Series Fest, The New York Television Festival, IFP Film Week and listed on HBO ‘Top 10 Projects to Watch’ list. 

HaJ is the creator of the award-winning, one-woman, stage-show Funnel Cake Flowers & The Urban Chameleons, which debuted Off-Broadway and won her a ‘Best Writer’ award. This innovative live show has been featured in The New York Times, Essence Magazine, Rolling Out, Variety Magazine, and NPR; and lauded as “George C. Wolfe’s Colored Museum for Millennials." MadameNoire named HaJ one of the ‘Top 15 Tech & Branding Gurus’ for the interactive film, HERadventure she produced and co-created with film and television director Ayoka Chenzira (Netflix Trinkets, OWN Network Greenleaf & Queen Sugar, Alma’s Rainbow). One of HaJ’s first short stories aired on The CW Network (formally known as UPN) and earned her a 1995 Emmy nomination when she was fifteen years old. Since then, HaJ has created, written, produced, licensed, and directed projects for networks including BET, VH1, Disney, ABC, and CBS.  

HaJ served as the Senior Producer for iOne Digital (Radio/ TV One) where she oversaw operations and creative development of the Pop Culture division. ¡Hola! :)

Me llamo Kiara Hayashida, soy de Lima, Perú y soy la creadora y "hacedora" detrás de todo lo que hay en Kiara Hayashida Ceramics (KHC).
 Fundé KHC en el 2015 cuando, tras la búsqueda de nuevos medios creativos, encontré la cerámica. Desde ese entonces emprendí en el fascinante viaje que este medio ofrece. 

Los objetos que produzco buscan realzar los momentos cotidianos por medio de los sentidos y ser un respiro en un mundo lleno de producciones masivas. Pausar para percibir el volumen, analizar los colores y texturas de los esmaltes y arcilla, y poder observar las huellas que el proceso deja, son experiencias que muy rara vez uno podría encontrar en un objeto hecho en masa. 
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hi :)!
My name is Kiara Hayashida, I am from Lima, Peru and the sole maker of Kiara Hayashida Ceramics (KHC).
KHC was born in 2015 when, after looking for new creative mediums, I founded ceramics and fell in love with it. Since then, I have embarked in the amazing journey ceramics offers you.

My pieces aim to enhance day to day moments through the senses and become a small break in a world full of mass made objects. To pause to perceive the volumes, the textures of the glazes and the marks that the process leaves in every object, are experiences that you can rarely find in a mass made one.
