teacher.aboutMe:
Somos Mariana Arriaga y Santiago Arriaga. Hermanos y co-directores.
Crecimos en una familia de narradores que desde muy niños sembraron en nosotros las ganas de contar historias. Ambos estudiamos comunicación con un sub-sistema en cine. Durante nuestros años de carrera tuvimos diversos trabajos: en compañías productoras de animación, comerciales y series de televisión. 
Al terminar la carrera decidimos dirigir nuestros propios cortometrajes de titulación. "Libre de Culpa", cortometraje de titulación de Santiago, fue la primera ocasión en la que co-dirigimos. A partir de ahí decidimos fundar una casa productora a la que nombramos Memento Mori Films (que significa recuerda que morirás). Con esta productora hicimos cortometrajes, fashion films, videos musicales, comerciales y piezas más experimentales. A lo largo de estos cinco años hemos colaborado con agencias y marcas tanto nacionales como internacionales. 
Nuestros cortometrajes nos han llevado a estar seleccionados dos veces a competir en los premios Ariel, otorgados por la Academia de Cine Mexicana, así como a competir en festivales en México y en el extranjero (Festival Internacional de Cine de Morelia, Festival de Cine de Venecia, LA Shorts, Festival Internacional de Cine de Guanajuato, Kustendorf Film Festival, entre otros).
Luego de cinco años de operar como casa productora, hemos decidido dejarla como un sello creativo, y enfocarnos en desarrollar nuevos proyectos en cine. Actualmente estamos en el proceso de llevar a cabo nuestro primer largometraje: A Cielo Abierto.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Mijal and I'm a graphic designer specialized in branding and packaging. 
I have been in the field for over 15 years. My profession led me to live in Argentina, USA, India and Israel.

I always liked the arts and all my hobbies somehow ended up being in the creative field. I was also born into a family with similar interests or professions, so for me, graphic design was a natural fit. As I went to school for design, I realized that the structure of classes and schedules and exams wasn't exactly for me, so I dropped out and decided to learn on my own. Looking back, this was, for me, a stepping stone to what would be my preferred method of learning and working.

As I started working as an In-house graphic designer it allowed me to continue learning on my free time and acquiring some free-lance clients. Fast forward a few years and I became a Creative Director for a marketing agency, later the owner of my own studio Bold Design.

While I was working for others, in an office setting, I found that this was not HOW I wanted to work. I loved the field, but not working as an employee. This realization made me re-think my career and what was important for me: Creativity and Freedom. By then, I had a new goal: take all I learned in my past experiences and become my own studio. And it worked. Once I established myself as a freelancer I joined forces with other creatives (copy writers, animators, web designer). This was the beginning of creating my studio. 

Today I love being an identity and packaging designer, and I love working in a freelance setting. I can't ask for more.

I have learned a few tricks along these years (sometimes the hard way), and I can't wait to share them with the world!

I'm a London based photographer and film maker, working in the fashion and music industry and in the field of portrait photography. I would describe my visual style as the combination of romantic painterly beauty and rock'n'roll attitude. 
 Having graduated with MA Hons. at London College of Fashion in photography, my clients include magazines such as VOGUE, Numero, Dazed, i-D, Wonderland, Glamour, Marie Claire, Instyle China; brands such as Marc Jacobs, Dior, Burberry, Diesel, Saint Laurent, Charles Jeffrey LOVERBOY or Pretty Green.
 I've worked with artists such as Sergei Polunin, ballet dancer, record labels, Atlantic Records and Sony Music and musicians such as Zara Larsson, Tom Walker, Sean Lennon, and bands such as The Horrors, Eagles of Death Metal, Sundara Karma or Fat White Family.
I'm originally from Hungary, and also graduated with BA Hons. at Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design in Fine Art Photography and at Eotvos Lorand University Budapest in Aesthetics, Film History and Theory. I've been a European CANON Ambassadors since early 2019.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Nastia Calaca, and I’m an independent ceramic artist from Ukraine, currently living and creating in Haarlem, the Netherlands.
 I have created a successful small ceramic brand, selling my works and putting smiles on people’s faces worldwide since 2016.
I consider my sculptures versatile and understandable, playful, sometimes humorous, and somehow narrative.
While I try to avoid using exact images or book illustrations as a base for my artwork, I come to them through my personal interpretations and childhood memories. 
Despite the fact that I’m focused mainly on the anthropomorphic subject in my art, I do admire people and they have always been a great inspiration to me.
I have happened to develop a style and chose a theme that people around the globe find appealing and worth investing in.
My own works make me chuckle, so maybe this is the answer.
I’m telling jokes and stories in clay.

teacher.aboutMe:
John is an award winning digital artist, director, and entrepreneur based in Los Angeles, CA.

He co-founded Warm & Fuzzy, a creative agency with offices in Los Angeles and Colorado. His studio is on the cutting edge of digital technology, offering animation, design, VR and AR services to some of the top brands in the world, including Nike, Adidas, Honda, Budweiser, Reddit, Facebook, NBC, Apple, Lululemon, Call of Duty, and New Balance.

In 2015 he graduated from Loyola Marymount University with a degree in film and animation. At age 20 his visual effects talent earned him the opportunity to work on feature films such as Avengers: Age of Ultron, Ant Man, Ghostbusters, The Finest Hours, The Shallows, The Walk, and Unbroken.

While working for Coachella for the past 6 years, he created their highest performing social media content. John has filmed some of the music industry's hottest acts, such as The Weeknd, Muse, ACDC, Guns N’ Roses, Skrillex, Kaskade, Zedd, Kid Cudi, and many more.

In addition to developing his professional career, John uses his odd obsession with donuts as inspiration for creating digital artwork, which has earned him an engaged social media following. He continues to explore emerging mediums for making new art, including the NFT and crypto art space.

teacher.aboutMe:
Mi chiamo Ivan Canu, sono nato ad Alghero e dal 1996 lavoro a Milano come illustratore, progettista editoriale, critico e scrittore. Ho lavorato come art director della Fondazione Internazionale Balzan e graphic designer della rivista Hystrio. Ho scritto libri per l’infanzia editi in Italia, Francia, Giappone, Cina, Corea; ho scritto articoli e interviste per La Repubblica, La Stampa. Dal 2009 sono direttore del Mimaster Illustrazione e curo il progetto The Illustrators Survival Corner per le Children’s Book Fair di Bologna, Shanghai, Mosca, Vilnius, Francoforte, Sharjah, Guadalajara. Sono co-autore con Giacomo Benelli della serie The Illustrated Survival Guide, dedicate ai mestieri dell'Illustrazione, dell'editore, dell'editor e del traduttore, edita dal 2018 da Corraini. Fra i miei clienti: L’Espresso, La Repubblica, Il Sole 24 Ore, La Stampa, Huffington Post, The New York Times, The Boston Globe, Die Zeit, L’Express, The Guardian, The Courrier International, Audible, Salani, Centauria, De Agostini, Feltrinelli, Einaudi, Mondadori. 
Ho illustrato i libri scritti da Paolo Mieli, La Storia del comunismo in 50 ritratti (2018), L’Italia di Mussolini in 50 ritratti (2020), L'Italia della Liberazione in 50 ritratti (2021) e L'Italia della Grande Guerra (2022), tutti per Centauria. Ho progettato, scritto e illustrato il libro God Save the Queen, le opere e i giorni di Elisabetta II Windsor, edito da Centauria nel 2021.
Sono stato premiato da New York Society of Illustrators, American Illustration, Creative Quarterly, Communication Arts, 3x3. 
Dal 2016 sono rappresentato da Salzman International (salzmanart.com) e dalla Galleria L’Affiche di Milano (affiche-fineart-shop.it)

teacher.aboutMe: Sono nato a Mantova e mi sono laureato in Architettura a Ferrara, dove ho iniziato autonomamente la mia formazione nel campo della storia dell'arte e della fotografia. Sin da piccolo amavo tantissimo stare da solo a disegnare, molte delle atmosfere che si trovano nelle mie foto provengono dalle mie visioni e sogni di bambino. Per diversi anni ho lavorato come architetto e nel 2015 ho deciso di iniziare contemporaneamente anche la professione di fotografo, nel 2019 questa diventerà la mia unica attività. Una forte impronta artistica caratterizza la mia produzione, rendendo il mio stile riconoscibile e apprezzato in diversi ambiti, mi occupo di fotografia di ritratto, di prodotto, di moda, di architettura e di regia fotografica in produzioni video, vendo i miei lavori attraverso alcune gallerie d'arte, sia in Italia che all'estero, partecipo a mostre personali e collettive, in Italia e in altri paesi, organizzo workshop di fotografia per scuole e privati, il desiderio di condividere tecnica e ispirazioni mi ha portato alla collaborazione con DOMESTIKA dove finalmente sono riuscito per la prima volta a realizzare in modo compiuto un corso in cui poter parlare di tutto il mio mondo fotografico e a mostrare come lavoro in studio per realizzare i miei ritratti dietro ai pannelli traslucidi. Pubblico spesso i miei scatti su Vogue.It e Icon Artist Magazine,  collaboro con il mondo dell'arte contemporanea, creando foto di cataloghi per artisti e mostre, ho realizzato alcune cover per romanzi italiani ed esteri. Fotografo anche opere del passato, soprattutto quelle legate al Rinascimento della mia città. Il mio studio si trova attualmente a Mantova dove vivo con la mia amata famiglia.

teacher.aboutMe:
Giselle Manzano Ramírez,  is a Colombian designer and multidisciplinary artist. Her mission revolves around empowering individuals through the medium of fashion, utilizing garments as a canvas to convey profound meaning and evoke emotions. Going beyond traditional boundaries, Giselle merges art with fashion, exploring unconventional printmaking techniques and surface embellishments to create unique and captivating works.

Her artistic journey has led her to showcase her creations at prestigious events such as Brooklyn Fashion Week, ReFashion Week, Bartschland, and KRATER. Collaborating with emerging artists and DJs within the underground music scene, Giselle serves as both a designer and stylist, curating unforgettable looks for DJs performing at renowned venues like Dekmantel, Boiler Room, and The Bunker. She brings her vision to life in legendary clubs such as Berghain, Basement, and Bossa Nova Civic Club, leaving an indelible mark on the fashion landscape and empowering individuals through her creative expression.

In addition to her individual endeavors, Giselle is the visionary behind KRATER—an awe-inspiring fusion of fashion design, visual art, and underground techno. This groundbreaking event serves as a platform for emerging designers who are pushing the boundaries of fashion, redefining its meaning as an artistic practice. Thanks to the Creatives Rebuild New York Guaranteed Income for Artists program, this celebration by artists, for artists, has become a tangible reality, demonstrating Giselle's commitment to supporting fellow creatives and building a vibrant artistic community.

teacher.aboutMe:
Originario de Casilda y formado en Rosario en diseño gráfico, durante más de 18 años he desarrollado mi carrera en diseño de packaging e ilustración en España y Buenos Aires. Actualmente en la Patagonia argentina.

Mi pasión por la ilustración empezó desde muy chico, la cual con el correr de los años se convirtió en una herramienta fundamental para mi carrera.  En 2008 estudié Lic. en Diseño Gráfico en la ciudad de Rosario y posteriormente dirección de arte en la escuela Underground de Buenos Aires.

Mi primera experiencia fue en el área de diseño editorial, en la dirección de arte de un diario deportivo de mi ciudad natal. A partir de ahí comenzó mi camino como profesional en diseño gráfico. Si bien editorial es una rama del diseño muy interesante, no tarde demasiado en darme cuenta que el packaging era mi lugar dentro de la profesión y es lo que hago hasta el día de hoy con más de 18 años de experiencia.

Trabajo en diferentes proyectos para marcas, estudios y agencias de Argentina y de diferentes partes del mundo como Fernet Branca, Estrella Galicia, Mc Donald's, Toyota, Cardenal Mendoza, BBDO, cerveza Quilmes, Undurraga, Bodegas Emiliana, cerveza Málaga Victoria, YPF, C. A. River Plate, Molinos, editorial El Ateneo, entre otros.
En 2023 obtuve el premio Cannes junto a la agencia Drafline, con el diseño e ilustración de la linea de cervezas Quilmes, Edición Mundial Qatar 2022. El proyecto se llamó "Coincidencias".

El packaging es mucho más que el contenedor de un producto, me gusta pensarlo como una pieza de arte valiosa que nos abra los sentidos, capture corazones y quien lo descubra sienta ganas de mostrarlo, compartirlo y quedárselo.
 
En mis trabajos me gusta contar historias, combinando componentes muy diversos, creando diseños con gran presencia de ilustración y lettering  a mano con énfasis en los detalles, obteniendo así un resultado artesanal y único.
 
Más allá del diseño de packaging de bebidas, la unión de la ilustración handmade y el diseño gráfico también me dio la posibilidad de trabajar para distintos proyectos que forman mi portfolio, como por ejemplo la creación de un mazo de cartas de póker estilo japonés, pasando por el diseño del escenario principal en un festival de música en España o el diseño e ilustración del famoso mural en el predio de la selección Argentina de fútbol.

Esto es lo que más me apasiona de mi profesión, que no existen límites a la hora de crear.

teacher.aboutMe:
Nací en Concepción del Uruguay, Entre Ríos, Argentina. A los 18 años me mudé a Buenos Aires para estudiar diseño gráfico.

Conseguí mi primer trabajo sin experiencia previa, simplemente porque le dije a mi futuro jefe: “Contratame. Sé que voy a servirte. No sé cómo explicarlo, pero estoy seguro”. Trabajé en diseño durante unos cuatro años, hasta que decidí hacer un curso de redacción y dirección de arte en Underground Argentina.

Ese famoso “click” creativo me costó bastante, pero al finalizar el curso logré entrar como trainee en McCann Erickson Buenos Aires. A partir de ahí trabajé casi diez años como director de arte en publicidad, pasando por agencias como McCann Erickson, Publicis, Grey y TBWA, entre otras.

En paralelo, desarrollé una de mis grandes pasiones: la música. Soy músico desde hace más de quince años, tengo mi propio proyecto musical, canto, escribo y toco la guitarra. Siempre realicé mis propios videos y, hasta el día de hoy, me encargo de la autogestión del proyecto.

Como director de arte no solo participé en el desarrollo de piezas publicitarias dentro de agencia, sino que también realicé numerosos diseños de tapas de discos, lo que me permitió combinar varias de mis pasiones: la música, el diseño y las ideas.

Después de casi diez años trabajando en agencias, decidí darle un nuevo giro a mi carrera. Tenía amigos que trabajaban en copywriting para entretenimiento y, en cada charla con ellos, entendí que ese era el próximo paso que quería dar.

No fue fácil conseguir una oportunidad, ya que en los papeles yo seguía siendo director de arte. Aun así, tomé el riesgo de dejar mi trabajo fijo en una agencia para cubrir una suplencia temporal en FOX, lo que me dio mi primera experiencia en el mundo del copywriting para entretenimiento.

Luego de esa etapa, trabajé durante cuatro años en NBCUniversal, desarrollando piezas creativas para señales como SYFY, Universal TV y Studio Universal.

Actualmente trabajo en The Walt Disney Company Buenos Aires como Senior Copywriter en Creative Services – Studios Marketing, donde desarrollo piezas para theatrical, digital y on-air, rol que desempeño hasta el día de hoy.

teacher.aboutMe:
CURSO DE GUIÓN CON DANIEL TUBAU EN VIVO (ONLINE PARA TODO EL PLANETA)
Escribir un guión, un viaje extraordinario – 3ª edición
Ver en losmundosdelguionista.com

Saludos. Soy Daniel Tubau, guionista, profesor, escritor y director de programas y series de televisión. 
A lo largo de más de veinte años, he escrito muchos guiones de todo tipo, de concursos, series, realities, talk shows, informativos satíricos y un montón de sketches. Un día hice un cálculo rápido y me salieron entre 500 y 600 guiones a lo largo de mi carrera. Y sin embargo, cada nuevo guión es un desafío en el que te puedes sentir perdido. Como creo que le sucede a casi todo el mundo, cuando me enfrento a un nuevo proyecto lo primero que pienso es: ¿por qué me he metido en este lio y por qué no elegí una profesión más previsible? Afortunadamente, la experiencia te va enseñando más y más cosas: no puedes evitar equivocarte y cometer errores, pero al menos sí puedes cometerlos bien, aprender de ellos y encontrar soluciones.  Ya verás que le doy mucha importancia a lo bueno que es hacer las cosas mal. Y también a que la situación mejora si primero intentas entender qué es lo que quieres contar y después ponerte en el lugar de los espectadores, para que también ellos lo entiendan (y lo disfruten).
En este curso he querido mostrar el proceso creativo tal como realmente se desarrolla, con todas sus dudas y dificultades, porque he visto que en muchos libros y cursos no se muestra cómo trabajamos realmente los guionistas. Así que espero que te sea útil el curso y, lo que es más importante, que te anime a escribir tus propios guiones. Porque, después de las dudas iniciales, cuando empiezas a escribir el guión, se disfruta mucho y acabas pensando que elegiste bien tu profesión.

Para que me conozcas un poco mejor, te cuento algunas de las cosas que  he hecho:  como guionista y director he trabajado en programas y series de televisión, como El Gran Juego de la Oca, El Informal, Mitos y Leyendas, Guardianes de la historia, Club Disney y muchos más. En la serie Trilocos, una idea original del gran payaso Miliki, fui guionista y director al mismo tiempo, eso que ahora se llama showrunner durante 130 programas. 
He publicado más de una docena de libros, cuatro de ellos dedicados al guión: Las paradojas del guionista, La musa en el laboratorio (sobre creatividad), El espectador es el protagonista y El guión del siglo 21. 
Pero también he publicado libros de cualquier tema imaginable , como No tan elemental, cómo ser Sherlock Holmes; El arte del engaño, La verdadera historia de las sociedades secretas, Recuerdos de la era analógica, Elogio de la infidelidad, o Cómo triunfar en cualquier discusión, entre otros.
Soy profesor de guión, dirección, literatura y creatividad en academias y universidades como el SAE Institute (México), Universidad de Lima (Perú), la Escuela de Cine de Cuba EICTV, la UASD de República Dominicana, la Escuela de Cine ECAM, la Universidad Nebrija, la Universidad Rey Juan Carlos, la Universidad Carlos III, y muchas otras. 
Y por cierto, si me buscas,  siempre me puedes encontrar en Los mundos del guionista (losmundosdelguionista.com)

Valentina D'Efilippo is an independent data designer and creative director. Her work has won many recognitions and has been exhibited internationally.

Her critically acclaimed book, "The Infographic History of the World", co-authored with data journalist James Ball, has been translated into eleven languages. Valentina is also the co-author and illustrator of the groundbreaking "Britannica’s Encyclopedia Infographica", an awe-inspiring encyclopedia for kids featuring thousands of facts and hundreds of original infographics covering a vast range of topics – from space to planet Earth, the animal kingdom and the human body.

Valentina's unique blend of creativity, storytelling, and data-driven insights has led her to collaborate with public organizations, start-ups, agencies, and global brands across a wide range of fields and formats. Her work spans theater productions, exhibitions, editorial content, and interactive platforms, establishing her as a leading voice in the field of data visualization and information design.

Valentina's passion for sharing knowledge has also led her to coach corporate teams and teach at universities around the world. She has lectured at Columbia Business School and runs a popular Guardian Masterclass.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy periodista y escritor. He publicado algunos libros de crónicas. Esa es mi especialidad: la crónica periodística. 

Entre mis libros están Camino al Este (la crónica de un viaje desde Madrid hasta Kioto, yendo país por país, en busca de historias de amor y desamor), Cuba Stone (sobre el show de los Rolling Stones en La Habana), Los crímenes de Moisés Ville (una crónica sobre 22 homicidios ocurridos entre 1889 y 1906 en una colonia agrícola de inmigrantes judíos rusos en el campo pargentino; homicidios que fueron registrados en un primer artículo por mi bisabuelo) y Sangre joven (crónicas de asesinatos de jóvenes cometidos por otros jóvenes). Colaboré en muchas antologías, como por ejemplo And We Came Outside and Saw the Stars Again: Writers from Around the World on the COVID-19 Pandemic, donde publiqué “The Life of a Virus”, cuya versión en español –“La vida de un virus”– veremos en Doméstika.

En 2010, Sangre joven ganó el Premio Rodolfo Walsh, a la mejor obra de no ficción, de la Semana Negra de Gijón (España), que es el festival más importante en español de literatura negra y de crimen.
 
Y en 2015 gané el Premio Gabriel García Márquez de la Fundación Gabo por mi crónica “Rápido. Furioso. Muerto”, publicada en Rolling Stone (Argentina), revista de la que fui editor. 
 
Mis crónicas se publicaron en los diarios La Nación y Clarín, de Buenos Aires;  y en revistas como Gatopardo (México), Etiqueta Negra (Perú), Letras Libres (México), Reportagen (Suiza) y Asymptote (Taiwán). Soy miembro del consejo asesor de Relatto, la primera plataforma web latinoamericana de historias reales on demand. Además fui corresponsal para Sudamérica de El Universal (México).

Soy staff de RED/ACCIÓN y dicté talleres y seminarios de escritura creativa de no ficción en España y en varios países de América Latina.

Somos un estudio de diseño basado en Monterrey, México especializados en la generación de sistemas de diseño integrales y fundamentados en conceptos de proyecto sólidos y atemporales. Expresamos nuestro proceso a través de distintas disciplinas como estrategias de marca y comunicación, interiorismo, arquitectura y principalmente diseño de sistemas de identidad gráfica para marcas y proyectos internacionales.

Creemos que para llegar a resultados únicos y profesionales, la investigación, el análisis y la síntesis de la información debe de ser siempre base para la solución de cualquier problema de diseño y es por eso que desde el génesis de Monumento nos hemos dedicado a construir nuestro proceso de trabajo alrededor de la construcción del concepto creativo, que es el punto en el que la investigación y la dirección de arte convergen para definir el camino estratégico que el proyecto tomará.

Estrategia de marca

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi, my name's Dan Forster, I’m a lettering artist and designer. I was lucky to grow up with a Dad who was a designer, lettering artist and calligrapher. So from an early age I was exposed to a ton of art and design. I spent a lot of time in his studio watching him work, rummaging through his books, or tracing my comics – so it was almost inevitable I’d end up in a creative career.

I tried my hand a calligraphy and lettering at an early age, but found it so hard that I gave up almost immediately. So initially I worked in design and branding but developed a deep love for type and typography. It wasn’t until after my Dad passed away in 2008 that I discovered the true depth and breadth of his lettering work. I was so blown away by what I found in his studio that it inspired me to pick up a pen and start drawing letters again. This time I stuck at it, slowly got better and eventually switched careers to become a full-time lettering artist. 

These days I’ve been lucky to work with clients from around the world on all kinds of lettering-based projects, from brand-marks, to book covers, to packing projects and everything in between. Letters are now my world and I love to experiment with new ways to create letter shapes, explore three-dimensional forms and I’m particularly obsessed with curves and flourishing.

teacher.aboutMe:
Adrianus Kundert is a product designer and a basketry enthusiast. Playfulness, experimentation and a process-oriented take on design are what characterises his work. His hands-on approach makes for groundbreaking projects that twist existing techniques into new crafts. Adrianus’ work tends to push the boundaries of functions, techniques and materials, striving for new discoveries through an iteration of trial and error. Having worked on numerous three-dimensional weaving projects, Adrianus masters many 2D and 3D weaving, plaiting and braiding techniques and developed his own cross-overs. His ongoing search for new modes of production between the traditional and the industrial leads to surprising discoveries, such as a hybrid basketry technique.

After graduating from Design Academy Eindhoven in 2015, Adrianus founded his own design studio. Independently and on commission, he works on a variety of projects. Since 2016, he has been active as a member of design collective Envisions, which focuses on experimental material research through collaborations with renowned industry partners. In 2020, Adrianus co-founded Basketclub, an Instagram-based platform on which designers and artists engage in playful basketry experimentations around a monthly changing theme.

teacher.aboutMe:
Somos Lettermafia, un grupo de diseñadores y diseñadoras especializades en Lettering, caligrafía y tipografía. Desde 2018 buscamos abordar los proyectos con un enfoque desde la riqueza que nos ofrece el universo de las letras, adaptándonos a las necesidades de cada desafío y aportando una mirada colectiva, propia del grupo.

Hemos trabajado junto a distintos clientes como Hermès, Spotify, Bodega Portillo, Persol, Gobierno de la ciudad de Buenos Aires, Canal Encuentro, entre otros.

El equipo se forma constantemente en torno a la caligrafía, la tipografía y el lettering. Y a través de diversas disciplinas como la ilustración, animación, packaging, etc; alimentamos nuestra curiosidad y encontramos que, trabajando juntes, podemos integrar nuestras miradas y llegar más lejos.

Cada propuesta de LetterMafia es un escenario de cocreación orientado a la ejecución detallista y a la alta calidad. Creamos soluciones comunicacionales a través de lo que nos apasiona: el dibujo y diseño de letras.

Además de trabajar con letras nos gusta proponer espacios de intercambio y aprendizaje. Por eso desarrollamos diferentes propuestas de talleres. En 2018 dictamos 3 talleres en la octava Bienal de Tipografía Latinoamericana Tipos Latinos. En 2019 fuimos parte de TRImarchi un festival de diseño en Mar del Plata, donde dictamos una versión intensiva de un taller de lettering que se llamó Grafito Paradise y el 2021 dictamos nuestra propuesta de taller de lettering integral 'Letterbondi' en Prints&Crafts.

¡También tenemos un podcast y se llama Familia Tipo!
En la primera temporada charlamos sobre motivaciones, inquietudes y todo lo que nos gustaría que Mother Nature ponga en nuestro camino. Escúchalo en Spotify, Apple podcast o tu plataforma favorita.

Creemos que las marcas deben ser percibidas como personas que tienen su propio carácter, voz, propósito y mensaje.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi, I'm João!

I'm a Lettering Artist and Type Designer, currently working from Lisbon, Portugal. 

My world revolves around letters of all shapes and sizes, in all mediums and colours. Attracted to everything related to typography, from typefaces and logos to murals and calligraphy, I constantly challenge myself to work with different materials, scales and styles. 

Calligraphy has a big presence in my work. Writing by hand is the birthplace of all lettering, so in my opinion, it is essential to have a firm base in calligraphy to do any typography related projects.

In 2020, I graduated with honours from the Master Type Design at École Cantonal d'Art de Lausanne. During my degree, I learned how to fuse the technical and detailed process of Type Design with an emotive and creative approach to Lettering pieces, and that is exactly what I strive to do. My creative process always involves both analogues and digital mediums, either for sketching or finalizing projects.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello, My name is Lydia I am a seamstress and I only wear clothes I have made. I have not bought a single item of clothing from a shop in over six years! I called the project Made My Wardrobe. It started as personal journey to reconnect with my body and has turned into a full time business sharing my clothes making skills with anyone who wants to make their dream wardrobe. We now have a team of six who design patterns, kits and courses to make sewing accessible and creative. We have a beautiful sewing studio in Bristol, England. Do pop by to check out our fabrics if you are ever near by!

My mum taught me to sew when I was a little girl. When I finished school I started an apprenticeship to learn how to design and make garments. My background is in costume for theatre, dance and live performance. I am fortunate to have worked with some of the most prestigious theatres in the UK such as Sadler's Wells and The Royal Opera House. 

Some of my favourite projects have come from working with my closest friends and I am lucky enough to be surrounded by a community of makers who inspire me constantly. My favourite thing about sewing is that there is always more to learn.

See you at the sewing machine!

teacher.aboutMe:
Meu nome é Ana Catalina Marchesi, sou figurinista e designer de moda nascida e criada na Patagônia Argentina. 
Moro no Rio de Janeiro desde 2014, cidade que me permitiu expandir o meu campo artístico de trabalho junto a diferentes marcas parceiras. Iniciei a minha trajetória profissional como figurinista no teatro San Martín de Buenos Aires, palco de grandes espetáculos onde aprendi a construir e dar vida às minhas personagens, onde comecei a trilhar o meu caminho no mundo da moda e figurino. 
Já no Rio, formei o projeto “LA POMPONERA” focado tanto na ressignificação de peças existentes quanto na criação de peças exclusivas, na projeção de espaços cenográficos, e na direção criativa para diversas campanhas da moda carioca. 
A minha experiência de trabalho, tem me dado a possibilidade de unir os dois mundos: o da moda e do figurino. e me dá como resultado um novo campo de ação híbrido, onde a moda se aproxima da fantasia para incorporar elementos com amplo potencial estético. 
A minha profissão também me proporcionou o exercício constante da observação. Aproveitando o estudo dos objetos e materiais do cotidiano. Com sensibilidade e, por que não coragem, para assumir outros usos.

Ciao mi chiamo Davide Sasselli, sono un 3D Character Modeller. 

Vivo a Londra ma sono originario di Cesena. Mi sono diplomato al liceo artistico nel 2009, da li ho imparato ad apprezzare la scultura ed il disegno.

Nel mondo del 3D Mi sono formato inizialmente da autodidatta, per poi successivamente frequentare un corso di Computer Grafica.
Da li in poi ho iniziato a lavorare come freelance e a lavorare per gli studi di di VFX come Jellyfish Pictures, Nexus Studios e Framestore.

Founded by Nerrisa after falling out of love with her first love of sewing, in a bid to find a mindful and less involved craft, she discovered Bargello after a late night of scrolling through Pinterest and was immediately struck by the bold patterns and colours.

If you're new to Bargello, it's a tapestry method which dates back hundreds of years and the technique of using straight stitches to create striking, geometric patterns and the craft had the biggest and best resurgence in the seventies.

Fast-forward to now and The Bargello Edit boasts a range of DIY projects and lifestyle kits to add a pop of colour to your home.

teacher.aboutMe:
Muchas veces nos preguntan cómo nació Desedamas y cómo terminamos trabajando juntas. 
Tener una infancia común y unos padres que siempre alentaron nuestra creatividad ayuda mucho. Compartimos mucho durante la infancia, y luego la vida nos separó temporalmente. Cuando nos volvimos a encontrar, ya adultas, empezamos a pintar seda en parte por hobby y en parte por terapia…  y descubrimos que eso era lo que queríamos hacer y además hacerlo juntas.
Las dos veníamos de ámbitos muy distintos. Cecília, Delineante Técnico de formación, trabajaba en empresa privada como Jefe de Compras. Mercè, Ingeniera Química, en el Departamento de Medio Ambiente en la Generalitat de Catalunya.
En el año 2000 decidimos darle un giro a nuestras vidas y convertir nuestra pasión en forma de vida. Al principio hacíamos artesanía con seda, siempre buscando darle un valor añadido a las piezas que realizábamos y no solo pintando. Todo pieza única, vendíamos nuestro trabajo en ferias de artesanía por toda España. En 2006 empezamos a pintar seda para patchwork y, aunque sabíamos coser, empezamos a aprender técnicas específicas. La seda siempre había sido nuestro “material” por lo que, aunque no es muy utilizada en arte textil, para nosotras fue natural seguir trabajando con ella. Unir estas dos habilidades, la pintura en seda y el arte textil nos abrió un campo inmenso en el que experimentar. Tanto es así, que hemos explorado y desarrollado técnicas propias para trabajar con este material, convirtiéndonos también en formadoras.
Actualmente trabajamos en sinergia entre la artesanía y el arte textil, ya que es difícil marcar los límites entre los dos. 
En 2013 nos otorgaron a ambas el diploma de Maestras Artesanas.

teacher.aboutMe:
Mi piace definirmi in diversi modi, perché quello che faccio è caratterizzato da quella che sono.
Su carta sono una stilista di moda ,ma anche artigiana , amo immergere le mani nei tessuti, disegnare bozzetti, dare forma alle tante idee che ho in testa.
Un ricordo indelebile di una me bambina è legato a quando accompagnavo mia mamma nei laboratori di sartoria e maglieria di fiducia ,dove lei si faceva confezionare stupendi capi, molti dei quali oggi ho ereditato; erano arredati con macchine da cucire, abiti e tessuti appesi ovunque, e vedevo  camminare da una parte all’altra diverse donne con indosso camici bianchi e dei lunghi metri intorno al collo che oscillavano a ritmo di passi a destra e sinistra, ero catturata da quello che facevano, era più forte di me.
C’era un profumo buonissimo in quel luogo.
Ora che ci ripenso era tutto bello li.
Avevo nove anni, ed ho iniziato a tagliare e cucire da quel momento.
Il mio percorso scolastico legato a questo ambiente è iniziato a 13 anni, ed ho avuto la fortuna di fare tanta gavetta presso piccoli e grandi marchi , anche nell’alta moda, conoscere l’ambiente, imparare il mestiere, le tecniche, affiancare sart* e stilist* eccezionali, tra Roma, Milano, Genova e Bologna, e forse avrei continuato su questa strada se non fosse che volevo qualcosa fatto apposta per me, così quando mi sono sentita più o meno pronta nel 2010 e’ nato Misstufi,il mio progetto di moda sostenibile, il mio mondo cucito su misura per persone speciali proprio come i capi che realizzo.
Pensati, studiati per durare nel tempo, mai fuori moda e confezionati non tralasciando nulla al caso, e nessuno perché non è assurdo pensare di poter vestire tutti, ambizioso forse, ma non impossibile .
La fortuna di realizzare abbigliamento su misura è proprio quella che non esiste, genere o taglia giusta, ci sono solo desideri, che possono essere realizzati in ogni momento, ed io adoro vedere quanto un semplice capo possa fare la differenza e strappare un sorriso, a chiunque lo indossi.
Ecco la mia idea di inclusivita’.
Il mio battesimo professionale nella società è avvenuto con la mia prima sfilata di moda nel 2011 presso una nota chocolaterie nel cuore di Savona in occasione dell’anniversario del film “ Colazione da Tiffany”.
Un ricordo che porto nel cuore tutt’ora perché mi ha fatto capire che volere è potere, con tanto impegno e dedizione certo, ma che se si ha la fortuna di capire quale strada si vuole percorrere, bisogna perseverare.
Dopo anni in giro per il centro e nord Italia presso diversi atelier, oggi Il mio laboratorio è a Bologna, dove ho messo radici, e dove posso dire di essere cresciuta professionalmente( oltre che aver trovato la mia metà nella vita ed esser diventata mamma nel 2020 di mio figlio Noah), tanto è vero che ho avuto la fortuna di raccontare il mio percorso e gli sviluppi durante diverse interviste, una delle quali per un bellissimo documentario realizzato da “ il vestito verde”, un progetto interamente Made in Italy che si impegna nella ricerca sfrenata alla sostenibilità a 360 gradi, racchiusa in un database, il primo in Italia, di tutti i brand di moda etica e sostenibile, dove appunto ci sono anche io. 
Ho visto Misstufi diventare sempre più simile all’idea che ho in mente, non solo abbigliamento su misura ma anche vere e proprie collezioni che hanno tratti distintivi e riconoscibili che si evolvono ad ogni cambio stagione, mantenendo sempre il carattere del mio brand ed i suoi forti principi per una moda etica e sostenibile, partendo dalla scelta dei materiali al packaging.
Sono su IG come @misstufisaraforlini

teacher.aboutMe:
Hugh Kretschmer grew up in Los Angeles, and one of seven children in a family of artists. At the age of 13, he was introduced to photography by his father who was a photo-instrumentation engineer for MacDonnell Douglas from the Mercury through Apollo missions. Ten years later, Hugh received a Bachelor of Fine Arts Degree from Art Center College of Design, graduating with honors. He then moved to New York City to start his career, collaborating with editorial, design, and advertising clients such as Vanity Fair, New York Times Magazine, National Geographic, GQ, Penn & Teller, Old Spice, Huggies, Toyota, and Sony. His images have been recognized by The International Photography Awards, American Photography, Communication Arts, PDN Photo Annual, Graphis Publications, and the Society of Publication Designers. His work has been profiled in many industry publications, books, podcasts and blogs, including Graphis, Communication Arts, Juxtapoz, Plastik, Vision Magazine, Beijing. His work has been selected for auction through Sotheby’s, Vienna and exhibited in galleries in Los Angeles, New York and Paris, and is in permanent collection of the 911 Memorial, New York City. His first retrospective came in 2021, at the Hoban Artrium Museum, Gwangmyeong-si, South Korea.
Hugh has lectured and lead workshops at Eddie Adams Workshops in Jeffersonville, NY, Gulf Photo Plus, Dubai and Fotorama, Serbia. He teaches photography part-time at Art Center College of Design, UCLA Extension, and the Los Angeles Center of Photography.

teacher.aboutMe:
Mi chiamo Monica Gamberale e sono una modista. Vivo a Mantova e nel mio laboratorio di modisteria creo cappelli su misura, con il mio piccolo brand Origami Hats. La mia passione per i cappelli è cominciata tantissimi anni fa, mentre studiavo in Accademia per diventare Designer di gioielli. Per molto tempo ho realizzato cappelli solo sporadicamente, come hobby personale. In quegli anni però, gironzolando per mercatini dell'antiquariato, ho acquistato tante forme per cappelli che consideravo stupendi soprammobili; successivamente, un amico scultore me ne ha regalato una borsa piena e così, inconsapevolmente, mi ha convinta a ridare vita a tutte quelle forme e ad abbandonare del tutto il design del gioiello per una nuova professione: la modisteria! Ho cominciato a frequentare corsi per perfezionarmi, a creare tantissimi cappelli e da allora non mi sono più fermata. Amo questo mondo, amo i profumi che si propagano nel laboratorio mentre lavoro, il benessere che mi dà creare qualcosa con le mie mani, la cura del dettaglio nella fase della personalizzazione, ma più di tutto è il sorriso di chi indossa una mia creazione ad avere un effetto benefico su di me: è un momento magico. 
Nel mio lavoro mi piace far somigliare ciò che creo a chi indosserà l’accessorio. In questo vedo una vera continuità con il mio lavoro di designer di gioielli. L'ornamento deve essere espressione della personalità e dello stato d'animo della persona: non deve sovrastarli, ma descriverli.

teacher.aboutMe:
Tesler + Mendelovitch is a material and product design studio that creates innovative, wood textiles — transforming them into luxury projects for automotive, architecture, and fashion.

“FORM FOLLOWS MATERIAL” | WOOD TEXTILES
Our design philosophy is based on what we call "form follows material" - which means that we believe that the best design is based on innovative materials and understanding their characteristics. The material itself can inform completely new shapes, geometries, and applications -  which is why we as a design team cross over many design disciplines. Our wood textiles are so versatile that they allow us to create fashion, furniture, wall panels, acoustic tiles, and even clothing. All we need to do is let it take shape and ensure aesthetic value, function and good proportion.

Itamar and I met whilst studying for our textile degree in Israel at the Shenkar University of Engineering and Design back in 2012. Our shared outlook in regards to design and aesthetics led us to invest time in creating wood textiles that could have the potential to redefine the way we both construct and produce three-dimensional products.
Design-wise we were and still are very inspired by the minimalism of clean lines and precision, but also like the idea of creating soft materials from hard and hard materials from soft. 

Mostly, the material itself inspired us, as we think that the material informs the product. At the time (after graduation), we felt that we would be happiest in creating a space where we could experiment with our own ideas and be our own creative directors. Initially, we knew that we wanted to work on surfaces and see where that led us in terms of product design. After working intensively for a year, we launched our Diamond woods furniture collection. From there, we began experimenting further with the wooden textile-working on a smaller and smaller scale till we achieved numerous product collections.

Each project begins as a flat wood textile. We then begin pulling and stretching, folding and bending in order to understand the textile's boundaries. We study the weak points and strengthen those so that we can pull the flat surface into a three-dimensional shape that it couldn't before. Each project, the material lets us know what it wants to become, we just allow it to take shape.

All products are 100% original, developed very carefully, and built to last.

Although being very much futurists in our aesthetics, all items made in the studio could have theoretically been made 100 years ago - ensuring high-quality control, clean and sustainable work methods as well as a very low carbon footprint.

While the textile’s geometric surface provides the necessary strength and flexibility - the wood texture is also soft and pleasant to the touch, at once both delicate and wear resilient.

Tesler + Mendelovitch continues to evolve and pursue multi-disciplinary projects, commissions, and collaborations, all based upon their expertise and vision in innovative wood textile design and unique construction methods.

I'm an artist and educator, originally from New York State, now living and working in Richmond, VA, USA. I have a background in textile design and I run the fiber and textile program at Virginia Commonwealth University.

I believe there is a strong relationship between the land and our interior landscapes. When we are connected to the land, we’re connected to ourselves, and one another.
 
I bring together materials and processes that express the union of humanity and the physical world. Whether stitching, drawing, planting seeds, or harvesting, my hands echo the gestures made by thousands of hands over thousands of years and I feel connected to the lineage of people working with textiles, plants and the land. Stitching, like agriculture, can be functional-- a technical solution to join materials/a means of survival-- or, both can be done purely in service of the soul, lifting the spirit through beauty and wonder.

Soy una artista textil especializada en la creacion de piezas bordadas y tejidas a mano para decoracion de interiores. Estudie diseño de modas y luego me mude a Barcelona, donde trabaje en Alta costura y confección de patrones. Después de regresar a Lima y trabajar como diseñadora de moda por varios años, decidi experimentar con fibras y telas creando piezas con diferentes técnicas de arte textil. 
Todas las piezas que creo están meticulosamente bordadas a mano con fibras e hilos de todo el mundo, particularmente con fibras peruanas. Mi fuente de inspiración suele ser el mundo natural y orgánico. A menudo influenciado por "concentraciones naturales" o elementos orgánicos agrupados estrechamente, como plumas, fósiles y vegetación. El océano es también una fuente importante de inspiración; el movimiento y formas del agua, la vida marina y los arrecifes de coral.

teacher.aboutMe:
¡Hola! Soy Marta y desde muy pequeña me paso el dia inventando.

Mi pasión son las lanas, los algodones, los hilos, los botones, las telas, las cintas y en definitiva ¡todo lo que se venda en una mercería!. Doy rienda suelta a mi creatividad en mi página y tienda de patrones online , donde desde hace más de 12 años, enseño paso a paso cómo tejer y confeccionar ropa y complementos.

La ropa de bebé es mi debilidad por muchas razones, obtienes resultados muy pronto y con muy poco material, además una prenda hecha a mano ¡siempre es el regalo perfecto!. Las prendas de niños y bebés son la base de una prenda de mayor envergadura ya que todo empieza con una version mini ❤️.

Soy Psicologa de formación y Marketiniana de profesion. Desde el nacimeinto de Creativa Atelier, compaginé mi trabajo en marketing con el compartir mis conocimeintos de knitting, crochet y costura en mi blog, hasta que en 2016, decidí decicarme en exclusiva a lo que me hacia más feliz: enseñar a tejer y demostrar que todo es mas fácil de lo que parece y que podemos hacerlo con nuestras propias manitas 🙌🏻.

Estoy orgullosa de haber colaborado con las marcas de hilaturas más prestigiosas y reconocidas del sector: Katia Yarns and Fabrics, Anchor Crafts, We Are Knitters, DMC, Knitive. Y revistas y publicaciones como The Sewing Box Magazine, Labores del Hogar, Molly Makes, Fair Cotton Crochet y Ser Padres.

Cristina Pagnoncelli é designer e artista visual com destaque em projetos de desenho de letras e murais.

Formada em Design Gráfico com Pós Graduação em Ilustração Criativa (Barcelona) e Especialização em Visual Branding (NYC), atua como profissional independente há mais de 10 anos. A partir de 2013 se tornou referência nacional com suas artes feitas com giz, lançando em 2015 seu projeto pessoal de ensino chamado "Oficina de Lettering com Giz" – através do qual viajou para várias cidades brasileiras capacitando muitos iniciantes interessados na técnica. 

Também com cursos e outros conteúdos próprios online, a partir de 2019 lecionou workshops e deu palestras em outros países como Argentina, Espanha e Itália. Além de suas artes feitas com giz, Cristina também desenvolve muitos murais com tinta e em grandes formatos, a maioria deles localizados em Curitiba, cidade aonde mora atualmente.

Seu trabalho retrata mensagens sobre as pautas que considera importante, destacando questões sobre direitos humanos, feminismo, ocupação urbana através da arte e da bicicleta. Sempre que possível, está viajando em busca de novas referências e aprendizado por meio de outras culturas.

I'm a Creative Director-level Copywriter, Tone of Voice Consultant and Trainer. 

I’ve been fortunate enough to do this for some fantastic brands, including Nike, Apple, Microsoft and Dunlop Sports. And I’ve picked up a few awards along the way. All helping to get the work seen by even more people.

Now based in Madrid, I run a growing copywriting studio called Craft Copywriting. I work with clients and agencies in London and here in Madrid including Dunlop Sports, Barrabes and Llorente y Cuenca. 

We also run writing workshops to help our clients write even better and I teach Digital Copywriting as part of the Master's in Visual & Digital Media at Madrid's IE University.

Hello beautiful humans. I'm Mojo, an illustrator and comic artist who lives in New York City. 

Growing up in Shanghai, drawing was a major part of my life since childhood. But it was more of a hobby until I graduated from university when I decided to pursue a career in illustration. After years of self-employment, I landed a position in ELLE MEN magazine as a photo editor, working with amazing artists.
 
In 2017, I quit my full-time job and moved to New York City for the MFA Illustration as Visual Essay program. I have been expanding the horizon of my new career as a freelance illustrator since then. 
Focusing on blurring the boundaries between illustrations and visual narratives, my works have been recognized by the Society of Illustrators and the AI-AP with a client list including Kiehl's, Nike, Apple, NYTimes, New Yorker, Wired Magazine, The Economist, and The Politico.

I am Cristian Grossi and I’m the creative director and founder of Kreativehouse studio.
I’m a campaign strategist with a decade experience working in both agency and in-house environments for a wide variety of sectors including, fashion, luxury, nonprofit, art/exhibitions, retail, marketing, PR and tourism.

In these years I worked with brands such as Barilla, Amnesty International, European Union, Mondadori, Pinko. And I have directed incredible artists from all over the world such as Jun Chen, Camille Walala, Camilla Falsini, Ale Giorgini

“Today, profit and nonprofit brands ask me to understand how to tell their values ​​by crossing traditional tools and new media. I have a strongly data driven approach: I analyze data and help brands make decisions.

I have gained a great deal of experience in the conception, management and curation of campaigns straddling the different media and platforms. My natural habitat is the campaigns in which the core-product is the idea as in fundraising, for example. But I also deal with studying, analyzing and designing trends for fashion brands and cultural events. I collaborate with artists, designers, copywriters, photographers and illustrators (if you want to show me your work write a few lines here). I like stories that have the power to motivate collective action.

I held courses on design and creativity management for profit, positioning strategies, viral communication and influencer recruitment and management, webmarketing. "

In addition to being a communication designer, Cristian is also a fashion illustrator and video artist.
His work is part of the Barilla Historical Archive, and his works have been exhibited at the London College Of Fashion (London), Usina del Arte (Buenos Aires), Palazzo Re Enzo (Bologna), Casa della Musica (Parma), Poland Fashion Week (Poland).

Soy diseñadora y profesora de prendas y accesorios de crochet. Estudié Historia en mi ciudad de origen y me mudé en 2010 a Londres, donde me formé como Educadora Infantil, especializada en pedagogía Montessori, la cual da forma a toda mi metodología como profesora, basándome en proporcionar herramientas valiosas que promuevan la independencia y den seguridad a mis alumnos para crear.

Creando mis propios recursos educativos me encontré con el mundo del tejido, el ganchillo y otras disciplinas craft. 
A través de Instagram encontré una comunidad creativa fascinante y empecé a compartir mis primeros trabajos y diseños.  Llegaron poco a poco colaboraciones con marcas del sector, primero simplemente como tejedora que compartía materiales interesantes y después oportunidades de diseño. Comencé a formarme en los aspectos más técnicos del crochet con clases y cursos en Londres, comenzando a diseñar y trabajar de manera más profesional con marcas importantes del sector, desarrolando y estableciendome como profesional en los últimos 5 años.

teacher.aboutMe:
Mesa Estándar (Estudio gráfico y editorial) nació en 2014 de la fusión de Mesa Editores (Editorial de arquitectura y arte dirigida por Miguel Mesa) con Taller Estándar (Estudio de diseño gráfico dirigido por Juan David Díez). 

Juan David Díez, es diseñador gráfico de la Corporación Colegiatura Colombiana. Realizó estudios de especialización en medios y tecnología para la producción pictórica en el Instituto Nacional de Artes, Buenos Aires, Argentina (2007). Fue docente de cátedra en taller de Diseño - Corporación Colegiatura Colombiana (2005-2008). Codirige Mesa-Estándar desde 2014 y se desempeña como diseñador gráfico e ilustrador.

Miguel Mesa, es arquitecto de la escuela de arquitectura de la Universidad Pontificia Bolivariana. Medellín, Colombia. Profesor del área de Proyectos de la misma universidad (2004-2021). Realizó estudios de doctorado en Proyectos Arquitectónicos en la ETSAB de Barcelona, Universidad Politécnica de Cataluña. (2001-2003). En 2008 publicó el libro: –La arquitectura del Hueco–. Fue columnista de la revista Arcadia entre 2010-2011. Codirige Mesa Estándar desde 2015 donde se desempeña como editor y diseñador.

Durante los últimos 8 años Mesa Estándar ha publicado más de 25 libros bajo su sello editorial independiente en las áreas de arte, ilustración, fotografía, arquitectura, libro infantil ilustrado y botánica. Y al mismo tiempo ha realizado más de una centena de publicaciones, proyectos gráficos y de señalización e identidad para clientes de diversa índole. Especialmente del sector cultural.

Las publicaciones de Mesa Estándar suelen nacer de las imágenes y tienen como objetivo pensarlas y disfrutarlas. Las historias y textos surgen desde los dibujos, las fotografías o las ilustraciones de diversos tipos. Por este motivo se trata de libros que ofrecen diferentes modos de lectura. Aunque sus publicaciones suelen catalogarse  como especializadas y de nicho, la verdad es que la editorial pone su esfuerzo principal en ofrecer al público general el arte y el diseño. En volver tema de interés colectivo estos asuntos. De ahí, en gran medida, nace la expresión gráfica de sus proyectos: de tratar de comunicar y llegar a quien menos se espera.

teacher.aboutMe:
Dreamfibre is Andrew Morgan, a multidisciplinary designer from Bristol, UK.

My journey into 3D design started as a child, creating levels for old PC games like Duke Nukem 3D and Doom. The desire to create virtual worlds hasn't left me since.

As an artist, I aim to create a timeless netherworld somewhere between past and future. Along the way, I reference videogame aesthetics, retro technology and near-future sci-fi, all the while drenching the experience in neon colours.
Today, I use Cinema4D and render technologies such as Redshift and Octane as my primary tools to create 3D visuals and animation. However, I have also started to create projects in game engines such as UE4, in particular for creating VR experiences.

If you have a project to discuss, don't hesitate to drop me a line. I have a diverse set of skills that extend out of 3D into more traditional graphic design, so I can often offer you an "all-in-one" solution for your project.

I’m an Italian lettering artist and type designer based in Berlin.
I create visual identities based on good typography and unique letterforms, looking for individual solutions that can simultaneously express diversity and match their environment.
In my studio La Letteria I revive the traditional techniques of sign painting and reverse glass gilding, which I believe really bring added value to today's visual appearances.
My main tool is the brush, which admittedly keeps me in thrall. From the concept onwards, I create various inscriptions for shop windows, signs, facades, vehicles and more. I love vernacular design and the idea of creating everyday things, enhancing the ordinary.
« The dream of the artist is to get his work displayed in a museum, while the dream of a designer is to get his work onto the street. »
(Bruno Munari, artist and designer, 1971)

I'm the designer and founder of RISOTTO; a leading risograph print specialist and stationary company; renowned for delivering jam-packed colour, bold graphics and fluorescent inks. 

Born out of my affection for hands-on production; the studio provides services for creatives looking to have their work printed in a vibrant and sustainable way. RISOTTO has evolved to host international workshops, and our stationery goods can be found worldwide with stockists that include Liberty London and Selfridges.

Outside the flurry of the studio, I've designed for brands such as Apple, Mini, Puma, and Swatch; with projects spanning from public art commissions to fashion collaborations. I've had the opportunity to exhibit internationally, and in 2019 opened one of V&A Dundee’s best loved exhibitions; Rules Of Play. teacher.aboutMe: ¡Hola! Me llamo Cristóbal y me dedico a diseñar tipografías y a diseñar libros. Soy licenciado en comunicación gráfica por la Escuela Nacional de Artes Plásticas de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM), especialista en producción editorial por la Escuela de Diseño del Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes, maestro en diseño tipográfico por el Centro de Estudios Gestalt (Veracruz, México) y también tengo un certificado en diseño de tipos por The Cooper Union (Nueva York, EUA). He desarrollado familias tipográficas para clientes como el Fondo de Cultura Económica, Librerías Gandhi y el Gobierno Federal de México. Algunas de mis familias tipográficas han obtenido reconocimientos del Type Directors Club y han sido seleccionadas en la bienal de tipografía latinoamericana Tipos Latinos. Soy autor del libro Espinosa. Rescate de una tipografía novohispana (México, Designio, 2005) y coautor de Cómo crear tipografías. Del boceto a la pantalla (Madrid, Tipo E, 2012), que ha sido traducido al inglés, polaco, portugués y chino. Desde 2011 imparto las asignaturas de tipografía y diseño de fuentes tipográficas en la Facultad de Artes y Diseño de la UNAM, así como materias afines en diplomados, especialidades y maestrías en diversas instituciones.

teacher.aboutMe:
JJ Zanetta’s passion of art and architecture attracted him to the profession of architectural illustration. A student of the craft, he is continually inspired by the master’s of architectural illustration as well as the new possibilities that technology brings.  Along with his dedication to his craft, he has an understanding and practical knowledge of architectural and urban design principles evident in the foundation of his renderings.

Beyond the technical aspects of a drawing, it is JJ’s goal to help his clients reach their audience on an emotional level.  The composition of the renderings are focused on breathing life into the design.  He aims to collaborate with the design team to gain an understanding of the vision and character of the place, and also help imagine what kind of life that environment will foster within it.  Whether, remotely or on charrette, his ability to quickly conceptualize and visually communicate plays an integral role on the design team.

He has had the good fortune to work with excellent clients on projects that present unique challenges and opportunities.   His project experience is wide-ranging; of all scales, character and project types.  For over 10 years he has served his clients, which consist of architects, urban designers, landscape architects, developers, and municipalities, with reliability and professionalism.

If you are interested in working together, I would love to hear from you!

teacher.aboutMe:
Phil Fisk is a photographer with ideas. He works across portraiture, still-life and motion.

His work is brimful of colour and creativity, embracing new photographic and film techniques to create beautifully-lit, conceptual studies in both still and motion formats.

Phil’s commissioned work includes an ongoing series of imagery for BAFTA as well as commercial campaigns for Channel 4, ITV, SKY and UKTV.  He regularly shoots for the Observer in all sections. Phil's recent work saw him transmit the Pet Shop Boys into a vast brutalist interior for their new album. Other clients include Ink Global's in-flight magazines, Wired magazine and foreign food publications and advertising campaigns for Klarna and HarmonyCa for DDB agency on London. 
He lives in South London and works everywhere.

After gaining a BA in Communications and Sociology from London’s Goldsmiths College Phil set out to gain real industry experience. An aborted attempt to gain an MA in Photography led to work first as a dark room technician then as a studio assistant  and eventually managing a lighting hire company. In 2007, he became an on-set photographer for TV dramas , mainly for Channel4 and the BBC with sporadic work on low budget European cinema films. This work is what enabled him to start exploring his own practice, providing funds and  equipment as well as lighting techniques he noted whilst on set. The portrait portfolio he put together in these years meant he could give up being the on set photographer and start being commissioned for his individual style and vision. 

Continually experimenting creatively, Phil’s personal projects include The Alan Project and Sex on the Radio, and have led to portrait commissions and still-life editorial work for weekly magazines such as Time Out, The Times and The Observer, publications he continues to work for. His diverse experience in location shooting ranges from the Prime Minister’s Drawing Room in 10 Downing Street,  to the Planet of the Apes film set in a Vancouver parking lot.  

Phil’s film and TV work includes an ongoing series of imagery for BAFTA: For the Love of Film, as well as commercial campaigns for the BBC, Channel 4, ITV, SKY, UKTV and of dozens independent TV and film production companies, taking him to far-flung regions such as Newfoundland and Tajikistan. The increasing demand for moving images has also allowed Phil to advance as a Director of on-air advertising campaigns,  BBC Radio 4 and for the drama Curfew on SKY1.

Other work includes commissions from The National Theatre, The English National Opera and The London Film Festival as well as marketing campaigns for iconic artists such as Madness and The Pet Shop Boys, and other literary and contract publisher work.

Twice finalist in The AOP Awards and Gold Winner in 2019, Phil was awarded a grant from the Arts Council of England in 2012 to produce the “Everyday People” exhibition, in partnership with London’s Roundhouse.  

Phil has been recognised globally for his award-winning photographs by shooting for print publications around the world and syndicates his portraits through Camera Press. 

He is represented by Flock agency in London.

teacher.aboutMe:
¡Hola! Soy Tania, una psicóloga que se enamoró de la luz y la belleza y que ya no puede vivir sin ellas. 

Nunca sabré definir (o con el tiempo quizás sí) si la fotografía llegó a mí para salvarme o yo la elegí inconscientemente como vía de rescate. En los últimos años he hecho muchas fotos, he conocido a gente maravillosa, viajado y he disfrutado de momentos increíbles gracias a la fotografía. Pero quizás, lo más significativo, es que ha sido mi fiel compañera de autoconocimiento. No sabría decir cuántas cosas he descubierto de mí al observar qué y cómo fotografío. Conocerme a través de mi mirada está siendo una experiencia única.

El retrato me apasiona. Disfruto captando la luz de cada persona con mi cámara. Contar historias con un retrato o captar una mirada llena de verdad  es lo que más me fascina de la fotografía.  Me enamoro de luces y sombras varias veces al día y busco constantemente la belleza en lo cotidiano.

En los últimos años he ido definiendo mi estilo propio caracterizado por el uso de la luz natural y el color. Me gusta crear imágenes armónicas que lleven al espectador a estados de ánimo como la calma o la nostalgia.

Desde hace unos meses tengo mi propio de estudio de luz natural. Un lugar en el cual experimento, juego y creo en total libertad y donde también estoy trabajando para marcas, realizando books a actrices, emprendedoras, e impartiendo formaciones presenciales. Como diría Virgina Woolf, al fin tengo mi cuarto propio.

teacher.aboutMe:
Née en 1989 dans le Sud-Est de la France et établie à Marseille, Delphine Dénéréaz est titulaire
d’un master en design textile de La Cambre (Bruxelles) obtenu en 2013. Elle est ensuite repérée et
soutenue par le MAD Bruxelles, et expose dans différents salons et galeries à l’international
(Cologne, Courtrai, Hong Kong...).
 En 2016, elle collabore avec le Who’s Next pour deux expositions à Paris puis à Tokyo. 
Revenue en France en 2017, elle axe sa démarche sur la technique du tissage de lirette en transformant en tapisseries des tissus domestiques qu’elle récupère : draps, nappes, rideaux, etc. 
En 2018, elle expose ses pièces à La Vallée Bruxelles, au Mucem à Marseille et à l’Été Indien à Arles. 
Elle rejoint l’Atelier Vé à Marseille en mai 2019 à l’occasion du PAC OFF et collabore avec Fada Records, un média, conçoit des expositions chez Backside Gallery Marseille, à Turin pour Nesxt Trasoloco, chez Askip à Nantes, et des
installations pour la Villa Noailles à Hyères et Lafayette Anticipations à Paris et des partenariats avec des marques ( Nike, Gucci..)
En 2021 elle est l’artiste associée du festival Marsatac. Elle signe la communication du festival avec le photographe Robin Plus, avec qui elle monte l’exposition Tira Lenso sous le commissariat de Anna Labouze et Keimis Henni en Août 2021.
Delphine Dénéréaz sera à l’automne 2021 en résidence à Coco Velten à Marseille et à la Collection Lambert en Avignon.

teacher.aboutMe:
Oie! Tudo bem? Sou o artista por trás do perfil Monsterbox (instagram.com/monsterbox). Carioca de nascimento e capixaba de coração, sou um ex web designer que descobriu no bordado livre em 2018 um passatempo e terapia, mas que viu a arte têxtil se encaminhar pra um rumo mais profissional conforme os pedidos de encomendas para bordados personalizados começaram a aparecer.

As linhas, agulhas e tecidos foram rapidamente tomando conta do quarto, da casa e se tornaram uma profissão de tempo integral no período de apenas 1 ano. Nesse tempo de trabalho com bordado já tive a oportunidade de criar e produzir centenas de encomendas personalizadas que já foram enviadas para todos os estados do Brasil e até mesmo para alguns países no exterior. Meus trabalhos feitos 100% à mão vão desde bordados comemorativos para datas especiais, memórias fotográficas bordadas, até os bordados realistas de Pet, que são minha paixãozinha e meu nicho de trabalho com maior sucesso.

Criar, bordar e poder fazer parte das histórias de vida de várias pessoas através do meu trabalho é algo que eu quero levar comigo pelo resto da minha vida. E aí, vamos juntes nessa caminhada? :)

teacher.aboutMe:
¡Hola! Soy Javi Bueno. Diseñador gráfico especializado en letterings digitales y director creativo/fundador de Siroko Studio. 

Estudié Diseño Gráfico en la Escuela Superior de Diseño de Aragón. En 2010 decidí establecerme como diseñador gráfico freelance.

En 2016 fundé Siroko Studio, un estudio de diseño estratégico en el que desarrollamos proyectos de comunicación visual. Ayudamos a nuestros clientes en todo el proceso de creación, activación y comunicación de su marca.. 

Me especialicé en lettering porque siempre me he sentido atraído por el uso y el poder de comunicación que tiene la tipografía. Donde realmente me gusta experimentar y jugar es en el diseño de letterings creativos digitales combinando conceptos, texturas y técnicas, aplicándolos a campañas e identidades para ofrecer una visión diferente y más expresiva.

Este estilo propio, ha hecho que agencias importantes, marcas reconocidas y clientes, hayan querido colaborar conmigo durante estos años. Marcas como Audi, Estrella Damm, National Geographic, Mikado, Fox, Inditex...

En la actualidad me encuentro más enfocado en la dirección creativa y artística de los proyectos de branding y comunicación visual.

Gracias por tu tiempo y te invito a que disfrutes del curso que imparto para esta gran comunidad de creativos que es Domestika❤️

Matthias Berghoff
As a consultant, trainer and coach, I support organisations in designing contemporary, people-centred management and leadership tools. From the perspective of identity-oriented management, I shape processes and programmes for the development of modern working environments. For this, I rely on my experience as a freelancer, manager and partner together with my academic education in the fields of communication, business administration as well as work and organisational psychology.

Anastasios Koupantsis
I am an experienced and award-winning multidisciplinary designer living and working in Düsseldorf, Germany. 
From 2008 to 2021 I ran Betty and Betty, my own design studio, which I founded during my studies. At the intersection of design and strategy, I worked with my team to create holistic identities and inspiring brand experiences that help businesses and brands evolve in a world of constant change. Always based on clear values and high aesthetics. 
As change is the only constant in life, I have decided to close my studio and join the great team at MetaDesign in 2021. My goal is to keep finding new ways to make identity visually tangible and to tell stories that connect brands and people.

teacher.aboutMe:
DaDa é uma marca de produtos para casa que tem em sua essência a experimentação gráfica em estamparia têxtil. Dirigida pela dupla criativa Florence Dagostini e Ana Conrado, o DNA da marca é o uso de colagens em papel para a criação de estampas autorais e coloridas. Nosso objetivo é fugir da monotonia e criar produtos têxteis para decoração - como mantas e tapetes - que sejam expressivos e transformem ambientes. 

A DaDa tem em Berlim uma vertente internacional. Sempre alinhada conceitualmente com a sede no Brasil, mas com total independência criativa, a DaDa Berlin trabalha com lã pura e processos de produção diferenciados, preservando o compromisso com a criação manual e com a experimentação visual.
Instagram DaDa Berlim: @dada_duo_eu

teacher.aboutMe:
Mi chiamo Matteo e sono nato nel 1982.  Sono cresciuto a Lecce, e nel 2001 mi sono trasferito a Milano, dove qualche anno più tardi ho conseguito la laurea in interior e product Design al Politecnico Di  Milano.
A 22 anni al mio secondo anno di Politecnico ho iniziato a collaborare con una azienda da cui ho imparato l'arte della curiosità e i primi rudimenti con le resine.
Nel tempo ho approfondito e mi sono appassionato  alla lavorazione di materie plastiche, come resine, siliconi, a cui ho poi affiancato metallo, legno e terracotta. Amo i processi produttivi degli oggetti e scoprire come vengono realizzati gli oggetti che compongono il nostro mondo. 
Nel tempo ho avuto modo di partecipare a numerose fiere internazionali, maturando una sensibilità alle tendenze commerciali del design.
Parallelamente, ho avviato un percorso individuale di creazioni concettuali, in cui tecniche e materiali diversi convivono al servizio di un appassionato senso critico ed estetico di reinterpretazione degli oggetti e del loro utilizzo. 
La versatilità del mio lavoro mi ha aperto le porte del mondo della moda portandomi a collaborare con aziende come Mila Schon, e ad avviare una autoproduzione di borse ed accessori realizzati a mano con tecniche e materiali innovativi.
Nel 2012 ho fondato  il suo studio a Milano, lavorando a progetti di interior su alberghi e residenze private, e ad oggetti di ricerca per alcune note gallerie milanesi. 
Sono inoltre relatore per il corso di product design per IED Torino, e insegno tecniche di lavorazione delle resine presso lo IED a Milano.

My name is Kyle Daily and I am a motion graphics designer with more than a decade of professional experience. I worked for corporations as an in-house motion designer while simultaneously freelancing, and I am now a full-time freelancer. I am a lover of design, especially typography, and I enjoy exploring new techniques to bring design and typography to life with animation.

Since I began freelancing, I've focused on making Cavalry a key integration into my professional work. There are things that I'm able to do with Cavalry in minutes that would take me hours in other programs, so I aim to maximize this efficiency in my work. I also love that the team at Cavalry is continuously improving on this product, specifically based on the feedback from designers like you and me. I hope to get as many of you excited about Cavalry as I am, as the possibilities are limitless.

teacher.aboutMe:
I am a self-taught macrame artist, working in Nova Scotia Canada. Living by the ocean, my work is largely influenced by organic shapes, foliage, and driftwood. I have a degree in Aerospace Engineering which has greatly impacted my designs - transforming a one dimensional piece of rope into something three dimensional is one of my favourite aspects of macrame.

I am the founder of the audience-first Design Agency, Studio BND. We create stand-out experiences for brands who put their audiences first and want to connect with them in new and captivating ways.

At Studio BND, we are always audience-first in our approach. From our background in the events industry, we see audiences as more than just metrics and as real people with ambitions and desires. We want to help our clients foster genuine connections. We create identity systems, digital campaigns and marketing comms that place our client’s audience at the forefront of their conversation. Enabling new and existing customers alike to feel seen and heard consequently increases their lifetime value as customers.

Alongside the day to day of BND I also lecture at the University of Hertfordshire on the BA Graphic Design & Illustration Course, Act as an industry consultant for Created Academy (Fancy) and speak at events/on podcasts and to anyone who will listen, often around the themes of overcoming failure, mental health awareness and accessibility within the creative industries.

As someone who lives day-to-day with ADHD it took me most of my early years to come to terms with who I am, and what I wanted to do with my life. In the process of this I was made redundant from my first three roles within the industry, and quit my last full-time role due to a mental health crisis and burnout. As a result of this, my outlook has always been one of trying to help others succeed in life based on what they deem to be a success (not what others tell them) or to help them to better navigate and prepare for anything which might come their way.

teacher.aboutMe:
Olá, o meu nome é Diana Cunha e sou uma artista têxtil portuguesa.

Apesar de eu desde cedo demonstrar muita criatividade, só aos 40 anos é que assumi a minha paixão pelos fios e pelo têxtil. Tirei a licenciatura em Relações Internacionais em Lisboa e entrei no mundo da banca onde trabalhei 20 anos. Vivi 6 anos em Angola (entre 2009 e 2015) e quando fiz 40 anos senti uma grande necessidade de dar largas à minha criatividade. Com uma grande curiosidade pela tapeçaria, frequentei dois workshops da artista australiana Maryanne Moodie. Desde a primeira peça que fiz no workshop que percebi que tinha encontrado o meu caminho. Desde essa altura, desenvolvi a minha própria linguagem e estilo, dando um caracter contemporâneo às minhas peças utilizando técnicas ancestrais como a tapeçaria em tear, o macrame e o bordado.

No inicio de 2016 criei a minha marca “Oficina 166” e no fim de 2017 mudei o meu atelier de minha casa para um atelier maior, onde trabalho com uma equipa de 2 pessoas a tempo inteiro.

Em Abril de 2018 inaugurei a minha primeira exposição individual na galeria do Museu da Carris e em Julho de 2019 voltei a expor na loja de design de interiores Puracal, ambas em Lisboa.

Numa busca constante de novos materiais e com vontade de explorar novos designs, o meu portfolio vai desde tapeçarias decorativas (misturando as técnicas de tapeçaria e macramé), troncos e ramos grandes tecidos, a coleções de candeeiros, telas bordadas e mobiliário exterior utilizando corda náutica.

Cada peça é única e tem a sua própria história. Faço mesmo questão de não fazer duas peças iguais, quero que um cliente sinta que tem uma peça especial e única. As peças que mais gosto de fazer são as de grande dimensão e os projectos e instalações grandes são já uma imagem da minha marca. 

O meu atelier recebe encomendas de particulares (quer portugueses, quer estrangeiros, por exemplo dos EUA, Luxemburgo,  Turquia e Angola), mas na sua maioria os meus clientes são do ramo hoteleiro e restauração, arquitetos e designers de interiores e empresas. Poderão encontrar algumas das suas peças no bem conhecido Bairro Alto Hotel (Lisboa), no White Exclusive Suites & Villas (São Miguel, Açores), no Hotel Albatroz (Cascais), em vários pequenos hotéis pelo país e em restaurantes, quer em Portugal, quer no estrangeiro, tais como o Tsukiji do chef Paulo Morais em Lisboa e o Banco Knokke na Bélgica.

Ensinar as várias técnicas passou a ser uma das minhas missões. Adoro ensinar e contagiar este amor pelo feito à mão e pelos fios. Durante todo o ano, organizo workshops, cursos e retiros criativos onde são abordadas as várias técnicas. Também dou workshops a empresas (por exemplo, workshops no âmbito de team-buildings) e para grupos de turistas que viajam para Portugal e pretendem usufruir de experiências criativas são também uma possibilidade.
