teacher.aboutMe: Finbarr O’Reilly is an independent photographer and multimedia journalist who works mosrly in conflict zones and complex humanitarian emergencies. He is the author of the nonfiction memoir, Shooting Ghosts, A U.S. Marine, a Combat Photographer, and Their Journey Back from War (Penguin Random House 2017). Finbarr lived for 12 years in West and Central Africa and has spent two decades covering conflicts in Congo, Chad, Sudan, Afghanistan, Libya, Gaza, and Ethiopia. He is the 2019 Nobel Peace Prize exhibition photographer and a frequent contributor to The New York Times. His photography and multimedia work has earned numerous industry honors, including First Place in the Portraits category at the 2019 World Press Photo Awards. He was also winner of the World Press Photo of the Year in 2006 and earned a 2020 Emmy for the PBS Frontline documentary Ebola in Congo. Finbarr has in recent years focussed on leading collaborative multi-platform projects that develop and promote a more representative range of voices and perspectives in the photojournalism industry while translating strategic and editorial objectives into engaging and compelling narratives that influence global audiences. He is committed to educational, mentoring, and personal development initiatives aimed a meaningful diversification of the media landscape and the promotion of social justice. Finbarr is a Canon Ambassador.

Hola Soy Katerine, una romantica artista Juguetera. 
Desde pequeña diagnosticada con una pasión descontrolada por los objetos, los animales, el DIY y crear cuentos en mi cabeza. De formación soy ilustradora de la Escuela Nacional de Caricatura (durante casi 10 años mi segundo hogar y la primera escuela de ilustración en Colombia). Donde aprendía a hacer maravillas y casi milagros. Allí trabajé en Diseño gráfico,  además de organizar expos, eventos y, ser docente de Ilustración. 
Un día renuncié a todo eso que tanto amaba y me fuí tan lejos como pude queriendo retomar mi proyectos propios de ilustración; después a una experiencia corta pero transformadora en mi paso por la HSLU y al volver a mi hogar me reencontré con mi amor de infancia: crear personajes e historias, en esa exploración tropecé con la técnica de Needle felting y no volví atrás, logrando así hacer las pases con mi formación en ilustración, mi deseo narrar y mi niña interior, de esa combinación nació Juanamatú.

En Juanamatú  El Gordo es nuestro oso embajador y durante mas de 5 años cada muñeco fabricado se ha vuelto un miembro más de la familia, por eso cuando hablamos de Juanamatú hablamos de nosotros.  Ser complices, mentores y amigos es nuestra pasión.
Nuestro trabajo es fabricar recuerdos de seres y cosas queridas.  
Hay días maravillosos en que alguien llega con una idea y la pone en nuestras manos con absoluta confianza de que haremos un muy buen trabajo. Nos confían a sus seres queridos: sus mascotas, alguien a quien aman, sus personajes favoritos y o sus diseños propios. A eso nos dedicamos, a materializar recuerdos, ayudamos a otros a hacer realidad sus proyectos y enseñar a otros que los anhelos del corazón se pueden convertir en emprendimientos.

Mi nombre es Dominique, soy artista chilena y desde que tengo recuerdos dibujo. Mi trabajo se centra en el dibujo a grafito y en lápiz a color sobre papel el cual comencé a intervenir con bordado hace algunos años. Mi obra busca hablar de la memoria y los recuerdos, utilizando fotografías familiares antiguas como modelos de mis dibujos. Me gusta el dibujo y el bordado porque al igual que las fotografías antiguas nos hablan de un lenguaje universal: todos hemos dibujado en algún minuto de nuestras vidas, y de esta misma manera el bordado también fue parte de el pasado de muchos, en mi caso mi madre fue quien me enseñó a bordar.

El hacer convivir ambas técnicas en un mismo espacio me permitió acercarme a mis trabajos de una manera diferente, logrando capas y texturas en una sola hoja para luego ir armando una imagen que se vela con los hilos, borrando parte de la información y así creando una especie de collage cuya columna vertebral es lo manual.

teacher.aboutMe:
I’m Allyson, a fibre artist based in Pictou, Nova Scotia, Canada. 


My weaving journey began seven years ago when I was studying Studio Art at the University of Guelph in Ontario, Canada. I was taking a variety of studio courses, and focussing much of my time studying painting, drawing, and sculpture, which included welding and woodworking. 
There were no textile or tapestry weaving courses in the Fine Arts department at the time, so I took to the internet to try and find anything I could to teach myself how to weave. There wasn’t much in the way of online resources at the time, which lead to me developing a practice that was completely self-taught. 


Three years later in 2016, I took a giant leap by quitting my job in retail and began weaving full-time. 
Since then I have exhibited my work in Canada, the US, and Europe, made hundreds of custom pieces for homes and commercial spaces all over the world, developed and created five online video weaving courses, and been featured in numerous publications including two books on contemporary weavers. 


A little bit about my process and philosophy: 

I make mostly small-scale work using fibres and other materials that I find second-hand as much as possible, and I weave with simple tools that I make myself or source from my local craft and hardware stores. 

It has always been really important to me that I do as much as I can with as little as I can, and that includes creating as little waste as possible by re-using all of my yarn scraps.

There are almost an endless amount of techniques that you can use to weave different patterns and designs, many different types of looms and tools, and more yarns in existence than you can imagine. All of this can make weaving seem really intimidating, which is why the goal of my artistic practice and as a teacher is to simplify the process as much as possible while maximizing the visual potential by using bold colour palettes and three-dimensionality. 

My hope is that this will help to make weaving more of an accessible art form and inspire others to explore their interest in the craft.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi! My name is Adeline and I am a self-taught punch needle artist and designer.

Over the years, I’ve dabbled in different art media and I consider myself lucky to have found punch needle back in 2019. My punch needle journey has been and still is evolving as I learn and grow in my practice. I started with small projects such as pillows, trivets, and crossbody bags. As I tried to perfect my stitches, I quickly moved on to larger projects like rugs and wall hangings. During that time, I advanced from traditional punch needle rug hooking to a broader multi-texture and multi-technique fiber world. I was able to incorporate weaving, embroidery, beading and tufting into my work and now the possibilities are endless!

These days, besides creating my own experimental and “just for fun” projects, I’m also designing digital punch needle patterns and working on commissions and collaborations.

Punch needle is my tool of self expression and my creative outlet. I’ve always enjoyed turning my own designs into functional beauties and it changed my life when I realized my art can also bring joy to someone else. It has lead me to a supportive community of fiber lovers and friends, for which I will be forever grateful.

Mi camino en el arte empezó como muchos: por curiosidad y gusto. El lettering comenzó como un hobby, pero poco a poco se volvió una de mis mayores pasiones. Siempre me han encantado las letras, así que decidí seguir aprendiendo y especializarme en lettering y tipografía para integrarlo más a mi estilo como diseñadora.

Cancún también ha sido una gran fuente de inspiración. Los colores, la naturaleza y la vibra del lugar se reflejan mucho en mi trabajo. Me encanta jugar con tonos vibrantes, ilustrar flores y acompañarlas con frases positivas que conecten con las personas.

El lettering y la botánica tropical son una parte muy importante de quién soy: alguien alegre, curiosa y creativa. Disfruto mucho los momentos tranquilos, como estar en la naturaleza con una taza de café, dejando que las ideas fluyan. Todo eso se mezcla en mi proceso creativo y es lo que me impulsa a seguir explorando y creando todos los días.

Ho lavorato e lavoro con clienti di ogni dimensione, dai microbusiness ai grandi gruppi; il mio approccio al digital marketing è concreto e operativo, non a caso la prima raccolta organica dei miei scritti aveva come titolo “Manuale di buonsenso in rete”.

teacher.aboutMe:
Howdy! I'm Erikas, a kid who loves cartoons, animals, video games, and comic books. Only now that I'm older, I get to draw my nerdy loves in my own way and share them with the world! I got started designing vector artwork in high school, and have taught myself most of what I know about the world of design through the Internet and courses just like mine since then. My style is inspired by the simple colors and geometry of mid-century design and folk art - I try to distill subjects into basic shapes and portray them in unique ways that hopefully bring a smile to the viewer's face. Currently I am lucky enough to draw for a living as a freelance illustrator, getting to create eye-catching infographics and editorial illustrations for clients.

I'm a New Yorker-turned-Texan, and spend my off-time barking at squirrels with my duck-tolling retriever Sammy, listening to some synthy jams, or yelling at the TV when my sports team disappoints. Lately I've been exploring creating art away from a computer screen, with my current obsession being acrylic paint markers and anything I can find to draw on. I look forward to connecting with creatives from around the world, sharing any bits of knowledge I may have to help unlock their creativity - and my own!

Check out some of my work and connect with me on Instagram! I'd love to hear from ya @erik_as_erik

Sus enseñanzas e influencias tuvieron gran impacto en mi proceso, por lo que desde entonces me especialicé en el retrato y la moda.

Mi trabajo se transforma entre lo editorial y comercial, lo que me ha permitido alcanzar clientes como Netflix, Missoma, Carlos Vives y marcas reconocidas como Delsey Paris, Prüne, Kika Vargas y Olga Piedrahita, entre otros. 
Siempre he pensado en mi trabajo como mi proyecto personal, por lo que me gusta explorar lo que me rodea resaltando la belleza a través de lo simple, contando una historia con los colores, la composición y la luz.

Actualmente me encuentro basada en la ciudad de Bogotá trabajando en fotografía de moda y retrato, tanto en el mundo editorial como en publicidad.

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm born in 1982 in Tortona (AL), I live and work in Voghera (Italy).
In 2007 i achieved my degree in painting at the Art Academy of Brera (Milan).

i work exclusively with colored pencils, I often represent the flora, fauna and female mystics of Sardinia from the 16th to the 18th centuries
Combining organic shapes and textures with chiaroscuro contrasts of light and shadow, my drawings portray isolated female faces framed by plants and animals. 
My imagery refers to the herbalist traditions and Sardinian folklore of the mystical seductresses who enchant, curse and cure. My body of work is a tribute to the legacy of healing women throughout history. 

my works appeared in books, newspapers and magazines such as The New Yorker, Juxtapoz Magazine, Hi Fructose Magazine, Les Arts Dessines, Arte Mondadori.
With Albin Michel I published the illustrated book "Poucette" (distributed in Spain for Edelvives with the title "Pulgarcita"). I'm preparing an illustrated book in collaboration with Sébastien Perez.

I collaborate with Jonathan LeVine Projects (New Jersey) and Thinkspace Projects (Los Angeles) for America, Gallery Benoni (Copenhagen), Galleria Patricia Armocida (Milan), Galleria Giovanni Bonelli (Milan) for Europe.
I took part in the 54th International Art Exhibition, Biennale di Venezia, Italian Pavilion, curated by Vittorio Sgarbi, Lombardy Regional Pavilion, Palazzo Te, Mantova, "Turn The Page: the first ten years of hi-fructose" at the Virginia Museum of Contemporary Art (Moca) (US), POW! WOW! Hawai'i at the Honolulu Museum of Art School (US), THE NATURE SQUISITE: BEYOND THE BOUNDARIES OF POP at the Stelline Foundation (Milan), The New Vanguard - at The Lancaster Museum of Art and History (MOAH) and IMAGO at the Much Museum in Munich (Germany).
Among my solo shows: “Dear Collapse” Thinkspace Project (Los Angeles), “Monism” Galleri Benoni (Copenhagen), “Il Ricordo è un Consolatore Molesto” Galleria Patricia Armocida (Milan), “Home” Galleria Giovanni Bonelli (Milan), “ Animanera ”Jonathan LeVine Gallery (NY).

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello! My name is Amy Isles Freeman, I am based in Brighton, UK, and I paint clothes, create murals, and design for print. My work explores female sexuality, joy and freedom, and this theme began in art school, when I dove into the world of feminist art. I loved the raw emotion, but whilst the anger in the work resonated with me, it didn't come naturally in my own expressions. Then, in 2013, I visited an exhibition of Dorothy Iannone's work, and that changed everything for me. Colourful, cheeky and hilarious, I walked around the show with my laughter bouncing off the walls. She used the best communication tool to carry her message - humour. From then on, I felt the freedom to make work that would illicit at least a smile, if not a chuckle. Making work that celebrates women and the joy of the female experience. 

Since graduating from Falmouth Art School in 2014, I created a range of hand turned, hand painted wooden bowls that have been stocked by Le Bon Marché, Paris, and Liberty, London. Since moving to Brighton in 2018, my hand painted, pre loved clothing became a mainstay of my practise, and my dungarees, jackets and boilersuits are worn across the world.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy El Norbi y me especializo en Infografía y Diseño de Información.
 
Trabajé en los diarios argentinos de alcance nacional como “Clarín”, “La Nación”, “Página/12”, “La Razón”, “Critica de la Argentina” y “Tiempo”. También he dado talleres de capacitación que en varios periódicos latinos. Desde los peruanos "El Comercio", "Perú 21", "Gestión" y "La República", pasando por los venezolanos "El Nacional", "El Mundo", "Líder" y "Últimas Noticias", el paraguayo "La Nación", hasta los argentinos "El Diario" de Córdoba y "El Sol" y "Los Andes", de Mendoza. 

Soy el creador de la Carrera de Diseño de la Información, única en Latinoamérica, en la Universidad de Palermo de Buenos Aires. También he sido profesor en la Universidad Austral, en la Abierta Interamericana y en la de Morón (Argentina); en la Universidad de los Andes, en la UTEM, en la Diego Portales y en la Católica (Chile); en la Universidad de Medellín (Colombia); en la Universidad de Acapulco (México); en la Universidad de Ort (Uruguay); y la Universidad Científica del Sur (Perú), entre otras.

He sido jurado de los Premios Internacionales Malofiej de Infografía, en Navarra, España.

Diseñé una serie de banderines con tipografías para varios equipos de la NBA, con el auspicio de la gaseosa Sprite.

Hice el lanzamiento de Coca-Cola de un litro, a través de un comercial que se usó como patterns en todo el mundo, para la agencia de publicidad McCann-Erickson. 

Me publicaron un libro de infografías de superhéroes y personajes de historieta que se llama “Infocomics: Los secretos de los superhéroes (y de otros personajes de historieta)”, para el mercado de habla hispana. Y recientemente se hizo una versión para Italia.

Soy el responsable del diseño, análisis y realización final de las infografías para las redes sociales de Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas y Censos (INDEC) de la Argentina.

teacher.aboutMe:
Sou Designer Gráfico em tempo integral desde 2010 com foco em Marcas e Identidade Visual.

Eu moro em Campo Grande-MS, onde comecei a trabalhar em diversas agências de publicidade e propaganda, estúdio de Design, e também atuando como sócio de um Estúdio de Branding.

O desenho sempre me interessou, desde pequeno. Eu era aquela criança que ficava desenhando nas aulas, sonhando com algo que eu não sabia exatamente o quê, muito menos o impacto que esse sonho teria na minha vida. Fiz faculdade de Design pela Universidade Católica Dom Bosco, que concluí em 2011.

Hoje atuo como Designer Sênior Independente em projetos pelo Brasil e em países como Áustria, Reino Unido, Israel, Estados Unidos, Emirados Árabes e Nepal.

Fiz participações no canal TheFutur, de Santa Mônica – Califórnia, onde dividi um pouco do meu processo de criação de marcas em Lives do Programa Logo Therapy, pelo Youtube.

Faço parte também de um programa internacional de pesquisa e preservação de marcas modernistas,
o LogoArchive, sendo um dos colaboradores aqui no Brasil.

teacher.aboutMe:
Sono nato a Milano nell’anno 77. Nell’85 vedo Ritorno al Futuro e Marty McFly su uno skateboard, inizio così una passione incredibile per arte, musica e tavola.
Oggi ho uno studio grafico che è focalizzato sulla progettazione grafica/art direction di prodotti che vengono soprattutto stampati: dal packaging alle copertine di dischi, da prodtti editoriali a brand identiy (Versace, Andrea Batilla, Pinbowl Skatepark, Paula Cademartori, K7! records, Wildhoney records, Maggioni Type, La Tempesta dischi, Le Grand Jeu, artisti della scena underground italiana e non: Auroro Borealo, The Gluts, Niklas Pashburg, Danielle, Black Lips, Pay… )
Dal 1999 ho collaborato come fotografo per alcune riviste/webzines, l’agenzia Retna di New York ed Mtv.it producendo diversi tipi di reportage, dai gruppi punk più improbabili negli scantinati della Brianza fino ai live di nomi blasonati a Coachella Festival (California).
Dal 2005 anni tengo 2 corsi presso lo I.E.D. di Milano: “Brand design” e “Printmaking techniques”.
Da sempre sono appassionato di serigrafia, base della produzione/cultura d.i.y. (do it yourself), ho partecipato a diversi corsi legati a questa disciplina presso il Saint Martin School of Art e East London Printmakers (Londra).
Quando non dormo serigrafo, quando non serigrafo scatto foto.

teacher.aboutMe:
Mein Name ist Simone Ryan und ich bin das Gesicht hinter dem Stricklabel "Rust Knitwear", das ich 2020 gegründet habe. Ich bin tätig als unabhängige Strickdesignerin und Bloggerin und unterrichte diverse Strickkurse hier in Zürich. Meine Hauptarbeit besteht darin, neue Strickdesigns (Pullover, Cardigans, Accessoires) zu entwerfen und dazu Strickanleitungen zu schreiben und zu verkaufen. Ab und an arbeite ich als Freelance Designerin für grössere Firmen. Meine Arbeit begleite ich visuell mit einem Instagram Blog unter @rust_knitwear.

Ursprünglich war ich im Feld der Psychologie aktiv, habe allerdings aufgrund der Auswirkungen der Pandemie meinen beruflichen Fokus geändert und lebe im Moment meine kreative Seite vollkommen aus. Das Stricken begleitet mich seit vielen Jahren und war immer wieder ein Zufluchtsort für mich. Meine unersättliche Leidenschaft zum Stricken und Kreieren hat anfangs 2020 ihren Anfang gefunden und ist seither quasi nicht mehr zu stoppen. Dass ich mit meinen Händen und etwas Wolle einfach eigene Kleidungsstücke herstellen kann, für mich und meine Liebsten, ganz nach unseren Farbwünschen und Materialvorlieben, wird nie aufhören mich zu beeindrucken. Ich liebe es mit den Händen zu arbeiten und das Resultat dann direkt anfassen zu können. Jedes Stück ist so wertvoll und begleitet einem mit der richtigen Pflege ein Leben lang. 

Ich liebe es, meine Leidenschaft und mein Wissen im Bereich des Strickens mit anderen teilen zu können, deswegen macht mir das Unterrichten von Strickkursen auch so viel Spass. Ich hoffe, dass ich mit meinem Kurs die kreative Seite in dir wecke und, dass du dir viele wunderbare wertvolle Sachen stricken kannst, die dich und deine Liebsten ein Leben lang begleiten werden. 

+++++++++++

My name is Simone Ryan and I'm the face behind "Rust Knitwear", a contemporary knitwear label which I founded in 2020. I work as an independent knitwear designer and blogger and teach a variety of knitting workshops here in Zurich.
My main focus is on designing new knitwear designs (like sweaters, cardigans and accessories) and writing and selling knitting patterns for these designs. Occasionally I work as a freelance designer for larger companies. My work is visually accompanied by a blog on Instagram, which can be found under @rust_knitwear.

Originally, I was active in the field of Psychology, however, due to the effects of the pandemic, I've changed my professional focus and am now living out my creative side to the fullest.
Knitting has been accompanying me for years and has always been my safe haven. My unsatiable passion to knit and create started its journey in 2020 has been unstoppable since then. To be able to create own garments with just my hands and some yarn and to be able to shape the pieces to my likings and colour preferences will never stop amazing me. I love working with my hands and being able to touch and feel the results. Every piece is so precious and with the right care, it will last you a lifetime. 

I love sharing my passion and knowledge in the field of knitting with others, that’s why teaching knitting workshops is giving me so much joy. With my workshop I hope to inspire you creatively and that you will knit lots of wonderful and precious pieces, which will accompany you and your loved ones over a lifetime.

teacher.aboutMe:
Bett Norris is an illustrator and lecturer whose practice is focused towards editorial, publishing and exhibition contexts.  Her work often explores themes of human connection and diversity, intending to create artwork that resonates with audiences. 

Bett has been commissioned as an illustrator for organisations including UNESCO, The National Portrait Gallery, The New York Times, Routledge, British Red Cross, The Royal College of Midwives, The Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists, Art Fund and The School of Life. She has illustrated five non-fiction books, published by HarperCollins, Ronshin, and Callisto. 

She has also created artwork for advertising projects with brands including Airbnb, Mars, Campari, Calvin Klein, Waitrose, Boots, Ocado, Avon and P&O. She is currently represented by creative production agency Making Pictures. 

Press interviews, features and coverage of Bett’s work include Creative Review, Juxtapoz, It’s Nice That, and Creative Boom. 

Bett leads contextual and practice-based modules on the USW BA (Hons) Illustration programme, and has been an invited speaker on the UWE MA Graphic Arts, and City of Bristol College’s ‘Work Forward’ programmes. 

In 2019, Bett was invited to deliver a talk about her practice and facilitated a workshop at the Apple Store, Carnaby Street, as part of their ‘Apple Today’ project. 

In 2022, she was invited by The Association of Illustrators to deliver a talk for their ‘Inside Illustration’ project.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is M.Tony Peralta and I was born/raised and live in New York City.  I’m a contemporary artist and creative director with over 20 years of experience in graphic design, art and fashion. I’ve been screen printing for 17 years and learned the art-form under the mentorship of master printer Larry Wright, (who’s worked with Warhol and Rauschenberg.)  I have a bachelors degree in Media Art from Long Island University but the majority of my experience has been self taught.  Through out my career I have worked on commissions and partnerships with At&t, Unilever, Barcelo Rum, Presidente Beer, Desus and Mero, Nike and even have had my own sneaker with Adidas.  My artwork is owned by Junot Diaz, Lin-Manuel Miranda, Swizz Beats and his wife Alicia Keys to name a few. Two of my art pieces have been exhibied and added to the permanent collection at the Smithsonian Anacostia Community Museum and have been featured in the New York Times for my “RECONNECTED” series.


In 2005, while working as a handbag designer I started an online clothing company called, The Peralta Project. Being a fan of streetwear, I’ve always had my own ideas for t-shirts, so I created the brand as a side project.  A couple of years later, I switched the concept of the brand from a streetwear brand to a latino lifestyle brand.  I focused on hyperlocal designs and created a niche for myself by designing clothing that represented my Latino and Dominican roots.  This natural progression opened up a new lane for me, since at the time, there wasn’t many brands focusing on the latino market. The business grew to a point where I was able to do it full time and in 2017 I opened up my first workshop/brick and mortar in my hometown neighborhood of Washington Heights and Inwood called Taller Peralta.

teacher.aboutMe:
I am a freelance illustrator based in Brooklyn, NY. My work is a pop art blend of surrealism and comics, and my clients include The New Yorker, The New York Times, The Washington Post, New York Magazine, and Popular Science, among others. 

I maintain an active personal practice and am at work on the second volume of my ongoing series Ellingson's Dreams, a collection of large-scale surreal drawings. I also teach a course on writing and critical theory for illustrators at the Maryland Institute College of Art's MFA in Illustration Practice program. 

I come to artmaking by way of writing fiction, and I approach each of my compositions with a writerly eye for brevity, repetition, and character. I like the idea that art has rhythms and syntax that can be read—not left to right or right to left, but intuitively, in directions negotiated by the artist, the viewer, and time.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi! My name is Manon Pons. I am a graphic designer and illustrator from the Netherlands with a passion for bullet journaling to keep me organized. I live in a village near Rotterdam, which is the city where I work, for over 4 years now. I am currently working in retail for a jewelry brand as a graphic designer. Besides my job I love a good work-out, some illustration, dancing, taking pictures and watching movies.

I always wanted to practice a creative profession. As a child you could always find me with a sketchbook. I just loved drawing, painting and taking pictures. After high school I went to Art School. Where I specialized in illustration.

After I found a job as a graphic designer I kinda lost the love for illustration. So I went looking for a way to practice drawing. This is when I found out about bullet journaling. I immediately bought a notebook and started doodling in it. I have tried several styles and techniques, but soon found out that watercolor is my favorite medium to use in my journal. On my profile I'll show you my bullet journal and illustrations. Leave me a message if you like!

teacher.aboutMe:
I’m Louise! A designer and artist who enjoys creating an accessible bullet journal.

After graduating from university and earning a Bachelor’s degree in Interior Architecture and Design, I sought to learn a new creative skill focusing on analogue materials as most of my everyday work had become digital. I turned my hand to brush lettering and discovered bullet journaling through this community. I fell in love with the duality of everyday organisation and the hands-on creativity that bullet journaling allowed me to explore. By utilising my new brush lettering skills with my appreciation for visual composition and layout, I began my first bullet journal.

In 2018, I decided to share my bullet journal online and thus, @doodlelou.co was born. My journaling style has evolved since then and I have found the methods that work more efficiently with my lifestyle instead of the traditional bullet journal method. My bullet journal career has grown enormously and have now been lucky enough to work with companies such as BBC, Papier, Cricut and Tombow. I truly believe that bullet journaling can be for everyone and fit into any lifestyle.

teacher.aboutMe:
Desde pequeño sentí la necesidad de expresarme a través de la voz, es por eso que a los 15 años ya estaba haciendo las locuciones artísticas para la radio de Mi ciudad idea y continúa en mi carrera Cómo locutor comercial, sin embargo mi sueño era incursionar en El maravilloso mundo del doblaje, alcanzarlo cuando me traslade a México aprender de los mejores a partir de ahí el tenido la oportunidad de darle vida a entrañables personajes como el pato Lucas el abuelo de Los Simpson payaso Krusty Mufasa entre muchos otros en el mundo de los videojuegos le he dado vida a Sub Zero El Commander Zavala y Marcus Phoenix por citar algunos. El hecho de llevar paralelamente las carreras de locución y doblaje permitido lograr matices Únicos y un sonido cálido y natural.
Cómo locutor a grandes marcas como AT6T, Ford, Detergentes Ariel, Trix, Movistar, entre muchas otras.
También me desempeño como voz de importantes medios de comunicación como . Televisa, TBS, Fox sports y Catoon Network, entre otras.


He recibido diversos galardones por mi trabajo como locutor del año, de la asociación nacional de locutores, premio José Lavat al mejor actor de doblaje, ciudadano ilustre de San Salvador de Jujuy y de la ciudad de Córdoba, Argentina.
Mi labor como actor de doblaje me ha llevado a recorrer casi toda Latinoamérica recogiendo el cariño de los fans en diversos eventos, teniendo entre otros, el honor de haber sido el primer acto de doblaje latino en haber sido invitado a la San Diego Comic-Con, el evento más importante del mundo de cultura pop.
Pero sin duda una de mis grandes satisfacciones, es poder transmitir mi experiencia con los nuevos talentos, ya que, como alguien que surgió de un lugar alejado de los grandes medios de difusión, considero casi una obligación ayudar a los que viene detrás, y sobre todo, inculcar el mensaje de que, no importa de donde vengas, siempre puedes brillar con tu talento. Solo es cuestión de pasión y dedicación.

Scott grew up in Switzerland, backpacked through the American West and trekked the Himalayas before spending the last 20+ years as a commercial photographer in New York City. After initially shooting sports, Scott's work eventually shifted toward the athletes themselves and portraiture. This led to photographing many of the best creative minds in Hollywood, the music industry and the worlds of business and government. Along with his advertising work for global brands and major magazines, Scott has created several personal projects including his “Scar Stories” portrait series, the highly acclaimed "Mandela Day” project and a series of portraits accompanying the film "Pop Culture" about the fatherhood experience. His work has shown at solo and group exhibits and is held in collections internationally.

Scott is also a director on a variety of projects through his production company Magenin Films. He recently directed a feature documentary "Danica: DRIVEN" that follows racing driver Danica Patrick in the lead up to her final race before retirement. The film was selected into ten film festivals, and has won awards for "Best Biographical Film", "Best Sports Film" and "Best Cinematography".

Scott is also an International Cinematographers Guild Local 600 member as a still photographer.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Mijal and I'm a graphic designer specialized in branding and packaging. 
I have been in the field for over 15 years. My profession led me to live in Argentina, USA, India and Israel.

I always liked the arts and all my hobbies somehow ended up being in the creative field. I was also born into a family with similar interests or professions, so for me, graphic design was a natural fit. As I went to school for design, I realized that the structure of classes and schedules and exams wasn't exactly for me, so I dropped out and decided to learn on my own. Looking back, this was, for me, a stepping stone to what would be my preferred method of learning and working.

As I started working as an In-house graphic designer it allowed me to continue learning on my free time and acquiring some free-lance clients. Fast forward a few years and I became a Creative Director for a marketing agency, later the owner of my own studio Bold Design.

While I was working for others, in an office setting, I found that this was not HOW I wanted to work. I loved the field, but not working as an employee. This realization made me re-think my career and what was important for me: Creativity and Freedom. By then, I had a new goal: take all I learned in my past experiences and become my own studio. And it worked. Once I established myself as a freelancer I joined forces with other creatives (copy writers, animators, web designer). This was the beginning of creating my studio. 

Today I love being an identity and packaging designer, and I love working in a freelance setting. I can't ask for more.

I have learned a few tricks along these years (sometimes the hard way), and I can't wait to share them with the world!

teacher.aboutMe:
Eu sou Cláudio Gil. Professor, Designer, Artista, Calígrafo.
Sou calígrafo autodidata, iniciei as investigações e ensaios em 2003 e realizei mais de 300 cursos no Brasil e no exterior desde então. 
Sou um pesquisador apaixonado por paleografia, escrita, caligrafia e linguagens visuais e já lecionei em universidades, bienais, instituições culturais e eventos de design e de artes no Brasil, América Latina, Canadá e Europa. 
A minha base é sólida e obtida através da prática e da pesquisa, o que me permite explorar e extrapolar os limites do clássico. O meu trabalho alcança muitas vertentes, sempre cheias de frescor e singularidade, algo que se tornou a minha marca no meu trabalho. As minhas produções já foram exibidas e publicadas em vários países e muitas das minhas obras estão em coleções de museus e centros culturais ao redor do mundo.

No meu trabalho entendo que a inspiração só acontece quando eu trabalho, quando me empenho nas disciplinas necessárias para me aprimorar. Só acontece com dedicação. Sem a minha transpiração a inspiração raramente ocorre. Eu costumo dizer aos meus alunos que só erra quem faz, que o erro faz parte da natureza humana. Já ouvi muito sobre aprender com os próprios erros, porém eu acredito que o aprendizado só é possível quando seguimos em frente, quando viramos a página e nos arriscamos novamente. Afinal de contas é por isso que estou aqui, pra me arriscar, mas a busca é pelo acerto, sempre!

A caligrafia pra mim tem uma relação direta com a pintura abstrata e por isso eu a utilizo como fundamento para os meus estudos e as minhas produções em artes plásticas e no design. Ela é referente ao gesto, ao “vazio”, ao ritmo, à composição. Eu amo a relação entre os elementos traçados pelas minhas mãos e os espaços de luz que os meus traços determinam. A forma somente não nos é suficiente, é preciso inseri-la no contexto da melhor maneira, seja a pintura ou no design.

Aprendi a apreciar o fato das letras se desligarem da sua função principal, de compor uma palavra ou um texto. Nesse momento é que a multiplicação dos sentidos acontece na minha cabeça. É quando inicia-se o jogo de construir em desacordo com regras, com os cânones ou modelos estabelecidos há muitos séculos. Mas é preciso conhecer essas regras para quebrá-las, pois se trata de construção, de sempre construir, pois para distorcer algo é preciso conhecer esse algo muito bem e para conhecê-la é preciso estudá-la, praticá-la. É construir conhecimento.

Praticar a caligrafia funciona muitas vezes como uma espécie de limpeza mental, o momento em que me concentro, me organizo e faço. E isso na minha visão é essencial para seguir adiante e  deixar de fora toda e qualquer informações ou sentimentos desnecessários. Isso me deixa em um estado de espírito de muita paz mesmo quando pareço estar agitado e vibrante. Pintar uma superfície utilizando diferentes instrumentos requerem força física e controle mental e essa energia é necessária para que o o meu espírito permaneça sereno enquanto trabalho. Quando  estou muito concentrado em algo eu sou capaz de perceber a energia que empenho nas minhas atividades e isso me faz bem, me renova, me equilibra.

Gosto de desafios e de viver as experiências. Isso é algo natural para mim. Não vejo uma separação entre arte e vida e sou muito grato pelo fato de que a minha profissão, as minhas escolhas, as minhas jornadas tenham me propiciado ampliar os meus horizontes e diminuir as distâncias entre o sonho e a realização dos mesmos. Foi através do design e da arte que eu construí a minha trajetória. É através desses campos de conhecimento que eu continuo conquistando os espaços onde eu desejo estar,  seja montando exposições, publicando trabalhos p, participando de conferências, congressos, festivais de arte, de design e de caligrafia. Amo conhecer as pessoas e aprender um monte de coisas com elas. Isso me move e me faz sentir cheio de amor para continuar a jornada. Gratidão. Sempre!

teacher.aboutMe:
Me dedico al diseño y confección de joyería fina, bajo mi marca homónima que creé el año 2019. Mi especialidad son las joyas de diseño de autor, producidas de forma manual y a baja escala, con metales preciosos, piedras naturales y la técnica italiana del micro mosaico. 

La magia detrás de las joyas ocurre en mi estudio en Santiago de Chile, donde confecciono las piezas y también recibo a clientes que quieren visitar mi taller y conocer más sobre mi trabajo. En mi cuenta de instagram comparto mi trabajo, el proceso detrás de las joyas y las cosas que me inspiran. Este medio me ha permitido relacionarme y llegar a gente a lo largo de Chile y el mundo. 

He tenido la oportunidad de vivir y recorrer distintos lugares, como Barcelona, Madrid, Mallorca, Italia y Chile por supuesto, lo cual me permitió formarme con diferentes maestros, aprender sus técnicas y el ‘saber hacer’ de cada uno de ellos.

Para mí, crear joyas es un proceso en el cual puedo expresar mis emociones, una forma de comunicarme a través de la naturaleza de los materiales y los símbolos, que se transforman en pequeñas obras de arte que acompañan en el tiempo. Me inspira profundamente trabajar con materiales tan nobles y maravillosos como los metales, el vidrio y las piedras naturales. Mi búsqueda personal es intentar acercar lo sublime a nuestro mundo cotidiano.

Forma&Cemento è un’eccellenza italiana della lavorazione artigianale del cemento. Dai tavoli alle librerie, dagli sgabelli ai vasi, fino ad arrivare a piani cucina e rivestimenti per pareti e pavimenti. Forma&Cemento crea prodotti di lusso facilmente riconoscibili dal trattamento esclusivo della materia e dall'appassionata ricerca della leggerezza e dello stile. 
La nostra mission è quella di progettare e realizzare manufatti in cemento in modo tale che la materia, tradizionalmente considerata povera al confronto, attraverso la sapiente lavorazione artigianale e al design ricercato, diventi pregiata tra i migliori marmi e i legni più raffinati.

teacher.aboutMe: Andrés Marti (Bogotá, 1989) es un artista / diseñador colombiano. Co-fundador y Director del Laboratorio de Imagen Comes Cake, Director de arte del Hotel Click Clack y Drag queen del colectivo Mis Amigas Drag. En su proyecto fotográfico Otredad, busca encontrarse a sí mismo retratando a otras personas de una manera melancólica y surrealista. Coloreando sus narices y párpados en rojo rubí sumerge a cada personaje en un universo atemporal que juega entre la realidad y la ficción. En sus retratos, cuya esencia es el collage, mezcla maquillaje con postproducción, luz natural y artificial, elementos reales y digitales. Su obra se ha exhibido en diferentes espacios y plataformas en Bogotá, Londres, Tokio y Madrid.

teacher.aboutMe:
Luca Barboni, pioniere del Growth Hacking in Italia.

Dal 2014 "rubo" la velocità e l'approccio delle startup della Silicon Valley affinché diventi accessibile agli imprenditori italiani.

Nel 2018 vengo segnalato da Klout (classifica di social influencer numero 1 al mondo) come il 2° profilo Twitter più autorevole sul tema, in testa a Sean Ellis, l’inventore della disciplina.

Sono autore del 1° libro italiano sul Growth Hacking: “Growth Hacking: fai crescere la tua impresa online”, edito dalla Dario Flaccovio Editore, che ha visto la sua prima stampa andare sold-out in soli 4 mesi.

Organizzatore del GHday, la più grande conferenza europea che accentra professionisti internazionali attorno a questa innovazione nel Digital Marketing.

Negli ultimi 4 anni ho formato più di 5000 studenti e professionisti sui temi dell’Imprenditoria e del Digital Marketing, insegnando nelle più prestigiose università italiane tra cui: La Sapienza, LUMSA, Bocconi, IULM, l’Università Cattolica di Milano e altre ancora.

Oltre a condividere conoscenza sul tema tramite insegnamento e mentorship in Italia, presenzio in qualità di speaker ad eventi in Silicon Valley. Le slide dei miei interventi sul GH sono diventate virali su Slideshare, ottenendo migliaia di visualizzazioni e condivisioni in poche ore.

Tra i pochi italiani ad essere stato selezionato da 500startups, l’acceleratore di startup legato al Venture Capital più attivo sulla Terra, con un progetto sull’intelligenza artificiale Made in Italy.

Vincitore nel 2014 del Telekom Innovation Contest: startup competition organizzata da Deutsche Telekom che ha visto +300 partecipanti, 20 finalisti, un’unica startup vincitrice dell’investimento di 150.000€.

Oltre a supportare la crescita delle startup, ho collaborato con la Comunità Europea e con grandi aziende in qualità di mentor sull’innovazione. In particolare: Enel, Mercedes, Unilever, Lottomatica, IGPDecaux, e altre ancora.

Nel 2018 il mio percorso da consulente e formatore si evolve nella fondazione di 247X: la prima azienda di consulenza italiana che offre Team dedicati di Growth Hacking ai suoi clienti.

Con 247X porto avanti la mia missione di aiutare imprenditori a far crescere il loro business grazie ad analisi dei dati e sperimentazione su prodotto e canali digitali.

Sono apparso su Techcrunch, Startupitalia, Millionaire, Corriere della Sera, Il Sole 24 Ore e molte altre testate.

Nel 2018 vengo inserito da The Roman Post nella Top 10 romani under 30 più influenti che ci siano.

Nel tempo libero mi dedico a progetti di volontariato digitale quali Startup Weekend o Skillando: startup a impatto sociale che organizza missioni in paesi del terzo mondo per aiutare l’ecosistema locale.

teacher.aboutMe:
I am Carol Fountain Nix, an award-winning entrepreneur, educator, designer, and calligrapher. My work is a fusion of mixed media and calligraphy. My inspiration originates from the colors and textures in nature, and I seek to create works that have an organic, earthy feel. I grew up in the Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina in the USA, which provides an endless array of visual stimulation: rock formations, tree limbs, vines, mossy beds, and cool creek sides lined with mountain laurel.

I am forever a student of calligraphy and I have studied with some of the world’s bests lettering artists. It is a skill that requires dedication, desire, and an acute attention to detail. My goal is to create and preserve the integrity of each letter – not an easy task when writing over many layers of media. Each piece relates directly and metaphorically with the content with regard to composition, color, tone, placement and style.

I have taught calligraphy, hand lettering and typography for many years and conducted workshops all over the USA as well as internationally. I also taught lettering sessions at Facebook's Analog Research Lab, at the company’s headquarters in Menlo Park, and workshops for Adobe  in San Francisco. It was particularly fun to be a featured instructor at the annual Adobe Max Annual Creativity Conference where I taught calligraphy basics to over 180 students – at a digital conference!

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi there,
My name is Chantal (* 1992 Schaffhausen, Switzerland) and I’m an artist that works with the medium of photography.
I moved to Basel in 2013 to study art education at the Hochschule Gestaltung und Kunst in Basel finishing my masters in 2018. I still live and work here in beautiful Basel. 
My aim was never to be an independent artist or photographer, it was something that happened naturally along the way. I discovered that I like to takes photos with 15 years old, but I only wholeheartedly started to dive into photography as an artform in late 2015, almost 8 years later. 
In 2019 I turned self employed.

Since then I worked for Polaroid, Lamarel by Sandra Rodrigues Pinto ( - I shot also her social media collaborations with Gucci, Omega, Bulgari, Nespresso, Sfera, Jean Paul Gaultier, H&M, Bally, Origins, TAGHeuer, Magnum etc.), Nakedintersection, Mondetto, Troo and a few others. But my main focus is and remains my personal work.
I published a first book called „permeable membrane" in 2020 and showed my work in several exhibitions.
Also I shows my personal work in a behind the scenes way on Patreon and the third specialization are my in-person multi-days Workshops and Open atelier projects.

teacher.aboutMe:
We are Nicole and Darjan from Superdot.studio. 
Our mission is to create impact through understanding, by visualizing complex issues with enjoyable and innovative solutions. 
📚 Learn more about our methods with our information design handbook on → shop.superdot.studio ← 📚 

Nicole Lachenmeier is a Swiss information designer and co-founder of the data experience agency Superdot, founded in 2011.
Alongside her team, she has developed over a hundred visual tools and design systems for large companies, NGOs and governmental organizations. A graduate of Art and Design Visual Communication from FHNW Academy, holding a Masters in Visual Communication and Iconic Research, Nicole also studied typography and design techniques with Wolfgang Weingart. Besides her agency work, Nicole teaches visualization (and design) at several design universities. She is a co-creator of the event series On Data and Design, promoting interdisciplinary knowledge exchange in information design. Collaborating with Darjan Hil, she developed the Modular Information Design system, co-creating Visualizing Complexity, the Modular Information Design Handbook, also with Darjan Hil.
Nicole has received several awards, including The Most Beautiful Swiss books 2009 & 2016, the Information is Beautiful Award 2016, the DPA Infographics Award 2015, and Out of Balance Criticism of the Present Infographic Winner in 2013.

Darjan Hil is an information designer. He co-founded Superdot (formerly YAAY) while working as a researcher at the University of Applied Sciences, Northwestern Switzerland.
Since 2017, Darjan has taught at various Swiss Universities, lecturing on data visualization and information design principles. The co-author of Visualizing Complexity, the Handbook for Modular Information Design, initiated the event series On Data And Design in Vienna, Basel and Berlin. Darjan grew up in Austria, where he earned a Master of Science in Business Informatics from the University of Vienna. In his early professional life, working in information technology, he experienced a great deal of inefficiency arising from digital tools, remote work, and countless problems deriving from miscommunication. Witnessing a colleague explaining complexity, using a pen and a flipchart, inspired Hil to rekindle his studies, eventually graduating in 2011 with a Master of Arts in Visual Communication and Iconic Research from the Basel School of Design.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Víctor.  I was born in Spain and have worked in several countries around the world during my career (US, UK, The Netherlands). I would define myself as a curious person who is always trying to learn new things and tackle new problems (in any space!). 

Out of the many jobs I have had over the years (project, sales, service, product…), I definitely think that product management is the one that I like the most as it combines learning, understanding and solving hard problems working with many different teams and disciplines.

I have been a product manager in several companies such as British Telecom, Amazon, Inditex and most recently Shopify and I have worked in a wide variety of problem spaces.  I started out working in the telco industry at British Telecom (BT), focusing on Cloud Infrastructure to deliver Contact Center capabilities to customers (long before AWS, Azure or even the concept of the CLOUD existed!). 

Following a small parenthesis in Sales (which was not my cup of tea) I joined Amazon (Kindle) and started developing my PM craft in a completely different way (a PM serves customers by solving problems that sometimes they did not even know they had!). I started thinking on behalf of customers, how can we make things better for them? How can they access ebooks in a faster way? 

After a few years, I moved to Prime Video to help develop their catalog infrastructure so we could support live events (NFL, LaLiga, NBA, etc…) and to help customers discover the movies and series they wanted to stream in an easier way. For example, how can we use data to help people find what they want? Are awards interesting? Would you choose a movie based on how much budget it had? What about the actors starring? Are you interested in the Rotten tomatoes ranking or the IMDb information? All this, helped me to develop different mental models when I was working on products to delight customers.

More recently, I jumped to a completely different space. Logistics and fulfillment - but always with the customer in mind. How can we help e-commerce be more efficient when fulfilling orders so customers can get them seamlessly and efficiently? I joined Zara.com to oversee their fulfillment strategies around the world (i.e. how their warehouses prepare and ship orders) and later on took on a new challenge with Shopify to help entrepreneurs around the world to make fulfillment simple for them.

Su investigación se basa en inventarios populares, carrocerías de camiones, negocios informales y carteles de supermercados. Buscar a través del mapeo de alfabetos y símbolos la continuación y rescate de esta sabiduría artística.

Há mais de 15 anos me dedico ao conteúdo editorial, incluindo passagem por duas das principais revistas científicas brasileiras, Mundo Estranho e Superinteressante, títulos com reconhecimento internacional nas categorias que envolvem direção artística. Esse período resultou em mais de 15 prêmios em narrativas visuais como infográficos, visualização de dados e ilustração, incluindo uma Medalha de Bronze no Malofiej 25.

Durante os anos como designer de revistas, colaborei com a condução de infográficos, visualização de dados e ilustrações de diversos temas, propondo soluções visuais que vão desde biologia, física, arquitetura, paleontologia, cultura pop, máquinas bizarras, complexas e muito mais. Nesse vasto mundo, trabalhei em conjunto com vários ilustradores desde a concepção do material, linguagem, direção de esboços e edição final para o design final das páginas.

Como ilustrador, tenho um estilo pessoal que combina hachuras, luzes e sombras sobre poucas cores. No entanto, gosto de trabalhar com múltiplas abordagens, sendo a vetorial uma das principais.

Desde 2017 trabalho como visual designer na Accenture e, de forma independente, lancei uma história em quadrinhos de autoria própria, Vagaluz (2016), ilustrei Alice no País das Maravilhas para a Editora Ática (2020), e lancei dois quadrinhos curtos: Pink Floyd – The Wall 40 Years (16 págs., 2019) e Grunge 30 Years (18 págs., 2021).

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi yall! My name is Alicia and I'm a full time Chicago based jeweler who specializes in adding unique textures to my sculptural jewelry. With a background in Cultural Anthropology as well as a degree in Jewelry Design from New York’s Fashion Institute of Technology, I apply my knowledge of ancient techniques like reticulation and acid etching to my more contemporary designs. 
My love of complex looking ceremonial jewelry created with minimal tools such as fire, sand and beeswax have led me to truly admire the work throughout the Mesoamericas and the African diaspora. I've honed my unique style while working for dozens of major jewelry companies in the fashion industry in New York City, learning the business ins and outs during the day, while creating at night. 
I truly love the creation of jewelry and just love to share what I know and what I'm still trying to figure out. I love that you can really hone in one one concept, like wax carving, beading or metal work and just keep making things in that aspect. If you want to explore more, you can and if you don't , it's fine too.
With almost two decades of experience under my belt, and a decade of being an independent jeweler in my own right with my eponymous brand, Lingua Nigra, I continue to fabricate new ways to explore bygone approaches to creating wearable art.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hola, soy Antonio Barahona. Sevilla, 1984.

En 2003 ingreso en la Facultad de Bellas Artes Santa Isabel de Hungría de Sevilla. Recibo en 2006 la beca Erasmus de Dibujo, cursada en la Fundación de Arte Pietro Vanucci de Perugia, Italia. Y me licencio en 2008 en la especialidad de Pintura por la Universidad de Sevilla. 

Con la intención de seguir formándome y adquirir experiencia participo en 2010 en la Cátedra Francisco de Goya de Caja Ávila, impartido por Antonio López García obteniendo una calificación de sobresaliente. Ese mismo año soy seleccionado por la Fundación Antonio Gala para formar parte de la novena promoción y así desarrollar el proyecto Costumbrismo andaluz; una reivindicación de la otra cara de la cultura andaluza a través de la pintura costumbrista. Durante este año investigo en el tratamiento de la vegetación al óleo. Durante los diez años posteriores me especializo en cómo la luz se conjuga con las plantas, el color verde y su complejidad.

Tras mi paso por la Fundación Antonio Gala, continúo asistiendo regularmente a cátedras de pintura y cursos impartidos por maestros internacionales de la talla de Antonio López, Golucho, Juan F. Lacomba o Andrés García Ibañez.

Mi pintura ha sido reconocida con numerosos premios y galardones, entre los que destacan el Premio Timoteo Pérez Rubio, Oliva de la Frontera, Badajoz (2020), Premio José Arpa, Carmona, Sevilla (2019), Premio Paul Ricard, Sevilla (2018) Premio Rafael Zabaleta, Quesada, Jaén (2016) o el Premio Ateneo de Sevilla, (2010) entre muchos otros.


He realizado diferentes exposiciones colectivas e individuales, participando en ferias internacionales de arte contemporáneo siendo las últimas “KunstRAI” Art Fair representado por GalerieMokum (2021), ”El asombro de lo cotidiano” Galería SharonArt, León (2019), - “Sobre verdes y otras verdades” Individual en Sala d ́art El Quatre, Barcelona. (2016), “1929 , Paisismo Contemporáneo” Exposición individual en Lugadero (Sevilla 2014).

teacher.aboutMe:
Konnichiwa! Yohey Horishita is an award-winning Japanese illustrator, educator, and CEO – Cheif Encouragement Officer! His detailed and uniquely colored work has been recognized by many trade magazines and annual competitions such as the Society of Illustrators, Communication Arts, 3x3 Magazine, and American Illustration. Horishita was also named one of the top New Creatives 100 by CMYK Magazine in 2012. 

His clients include – the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the New York Times, Politico, Sports Illustrated, Casio, Canon, Yomiuri Newspaper, Penguin Random House, Big Brothers Big Sisters of America, and more. 

Horishita was born and raised in Japan and moved to Alabama, then Georgia, where he earned his BFA and MFA in Illustration from Savannah College of Art and Design (Atlanta). Soon after relocating to New York City in 2014, he began his freelance illustrator and teaching career. Now he is a full-time professor in the Illustration department at Maryland Institute College of Art (located in Baltimore, MD).

"Tradigital" is the best to describe his illustration-making process. Horishita loves the intensity of traditional ink drawing and the unexpectedness of the digital coloring process. The intricacy he can achieve with this material and technique is simple and complex. He finds beauty in the balance of chaos and harmony. 

After living in different places and experiencing peaks and valleys as an immigrant, minority, and queer individual, Horishita is a strong beliver of how important one's personal heritage and upbringing are in illustration making. Whether your illustration is commercial or not, in the end, it should be a gift to yourself today.

teacher.aboutMe:
After surviving cancer as a child, Bob Dobbie aka Bob Dob was forced to give up his dream of becoming a pro baseball player and his interest gravitated towards music and art. Growing up in Hermosa Beach, CA and playing in the punk band “Lunacy” for ten years, his exposure to the music scene in Los Angeles had a great influence on his art. 

While focusing on music theory at a local community college, Dob began taking drawing and painting classes. Eventually his interest in art took over and he transferred to Otis College of Art and Design in 1998 where he earned his Bachelor's of Fine Arts Degree in illustration. His illustrated paintings featured Dob’s sardonic humor spotlighting pop culture icons, video game characters such as Mario/Luigi, beach culture stereotypes, historical references and Disney characters.

In 2004 Dob had his first gallery exhibition at La Luz De Jesus Gallery in Hollywood, CA. He has been a frequent participant in group and museum shows in the United States and Europe along with a dozen solo exhibitions. Professionally, his work has been featured worldwide in advertising campaigns by Kraft Foods, AFLAC, Intel and Hurley where Dob lent his most iconic characters to an artist series line of apparel.

His work has been collected by; Ian McShane, Conan O’Brien, Nick Cassavetes, Rupert Grint, and Kate Flannery.

teacher.aboutMe:
Je suis une photographe de 35 ans spécialisée dans le lifestyle.

Je travaille avec des marques, des entreprises et des magazines depuis 6 ans, créant du contenu pour les médias en ligne, les réseaux sociaux, des campagnes de marque, l’édition.

Je travaille en lumière naturelle uniquement car je pense qu’il n’y a rien de plus simple et beau pour sublimer un produit.

Grâce à mon métier j’ai pu faire des rencontres avec des artisans extrêmement talentueux. En les photographiant et en discutant avec eux, j’ai pu constater qu’ils étaient souvent confrontés à la difficulté de présenter leurs créations en ligne. En effet, le fait de posséder un site professionnel, de devoir faire appel à un photographe pour photographier leur produits leur semblait complexe et onéreux. L’investissement était trop important et ils se sentaient bloqués dans leur évolution.

Aujourd’hui, grâce aux réseaux sociaux et à internet, vous pouvez faire connaitre votre talent et votre travail au monde entier. En ayant une communication visuelle de qualité, simple, qui vous ressemble, vous pouvez vendre vos produits en ligne et être démarché directement pour des projets.

Mon cours s’adresse aux makers, artistes, artisants, créatifs, qui souhaitent développer leur communication. Pendant ce cours, je vous donnerai des techniques simples pour photographier et mettre en valeur vos créations à l'aide d'un smartphone et de lumière naturelle.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi, I'm Hana, a social media marketing consultant working with small to medium-sized companies and female founders. Some clients I worked with include Amazon, glh Hotels, Olixa, and Children's Salon, to name a few.

My journey in social media marketing started in 2007 – blogging for an Apple magazine and later founding a fashion magazine, for which I wrote over 1,500 blog posts. Then, through a series of workshops on blogging for the general public that I ran in Prague, I got connected to working with people and training them on social media.

After I moved to London in 2014, I became a lecturer at the University of the Arts of London, where I taught social media marketing, Instagram marketing, and blogging for seven years. During this time, I started my consultancy, filmed two marketing courses with an online learning platform Domestika, taught marketing at a recognised international university Istituto Marangoni, and trained teams, staff members and business owners of new and well-established brands from America to Tasmania.

My vision is that brands and companies succeed on social by gaining visibility and reach and training provides them with a complete skillset, effortless strategy and results, and a simple and enjoyable process.

teacher.aboutMe:
I am Akemi Lucas, a Japanese calligraphy master and also known as the artist 'Koshu'. I was born in Japan and embarked on my journey as a calligrapher at the age of eight, when my mother sent me to calligraphy school to improve my writing and sense of balance, which had been compromised from losing sight in my left eye from cancer. I was very sensitive and empathetic child, feeling emotions from others, which caused many illnesses on top of cancer from a young age. So I have learned how precious life is and also how powerful artworks are showing the artists's lives and emotions, which showed how important the mindset is when I hold my brush.

I was taught under Master Seizan Fujimoto, whose lineage is traced back to a well-known calligrapher of the Meiji period, Meikaku Kusakabe. At the age of 16, I started learning the style of Mr Goseki Nishiwaki through the Bunka Calligraphy association in Tokyo, and over time, I have learnt many diverse styles of calligraphy used by other well-known calligraphers.

At the age of 24, I was qualified as a calligraphy teacher and was given the name of "Koshu" by my master, then set up my own school, teaching calligraphy in Japan. After my English husband's death, I followed his wish and moved to the UK. I managed to re-start  my calligraphy and Sumi painting courses as “Koshu Japanese Art". My distinct style of calligraphy builds on traditional skills and the expression within my sumi paintings further embodies the fusion of the ancient and the modern, the eastern and the western, the before and the after.  I pour my deep love, with my faithful heart into every single stroke and hope that the messages in my artworks reach into people’s hearts and leave an echo for future generations.  

I have held several exhibitions in the UK, Japan, USA, and Georgia, and in 2019, in excess of 40 of her artworks were exhibited at the National Museum in the Capital city of Georgia, hosted by the Japanese Embassy. My workshops, demonstrations and online classes continue to be in high demand all over the world.
I also undertake commissioned work with recent highlights being; the creation of the label for the craft Gin and Liqueurs brand Kokoro, that received a Gold award for design in 2018; creating the artwork for new packaging for the Japanese food brand, Yutaka; I was also commissioned to create artworks for the Rugby World Cup Awards, that were held in Tokyo in 2019; and undertook a major commission for the Aldi, Team GB, Tokyo Olympic 2020 advertising campaign.  In May 2021, I launched my first online sumi painting course with Domestika, and soon after, launched the second course. In 2022, I also reopened my school Dream House in Japan, and will start organising residential courses and day workshops from 2024. My first Sumi painting book will be published in 2024. My artworks and courses have brought a broader appreciation of Japanese art and has introduced my work to a wider international audience.

teacher.aboutMe:
A potência de viver e a constante busca pela liberdade artística são o combustível para Alex Rocca produzir suas tapeçarias. Com um olhar poético para sua arte, todas as peças têm forte inspiração em referências vividas dentro de vários cenários como cinema, design de interiores e arquitetura. Sua observação através de uma lente democrática, para com o mundo e com si mesmo, é a mais importante variável desta equação. 

Seu olhar permite que durante o trabalho, solitário e meditativo, o artista perceba as texturas, as cores e os padrões que o mundo apresenta. Dentro de uma rica poética com abundantes significados, Alex desenvolve sua arte, com calma e nitidez. 

A tapeçaria significa muito mais do que apenas um objeto decorativo. Cada peça transborda camadas de conteúdo e afeto, culminando em uma obra que é o espelho da própria alma. 

Assim como o mundo que serve de observatório, o artista vive um eterno transmutar. Estar aberto ao novo e a tudo que um outro amanhecer apresenta são a matéria prima mais abundante e, ao mesmo tempo, singular de que Alex se alimenta. Assim como o universo, que cresce, amadurece e muda conforme o tempo, o artista também assim permite se sentir.

teacher.aboutMe:
En el año 1983 me integré a un grupo de teatro amateur llamado “Tell el Amarna”, bajo la dirección de Martín Rivas Ortega, ahí confirmé que en realidad quería ser actriz para poder representar varios personajes con historias diferentes, y en 1986 me inscribí en el Instituto Andrés Soler, egresando en 1989.
Independientemente de la escuela, tomé cursos de Teatro en Bellas Artes con Isabel Quintanar, en la UNAM, de doblaje en Audiomaster 3000 y Conjuntos Corales en Casa de las Humanidades de la UNAM.
En 1990 me empecé a reportar en doblaje, pensando en que solo me quedaría por unos cuantos meses, pero desde mi primer llamado, algo mágico sucedió, que me quedé. Sabía que el doblaje me daba la oportunidad de interpretar un personaje diferente cada día. A diario me reportaba con la ilusión de dar voz a un nuevo personaje y así fue. Cuando entré a una sala de doblaje y vi que estaban doblando caricaturas, me emocioné mucho, porque yo tenía esas ganas de interpretar  algún día a un personaje animado. Años después me llamaron para participar en el casting de Dee Dee del Laboratorio de Dexter, y para sorpresa mía, me quedé con la voz del personaje. Esa fue mi primera participación en caricaturas, después le siguieron muchísimas más, así como animes como; Súper Campeones, Mojako, Corrector Yui, Digimón, Ben 10, Yugi Oh GX, Jimmy Neutrón, Campamento de Lazlo, Chicos del Barrio, Ed Edd y Eddie, Sakura Card Captor, Elfen Lied, Chicas Súper Poderosas, Regular Show, Doraemon, Hora de Aventura, Gumball y Naruto entre muchos otros.
A lo largo de todos estos años, no solo he participado doblando caricaturas y animes, sino también  películas, telenovelas, documentales, realitys, series y videojuegos.
Doblaje me ha dado la oportunidad de compaginar mi carrera con otras especialidades como: TEATRO ( De la Noche, Matrimonio y Mortaja del Cielo Bajan, Los Chicos del Coro, Quién Despeina a Nieto, etc) CINE (Cartel 5 y La Gata Kristy) TELEVISIÓN (Mirada de Mujer, Como en el Cine, El Candidato y La Calle de las Novias) RADIO (Dinero y Bienestar Familiar, Ciudad Mujer, Capsulas Informativas, etc) LOCUCIÓN COMERCIAL (Coca-Cola, Nescafé, Tooth Defenders, Genoma Lab, Sabritas, Liverpool, Santander y muchos más) SHOWS DE COMEDIA (presentaciones en bares y programas de televisión).
Me siento feliz de haberle cumplido el sueño a esa niña que añoraba con ser actriz, que veía la televisión pensando en que algún día, ella formaría parte de algún programa televisivo o de alguna puesta en escena.
He recibido de parte de mi Sindicato de Actores, la medalla Virginia Fábregas por 25 años de trayectoria ininterrumpida, así como reconocimientos por participaciones en conferencias. 
Con casi 32 años de experiencia me siento emocionada de poder compartir contigo mis conocimientos y experiencia, para que de mi mano, descubras tus habilidades y tu potencial para que te animes a cumplir tu sueño de poder llegar a hacer doblaje.

teacher.aboutMe:
ABS Objects is a design, art direction and ceramic studio founded in 2018 in Tel Aviv by Avi Ben Shoshan.
In our studio we produce our objects collections focusing on creating sustainable and timeless products. We produce all  of our ceramics & materials, paint and glaze each object from start to finish. All of our objects are hand made, which makes each one of them unique and slightly different. We love the natural inconsistencies of the ceramic process. The studio works on different projects during the everyday production of our collection. We have a large variety of projects from personal design for customers to collaborations ’ capsule collections, exhibitions and more.
The visual language of ABS Objects refers to nature, organic shapes, the middle eastern colors and materials. Our inspiration comes from history, archeology, art and design history and cultural methods of craft and traditions. We are interested in the relationships between human and object, as we try to reflect those relations on our collections, we aim to create sensitive and soft forms objects that we can find ourselves living with them for a long time. All ABS Objects are produced in a traditional artisan way and all are hand made in Tel Aviv by Avi Ben Shoshan. 
Avi Ben Shoshan is a Tel Aviv based designer and maker, bachelor of the Industrial Design department of Shenkar college of art design and engineering. Specializing with a variety of materials in a studio located in Tel Aviv, Israel.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy Loly Ghirardi, muchos me conocen también como Señorita Lylo.
Soy bordadora y diseñadora gráfica. Barcelona me recibió hace 20 años y aquí sigo encantada entre el mar y la montaña. Desde que me recibí en la Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA) estuve trabajando siempre en proyectos de diseño, pero con el tiempo y  poco a poco me fui yendo de lo digital y dándole más espacio a lo hecho a mano y el bordado me atrapó para siempre. 
Junto a los bastidores, hilos y agujas creo piezas únicas y experimento en distintos soportes.
Cada proyecto tiene su búsqueda conceptual y cada puntada está acompañada de alguna anécdota, de historias personales o lugares transitados. 
Con el tiempo llegó la posibilidad de enseñar todo aquello que conocía sobre el bordado, y en verdad es una tarea que me reconforta y me sigue enseñando cada día más. Bienvenida, bienvenido un placer que pasees por aqui.

Meine Spezialisierung liegt in prozeduraler Illustration und abstrakter generativer Kunst. Neben diesem Schwerpunkt erstreckt sich meine Expertise auch auf Branding, Typografie und Visual Design. Mein Stil wird oft als sehr futuristisch beschrieben – sehr experimentell und abstrakt, aber visuell stark von Natur und Wissenschaft inspiriert.

Studiert habe ich integriertes Design an der Anhalt University of Applied Sciences und bin seit 2015 freiberuflich tätig. Neben meinen persönlichen Werken konzentrieren sich meine Auftragsarbeiten meist auf Logo oder Brand Designs, Illustrationen, Packagings sowie Visuals und NFTs. My name is Martin Naumann, I’m a digital artist and multidisciplinary designer from Germany, currently based in Dessau. My specialization lies in procedural illustration and abstract generative art. Besides this focus, my expertise also extends to branding, typography, and visual design. My style is often described as quite futuristic – very experimental and abstract, but visually strongly inspired by nature and science.

I studied integrated design at Anhalt University of Applied Sciences and have been freelancing since 2015. Besides my personal work, my commissioned projects mostly focus on logos or brand designs, illustrations, packagings as well as visuals and NFTs. So far I have already worked with clients like Universal Music, Xiaomi, Anjunabeats, Die Zeit or Lando Norris.

I am a Brazilian-born, American-adopted Director of Design and artist in Los Angeles. My passion is fusing a strategic foundation with beautiful craft to create meaningful concepts. 

Self-taught, I started my career at fifteen as a web designer. Over the last two decades, I’ve developed a distinct visual style across the variety of media I work in (illustration, typography, animation, photography)—which has led me to work with most Fortune 500 brands.

My body of work has earned frequent press coverage and the highest honors in the industry, including a Grand Prix for Good in 2016 for the animated short “Malak and the Boat,” created to raise awareness around the Syrian refugee crisis.

I’ve led and built design teams, been featured in art galleries, co-founded a digital agency in Brazil and owned a design studio in LA. These days, I divide my time between my family and leading the Design Department at Deutsch, LA. I continue to experiment with new media in between lectures and workshops worldwide. When I’m not designing, I’m creating.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello!

We are Caroline Ziegler and Pierre Brichet from Studio BrichetZiegler.
Our design studio was created in Paris in 2010. We propose a transversal and open-ended vision of design through a technical and poetic approach. 

We work at all scales, from craft to industry, in the field of furniture and lighting design.
Passionate about know-how and making, we take a new look at materials and forms.
We like to design colorful, graphic and expressive objects, where material is highlighted, as well as uses.

In 2015, seeking to go further on material experimentations and make new products come to life, we were among the first French “designer-makers” to launch a self production collection, called By Hands. A family of objects and furniture, imagined, designed and made by ourselves in our workshop, in limited edition. 

In 2017, we have been awarded the Grand Prix de la Création de la Ville de Paris.
Some of our products belong to Mobilier National and CNAP permanent collections. 
We teach design at Ecole Camondo in Paris since 2013.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Talisa and I am the owner of Boss Stitch. I am an embroidery artist specializing in goldwork embroidery. Goldwork is an ancient embroidery technique that uses metal threads instead of normal embroidery thread to make beautiful pieces. It is most commonly used in military and royal regalia. Goldwork is going through a revival, with many fashion ateliers and designers using goldwork embroidery in their collections.


My work is inspired by insects, flowers and symmetrical patterns and I like to call this entomology style goldwork embroidery. I have been stitching for many years but only recently became interested in goldwork embroidery and when I found this style I knew it was the art form for me. I like to embroider insects because they are incredibly interesting to learn about and I can use different thread types and colours to make them look realistic or completely abstract. 


There is something incredibly satisfying about picking up needle and thread and being able to create any type of art you want with it. Embroidery is a very therapeutic art form and it can really help with your mental health, this was one of the reasons why I first got into stitching. After a long day in my full time job I can come home and unwind with some stitching.


If I'm not embroidering you can find me working full time as an Event Producer, living in London with my soon-to-be husband John and my cat Lola! In my spare time I like to watch TV, see friends, go to the pub, eat pizza and go to museums.

teacher.aboutMe:
I am a  British award-winning independent wallpaper, textile and surface designer renowned for my illustrative and engaging designs. Based in the heart of East London, I have long upheld principles of craftsmanship and sustainable design through up-cycling and re-appropriation of authentic heritage materials. Trained in the traditional process of silk-screen printing at the Royal College of Art, I set up my studio in 2007 to make bespoke, hand printed wallpapers and crafted interior surfaces exclusively made to order. Drawing has always underpinned my surface pattern designs, and many have references to a time or a place to form engaging narratives. I utilise technologies, such as laser engraving, to create many of my unique designs. The outcomes cross the boundaries between technology and craft to create modern design pieces that embody traditional values yet contemporary aesthetics.

I am an experienced academic and I have lectured Textiles at a range of universities, including The Rotal College of Art, Loughborough, Manchester, Bournemouth, Staffordshire, Bucks New University and Central St Martins and I also provide mentoring for young designers through the Colour in Design Award, for which I am a trustee. Clients include Swoon Editions, Panasonic Europe, Farrow & Ball, Heal’s and Anthropologie (US), among others, as well as numerous private clients. I exhibit and sell my work internationally including in Europe and the US. 

I am also a proud brother of the Artworkers’ Guild, London, which was founded by William Morris.

teacher.aboutMe: My name is Fanny and I am a passionate, self taught fiber artist and fiber supplier from Sweden, known as Createaholic on Instagram which is also the name of my company. Since 2014 when I first discovered macramé my life has revolved around ropes, knots and all things fiber. Createaholic has been my full time job since 2017 and I have written two bestselling books about macramé. Together they have been translated into 12 languages and sold over 200.000 copies worldwide. In recent years, I have sought to challenge myself to learn more techniques and have therefore focused a lot on the art of weaving. This in turn opened up the world of macraweaving - the combination of macramé and weaving - and since then a lot of my work has revolved around this intriguing technique. With Domestika I hope to inspire more people to discover this wonderful artform!

teacher.aboutMe:
Hola! I'm Santiago Avila, a motion and graphic designer from Argentina, currently based in London. 

I have been working in motion graphics and animation for over 10+ years, both as part of in-house teams and as a freelancer. I have contributed to projects that range from film, broadcast, music live visuals, and digital content. This has given me the opportunity to experiment with 2D and 3D animation for both graphic and character-driven storytelling.

Developing hybrid techniques and approaches is what I enjoy the most when working on a project. I believe blending traditional 2D mindsets with fully-digital tools and executions is a sweet spot to generate unique visual languages. In a social media landscape where trends tend to quickly come and go, taking the time to find a design and animation style that's tailored to a project will make it more memorable and long-lasting.

I have worked for clients such as Nike, MTV, FOX, Spotify, Condé Nast, Netflix and BFI. I have also worked for artists like Kylie Minogue, Disclosure, London Grammar and Anne-Marie.
