teacher.aboutMe:
I like to play. That is the best reason I know for drawing anything at all; to play. I've been quite serious about it since I was shouting at the other kids for not playing properly as we ran around in kindergarten, and nothing much has changed since then, except the tools have become fancier and the rules have become a lot more intricate.

I play by making worlds, and stories, and characters and things, and my toys are pens and stylus, procreate and imagination. My game consists of weaving worlds that work, like our own, but different, and letting the characters and creatures make magic by bringing the world to life, making little stories of their own. It is the most fun I know how to have, and I would love to share it if you want to play along.

Soy diseñador de producto, experto en diseño multimodal y en interfaces conversacionales. A pesar de ser un gran aficionado a las palabras y a construir historias con ellas, empecé a trabajar como diseñador visual en 2010. En 2015 descubrí los chatbots y entendí que podía juntar los dos mundos y que se podía diseñar con las palabras.

Durante varios años lideré los proyectos de diseño conversacional en BBVA Next, inventado y probando nuevos casos de uso y aprendiendo cómo aplicar mis conocimientos en diseño de interfaz gráfica a este nuevo soporte. Fueron años muy emocionantes donde no había casi nada escrito y donde todo se podía intentar.

En 2018 decidí profundizar más en las interacciones conversacionales y entré a formar parte del equipo de Amazon Alexa para Francia, Italia y España, ayudando a empresas externas a crear Skills para Alexa. En 2020 acepté un nuevo reto y desde entonces trabajo en el equipo de Alexa Auto, inventando el futuro de las experiencias multimodales en el coche.

También puedes leer mis artículos en mi página jesusmartin.eu

teacher.aboutMe:
Mi chiamo Silvia Molinari e sono un’artista italiana.
Ho una particolare attrazione per i soggetti naturalistici, animali e piante selvatiche che incontro nella campagna vicino a casa e che ritraggo principalmente ad acquerello, la mia tecnica prediletta.

Faccio parte degli artisti della galleria Salamon Fine Art di Milano e  JGO Gallery, Park City, Utah.
Ho esposto alla Biennale di Venezia nella sede regionale dell’Emilia-Romagna, all’Affordable Art Fair di New York, a Tokyo con la galleria Ginza 1 Chome.

Ho realizzato opere per LIPU Onlus e per la rivista Gardenia, illustrato libri per l’infanzia con Edizioni Corsare e Topipittori.
Sono ambassador di Borciani e Bonazzi, pennellificio con cui ho realizzato un’innovativa linea di strumenti.

Mi dedico alla didattica guidando seminari d’acquerello.


*EN*
My name's Silvia Molinari and I'am an Italian painter.
Whether in nature or on a sheet of paper, open spaces have forever drawn my attention, on account of the lifeforms that inhabit them and the confused freedom in which they do so, and for the change they bring. I almost always approach them in watercolour.

My diploma is in Decorative Techniques from the Toschi di Parma Art Institute. My works feature in the permanent collection at the Galleria Salamon Fine Art in Milan and JGO Gallery in Park City, Utah.
I have exhibited in solo and group exhibitions, at the Venice Biennale, and at the Affordable Art Fair in New York and Milan.

I lead courses and workshops, and I collaborate with illustration magazines, and profit and non-profit brands.

teacher.aboutMe:
Viaggiatrice, sognatrice, idealista. Fin da piccola coltivo la passione per la lettura, la scrittura e viaggiare. 

Nel 2008 mi trasferisco a Londra per uno stage che poi diventa un contratto a tempo indeterminato in una delle 5 più grandi agenzie di executive search. Per circa un decennio ho lavorato come consulente nell'ambito delle risorse umane e come management consultant, prima di approdare in una grande multinazionale americana in qualità di Senior Project Manager Europa. 


Dopo aver raggiunto tutti i miei obiettivi professionali, nel 2015 decido di prendere un periodo per viaggiare. Lascio il mio lavoro e parto per un sabbatico che doveva durare 6 mesi, ma è durato infatti 2 anni. Durante questa incredibile avventura mi accorgo che il mio lavoro, un ibrido tra ciò che facevo in azienda e ciò che mi appassionava (il marketing e la scrittura) può essere svolto da ovunque pertanto, computer in spalla, inizio ad avere i miei clienti freelance nell'ambito SEO e strategic planning. 

Alla fine del 2015, da Sydney, avvio la mia prima attività di consulenza focalizzata proprio nell'offrire le mie competenze in ambito business e marketing a freelance e piccoli imprenditori che volevano migliorare la loro performance. Il Business Model Canvas è il mio strumento base per aiutarli a strutturare al meglio una nuova attività o a rivoluzionarla nel miglior modo possibile. Ad oggi, tramite "The Human Collective" ho aiutato clienti da tutto il mondo a lanciare, migliorare, scalare il loro business online con il mio approccio "misto". 

Nel 2017, curiosa di mettere in pratica tutto ciò che facevo per i miei clienti, decido di  avviare una mia seconda attività: un brand ed e-commerce di cartoleria sostenibile, Inchiostro and Paper. Nominata miglior cartoleria online  nel 2020, ad oggi conta oltre 30 rivenditori e migliaia di clienti affezionati in tutto il mondo. La missione di Inchiostro and Paper é quella di cambiare il mondo, un giorno alla volta, grazie alla scrittura, alla crescita personale e prendendosi cura del nostro pianeta.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hola! My name is Santiago Celio Cioli, but everyone knows me as Santo Cielo (kind of an anagram with my name).
In my childhood, I remember being surrounded by fabrics, threads, and dressmakers. For many years, my mother owned a haberdashery in the little town where I was born, and I tend to think this had an influence on my later decision to study Industrial Design in Textiles.
I started learning embroidery in 2015 while I was doing a joint degree thesis about hand embroidery and national identity: We created an interview/workshop system where embroiderers, in this case, women of various ages, would tell us stories relating to their craft, teaching us one or two stitches at the same time. Thanks to them, I was able to discover and learn beautiful techniques.
Nowadays, I focus mostly on portraits of animals and humans using the thread painting technique. Many portraits are created in response to customer requests I receive through Instagram and my website; through family photos, I get involved in people’s lives to create a memory they can treasure for years to come.
I love to impart my passion and skills to others because I find beauty in the verbal and mimetic transmission of this knowledge, just as those women did for me.

También doy charlas y conferencias sobre literatura y el fomento de la lectoescritura. 

Soy uno de los socios fundadores de Atrapavientos, una organización sin ánimo de lucro que persigue el desarrollo, la investigación y la difusión de toda clase de actividades relacionadas con la literatura infantil y juvenil. Pero, sobre todo, somos especialistas en crear campañas de fomento a la lectoescritura. Lo que más me gusta es que la gente joven lea y escriba sus propias historias. También somos Premio Nacional de Fomento de la Lectura concedido por el Ministerio de Cultura y Deporte de España.

Bastante a menudo tropiezo con mi voz creativa. A lo mejor a ti también te pasa. Yo todavía no me he acostumbrado a escucharla a todas horas. Cosas mías.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy guionista, escritora y redactora creativa. Lo que vendría siendo una cuentacuentos profesional, vamos. Me fascina contar historias. Eso es lo quería hacer con mi vida y ¡es justo lo que estoy haciendo! Con los años, me he especializado en la escritura de ficciones sonoras. Y ya llevo más de siete años creando historias en audio, imaginando ambientes sonoros, explosiones, persecuciones..., pero también escuchando cómo hablan mis personajes. Porque puedo hacer que estos cobren vida. ¡Es fantástico escucharlos crecer y evolucionar a mi lado!

Soy la autora de “Ladrones de memoria” (que cuenta ya con dos temporadas) y “Operación Reset” para Storytel, de "La vecina indiscreta", "Espero tu email" y "Ni en tu casa, ni en la mía" para Podimo y la creadora y productora de "Mai no ho sabreu" ("Nunca lo sabréis"), un podcast de ficción que cuenta con el soporte del Departamento de Cultura.

También trabajo para grandes y pequeñas marcas comerciales y editoriales; algo que trato de compaginar con la investigación de nuevas narrativas y formatos interactivos y la escritura de guiones de cine. En resumen: siempre que haya una buena historia que contar, allí me encontrarás, buscando la mejor forma de plasmarla.

teacher.aboutMe:
Me llamo Alina Alvarez Etchegaray y soy una publicista mexicana. He trabajado en proyectos y agencias con diferentes enfoques, desde publicidad tradicional, como televisión, out of home y radio, hasta eventos, activaciones y, sobre todo, publicidad digital. Hoy trabajo como directora de innovación en una agencia digital. 

En mi tiempo en la industria, he formado parte de equipos a cargo de algunas de las marcas más reconocidas del mundo como Samsung, Luuna, Heineken, Tecate, Adidas, Doritos, MINI, OXXO, Novartis, Oreo, Ritz, Moët Chandon, 7up, Aspirina y Salesforce. He sido reconocida con algunos premios de la industria como el ASPID y el IAB Mixx y he participado como jurado en los premios Círculo de Oro, del Círculo de Creativos de México y Young Lions el festival más importante de publicidad para jóvenes, que se lleva a cabo en más de 20 países alrededor del mundo.  

Hace un año, creé la cuenta @directora_creativa en Instagram, que buscaba ser un punto de acceso para los que quieren ser publicistas y aún no entendían cómo hacerlo. Con un enfoque educativo, compartí algunas pautas e ideas que he cultivado en este tiempo. La comunidad publicitaria recibió muy bien la cuenta, lo que me ha llevado a dar conferencias con diferentes universidades y empresas de todo México.

teacher.aboutMe:
¡Hola! Soy Carla y vivo en Buenos Aires, Argentina.
Amo las muñecas. Vestirlas. Peinarlas. Siempre me han gustado y todavía las compro para mí, ¡aunque tengo cuarenta y dos años! Aprender a tejer a crochet y poder hacerlas yo misma ha sido un punto de inflexión en mi vida. Siempre me ha gustado lo craft (tuve mis épocas en las que me hacía mis propios collares y pulseras), pero nada me ha dado la alegría y la satisfacción de tejer a crochet. Es mi mejor terapia posible.

Y también es mi poder secreto. Porque en el mundo real, aquel habitado por humanos, soy periodista y productora de un programa de televisión sobre Política Nacional y casi nadie en mi lugar de trabajo conoce mi identidad secreta como diseñadora de muñecas. Me encanta ser parte de dos mundos tan diferentes.

En el universo del crochet me conocen como “Amour Fou”, que en francés significa “amor loco”. El nombre surgió cuando tuve que entregar mi primer pedido de muñecas a una juguetería local. Estaba tan enamorada de mis primeras creaciones que me daba pena tener que entregarlas. A mi marido le pareció una ridiculez total y decretó que ese amor que les tenía era “una locura”… Y bueno, esta locura ya está por cumplir 10 años. Ya no vendo las muñecas terminadas sino los patrones de mis diseños a través de mi tienda ETSY. Esto me permite tener tiempo para crear muñecos nuevos todo el tiempo. Me pueden seguir por Instagram como @amourfou_crochet.

En 2020, junto a la editorial David & Charles, publiqué mi primer libro: “Crochet Iconic Women”, un compilado de patrones para tejer a 15 mujeres icónicas y extraordinarias que han dado forma a nuestro presente o que actualmente están construyendo nuestro futuro. A través del crochet me di el gusto de homenajear a todas estas mujeres que para mí representan una fuente inagotable de inspiración. También trabajé con la editorial Thunder Bay para una serie de kits de títeres de dedo de los personajes de Star Wars y las Princesas y Villanos de Disney.

Mi próximo libro estará llegando a medidados de 2022 y es una sorpresa aún!

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm a painter currently living in Los Angeles.  My work is defined by technique in application and dynamic color stories, usually with a focus on organic subjects such as animals or body parts.   

My paintings are layers of independent shapes, stacked with precision to imply light, texture, and form.   Careful color shifts and loud punches of contrasting hues result in harmony and vibration.  Acrylic paint is my preferred medium, and I choose to create work on wooden surfaces, as the smoothness best lends itself to the clean and precise marks that evolve into my visual geometry.  My paintings are designed to exist carefully between mechanical and fluid, representational and abstracted.

 The subjects I choose to paint provide me with an opportunity to find unique ways to present things that are more or less familiar.  I like exploring visual concepts of wetness, softness, and hardness without being too caught up in realism-- using somewhat relatable subject matter, such as rare birds or animal eyes, gives me more freedom to play with technique.  

Though I'm originally from Ohio, I currently live and create in Highland Park, CA.  I've got a rescue rabbit that lives in my studio and watches me paint, and my time outside of work is spent cooking, making cocktails, and exploring the city.

teacher.aboutMe:
I currently live in Phoenix, Arizona.  

However, growing up in Detroit, my blue-collar Dad said many times, “son, I don’t want you to grow up to take a job. I want you to grow up to create a job.”  

After high school, I joined the army and rose to the officer ranks. Later I studied Industrial Design, which included interning in France. Soon after, Ford Motor hired me as a concept car designer.  

In 1995, I learned at a public lecture for the very first time that the ghetto is and continues to be because of brain drain. 

That revelation moved me to suddenly quit Ford and rededicate my life to building a custom design and furniture manufacturing business within the community that produced me. I am a self-taught furniture designer and woodworker.

teacher.aboutMe: Mi chiamo Roberto Perrino e sono un graphic designer e fondatore di Indieground Design, uno studio che crea e progetta risorse e templates di grafica, principalmente basati su Photoshop. Il mio focus è creare risorse di alta qualità, facilmente personalizzabili e riutilizzabili, ottimizzate per coloro che cercano soluzioni pratiche e flessibili nel mercato del design. Nel corso degli anni, ho percorso diverse strade per sfruttare al massimo le potenzialità di Photoshop, che non solo rimane il mio strumento principale di lavoro, ma è diventato una vera e propria passione. Ogni volta che realizzo un nuovo progetto, cerco di farlo in uno stile “nostalgico”, un tributo alla mia generazione e al vibrante universo della cultura pop che ha segnato la mia crescita. Nonostante per alcuni tipi di progetto alcune applicazioni come Illustrator e InDesign potrebbero essere più appropriate, io credo fermamente nella versatilità e completezza di Photoshop. Questo software è infatti ricco di funzioni nascoste, rendendolo ideale per soddisfare qualsiasi esigenza di design. Con il mio corso, intendo dimostrare che Photoshop può essere utilizzato efficacemente per una vasta gamma di progetti di design, facendone un punto di forza per ogni graphic designer.

Melissa Galbraith is the fiber artist behind MCreativeJ. She was born and raised in the desert of Washington state, where her mother instilled a love of making things by hand at an early age. Drawing on her love of nature, Melissa creates whimsical and modern embroidery patterns and kits. She loves sharing how anyone can embroider with her embroidery kits, patterns, and virtual workshops.

​Melissa was reintroduced to hand embroidery after finding her desk job monotonous and needing a creative outlet. She loves that embroidery allows her to play with texture and color and is also a portable craft. Along the way, many crafty minded makers also wanted to learn how to embroider too but were daunted by where to start. So Melissa began to share her embroidery knowledge.

Melissa's embroidery kits and patterns make it easy to learn a new craft for makers of all skill levels. She loves seeing makers fall in love with the needle arts and seeing that magical ah-ha moment of learning something new.

teacher.aboutMe:
I am a 3D artist based in London who specialises in Adobe Suite, Cinema4D, Marvelous Designer/Clo3D, and Substance Painter. My artistic practice centres around building garments and the world in which they live whilst exploring and expressing my British Chinese identity where I fuse modern techniques with traditional Chinese elements.. My art provides integration, both physical and in the metaverse, through her NFT artworks and AR applications. I have worked with clients such Vogue Singapore, Highsnobiety, Glenfiddich, Jo Malone, Xbox and Paco Rabanne; and has been featured in VICE, Nylon Magazine and Hype Beast.

Across my artworks, I strive for a balanced composition imbued with vibrant colours. Usually I initially sketch the garment digitally, creating a raw outline for the final artwork. Next, I bring the art to life by transforming the artwork from 2D to a three-dimensional object. Upon completing the 3D modelling and motion graphics, I then layer additional textures and patterns which provide deeper meaning and complexity to the piece. Finally, I finish the process by editing the environment’s settings.

teacher.aboutMe:
Everything I do is underpinned by a simple but powerful idea: Positive Creativity. From the creative process to the final output, I believe design can bring people together, create sustainable choices and foster wellbeing.

I set up Studio Emmi in 2005 to partner with clients and creatives who want to make a positive contribution to society and planet.

Whether it’s engaging audiences through purpose-led brand identities, mentorship for creative wellbeing or making engaging spaces, I work with people to find the very best solutions through design.

You can’t just arrive at a solution. In design and in life. So I like to ask questions, to listen, pause for reflection. It’s important to stay curious, to find the unusual in the usual. Take a second look. Think again.
Problems hold the key to their own solution if we bring our awareness to them.

I am author of the book Common Interest: Documents, and have contributed to industry magazines on topics ranging from typography to women in design. I regularly lecture on design topics at various universities based in the UK and beyond.

I also give talks and workshops about my personal design journey and CREATIVE ECOSYSTEM, guiding creatives in their wellbeing and careers.

Born in Finland, I’m a strong advocate for a balanced life full of curiosity, growth and wonder. I studied graphic design in the UK at the University of Brighton. In 2001 I moved to northern Italy to work at Fabrica, Benetton Group’s prestigious communication research studio for young designers. I then worked at Karlssonwilker in New York and Futerra sustainability agency as their UK Creative Director. I now run Studio Emmi, based in London.

Let’s create together.

teacher.aboutMe:
Ricardo Laganaro, é considerado um dos diretores de realidade virtual mais inovadores do mundo. Sua última peça, A Linha, recebeu vários prêmios em todo o mundo, incluindo “Best VR Experience” no Festival de Cinema de Veneza e um Primetime Emmy® Award por Inovação Excepcional em Programação Interativa.

Há 10 anos na indústria de XR, Ricardo criou peças icônicas como o renomado documentário em VR “Step to the Line”, produzido pela Oculus; e "Cosmos", uma projeção full-dome para o Museu do Amanhã no Rio, produzida pela O2 Filmes. Seus projetos foram selecionados por mais de 50 festivais ao redor do mundo, como Venice, Emmy, Tribeca, FoST, Cannes XR e Raindance, entre outros.

Laganaro também é sócio e Chief StoryTelling Officer, da ARVORE Experiências Imersivas, maior estúdio de conteúdo imersivo do Brasil, com mais de 60 colaboradores no país e braços nos EUA e Europa. Além de dirigir seus próprios projetos no estúdio, Ricardo também é o Head of Content ajudando a descobrir uma estrutura criativa adequada para desenvolver todos os projetos interativos no estúdio, como a franquia de jogos Pixel Ripped, YUKI e outros.

Além de já ter palestrado em eventos como SXSW, CCXP,  Tribeca, Mediamorfosis, Pixel Show, Mostra de Veneza, entre outros; pela inovação no seu trabalho de contador de histórias, ele foi convidado a falar na “Global People’s Summit” durante a Assembleia Geral da ONU de 2017.

teacher.aboutMe:
Julien Gachadoat has been exploring generative drawing for many years, creating unique art with algorithms. He works with the emergence of abstract form, combining monochrome, geometric shapes, playing with repetition and using random operations to generate an element of surprise.

Developing his own tools of creation based on simple graphic rules, Julien Gachadoat uses the computer - “this unique performer”  (Vera Molnar) - to explore the formal possibilities that ensue.  It is through the process of printing these unique pieces, using a plotter, that he creates a link between text and code.
“To leave a unique mark, aesthetically palpable, that is not in defiance, but rather in aid of the digital.” This is the philosophy of the artist from Bordeaux, who has developed an international following through social media. He brings together on paper the computer and the pencil, the rigour of code and the poetry of art.

He has been exhibiting his work in Bordeaux (Galerie Métavilla) in Paris (Galerie Binôme), in Bayonne (DIDAM, Contemporary Art Space), in Berlin and in Venezia (Biennale).

Constantly looking to work with others and in new ways, he has also done a series of silkscreen prints with the Atelier SereJoint in Rochelle as well as drawings with an industrial robot in collaboration with studio AATB Marseille. 

In 2021 he started work in the field of crypto-art, with the desire for make moving images as well as a means to experiment, explore new areas and promote his unique works. In May 2021, he is selected by the platform ArtBlocks, presenting his first project with them in July of the same year. His work was exhibited in November 2021 at the online Feral File —GRAPH exhibition curated by Casey Reas.

Julien grew up in the 90s with the avant garde demo-scene, making visuals with code. Ever since, programming languages have been his creative tool. He was the co-founder of the interactive digital art studio 2Roqs with Michaël Zancan, working on numerous interactive installations.  He has been teaching « creative coding » for more than 15 years in schools in France and abroad.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy Eva Sánchez y soy UX/UI digital designer asentada en Barcelona. Empecé mi trayectoria formándome en diseño gráfico en Tenerife y trabajando en publicidad. Poco tiempo después me trasladé a Madrid donde trabajé y estudié, siendo aquí donde empezó mi pasión en el diseño web. En 2019, llegué a Barcelona para empezar a ejercer  exclusivamente como diseñadora digital, trabajando en reconocidos estudios de diseño como Vasava y Toormix. 

Como persona creativa e inquieta, empecé a compartir mis exploraciones y conceptos en mis redes sociales así como crear mi web portfolio, la misma que me permitió ganar varios méritos, entre ellos un Honorable Mention y ser parte del jurado en Awwards, una comunidad de creativos internacional del ámbito digital. 

A partir de aquí mi trabajo comenzó a ser reconocido y empecé a colaborar con otros estudios independientes como Fuego Camina Conmigo, Ophion, Rebeka Arce Studio o Réplica Studio, entre otros. Asimismo, actualmente trabajo en Jam3, una agencia internacional dedicada en exclusiva al diseño enfocado en la experiencia e innovación digital.

teacher.aboutMe:
Camille Baudelaire, fondatrice et directrice de création du studio, œuvre depuis plus de 10 ans à l’intersection du design graphique, de l’innovation, de la 3D et du design d’espace. Elle a toujours collaboré en tant qu'indépendante avec des organismes allant des musées aux grandes entreprises, mais aussi auprès d'artistes, commissaires, designers et architectes de renom. Elle réalise des projets allant de l'objet imprimé (édition, identité...) au graphisme déployé dans l'espace (scénographie, signalétique, design couleur et matière), en passant par les médias interactifs (sites internet, installations protéiformes...). Consciente de la responsabilité du designer, Camille Baudelaire propose une démarche engagée, valorise la justesse du sens et l’éthique dans ses propositions. 

Diplômée de l’école Estienne, de l’ESAA Duperré et de l’ENSAD, Camille s'investit notamment afin que la proportion de femmes auteures reconnues et de femmes fondatrices de studio s'aligne avec celle des femmes en école d'Art. Elle agit dans son propre studio, auprès de l'association Contemporaines, ainsi qu'en école par le biais de workshops.

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm an award-winning illustrator/educator/entrepreneur who was trained as a photographer, and have worked professionally as an advertising art director, publications designer and art director;  and VP/creative director.

I'm the founding director of the MFA in Illustration Practice at the Maryland Institute College of Art [MICA] where I teach graduate students; co-director of Dolphin Press & Print at MICA where we develop print and book edition projects with noted artists; and proprietor of Whitney Sherman Illustration and of Pbody Dsign, a limited edition homewares studio that expands the idea of how illustration is used today.

My experience also includes being co-editor and contributing writer of the History of Illustration, the first book of its kind to examine cultural, social and technical topics on illustration practice across the globe; and author/writer of Playing with Sketches, a book of 50 exercises in a variety of formats to expand the idea of drawing practice in a variety of disciplines. 

I've exhibited my work in Japan, Germany, Mexico, China and the US in such varying places as the Norman Rockwell Museum, Giant Robot and Gallery Nucleus. Several of my illustrations are in the Collection of the Library of Congress.

I live in an Arts & Crafts bungalow in Baltimore with my husband Paul and cat Shelby.

teacher.aboutMe:
Desde os 6 anos de idade treina desenhos de observação e a dinâmica das cores. Formou-se em design gráfico e concebeu sua primeira série de obras autorais aos 20 anos, quando começou a estudar artes visuais. Em seus estudos Escañuela entra a fundo nas teorias da arte contemporânea, desenvolvendo uma linha de pesquisa onde passa a usar sua técnica a favor de narrativas conceituais.

Seu trabalho toma como diretriz principal o primor minucioso da técnica hiper-realista à óleo unido às experimentações teóricas sobre a representação anatômica, inserindo-a em novos contextos e lugares. O artista utiliza a representação como um instrumento que converge com a iconografia brasileira para o desenvolvimento de novas narrativas plásticas e conceituais. Ao trabalhar a artesania da técnica junto à temáticas de denúncia, o trabalho converge em possibilidades de fascínio e reflexão que a pintura figurativa ainda desperta nas pessoas, sejam elas entusiastas ou leigas em arte.

Seus trabalhos ganharam notoriedade com uma série de rostos hiper-realistas de grandes dimensões. O artista criou seu próprio estilo no hiper-realismo, dando enfoque no fluxo dos poros, manchas, marcas da passagem do tempo e dando à pintura da pele novos significados e propriedades.

Tensionando os limites entre o micro e o macro e as características dialéticas entre o corpo e seu ambiente, sua obra propõe a concepção do ser humano como espécie e ser social, buscando
as propriedades da pele e do corpo em justaposição à temáticas históricas, iconográficas e cartográficas brasileiras. Para Escañuela o artista precisa estar atento às questões do seu tempo ao investigar a produção de tempos anteriores, analisando as possibilidades de se propor o novo e o disruptivo.

teacher.aboutMe:
POETÓGRAFA / Autora del libro EL OFICIO DE DESVESTIRSE
Fotógrafa, poeta y coleccionista de diarios y cajas de fósforos. Mi forma de crear es completamente transdisciplinar. Creo en los diálogos entre múltiples lenguajes y trabajo desde ese lugar: la mezcla de poesía visual y escrita, video ensayo, performance, fotografía, y por supuesto el diario como hilo conductor para contar historias. 

Estudié Comunicación Audiovisual en la Pontificia Universidad Javeriana (Cali, Colombia). Hice una Maestría en Fotografía Contemporánea y Proyectos Personales en EFTI (Madrid, España). A lo largo de mi trayectoria como fotógrafa y realizadora, he retratado diferentes personalidades en Colombia. 

Como artista y poeta trabajo sobre lo íntimo, lo personal y lo autobiográfico, generando diálogos poéticos en distintos formatos. Diarios, poesía visual y escrita, video ensayo, instalación, fotografía y performance. Esas creaciones desde la intimidad hablan de feminidad, del cuerpo , del espacio que habitan los cuerpos, de sus gestos, del espejo, de la mirada propia y ajena; del tiempo como instante pero también como herencia; del gesto cotidiano, de la rutina de existir en tiempos y espacios virtuales, físicos y emocionales.

¿Plataformas? El papel, las pantallas, la calle, los encuentros, talleres y tertulias que organiza para compartir y crear, desde la sensibilidad, los afectos, lo colectivo y lo poético.

Mi trabajo está basado en la experiencia y el proceso como acto creativo por encima de un resultado final. Las emociones son el hilo conductor de toda mi obra.

Sacha Léopold and François Havegeer have worked together as syndicat since 2012.
      Their cross-disciplinary practice, taking in self-initiated projects as well as design-based commissions, addresses issues of originality, reproduction, and reproducibility in the context of art today, using their expansive knowledge of printing and manufacturing techniques whether designing books, creating visual identities, or curating exhibitions.
      Syndicat has actively collaborated with contemporary artists and art centers to create one-of-a-kind visual identity programs, publications, monographs, and artists’ books, leading in 2015 to the creation of Empire, their own publishing imprint and Revue Faire: a bi-monthly printed graphic design magazine.
      Alongside their design activities, they have curated several exhibitions exploring printing techniques process.

Leonardo Finotti é artista visual e tem sua trajetória estruturada através de dois pilares complementares. Ele empreende, através da fotografia, uma exploração rigorosa da Arquitetura Moderna e uma investigação dos espaços urbanos anônimos ou informais. 

Após se graduar em Arquitetura e concluir uma pós graduação na Bauhaus Foundation, (Dessau, Alemanha) começa sua carreira como fotógrafo em Portugal, onde viveu por seis anos, colaborando com os mais importantes arquitetos portugueses. Inicia então um projeto sistemático de releitura do Modernismo em diferentes continentes, que prossegue quando do seu retorno ao Brasil. Contribui internacionalmente com diferentes arquitetos e publicações,  ao mesmo tempo em que desenvolve diversos projetos pessoais (exposições, publicações) tendo a arquitetura e a cidade  como eixo principal de sua pesquisa visual: Pelada (2014), latinitudes (2015), Rio enquadrado (2016), A Collection of Latin American Modern Architecture (2016), para citar apenas alguns.

Já realizou diversas exposições individuais e coletivas e seu trabalho faz parte de coleções de algumas das mais importantes instituições públicas e privadas, tais como Bauhaus Dessau Foundation (Alemanha), Fundação EDP (Portugal), AzW (Áustria), MOT (Japão), Cité de L'Architecture & du Patrimonie (França), MAR (Brasil). Representou o Brasil em duas Bienais de Arquitetura de Veneza, na X Bienal de Arte do Mercosul e foi premiado na XV Bienal Internacional de Arquitetura de Buenos Aires. 

Em 2008, Finotti foi convidado por Barry Bergdoll, curador-chefe do MoMA-NY, a fazer parte da exposição “Latin America in Construction: Architecture 1955-1980”. O projeto, desenvolvido ao longo de sete anos, reinterpreta visualmente o legado da arquitetura moderna da América Latina. O trabalho além de integrar a exposição, teve 15 obras adquiridas para sua coleção permanente e recebeu um capítulo no catálogo, sob a forma de portfolio.

My name is Briony Machin and I am a mosaic artist based in Lancashire, UK. I have always loved surface pattern and in the past I have worked in ceramics, illustration and printmaking but more recently I started to implement my surface patterns into mosaic. I have never had any sort of formal training for mosaic, instead I have taught myself through experimentation and practice which has led me to create a range of totally unique, modern mosaics which I hope will bring a little bit of joy to peoples homes or gardens. 
 I also love how therapeutic this craft is, hence why I decided to run workshops and create DIY mosaic kits for people to enjoy mosaicing from the comfort of their own home. I want my workshops and online courses to be as much about the mindful process of mosaicing, as it is the finished piece. 
When I am not in my studio, I love to be outside in nature. Either up a mountain, on a beach or exploring botanical gardens in a different city.

Hey! Mein Name ist Elisa Ems-Domenig, ich bin ausgebildete Diplompsychologin und Mama von 5 Kindern. 
Vor Jahren hat mich das Häkelfieber gepackt und es vergeht kaum ein Tag wo ich nicht mit Wolle und Nadel zugange bin. Angefangen als Hobby und um selbstgemachte Kuscheltiere und Puppen für meine Kinder herzustellen, ist es nun viel mehr als das! 

Das Häkeln, vor allem das Häkeln von sogenannten Amigurumis (das sind Figuren mit einem hauptsächlich niedlichen Erscheinungsbild), hat mich komplett in seinen Bann gezogen und eine kreative Leidenschaft in mir geweckt, die mich seitdem nicht mehr loslässt. 

Dies hatte zur Folge, dass sich nun auch hauptberuflich bei mir alles um die kleinen Wollfreunde dreht. 2016 habe ich mich selbstständig gemacht und entwerfe unter meinem eigenen Label namens „Lulu loves the moon“ Amigurumi-Designs, die jeder mithilfe von Download-Dateien, selbst nachhäkeln kann.

Umgeben von Bergen und Wäldern im Süden Österreichs entwerfe ich fortlaufend neue Designs, die hoffentlich viel Freude und Wärme in die Herzen derer bringen, die meine Figuren nachhäkeln wollen.


Hey! My name is Elisa Ems-Domenig, I am a studied psychologist and mom of 5 kids.
Years ago the passion of crocheting hit me and since then hardly a day goes by where I don’t work with yarns and hook. First started as a hobby to create cute toys and dolls, especially for my kids, it soon became much more than this!
Crocheting, especially crocheting amigurumis (these are cute looking figures), is now a big part of my life and I never want to live without again! It gives me space and room to live out my creative streak.
Therefore I started in 2016 to make crocheting to my main job. I started my business called “Lulu loves the moon” and I am designing my own amigurumi creations, which can be purchased internationally so that everybody can crochet them as well.

Surrounded from mountains and forests I live in the south of Austria. Here I find my inspirations so that I can create continuously new designs which hopefully bring much joy and warmth in the hearts of those who want to crochet my creatures.

teacher.aboutMe:
¡Hola! :)

Nosotros somos Lili Cuéllar y Willie Soto, fundadores y diseñadores de pasteles y galletas decoradas en VanilleCouture, un espacio de arte comestible donde impartimos cursos de repostería creativa y desarrollamos nuestra pasión por postres en general.

Lili estudió hotelería y yo, Willie, estudié gastronomía. Durante nuestras prácticas profesionales, ambos encontramos nuestra pasión por la repostería y, unos años más tarde, nos conoceríamos en cursos de decoración de pasteles, nos hicimos amigos, luego novios, y comenzamos a trabajar juntos desde una cochera vendiendo cupcakes. Un año más tarde fundamos VanilleCouture Cakeshop, donde tomábamos pedidos de pasteles y galletas y que nos permitió crear nuestras propias técnicas en pastelería para, posteriormente, comenzar a impartir cursos.

Nuestro perfeccionismo en el trabajo y pasión por la enseñanza nos ha permitido impartir clases en países como Estados Unidos, Colombia, Argentina, Brasil, Costa Rica, y por todo México, además de ser jueces en diversos concursos profesionales de "cake design".

Hemos trabajado para marcas como Netflix, donde creamos todos los retos de pasteles, galletas y postres que ves en Nailed It México temporada 2 y 3; contamos con una colaboración de colorantes con la marca de colorantes más prestigiosa en México llamada ENCO Alimentos, la cual puedes encontrar en países como Estados Unidos, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Panamá y Puerto Rico; también hemos trabajado con marcas como KitchenAid, Amazon, Satin Ice, Tiffany & Co., Larousse Cocina, entre otras.

Es muy gratificante para nosotros poder compartir lo que amamos con muchas personas por medio del contenido en nuestras redes sociales y nuestras clases, las cuales, suelen ser muy solicitadas por el compromiso que el alumno recibe de nuestra parte, y donde les mostramos los procesos reales y sin secretos detrás de cada producto que ven en foto.

¡Gracias por estar aquí y formar parte de nuestra comunidad de vanilos!

Deseamos que disfrutes mucho nuestra clase, y realices los retos etiquetándonos para ayudarnos a conquistar el mundo una galleta a las vez.

¡Nos vemos en clase!

teacher.aboutMe:
I am an architect and picture books illustrator and author, as well as an editorial illustrator. My passion is for introducing kids to architecture and cities via inspiring, memorable picture books. 

As a children’s book illustrator, I work with such major publishers as Candlewick, Schwartz & Wade, G.P. Putnam, Scholastic, Dial, Abrams, and Holiday House. My first author-illustrator book, Building Zaha: The Story of Architect Zaha Hadid, represents my artistic achievement to date.  It received several starred reviews and was selected as Editors’ Pick for Amazon’s Best Non-fiction For Kids. It also won the International Contest ‘Image of the Book’ in the category ‘Best Illustrations for Non-Fiction’. 
The art from my books was selected for the Original Art Show at The New York Society of Illustrators in 2020 and 2021, and Bologna International Book Fair. I have presented at the Society of Children’s Books Writers and Illustrators and received Honors Award at their Illustrator Showcase in 2017, and a Grand Prize in 2019. 

As an editorial illustrator, I work for such clients as The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Boston Globe, The Washington Post, Endless Vacation, Cricket Children’s Magazine, and British Chemistry Education. My first two covers for The New Yorker came out in 2022.

I am inspired by fantasy and possibility that is found in cities, especially those cities that are near and dear to me: New York, St Petersburg, and Venice. All three are situated on the water and are rooted in the interplay between water and urban spaces. What makes capturing them magical for me is using watercolor.  I love to travel and I am never without my paints, sketchbook or Ipad. I paint and sketch everywhere and my travel experiences inspire my ideas and get incorporated in future books.

Alongside his studio practice, Marcelo is also an educator. More than 3,500 students worldwide have enrolled in his online courses, where he shares a structured, method-driven approach to oil painting based on classical principles and refined through years of practice.

teacher.aboutMe:
I’m an artist-illustrator based in London, UK.

Combining bold, expressive brushstrokes and decisively drawn lines, my paintings of nature feel spontaneous and joyful whilst avoiding the sentimentality often associated with wildlife. I'm interested in the way we romanticise the natural world, how we anthropomorphise or uphold elements as desirable whilst disregarding others as a nuisance.

As a teacher, and an artist, I focus on the mistakes. They are fundamental to making creative discoveries and in trying to avoid them we risk stifling ourselves. My courses invite students to draw and paint in unusual and experimental ways, to let go of being in complete control and become open to the unexpected.

I draw mostly in watercolour, ink and coloured pencil, but also experiment with found materials and tools (bubble wrap, emulsion paint, sticks, teabags, squashed blackberries, paintbrush handles…). I often stand to draw and paint on the floor which injects an energy and playfulness to my drawings - the process for me is very physical, almost like a dance.

My work can been found on books, homeware, fabric and fine art prints, and includes clients such as Waterstones, John Lewis, Laura Ashley, Whistlefish, Woodmansterne and Profile Books.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello! 

I'm a designer and Creative Director of Conscious Made design studio, based in Manchester, UK. Specialising in branding and print design with an emphasis on sustainability and wellbeing. I work mainly with clients in the health, culture and tourism sectors, including Material Source, WithPrint and Nordic Muse, amongst others. My process is informed by conscious made decisions that are designed to feed the mind, warm the heart and please the senses. 

All my projects are guided by two basic principles: a need for checking and a need for order. Both have played a dominant role in giving my style its distinct sense of minimalism and symmetry. An approach that seeks to combine functionality with beauty. My mission is to help companies reimagine themselves through effective strategies and distinct identities. This includes everything from naming and logo design, to creating bespoke typography, brand guidelines and 1-to-1 consultancy. 

My focus on print design allows me to reimagine brands in a very personal and tactile way. This includes everything from small-scale to large-scale print such as marketing materials, packaging, stationery, merchandise, exhibitions and interior/exterior signage. My extensive knowledge in print production and circular design helps me to push the possibilities of sustainable print, which also led me to curate my own Paper Lab – a library of 500+ sustainable papers. From this I can effortlessly specify and source best papers to match with your brand, colours and environmental goals. As well as working along side The World Land Trust to calculate the carbon impact of your paper and print production and offset the unavoidable emissions.

My obsession for paper and print extends to talking about it at events such as Glug, PechaKucha Manchester and on the Arrest All Mimics video podcast with Ben Tallon. I've also led discussion panels at TopDrawer in London, for both PaperFEST and RetailFEST. And been on the judging panel for Creative Review's Annual Awards. I have also been featured in exhibitions like Manchester in Mind and Mate Act Now. Plus had the honour of being interviewed for Creative Review, Creative Boom, Computer Arts and ELLE Decor magazine, amongst other publications. I'm also dedicated to supporting independent designers and makers who create well-crafted products with a responsibility for people and the planet. Through Kickstarter I self-published Design Giving magazine, which sold in 15 countries and was featured in Hiut Denim's 'Do One Thing Well’ report.

Then I started working on my portfolio and sending it to a couple of publishers that I want to work with. That’s how my journey started. Since then I’ve done many projects in different countries for kids like children’s books, editorial illustrations, illustrations for kids apparel, workshops. 

Working on different projects has inspired me a lot and helped me to find my own focus in life then I discovered how much I care about sustainable and equal living. I believe in early education about these topics, so I'm always prioritizing these projects. I had a chance to collaborate with some amazing NGOs and publishers like Justdiggit, UNICEF and Mo’s Daughters and we ended up with lovely books to reach many enthusiastic kids. I'm also working on my own books, a couple of books out and one to be published soon.

Besides being an art enthusiast, I’m addicted to yoga, piano sounds & sky as huge source of inspiration for my work.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy Lu, Luchi o Luchinés y esta es la parte más difícil de escribir: la de presentarme. Pero acá vamos. 
Soy Publicista, me especialicé en Redacción Creativa y trabajé durante 10 años en agencias de publicidad en Buenos Aires, México y Miami. Soy militante del cuaderno y del helado de pistacho. 

En mis años en agencia me la pasé escribiendo, pensando y creando campañas para muchas (muchísimas) marcas de todo el mundo que me dieron todo el conocimiento que hoy tengo sobre creatividad, redes, marcas y comunicación.

A fines del 2019 me di cuenta que quería usar todo eso que había aprendido de otra manera, así que decidí renunciar al trabajo en oficina, me tiré de clavado y empecé mi camino freelance. 
Entre otras cosas que hice luego de renunciar, tengo grandes hits como: 
- Me animé a publicar contenido en mi cuenta personal (con mucho miedo, pero lo logré) 
- Escribí dos ebooks sobre redacción creativa y contenido en redes.
- Creé 3 talleres por los que pasaron más de 500 personas. 
- Di charlas
- Le gané a mi síndrome del impostor y trabajo todos los días para seguir venciéndolo e inspirando a otras personas a que se animen a usar su creatividad para alcanzar eso que quieren :)

teacher.aboutMe: Nací y crecí en Bogotá. Desde muy pequeña supe que las artes y el diseño eran mi pasión. Toda mi infancia y adolescencia dibujé casi que compulsivamente. Estudié diseño gráfico y luego me fui a Barcelona a la Escuela Elisava para estudiar una Maestría en Estrategia y diseño de identidad corporativa. Estuve viviendo en Barcelona durante 6 años y esa experiencia cambió mi mundo pues tuve acceso a escenarios de diseño muy interesantes e importantes de diseño europeo. En 2015 empecé mi propio estudio en Bogotá; Manta Raya ha sido mi proyecto profesional y gracias a él, he podido crear equipo con diferentes personas talentosísimas que han aportado valor a cada cliente y al estudio mismo. Hemos visto marcas crecer y exceder sus metas y muchos de ellos son ahora no solo clientes sino amigos. El diseño sigue siendo mi inspiración y gran pasión. Me interesa el diseño inteligente, intuitivo, que responda a las necesidades específicas del cliente y su público, el diseño sostenible que aporte para crear un mundo mejor y una comunicación clara, alegre y respetuosa.

teacher.aboutMe:
Nos enfocamos en el tratamiento tipográfico a través del diseño de identidad visual de marca, así como proyectos de refinamientos de logotipos, fuentes a medida y énfasis en signos numéricos.

Nuestros proyectos tipográficos han sido premiados por el LAD Fest, la Bienal Iberoamericana de Diseño BID, La Octava bienal de tipografía Tipos Latinos y el Communication Arts 2020. Sus fuentes han sido expuestas en espacios académicos como la Universidad de Artes de Berlín y la Universidad Católica de Chile.
 
El estudio los fundamos en Bogotá a finales del 2016, somos Seb de la Hoz, MA en diseño tipográfico de la Universidad de Reading, UK. y Jason Guzmán, diseñador gráfico y diseñador de tipos autodidacta. Como parte del funcionamiento, el estudio hemos generado espacios de discusión con otros profesionales en tipografía y estudiantes para consolidar un nuevo punto de vista frente al diseño de tipografías en Latinoamérica y el Caribe.

teacher.aboutMe:
Sandy or Sand to his friends and family is a bespoke furniture designer-maker based in Beckenham, SE London. 

Previous to setting up Sand Buchanan , Sandy had a 10 year career in the Oil & Gas E&P sector working around the world as a Geoscientist. He holds a BSc and MSc in Geoscience.

After several redundancies, a general dislike for big corporate politics and a growing unease about what the sector was doing Sandy turned to making and craft in the pursuit of meaningful work.

His work exclusively uses fallen British grown timber from as local to his workshop as possible. With this emphasis on sustainability Sandy's work celebrates natural imperfections to reconnect clients with the natural properties that make timber so unique.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello! I am a multidisciplinary Architectural Designer that works at the intersection of mixed media and architecture.
Since graduating, I lived in Beirut and worked with various international architecture firms such as Atelier des Architectes Associes and Bernard Khoury Architects. 

I moved to London 8 years ago and have developed further my career by working with Zaha Hadid Architects as a Lead Architectural Designer for the past four years. 

I have recently opened my first multidisciplinary design studio, where my generative design agenda is highly influenced by art, geology, media, cinema, and music.

I also have taught generative art and design at various institutes, such as UCL the Bartlett School Of Architecture, BPro program, DesignMorphine and Middle East Architecture Lab since 2020 to name a few.

My work has been exhibited worldwide in international exhibitions such as Galerie Fractal in Paris and the Venice Biennale.

teacher.aboutMe:
HELLO DESIGN THINKERS! 
My name is Lisa, and I’m an innovation consultant, design thinker, and workshopper (also known as a facilitator). 
I run innovation and Design Thinking workshops to help teams unlock their superpowers, solve business problems, make decisions, and design better products, faster. 

I am based in Vienna, Austria – but I run remote innovation workshops for corporates and startups all over the world, and lead international businesses like Ikea, Novartis, Usersnap and Talent Garden through collaborative design processes. 

After studying design and working as a designer for 15 years – I felt the pain of being a designer, stuck in endless feedback loops and projects involving too many stakeholders, and feeling I had little impact to drive my projects to success like I’ve envisioned. 

So, 5 years ago - I quit. I started my own innovation business, and moved away from design execution towards design leadership – using Design Thinking as my toolbox and Innovation workshops as my method. 

Today, I am ready to teach you what I know, so it doesn’t take you years but rather a couple of days to implement Design Thinking. My hands-on, battle-tested Design Thinking process is designed to save you valuable time, resources, money and pain. I will show you how to lead, co-create and drive efficient and successful design projects from start to finish, so you can design better products, faster - together with your clients and teams, just like me. 

I’m excited to show you how to fast-track your design process using a human-centered Design Thinking approach, and encourage you to fully step into your creative leadership. 

Are you ready to level up and stand out as a designer? Let’s go! :D

teacher.aboutMe: George Kroustallis is a London-based photographer and director, and founder of Minorstep. His practice is centred on product, still life, beauty and automotive image-making, with portraiture, film, CGI and mixed media forming part of the same visual language. Across still and moving work, he builds precise visual worlds through sculptural light, material sensitivity, bold perspective and close control of colour, texture and form. George works across commissioned campaigns, editorial projects and self-initiated research. He leads projects from concept and image direction through production and post-production, bringing in specialist collaborators where the work demands it. The result balances experimentation and physical tactility with clarity for brands. Selected clients and collaborators include Lancôme, Monster Energy, Lucid Motors, Hypebeast, Google, Adobe, Reebok, Polestar and Burberry. Based in London, working internationally.

teacher.aboutMe: I am a watercolour artist and illustrator specialising in natural history artworks and botanical illustrations. Having graduated in Illustration from the University of Brighton I am now living and working in Northern Ireland. My work resides predominately in the natural world as it is an endless source of inspiration to me. I seek to highlight the importance of biodiversity and to explore the relationship that humankind holds with the rest of nature. I hope for my work to bring about a sense of wonder and awe in our living world and its intricacies. My work draws influence from traditional biological illustrations but I seek to bring a contemporary approach to this way of working by nodding to fantasy, surreal realms and contemporary design.

teacher.aboutMe:
Meu nome é Hugo Santarem, sou fotógrafo e criador que desenvolve projetos para cinema, documentários, publicidade, projetos editorais e artísticos.

Sou o criador e autor do projeto original do longa-metragem Pureza, que fiz em 2006. Também trabalhei por muitos anos como criativo e diretor de arte em agências de publicidade e fiz fotografia still de cinema.

Como eu vim de uma formação publicitária, o caminho natural para mim foi trabalhar em projetos mais comerciais, mas com o tempo vi que essa não era a razão que havia me motivado a ser artista e comunicador, e depois de muito tempo voltei à produzir trabalhos autorais que refletissem minhas idéias.
 
Meus projetos ganharam reconhecimento em festivais e prêmios no Brasil, NY, Londres, EAU, e foram compartilhados em plataformas como Lürzer's Archive, Communication Arts, Abduzeedo, FUBIZ, My Modern MET, Al Jazeera, G1, Update or Die, Fotografe Melhor, entre outros.

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm an illustrator, painter, teacher, and urban sketcher originally from the Washington, DC area, but I've lived in Seattle since 2017. I hold a BFA in Communication Arts from Virginia Commonwealth University and work as a freelance artist and teacher. My clients include Hilton hotels, Penguin Random House, Kroger, the Seattle Times, VICE, and of course Domestika! My work captures realistic subjects and imbues them with significance and character, and drawing from life is the heart of my practice.

I love using mixed media and experimenting with a lot of different materials, but I most often use my good old watercolors and ink pens. My favorite thing to do is travel with my sketchbook and wander around in new cities, and also ride my scooter in rural areas and explore them.

Other than sketching, some of my hobbies are bouldering, hiking, watching & appreciating animated movies and TV shows, mending/sewing, and sipping a good americano on a rainy day.

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm a 3D/2D artist From BC, Canada! Ive worked in the animation industry for 8 years and games for 2 years and now have transitioned to a fulltime freelance career. During those first ~10 years, I've also freelanced for big clients like Google, Wizards of the Coast, Royal Canadian mint, and a long line of small indie studios! My freelance work mostly focuses on creating illustrations for clients such as Art for Magic the Gathering card art, Designs for collectable coins printed onto real gold/silver! I also had the pleasure of creating art for 3 board games now, even including the soon to be released DnD boardgame!

 I like to focus on making epic Sci Fi and Fantasy landscapes using different styles and workflows. I tend to float between a few quite different styles! My main stay lately has been using Arnold renderer creating bright vibrant scenes, which I cover in the course. I also like to use Octane Render to create realistic scenes focusing on nature landscapes, which tend to be much darker and moodier. And lastly, I love to paint using photoshop! mimicking that oil painterly look with different brushes and textures.

teacher.aboutMe:
Cursa estudios de diseño gráfico en la escuela Elisava y a partir de 1988 ejerce de profesor en la misma escuela.

Su trabajo profesional se centra en el diseño de revistas, portadas de libro, imagen corporativa y ilustración. Ha trabajado para diversas entidades y empresas internacionales y nacionales entre las que destacan: Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona, Diputació de Barcelona, Ajuntament de Barcelona, Fundación Caixa Catalunya, Fundación “la Caixa”, Generalitat de Catalunya, Grup 62, Grupo Planeta, Grupo Z, La Vanguardia, Museu d’Art Contemporani de Barcelona MACBA, Random House, The Boston Phoenix, RBA, Sala Beckett, Sàpiens, The Chicago Reader, Universitat Oberta de Catalunya, The New York Times, IESE, Casals, Global Rhythm, Museu Picasso.

En colaboración con Marcus Villaça ha desarrollado diversos proyectos editoriales como el rediseño de los periódicos Chicago Reader y Boston Phoenix.

En 1991 forma con otros diseñadores el grupo tipográfico Type-Ø-Tones que desarrolla fuentes distribuidas por FontShop (Berlín).

Desde hace dos años lleva el blog visual Weekly Garden Thoughts.

Desde septiembre de 2005 a abril de 2009 fue presidente de la Asociación de Directores de Arte y Diseñadores Gráficos ADG-FAD y posteriormente fue durante dos años miembro de la junta directiva del FAD. Sigue vinculado a la entidad organizando cursos para profesionales.

Es autor de diversos artículos sobre diseño y del libro Veintidós consejos sobre tipografía (que algunos diseñadores jamás revelarán) y veintidós cosas que nunca debes hacer con las letras (que algunos tipógrafos nunca te dirán) publicado por Actar. En 2012 publicó con la editorial Gustavo Gili Pensar con imágenes.


Actualmente es director del Máster de Tipografía Avanzada de la escuela Eina, en associación con la Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona. También es profesor invitado en el Máster en Dirección de Arte en Publicidad de la Universitat Ramon Llull (Barcelona), del Máster en Diseño y Dirección de Arte y del Máster en Diseño Publicitario y Comunicación Elisava (Barcelona) y profesor principal del Master Course of Typography en la Lapland University (Finlandia).

Ha dado diversas clases y talleres de tipografía, edición digital y semiología aplicada en la Universidad de Chile, la Universidad Diego Portales (Chile), la Universidade do Porto (Portugal) y la Universidad Iberoamericana de México.

En octubre de 2009 recibió el Premio Nacional de Cultura en el apartado de diseño que otorga la Generalitat de Catalunya.

Ha recibido también diversos premios profesionales ente los que destacan algunos Laus, ED Awards, D&AD y los prenios Malofiej de infografía.

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy fotógrafo y retocador profesional. Estoy certificado por Adobe como Experto en Adobe Photoshop y Adobe Photoshop Lightroom. Soy coordinador del área de postproducción en la escuela La Máquina de Madrid y llevo más de 7 años trabajando como profesor de edición y retoque fotográfico. Mi trabajo se ha publicado en periódicos como el País o el Mundo, revistas como National Geographic o Digital Camera y mi última publicación es el libro “Domina el retoque con Photoshop” que ya va por la segunda edición y la tercera está a punto de salir.

Mi especialidad es el reportaje de viajes y street photography. He obtenido más de 40 galardones en certámenes internacionales como los Sony World Photography Awards (UK), los Premios IPA (USA), Prix de la Photographie (Francia), International Loupe Awards (Australia), Black & White Spyder Awards (USA), Siena International Photo Awards (Italia), International Color Awards (USA), National Geographic España, Eurostars Madrid Tower, entre otros.

Mi obra ha sido expuesta en numerosas galerías nacionales e internacionales, entre las que destaca la Somerset House de Londres.

teacher.aboutMe: Tener un padre lector y una madre que es una gran narradora de historias familiares sin duda influyó en mi decisión de ser escritora. El cine se coló en mi vida gracias a los fines de semana en los que rentábamos todo tipo de películas: desde romance hasta horror. Estudié psicología pero no ejerzo como terapeuta: todo lo que aprendí en la carrera lo aprovecho para desarrollar personajes y en mi labor como maestra. Doy clases de creación y análisis de personajes para realizadores de medios audiovisuales en la Universidad de Medios Audiovisuales (CAAV), donde también asesoro guiones de mis alumnos. Desde hace siete años, imparto talleres dedicados a la formación de nuevos cuentistas y novelistas. Gané un premio nacional de cuento y otro de novela. Hasta ahora he publicado tres libros de cuento y dos novelas, además de haber participado en varias antologías. Hace un par de años fundé,  junto con Ada Cabrales, una pequeña editorial independiente: Atípica Editorial. Conduzco, junto con la artista visual Diana Martín y creadoras de distintos medios, un videopodcast dedicado a la crítica y análisis de series y películas llamado Juego de Pomos. Creo que los personajes son la base de cualquier buena historia, la clave para involucrar a lectores y espectadores.

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm Chalo Gallardo.

I've spent over 12 years working in advertising. I've led art direction, managed creative teams, and learned that no award matters more than an idea that truly connects.

I'm currently Creative Director and Creativity professor at Universidad Diego Portales, where I try to teach what I practice: thinking with the heart and building with your hands.

I studied Communications at UDP, trained in Crossmedia at Academia Mac, earned a Master's in Creative Branded Content at Miami Ad School Madrid, and became Adobe Certified in Premiere Pro and Photoshop.

I’ve worked as Art Director at agencies like Simple, Why, and Prolam Y&R, as Creative Director at BBK ONE, as Group Art Lead at VML and Head of Art at Leo/Publicis, and now as Creative Director in a local super fresh agency: Jenaro.

I’ve had the chance to create campaigns for brands like Samsung, McDonald's, Unimarc, Chery & Exeed, Great Wall Motors, Tottus, Bci and the Government of Chile, among many others.

My work has been recognized at Cannes Lions, Clio, One Show, El Ojo de Iberoamérica, FIAP, Effie, PHNX, WINA, Madstars, and ACHAP, and I’ve served as a juror for FIAP, New York Festivals, Madstars, and PHNX.

In 2022, I took part in LIAisons, an international mentorship program that helped me confirm something simple: talent can be trained, sensitivity must be nurtured, and the path —well, you build it yourself.

teacher.aboutMe: Soy artista, pinto y enseño a pintar con acuarelas. Esta actividad se ha convertido en una fuente de creatividad y crecimiento para mi y surgió de un momento difícil en mi vida.  En el 2016 una enfermedad me forzó a buscar una salida, una nueva forma de vida... Inicie así un proceso de cambios de actitud, de hábitos y hasta de profesión. En Abril del 2017 dejé  la arquitectura para dedicarme de lleno a este nuevo oficio. Crecí en el campo y desde siempre la naturaleza ha sido fuente de inspiración. Disfruto las actividades al aire libre, caminar, contemplar, respirar... hoy admiro paisajes y estudio las variedades de plantas que me siguen llenando de vida y paz. Hace dos años empece a pintar como jugando y hoy son una herramienta para explorar, sanar y compartir.

teacher.aboutMe:
Fred Van Lente is a six-time New York Times bestselling comics writer, novelist and playwright whose work spans mystery/thrillers to historical fiction to superheroes to comedy.

Van Lente burst onto the scene with his first collaboration with cartoonist Ryan Dunlavey, "Action Philosophers", which became a American Library Association Best Book for Teens and the New York Times called "intensely goofy but intellectually rigorous”.

From there he went on to a long career at Marvel, where he worked on titles like "The Amazing Spider-Man", "Captain America" and "Marvel Zombies". He’s also written for DC, Archie Comics, Dark Horse, Boom! Studios, Dynamite Comics, and Valiant, where his run on "Archer & Armstrong" was nominated for a Harvey Award for Best Continuing Series.

Van Lente has continued writing non-fiction graphic novels, often with his artistic collaborator Ryan Dunlavey, including the bestselling Comic Book History of Comics and the middle grade series "Action Presidents". Two entries in the series were nominated for the Excellence in Graphic Literature Awards. In 2021, the third volume won the Theodore Roosevelt Association's Theodore Roosevelt Children’s Book Prize.

His Platinum Studios graphic novel "Cowboys & Aliens" was adapted into a film in 2011 starring Daniel Craig and Harrison Ford, directed by Jon Favreau. The following year, Helen Cho, a character created with co-writer Greg Pak in their acclaimed "Incredible Hercules" series, made her MCU debut in the blockbuster "Avengers: Age of Ultron". His "MODOK’s 11" and "Scorpion" became Hulu’s "Marvel’s MODOK", which named the elementary school in the show after him.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Sean Scherer. I am an artist, designer, and owner of Kabinett & Kammer, a contemporary curiosity shop of antiques, natural wonders, and art.

I was born and raised in Miami, Florida but have lived in many cities since then, including Paris, Toronto, and New York City. 

I have always had a passion for art and design, and objects. I bought my first antique at age 16 and have been collecting and dealing ever since.

I studied art at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago and the Independent Study Program of the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York. As a result, my paintings have been shown extensively in North America and Europe. 

In 2002 I moved to the Catskills area of New York State, where I opened my store, Kabinett & Kammer.

My art and design work has been featured in The New York Times, House Beautiful, Martha Stewart, The Times UK, and elsewhere. I was also an art history professor for more than 15  years at the State University of New York at Oneonta.

In 2020 Vendome Press published SEAN SCHERER'S KABINETT & KAMMER, CREATING AUTHENTIC INTERIORS. The book represents ten years' worth of work. I see the book as a celebration and a guide to collecting and showing how lively design can integrate disparate objects into beautifully layered ensembles. Each photograph is a lesson on color, texture, focal points, and room size. Though styles fluctuate and tastes are unique, design principles are immutable, and good design is good design. 

I would love to share my joy of objects and show you how to create an interior vignette with your favorite items that express who you are in your home.

teacher.aboutMe:
Besser spät als nie: Ich bin Theresa, habe einen ziemlich normalen 9 to 5 Job und dachte bis zu meinem 28 Lebensjahr, ich bin gar nicht künstlerisch begabt. Und mit Handarbeit hatte ich erst recht nichts am Hut... Bis ich auf der Suche nach einem "Lockdown-Hobby" erst das Jonglieren und dann das Sticken für mich entdeckte. Jonglieren ging, Sticken blieb. Bis heute. Das Hobby wurde schnell zu einer Leidenschaft.

Denn ich habe schnell gemerkt: Sticken bedeutet nicht einfach "spießige Blümchen auf Omas Tischdecke". Sticken ist modern, kreativ fordernd, feministisch und progressiv. Durch die schier endlosen Kombinationsmöglichkeiten von verschiedenen Stichen, Stilen, Farben und Materialien ist jeder Stickrahmen ein kleines Kunstwerk für sich!

Und genau deswegen lautet meine Mission: Mehr und mehr Leuten mit meinen beginnerfreundlichen Stickvorlagen von diesem alten, aber doch so erfrischendem Handwerk zu überzeugen. Come stitch with me! 


ENGLISH:
Better late than never: I'm Theresa, I have a pretty normal 9 to 5 job and until I was 28 that I thought I wasn't artistically talented at all. To be honest I never crafted in my life before. Until I was looking for a "lockdown hobby" and discovered juggling and embroidery. I gave up Juggling, but embroidery stayed. Til today. The hobby became a passion.

Because I quickly realized that embroidery doesn't just mean "old flowers on grandma's tablecloth". Embroidery is modern, creatively challenging, feminist and progressive. Due to the almost endless possibilities of different stitches, styles, colors and materials, each hoop is a small work of art in itself!

That's way my mission is to convince more and more people of this old but refreshing craft. Therefore I started selling  beginner friendly embroidery patterns and now even an online course to learn. Crazy how life works, right? Come stitch with me!

He has also written for numerous print and online channels, including Work Design Magazine, The Startup, Better Humans, Live Write Thrive, ChildArt Magazine, and Archinect.

Educator and practitioner as well as author, Rattner has taught at the University of Illinois, New York Academy of Art, New York University, and Parsons School of Design. Workshop and speaking venues include the Creative Problem Solving Institute, Creative Mornings, NeoCon, the American Institute of Architects, universities, libraries, and corporate events. His work has been featured on CNN, in such publications as The New York Times, Architectural Digest, Robb Report, Town & Country, and Houzz, and he has been interviewed on numerous podcasts. Rattner holds a Bachelor’s in art history from Columbia and a Masters of Architecture from Princeton.

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm a portrait and lifestyle photographer and for the last ten years I've been living in London and working all over the world. 

I picked up a camera having spent my childhood surrounded by photos taken by my Mum, my grandpa and my grandma. I wasn't a good photographer as a child; always with my finger or hair in front of the lens, never pressing the button quite at the right time. But at some point, something clicked (yes, I did that on purpose). By 15, I'd decided that I wanted to be a photographer. 

My parents had other plans for me, so I took a French degree, but afterwards, free to do what I wanted I came back to photography, made enough money to move to London and started working in studios and assisting photographers, always shoot my own work. Eventually, I got enough work to make it on my own and that's where you find me now. 

I've shot for Apple, Adidas, Battersea Dogs and Cats Home, The Guardian, The Telegraph, Riposte and Patagonia, amongst others and travelled to a lot of different fun places. In 2021, I shot and co-authored my first book with food writer Clare Finney; it's called The Female Chef.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Diana Buitrago, I was born in Cartagena, Colombia and I am a classically trained realist painter who lives in Jersey City and works in New York City. The focus of my work is on both Landscape Painting and Portrait Painting from life. My extensive formal artistic training in the classical atelier method includes the four year program at the Art Students League, Artistic Anatomy coursework at Drexel University's School of Medicine, and the four year Core Program at the Grand Central Atelier. I have studied under artists Michael Grimaldi, Dan Thompson, Jon deMartin, Jacob Collins, and Colleen Barry. My work has been exhibited in New York in Eleventh Street Arts Gallery, Robert Simmon Fine Art, Salmagundi Club, The Phyllis Harriman Gallery and as well as at the Colombian Embassy in New York. 

I now teach painting to the advanced students in the Core Program at the Grand Central Atelier. I also teach several online courses such as Studio Landscape Painting, Portrait Painting, Master-Copies and I teach private lessons as well.  I’ve also taught workshops for The Art Students League of New York and in other institutions around the world such as Paris, Vienna and Mexico City.  When I’m not teaching, I am at home painting in my studio or out traveling painting landscapes on Plein-Air. In 2018 I was awarded a Fellowship with The La Napoule Foundation which brought me to the South of France to paint the beautiful Cote D'azur. I’m also a four time Hudson River Fellow which allowed me to paint breathtaking landscapes in New Hampshire, New York’s Hudson Valley and Connecticut. In 2019 my painting “Portrait of a Young Dancer” won a certificate of Excellence from the Portrait Society of America. 

All this experience has brought me countless hours of working from life and painting outdoors directly from nature. My experience as an instructor has led me to demoing many copies from the old master for my students. This and the study of nature has actually impacted my own work and my technique and this is what I would like to share with you in this course. 

In my own personal work I try to show a high degree of technique and understanding of how the light affects the form of my subjects, whether it is a portrait or a mountain in the distance. I want my work to look cohesive and realistic because I have a high level of understanding of light, form, composition, etc. All of that alone will make for a very sterile painting, however.   While I am a realist painter,  I’m not trying to paint photorealistically.  My personal style is to have a slightly more painterly effect upon my canvas. I want to show energy, life and personality in my brushwork, mark-making and color. I hope I can transmit this idea to each one of my students in this platform.

teacher.aboutMe:
I’m a digital artist based in LA. My work combines custom lettering and 3D illustration into intricate pieces living in contained and clean environments, delving into volume, form, color and material behavior with a taste for dynamic and organic pieces.

Born and raised in Barcelona, my work got influenced by the Catalan Modernism, an art and literature movement that emerged around the turn of the 20th century, equivalent to the Art Noveau in France or the Jugendstil in Germany. Its attention to detail and visual richness always attracted me and it influenced my style making my designs dynamic and elaborated.

In 2009 I moved to New York City, where I fell in love with typography and where my work acquired a more rational and organized flavor too. Barcelona gave me a taste for illustration, New York brought me to typography, and now both disciplines live in L.A., with expressive digital lettering and 3D art.

teacher.aboutMe:
My name is Nejc and I'm a 3D visualization specialist which basically means I create computer generated imagery of products in cool places that (typically) don't exist in the real world.

I've been working in the field of product visualization for the last 9 years or so and my client list includes Samsung, Dell, Netgear, Arlo, Wild, Pepe Jeans and a couple of others. I really like helping companies grow their brands and so besides creating the images themselves I also like to focus on the brand strategy the images themselves help drive.

As far as my visual style goes, I'm really into moody images. I like putting a sense of emotion into my imagery. I'm also trying to be a stickler for realism and detail.

My beginnings weren't quite straightforward. 

For the longest time I didn't even fully realize my profession exists. Sure, I've always been into computers and video games. I also had basic 3D courses as part of my college curriculum but I've never really been drawn to it until I saw my significant other, Natalija, work on her diploma - which was all about 3D. The way she approached it looked fun and the end result was so inspiring that it got me thinking 3D can be lots of fun. Plus, you can make a living out of it.

So I started doing Youtube tutorials and online courses until I thought I had enough knowledge to tackle actual commercial projects. I put my name out there, started kinda slow for sure but eventually I landed a couple of projects and things sort of snowballed from there.

I was always interested in how businesses work and so as I got better creating the actual images I started supplementing my artistic knowledge with business knowledge. After all, if I wanted my images to help my clients grow their businesses I needed to understand how business works.

To this day I find this profession extremely fulfilling as I'm doing something that I find "fun to do" and at the same time I help other people succeed. Lately, I've been also very active creating educational content so that hopefully other people can join in on the fun as well.

teacher.aboutMe:
Je m’appelle Nicolas Bossard, j’ai 31 ans. Je suis architecte, je vis et travaille à Paris. J’ai créé mon agence d’architecture et de design à Paris il y a 3 ans, après avoir travaillé dans un studio d’architecture dans laquelle j’ai appris la gestion de projets ambitieux et techniques. 

Les projets sur lesquels je travaille, dans un contexte urbain dense, ont tous pour enjeu principal l'optimisation qualitative des espaces : comment réaliser un lieu de vie ou espace de travail dans lequel chaque usage ait été pensé, puis conçu et traduit spatialement, dans une économie de place et une économie de moyens. 
 
En 3 ans, avec mon équipe de 6 architectes, nous avons conçu et réalisé plus d’une trentaine de projets d’architecture, de programme et d’ambition variés : de la rénovation complète d’un appartement, à la restructuration et surélévation d’une maison de ville, jusqu’au projet de construction d’une extension. Nous développons les projets de maîtres d’ouvrage privés, particuliers et professionnels. Pour chacun de nos projets, nous faisons équipe avec des artisans dont la compétence et le savoir-faire permet de construire tous les concepts que nous avons imaginé.

teacher.aboutMe:
Formé au design graphique à l’EPSAA, le jeune parisien a fait ses gammes à New York auprès de la styliste Gaby Basora. À son retour, Kim Roselier décide de s’éloigner du graphisme pour se consacrer au dessin, la couleur est alors venue tout naturellement s’associer à son trait. S’il favorise la peinture a ce début, qui lui permet d’approfondir sa maîtrise de la couleur. Aujourd'hui il travail sur ordinateur ce qui donne a ces illustrations une force graphique. 

Il puise son inspiration chez Tom Purvis , Georges Barbier, Elsa Shiaparelli ou Horace Taylor pour raconter des histoires qui laissent place à une libre interprétation. A la frontière entre l’art graphique et l’art pictural, Kim Roselier associe les couleurs et abstraction géométrique à la perfection pour offrir une iconographie charnelle et poétique à ces illustrations.
