teacher.aboutMe:
Estoy viviendo un sueño y todo fue porque empecé buscando la luz. Eso suena algo espiritual, y sí, pero me refiero a que un día fui estudiante de Comunicación Social en la Pontificia Universidad Javeriana y mi énfasis en lo audiovisual me llevó a la búsqueda de la luz. Ahí comenzo un camino de continuo aprendizaje que me ha permitido representar la luz en diferentes formas, también de esa constante busqueda es que viene mi empresa y su nombre: White Studios, que a día de hoy tiene operación en mi Colombia y en Canadá, donde actualmente vivo.

Me gusta mucho saber que empresas como Falabella, MNG o Dafiti, aparecen dentro de mi portafolio, pero mi verdadera alegría está en cada ocasión que logro componer con imágenes una historia exitosa que logra llevar un producto hasta su público. Eso es lo que quiero compartir contigo, las enseñanzas que la experiencia en fotografía de moda y de producto, a lo largo de estos siete años, me ha dejado.

¿Por qué le gusta mi trabajo a mis clientes? Porque siempre estoy pensando en cómo algo se puede ver mejor. Lo hago con sus marcas, con sus productos y con sus e-commerce. Después de compartir este curso juntos, vas a estar en capacidad de entregar a tus clientes una mejor imagen de cara al mercado que les espera.

Hay mucho camino por delante y todavía la historia se está construyendo. Por ahora, vamos a aprender a sacar lo mejor de tus habilidades y lo mejor de los productos frente a la luz.

🤖🧠 IA, Dev y Producto

Desde mi juventud, la tecnología y la informática han sido mi pasión. A los 16 años, mis primeros pasos en la reparación de ordenadores y mi inmersión en la informática marcaron el inicio de mi viaje. Una beca me llevó a Irlanda, donde amplié mis conocimientos de programación y me sumergí en la cultura empresarial. En este periodo, mi interés por el cloud computing se desarrolló, y trabajé como consultor externo para Microsoft.

Al regresar a España, continué explorando el desarrollo de aplicaciones web y el diseño de páginas mientras trabajaba como diseñador web para un ecommerce. La búsqueda de nuevos horizontes me llevó al marketing online, pero el cierre de la empresa me brindó una oportunidad única. Durante 8 meses, aproveché mi desempleo para sumergirme en mi pasión por el SEO, lo que me llevó finalmente a liderar un departamento de experimentación SEO en una gran agencia. Mi fascinación por la inteligencia artificial me llevó a adentrarme en este campo en evolución, aplicándolo primero en una empresa bancaria y posteriormente con el lanzamiento de productos como GuruAssistant, un asistente de atención al cliente impulsado por IA.

Mi compromiso con la comunidad me lleva a compartir mis conocimientos en LinkedIn, mediante una newsletter y el podcast "El Test de Turing". Mi sitio web es un recurso adicional donde ofrezco consejos sobre IA y empresas. Estoy convencido de que estamos en un camino de posibilidades infinitas gracias a la tecnología. Mi entusiasmo por ser parte de esta revolución y compartirlo con otros es innegable, pues la historia enseña que debemos abrazar y evolucionar con el cambio.

After living in the United States for 20 years, I've recently moved to a small coastal town in Spain where I live with my husband and my vast collection of cookie cutters.

Hey there, art lovers!

I'm Hannah Stelter, but you can call me your multidisciplinary art cheerleader. I specialize in watercolor and acrylic but dabble in wire sculpture, dance, and more! Beyond creating, I'm also an entrepreneur and, most importantly, a self-love champion.

Being a full-time artist was just a dream, until... well, it wasn't!  I started sharing my work online in 2020, inspired by other amazing artists. My relatable art and empowering message resonated quickly, and I built a fantastic community.

Within a year, my art was bringing in a whopping $100,000, and I was living my dream job!

People often ask how I did it. The answer? Learning tons, creating even more, and ditching perfectionism. (I even gave a TED Talk about it - "The Middle Finger Method", check it out!)

Now, I love sharing tips and tricks for other aspiring artists, teaching classes on embracing the creative mess, and of course, creating art that makes you smile!

Want to know more? Head over to hannahstelter.com and let's connect!

I truly believe that expressing oneself through art gives us the power to unearth our deepest feelings, heal our emotional wounds and ultimately, save lives. It’s a beautiful way to communicate the emotions and experiences that you can’t always capture with words. 

In my courses, I boil down the essentials of painting and make them easy to digest for anyone. When you’re covering the basics, there’s always something to learn! It’s important to me that after my course, you will have all the tools you need to start expressing yourself artistically with paint.

I hope I can so blessed as to be a part of your creative journey. There truly is an artist in all of us. I can’t wait to meet the artist in you!

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello all! I am Geonna Snyder or the theatge. I am a multi media artist who specializes in SFX makeup. I started doing special effects makeup in 2014 for an independent film company, I took a break for a couple of years and went back to it in 2017. I graduated from college in 2017 with my associates and applied sciences related to funeral home work. The restorative arts portion of my classes got me back into special effects make up. A lot of what I have learned has come from medical books along with also restorative arts based books. Since just around 2019, I started posting special effects, makeup tutorials, online mixed in with DIY content and educational content related to medical terminology shown with special effects makeup. 

My favorite part about special effects makeup is the fact that I can be anyone or anything that I want to for a certain period of time then I get to take off the make up and create something new. There's something so human about creating artwork that you can both live, breathe, and also destroy. I hope that you enjoy my lessons on here get creative and shape-shift into something fun and new. Be the art, make a mess, learn something new, and get creative!

Hello everyone! I’m thrilled to join the Domestika community and share my expertise on leveraging AI tools to start and run a business. With an MBA and a Bachelor’s in Business Administration from the University of Piraeus, my journey in the business world has been both diverse and rewarding.

For over a decade, I honed my skills at Procter & Gamble and Diageo, where I served as a Brand & Marketing Manager. I had the privilege of managing iconic brands like Johnnie Walker, Ariel, Duracell, Pantene, Braun, and Pringles, across Greece and Western Europe. This experience provided me with a solid foundation in brand strategy and marketing execution.

Since 2015, I have been at the helm of CHAMPIONSID.COM, a venture that earned me the Greek entrepreneurship award twice in 2016. Our innovative approach caught the attention of the White House, leading to our selection and funding to compete in the Global Entrepreneurship Summit in Silicon Valley. This recognition was a pivotal moment, propelling our company onto the global stage.

In April 2017, I founded SimplyDigital.gr, a full-stack marketing agency that collaborates with businesses generating eight to nine figures worldwide. SimplyDigital has grown to become the largest digital marketing channel globally on TikTok, Instagram, and Pinterest, boasting 3.3 million followers. Our mission is to empower businesses to harness the power of digital marketing to achieve their goals.

As a Marketing & Sports Management instructor for the Greek Ministry of Sports, I have a passion for teaching and inspiring the next generation of business leaders. My upcoming course on Domestika will provide practical insights and hands-on techniques for using AI tools to streamline business operations and drive growth.

I’m excited to see your projects and hear your feedback. This interactive exchange will not only help you grow but also inspire me to develop new course content. If you’re interested in more of my work or want to stay updated on my latest ventures, please visit my website and subscribe to my newsletter.

Let’s embark on this learning journey together and unlock the potential of AI in business!

teacher.aboutMe:
I'm Luisa Hurtado, but you might know me better as @designerluisa from TikTok, or @imluluisa on Instagram. I'm a passionate upcycler and Fashion Designer.

I grew up in a small town in Mexico, where as a child, fashion always fascinated me. I dreamt of wearing unique clothes, different from what everyone else had. 
I realized I wanted to start making my own garments because I was asking way too much from my grandma and my mom. So I decided to learn!
I was able to attend a university in my own state, in Mexico, where I graduated with honors in Fashion Design & Garment Industry. 
Right after I graduated I was an assistant teacher in my own university teaching sewing & pattern making.. After that I had a few collections come out and Fashion Shows at city events that allowed me to reach a new market.
Not long after that, I met the love of my life, and moved to the United States where I started from scratch, without recognition, which was challenging.
I had fun during this time as well, I even made my own wedding dress and created some fun pieces for friends and family. I sold my designs at small local events, always seeking ways to share my passion for fashion.

This passion to share & teach led me to start my Youtube channel, and later TikTok. 

It was on TikTok where my work, particularly a backpack made from upcycled jeans, caught the eye of many, including major brands like Levi's.

Now, I am focusing on sharing my knowledge with others and helping people around the world get started on their own projects, prioritizing creativity, sustainability, and lots of fun!

-Luisa xx

teacher.aboutMe:
"What's up guys, Groovy Guitar Dude here!"
If you came here from YouTube, chances are you have heard me say that before! My name is Cody and I teach guitar and ukulele lessons for beginners on YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram as The Groovy Guitar Dude! 

I love music. Period. I can barely go an hour without listening to it. I refuse to leave my house without my guitar or ukulele. Music has been a soundtrack to my very best memories. Music has been there for me through some of my hardest times. I LOVE MUSIC!

When I first started playing guitar and ukulele in 2007, my dad had cancer. He passed away a few months after I started playing. After he passed, my family did not have the money to pay for expensive weekly music lessons for me, so I was stuck learning on my own. At first, I took this as a disadvantage and seeing my friends taking formal guitar lessons and progressing faster than me was discouraging. Then I discovered that there were THOUSANDS of free guitar and ukulele lessons on YouTube! And oh man, did that open a whole new world to me! After a while of learning the songs I loved, I realized, this is how people should be learning music.

Fast-forward about 15 years. I have people constantly ask me how I learned and who was my teacher when I was first learning so that they or their children might learn as well! Not that I am an AMAZING guitarist or anything, there are many others that are better than me. But people seeing the passion and joy I have for the music leads them to inquire. 

My goal in teaching is always to do my very best to share that passion that I have with others, and give them the tools to express that passion through music! My greatest hope is that that shines through in my guitar and ukulele tutorials! 

I love music and I love all opportunities I get to share that love of music with others. So thank you for taking the time to stop in and read a little about me and what I do! 

- Cody (The Groovy Guitar Dude)

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello all! I am Geonna Snyder or the theatge. I am a multi media artist who specializes in SFX makeup. I started doing special effects makeup in 2014 for an independent film company, I took a break for a couple of years and went back to it in 2017. I graduated from college in 2017 with my associates and applied sciences related to funeral home work. The restorative arts portion of my classes got me back into special effects make up. A lot of what I have learned has come from medical books along with also restorative arts based books. Since just around 2019, I started posting special effects, makeup tutorials, online mixed in with DIY content and educational content related to medical terminology shown with special effects makeup. 

My favorite part about special effects makeup is the fact that I can be anyone or anything that I want to for a certain period of time then I get to take off the make up and create something new. There's something so human about creating artwork that you can both live, breathe, and also destroy. I hope that you enjoy my lessons on here get creative and shape-shift into something fun and new. Be the art, make a mess, learn something new, and get creative!

Caitlin's journey into the digital realm began as a hobby in 2020. She started posting these projects to social media, and was surprised to see how much people enjoyed them. What started as a personal outlet soon evolved into a thriving career as Caitlin discovered her knack for creating fun videos and inspiring people across the globe to sew, thrift and upcycle.

Beyond creating content and sewing, Caitlin is mom to 3 kids and one senior dog. She has also been married for 15 years to her husband, who is in the United States Marine Corps. They currently live in San Diego, California.

teacher.aboutMe:
🤖🧠 IA, Dev y Producto

Desde mi juventud, la tecnología y la informática han sido mi pasión. A los 16 años, mis primeros pasos en la reparación de ordenadores y mi inmersión en la informática marcaron el inicio de mi viaje. Una beca me llevó a Irlanda, donde amplié mis conocimientos de programación y me sumergí en la cultura empresarial. En este periodo, mi interés por el cloud computing se desarrolló, y trabajé como consultor externo para Microsoft.

Al regresar a España, continué explorando el desarrollo de aplicaciones web y el diseño de páginas mientras trabajaba como diseñador web para un ecommerce. La búsqueda de nuevos horizontes me llevó al marketing online, pero el cierre de la empresa me brindó una oportunidad única. Durante 8 meses, aproveché mi desempleo para sumergirme en mi pasión por el SEO, lo que me llevó finalmente a liderar un departamento de experimentación SEO en una gran agencia. Mi fascinación por la inteligencia artificial me llevó a adentrarme en este campo en evolución, aplicándolo primero en una empresa bancaria y posteriormente con el lanzamiento de productos como GuruAssistant, un asistente de atención al cliente impulsado por IA.

Mi compromiso con la comunidad me lleva a compartir mis conocimientos en LinkedIn, mediante una newsletter y el podcast "El Test de Turing". Mi sitio web es un recurso adicional donde ofrezco consejos sobre IA y empresas. Estoy convencido de que estamos en un camino de posibilidades infinitas gracias a la tecnología. Mi entusiasmo por ser parte de esta revolución y compartirlo con otros es innegable, pues la historia enseña que debemos abrazar y evolucionar con el cambio.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi, I am Nghi Ho, a successful self-taught Macramé artist and content creator, as well as the published author of Macramé: The Power of Knots, which has sold thousands of copies worldwide.  

As a kid, I was amazed at how, with just my hands and a bit of creativity, I could create something beautiful. One of my fondest childhood memories is making lanterns for the Mid-Autumn Festival. Following my passion, I earned a bachelor’s degree in Fashion Design. After graduating, I worked as a graphic designer but later decided to become a freelancer to have more artistic freedom and choose projects I was truly passionate about. Over time, I developed an interest in other digital ventures, teaching myself basic coding, programming, content recording and editing, image composition, web development, and building a social media presence.  

It took me a while to master the art of Macramé, and at one point, I grew frustrated with the available resources. That’s when I decided to give it a try myself and started creating my own content. I’ve since built a strong presence in the online Macramé community, using platforms like Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok to inspire others to explore Macramé. I create easy-to-follow tutorials designed to spark creativity and encourage artistic self-expression.  

In addition to managing my social media channels, I’ve developed my own brand of Macramé supplies, Miss Knottie Macrame. My online store has made it possible for people around the world to access everything they need to start tying knots.

Hi! I'm Lindsey, a cupcake designer and content creator, also known as Lindsey Baked This on social media. I discovered my passion for cupcake decoration in 2020, transforming what started as a hobby into a thriving career.

I began my artistic journey as a student at Rhode Island School of Design, where I majored in illustration. There, I not only learned the fundamentals of drawing and painting, but also cultivated an eye for detail and a penchant for imaginative expression.

Building on my artistic background, I embarked on a 14-year career in the advertising industry, serving as a creative director. In this dynamic role, I mastered the art of conceptualizing, crafting compelling aesthetics, and bringing concepts to life through graphic design and photography. This experience equipped me with the tools to seamlessly translate my artistic vision onto the canvas of cupcakes.

Fueled by my passion for creativity and a desire to spread joy, I have amassed a dedicated following on social media, captivating audiences with engaging and entertaining decorating videos. For me, buttercream is more than just an ingredient—it's edible paint, a medium through which I brings my imaginative designs to life.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello!

I’m Josie, the founder and pastry chef behind Sweet Josie Bakes! I started Sweet Josie Bakes back in July 2018 during a time when I was dealing with a lot of anxiety and depression. I felt incredibly lost back then and wanted a fresh start. I had always loved baking and art, and nothing made me happier than when I could bring joy to others, especially when that joy came in the form of delicious desserts.

Hence the creation of Sweet Josie Bakes, a place where I could bring my love of art and baking into one. And while I had no idea how to run a small business, I knew I wanted to share my passion with others, in hopes of inspiring a few to follow their dreams as well.

Over 5 years later, not only have I been lucky enough to do what I love every day, but I’ve also discovered a love of teaching. During the 2020 pandemic, I started teaching online classes and have since taught thousands of students during the last 3+ years, which I couldn’t be prouder about!

I’ve come up with my own signature style of teaching, which I like to call “Lazy baking”! Taking hard techniques such as tempering chocolate or piping buttercream flowers and breaking them down into easy, fun steps that anyone can learn, no matter their skill level.

I’ve been fortunate enough to work with amazing brands such as The Toronto Raptors, YouTube, DoorDash, Tre Stelle, Country Crock, Beekman 1802, Post Cereals, and so many more. My work has been featured on prominent platforms such as YouTube, Food Network, Buzzfeed Tasty, CTV, Buzzfeed, Unilad, and 9gag.

Thank you for being here, and I truly hope you enjoy the class!

Love,
Sweet Josie

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy Patricio Ortega, soy arquitecto de profesión y carpintero mueblista de oficio, y hace 9 años fundé junto a Francisca Araya mi mujer, un proyecto que denominamos Maderística.

Maderística es un pequeño taller de diseño y fabricación artesanal de muebles de autor, un espacio donde desarrollamos, con nuestras propias manos, proyectos en los que imprimimos nuestra visión del diseño y el arte de la carpintería, así nuestros trabajos no solo representan un puñado de preferencias estéticas, sino que además son expresión de nuestro modo de trabajar la madera, por eso decimos que son “obras” y no solo “objetos”.

Hace algún tiempo Francisca dejó el proyecto para dedicarse a su carrera y se llegó Carlos Aracena al equipo, desde entonces somos solo dos personas las que materializamos todos los proyectos que puede ver en nuestro catálogo.

Nuestro trabajo ha sido publicado en diversos medios impresos y digitales, dentro de ellos los más destacados son el libro “Nuevos Creativos Chilenos, Diseño de Productos” de Juan Pablo Fuentes, el cual recoge el trabajo de 36 diseñadores chilenos que se han destacado en los últimos 10 año en nuestro país, la web serie “Manufactura”, la cual registra el trabajo de la nueva generación de artesanos que se han destacado en distintos oficios, y la selección de uno de nuestros muebles para 5° Bienal Iberoamericana de Diseño en Madrid. Además hemos colaborado con Arauco en el desarrollo de una placa de contrachapado de nivel superior.

El 2015 y a pedido de nuestros seguidores en redes sociales, comenzamos a compartir nuestra experiencia impartiendo un curso de “Introducción a la Maderística” a alero de lo que denominamos el “Instituto Maderístico para el Carpintero del Mañana”, y es que teníamos muy en claro que lo que nos interesaba no solo era enseñar algunas técnicas, sino además reposicionar a largo plazo un oficio que durante mucho tiempo ha sido mal valorado en nuestro país. A la fecha han pasado casi 1000 estudiantes por nuestro taller.

teacher.aboutMe:
Camilla Mendini, known on social media as @carotilla_ , is an Italian content creator focused on sustainability and a sustainable entrepreneur. She has lived in the United States since 2015, first in New York and since 2020 in Florida.

Camilla started making informative videos on social media about slow fashion, circular economy and zero waste in 2016, at first as a conscious consumer and then as a entrepreneur involved in sustainability, becoming the first Italian Green Influencer to discuss these topics on Instagram, TikTok and Youtube with passion and consistency. 

In 2018 she launched her clothing brand Amorilla, based on principles of sustainability and ethics, offering, instead of the classic collections, two Love Stories per year, with particular attention to sustainable fabrics' sourcing, natural dyes and ethical labor. Amorilla's philosophy is to rediscover the textile traditions that have given life to fashion and resume them to create capsule collections for women, while being ethical and sustainable.

In 2019 and 2020 she received the title of Top Green Influencer, the first year from Green Style, the second from the Alkemy-Il Sole 24 Ore Observatory. She was included by Vogue in the Italian list of environmental activists to follow on Instagram, together with Greta Thunberg.

In 2020 Camilla wrote the book “(Im)Perfect Sustainable. Daily gestures for sustainability within everyone's reach" published by Fabbri Editori. Camilla believes that becoming perfectly sustainable, although ideal in theory, is not what we should aim for: an army of imperfect sustainable people is stronger than a small group of people who are sustainable in every way. This book is about how to consume causing the minimum impact of the planet and it focuses on 5 different topics: sustainable fashion, sustainable beauty, sustainable food, sustainable home and kids and sustainability.

In 2021 she created COR, a sustainable beauty brand of shampoo, face and body bars which formulas are completely biodegradable and vegan. COR is a plastic-free band and zero waste brand. Camilla's goal is to give the opportunity to the general public to access the evolution of the cosmetic product, effective and high quality, in a conscious way. Respecting the skin’s PH and respecting the planet.

In 2023 Camilla and several other Italian professionals working in the fashion industry created "Movimento Moda Responsabile" (Responsible Fashion Movement) a network of brands, companies, manufacturers, associations, and professionals promoting an alternative towards a more socially and ecologically responsible fashion. In MMR we believe in a more ethical, critical, and sustainable fashion, that can bring new value to our territory, we create awareness and we promote a necessary change in the fashion system and production.

Soy fotógrafo y retocador profesional. Estoy certificado por Adobe como Experto en Adobe Photoshop y Adobe Photoshop Lightroom. Hey there, art lovers!

I'm Hannah Stelter, but you can call me your multidisciplinary art cheerleader. I specialize in watercolor and acrylic but dabble in wire sculpture, dance, and more! Beyond creating, I'm also an entrepreneur and, most importantly, a self-love champion.

Being a full-time artist was just a dream, until... well, it wasn't!  I started sharing my work online in 2020, inspired by other amazing artists. My relatable art and empowering message resonated quickly, and I built a fantastic community.

Within a year, my art was bringing in a whopping $100,000, and I was living my dream job!

Now, I love sharing tips and tricks for other aspiring artists, teaching classes on embracing the creative mess, and of course, creating art that makes you smile!

Want to know more? Head over to hannahstelter.com and let's connect!

From the beginning, and still to this day, my goal is to spread joy and positivity through my art. But no matter what form in which art is consumed, it is such a vital part of society, and I believe it should be accessible to everyone. I love using my small business to show that art can be done by anyone and is available to everyone, whether it’s digital or traditional! Thank you for stopping by, and have fun creating!

teacher.aboutMe:
Aprender para compartir y compartir para aprender. Esa es la base de mi trabajo como consultora, formadora y conferenciante en comunicación digital e inteligencia artificial. Acompaño a profesionales y organizaciones en un momento en que la tecnología cambia a gran velocidad y necesitamos encontrar formas auténticas y sostenibles de comunicarnos. Mi objetivo no es solo optimizar procesos o introducir nuevas herramientas, sino ayudar a que la comunicación digital y la IA se conviertan en aliadas para crear, conectar y transformar.

Trabajo desde una visión estratégica y práctica:

- Auditorías y planes de acción que aportan claridad en la toma de decisiones.
- Estrategias de marca y comunicación que combinan creatividad y foco.
- Selección de profesionales, proveedores y aplicaciones digitales y de IA
- Programas formativos que desmitifican la tecnología y la hacen accesible.
- Conferencias y ponencias que acercan la IA y la innovación a todo tipo de públicos.

Mi labor es traducir conceptos complejos para que sean comprensibles y acercar la innovación tecnológica a las personas sin perder la esencia humana. Concibo la IA como un partner y una herramienta de cocreación que nos apoya en el análisis, la ideación, la toma de decisiones e incluso en desbloquear la creatividad en momentos clave. 

Me dedico a la comunicación desde 2002. En 2009 empecé a liderar estrategias en redes sociales en agencia y desde 2011 desarrollo mi actividad como profesional independiente de la comunicación digital. Desde 2022, con la apertura de ChatGPT al mundo y de otras plataformas, me he enfocado en la aplicación de la IA en comunicación y marketing digital y en la innovación y la cultura de empresa.

Trabajo con empresas y profesionales de diferentes sectores e imparto conferencias y clases en eventos y universidades.

He publicado siete cursos en Domestika con más de 170K alumnos en todo el mundo:

- Estrategia de comunicación para redes sociales
- LinkedIn: construye tu marca personal
- Instagram: concursos, sorteos, UGC y otras acciones tácticas
- Creación de contenidos con IA
- Introducción al Community Management con IA
- Creación de marca con IA
- Creación de asistentes de marketing digital con IA

Mi motor es la curiosidad: explorar cómo la tecnología puede ampliar nuestras posibilidades y compartir ese conocimiento para que otros puedan aplicarlo en su propio camino.

Si crees que puedo aportar valor a tu proyecto o te apetece conversar sobre cómo comunicar y crecer en la era de la IA, escríbeme, estaré encantada de escucharte.

teachers.aboutMe:
I'm born in 1982 in Tortona (AL), I live and work in Voghera (Italy).
In 2007 i achieved my degree in painting at the Art Academy of Brera (Milan).

i work exclusively with colored pencils, I often represent the flora, fauna and female mystics of Sardinia from the 16th to the 18th centuries
Combining organic shapes and textures with chiaroscuro contrasts of light and shadow, my drawings portray isolated female faces framed by plants and animals. 
My imagery refers to the herbalist traditions and Sardinian folklore of the mystical seductresses who enchant, curse and cure. My body of work is a tribute to the legacy of healing women throughout history. 

my works appeared in books, newspapers and magazines such as The New Yorker, Juxtapoz Magazine, Hi Fructose Magazine, Les Arts Dessines, Arte Mondadori.
With Albin Michel I published the illustrated book "Poucette" (distributed in Spain for Edelvives with the title "Pulgarcita"). I'm preparing an illustrated book in collaboration with Sébastien Perez.

I collaborate with Jonathan LeVine Projects (New Jersey) and Thinkspace Projects (Los Angeles) for America, Gallery Benoni (Copenhagen), Galleria Patricia Armocida (Milan), Galleria Giovanni Bonelli (Milan) for Europe.
I took part in the 54th International Art Exhibition, Biennale di Venezia, Italian Pavilion, curated by Vittorio Sgarbi, Lombardy Regional Pavilion, Palazzo Te, Mantova, "Turn The Page: the first ten years of hi-fructose" at the Virginia Museum of Contemporary Art (Moca) (US), POW! WOW! Hawai'i at the Honolulu Museum of Art School (US), THE NATURE SQUISITE: BEYOND THE BOUNDARIES OF POP at the Stelline Foundation (Milan), The New Vanguard - at The Lancaster Museum of Art and History (MOAH) and IMAGO at the Much Museum in Munich (Germany).
Among my solo shows: “Dear Collapse” Thinkspace Project (Los Angeles), “Monism” Galleri Benoni (Copenhagen), “Il Ricordo è un Consolatore Molesto” Galleria Patricia Armocida (Milan), “Home” Galleria Giovanni Bonelli (Milan), “ Animanera ”Jonathan LeVine Gallery (NY).

I am a watercolor artist and urban sketcher currently living in Paris. I’ve sketched and drawn all my life, and when I moved to Paris five years ago I fell in love with the way light glances off the amazing architecture. I find watercolor to be the perfect medium for capturing the effects of light and shadow, and the elusive nature of sunlight on buildings. 

I was born in England and grew up in California where for 20 years I have worked as a storyboard artist and illustrator for feature films, television, and commercials. Because of this background, I use the language of cinema to inform my paintings. I think in story scenes, camera angles, and cinematic characters. Paintings tell stories, and I aim to create images that convey the mood and character of a place, just as film scenes do. For me, sketching and plein air painting is a form of meditation, and the best way I’ve found to discover the hidden corners of the city and uncover its stories. 

My works have been exhibited in solo and group shows in Europe, the United States, and Russia. I conduct regular workshops and masterclasses in watercolor painting and sketching in Europe and the U.S., teaching students of all levels and backgrounds how to infuse their paintings with new life. I’m also very active on social media and proud to be part of this global community of creatives.

My name is Mattias Adolfsson I live in a small town called Sigtuna just outside of Stockholm Sweden. I have a master of fine Arts in Graphic design, I worked ten years doing computer games and 3d modelling before switching to Illustration in 2007. About half of my time I work on commission work and the rest on my own drawings producing originals and books. I have worked with a lot of large commission work from all over the world and I have also been lucky to be able to travel to art and book festivals and even to some music festivals showing my art. 

Some of my commission works Psyop TV, WIRED, Atelier Choux, Google, Ragdoll Limited, Die Weltwoche, Wired Italy, The New Yorker, Dance Gavin Dance, HHMI, Arnold, Carlton Books, Nickelodeon, Hollywood reporter, Cartoon networks, Lowe Vietnam, Warner Brothers, Dreamworks, Disney, DDB, IBM, Chipotle, Area 23Norwegian State Railways, Amnesty International, Dali Speakers, Heye Puzzle and Mac Guff.

Awards:
Little Hakka award, AOI (Association of Illustrators) world Illustration award, Hiii Illustration 2016, American Illustrator, Winner Most beautiful book ”Second in Line”, 3x3 show, Winner Kolla!

I'm a Dutch illustrator living in Amsterdam. I love nature, food (especially cakes and coffee), cosy indoor moments and drawing in my sketchbook.
I studied literature in Amsterdam and children's book illustration in Cambridge UK, and I've made several children's books and worked with different international magazines

I’m an artist-illustrator based in London, UK.

Combining bold, expressive brushstrokes and decisively drawn lines, my paintings of nature feel spontaneous and joyful whilst avoiding the sentimentality often associated with wildlife. I'm interested in the way we romanticise the natural world, how we anthropomorphise or uphold elements as desirable whilst disregarding others as a nuisance.

As a teacher, and an artist, I focus on the mistakes. They are fundamental to making creative discoveries and in trying to avoid them we risk stifling ourselves. My courses invite students to draw and paint in unusual and experimental ways, to let go of being in complete control and become open to the unexpected.

I draw mostly in watercolour, ink and coloured pencil, but also experiment with found materials and tools (bubble wrap, emulsion paint, sticks, teabags, squashed blackberries, paintbrush handles…). I often stand to draw and paint on the floor which injects an energy and playfulness to my drawings - the process for me is very physical, almost like a dance.

My work can been found on books, homeware, fabric and fine art prints, and includes clients such as Waterstones, John Lewis, Laura Ashley, Whistlefish, Woodmansterne and Profile Books.

I am a French artist living in Barcelona. I define my self as a mobile illustrator and I register my life in drawings: I filled about 200 sketchbooks during the past 18 years.
I use to sketch on vintage accounting books that I find in flea markets. This yellow paper with red and blue lines remind me the first paintings and observations that bring back the scientist expedition of the XVIIIth century like Cook or Laperouse from unknown civilisations and lands. I secretly want to become one of those explorers.
The economy of medium is also what I appreciate. I'm traveling light and don't need much more than a sketchbook, inkpens, watercolor and my folding stool. The street is my studio. 
Nowadays that most of the people are focused on digital, being unplugged with a simple sketchbook made of second hand paper and inviting the spectator to look through it flipping the pages is magic.

Sketching from direct observation and reporting become my main activity. I already published 30 books about Barcelona, Paris, Berlin, Cuba, Ouessant island (…) and thematic like "art nouveau", "vintage cars" or "planes" after my nomination as an official air and space painter for the french army.

Follow my daily adventures on my instagram:

German artist, illustrator and author of several books about drawing, sketching and watercolor.
Professor at the münster school of design, lives in berlin, Germany

I am an illustrator and instructor based in LA. I teach Foundation Sketching and Advanced Sketching at Brainstorm School, and have taught workshops at Dreamworks Animation. For my personal work, I draw most of my inspiration from the natural world. I specialize in working with ink, and I absolutely love sketching animals, plants, and creatures.

I love to draw! I teach figure drawing and perspective courses online. Sometimes I also draw storyboards for companies like Universal Studios, The BBC, and Aardman Animations.  

I began drawing on March 28th 2010, after reading a book about needing to do 10,000 hours of practice to be a professional international standard at your craft.  I chose drawing randomly from a list of other things that I could have ended up spending 10,000 hours in, and I have been drawing ever since!  Before that, I never really drew and had no interest in it.  I started because I had the drive to practice a craft.  It was almost a quest in how seriously I took it! I had to get to a certain level! I realise now, there's no need to try to "get somewhere" with your drawing, and you can start enjoying it immediately, from the minute you pick up the pencil! To date, I've done more than 20,000 hours of drawing, and I'm still learning every day!

I teach a relaxed approach to drawing where the focus is on enjoying the process rather than worrying about the results.  The whole point of drawing is to have fun and enjoy yourself! That's why we do it as kids.  At some point, many people lose that attitude and start to take it all seriously.  I hope thse you'll see that there's no need to feel pressure to make a "pretty" draw in my courseg, and that you can always approach it feeling relaxed!

Kilpatrick's work has been featured in publications such as Fortune, the L.A. Times, Nautilus magazine, and the Wall Street Journal. His illustration can be found on the Olympic medal for the XIX Winter Games in Salt Lake City. Most recently his work can be found in the form of a series of large-scale murals on the newly built Little Caesar’s Arena in Detroit.

Additionally, he has exhibited his artwork in Detroit, New York, Los Angeles, Philadelphia, Tokyo, and Miami. He has regularly shown his work in both group and solo gallery shows, and most recently in January 2019 at M Contemporary gallery in Ferndale, Michigan. This recent show included prints, woodcuts, paintings, and a collaboration with renowned bespoke shoemaker and artist Noriyuki Misawa.

teacher.aboutMe:
Jono Dry is a self-taught artist from South Africa, born in 1989 in Pretoria and currently residing in Cape Town. Known for his large-scale graphite drawings, Dry blends hyperrealism with surrealism to create visually and emotionally engaging pieces.

Inspired by his efforts to make sense of his relationships, Dry works intuitively, often discovering deeper meanings and coincidences in his art years after their creation. His work serves as a form of therapy, profoundly influenced by his experiences with anxiety and loneliness. The meticulous technique and attention to detail in his drawings allow him to produce photorealistic images that often feature dark, empty backgrounds, isolating his subjects and highlighting their emotional depth.

Recurring motifs such as kudu horns, flowers and plants, hummingbirds, and bandages weave through his pieces, each symbolizing different facets of his journey. The kudu horns represent resilience and strength, flowers and plants signify growth and healing, hummingbirds evoke a sense of fleeting beauty and joy, and bandages hint at the ongoing process of emotional recovery. These elements intertwine, creating a visual narrative that reflects both the fragility and the resilience of the human spirit.

Jono has exhibited his work both locally and internationally, including shows at the Zeitz MOCAA in Cape Town, the Vienna Contemporary Art Fair, and the Di Carta Papermade exhibition in Italy. His dedication to his craft is evident in each piece, often taking months to complete, reflecting his commitment to perfection and intricate planning.
Dry also shares his creative process and techniques through social media and educational videos, fostering a community of artists and art enthusiasts who learn from and engage with his work. Through his art, Jono Dry aims to bridge the personal and the universal, connecting with audiences on a deeply emotional level and shedding light on the hidden aspects of the human experience.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello, I'm Natasha, I'm a full-time wet felting artist, teacher and author who has been addicted to wet felting since 2005!  Although I enjoy all types of decorative wet felting, I'm particularly interested in three-dimensional structural forms which can be created with wool fibre.  This has led me to specialise in the felting on a ball resist technique to create felted bags, baskets and bowls, which I regularly teach on workshops in my studio in the seaside town of Exmouth, Devon on the UK south coast.  

I love experimenting with wet felting techniques and materials to develop new projects, as well as sharing my knowledge to help others develop their feltmaking skills to create beautiful finished items.  This has led me to create several online courses and tutorials on wet felting.  I've also written over 25 magazine project articles covering felting and textile craft, including for the International Feltmakers Association (IFA) magazine Felt Matters.  My first book, Wet Felting, which covers all aspects of wet felting, from flat felting to working with both two and three-dimensional resists, was published in April 2022. My second book, Three-dimensional Wet Felting, was published in May 2024 and focuses in depth on felting on a ball.  It covers all the techniques you need for successful results, along with a range of inspiring projects to create yourself.

Sharing the magic of wet felting has become a real passion for me and I regularly share videos and photos of workshops and wet felted pieces on my social media accounts @natashasmarttextiles, where you can find more inspiration for your own creations.

teacher.aboutMe: Hi! My name is Erin and I'm and I'm a self-taught embroidery artist, specializing in floral embroidery. I picked up embroidery (and several other mediums and fiber crafts) in 2010 while healing from a traumatic car accident using books and iron-on patterns I ordered online. Learning embroidery gave me a space to be creative and focus on something positive. I put my embroidery journey on hold in 2016 to further my education. In early 2020, myself and the rest of the world found ourselves spending a lot more time at home. This extra time allowed me to dive back into my beloved stitching. Eventually, a friend suggested I start making embroidery stitch tutorials... SO I DID! Nothing could have prepared me for what happened next. My stitch tutorials were a huge hit and my TikTok channel grew exponentially. In 2022, I started my own business selling embroidery patterns, kits, and all of my favorite embroidery tools. Today, High Crafting is the largest embroidery channel on TikTok, and getting to share my love of embroidery with people all around the world brings me so much joy.

teachers.aboutMe:
I am an embroideress inspired by nature and the seasons. 
Painting with thread is my dearest passion and most loved art form. It allows you to create realistic effects by using one single strand of thread, this technique is often referred to as needlepainting, threadpainting or silk shading. You can create beautiful colour gradients, magical details and flowing stitch directions that are perfect if you want to embroider animals, people, flora and fauna. I have been stitching every day since I fell in love with embroidery in 2013.

I think it’s important during this technological era of the world to take the time to create something with your own two hands. It makes you feel connected and rooted to the world. When I'm not embroidering you can find me exploring my local english countryside, reading books about folklore or making memories with friends and family. 

You can find more of my tutorials in my Etsy shop :)

Hi! I’m Yulia and I’m a self-taught hand embroidery artist based in Cleveland, Ohio. You can find me on Instagram @mossandfeather. I’ve been embroidering for three years now. I’ve always liked art, like painting and drawing, but it wasn’t until I discovered embroidery that creating art became one of the most important aspects of my life. 

I specialize in thread painting, which is a technique used to create realistic embroidery. It’s a lot like painting on a canvas but using thread instead of paint. Using this technique, you can achieve fine artistic detail, including shading, highlights and smooth color gradients. 

I’ve always been inspired by nature and animals and I love how well thread mimics the look of fur and feathers. It’s really the perfect medium for the type of art I like to create.

I am an embroiderer who lives in the north of England, close by the beautiful North York Moors and the nature that inspires my work. I use needle painting embroidery techniques and sewing thread to create my embroideries, and as well as selling original pieces I have worked with a variety of publishing clients to make embroidered book cover designs and children’s books.
I fell in love with embroidery and the meditative nature of this work the first time I picked up a needle, and I hope I can help introduce more people to this amazing craft!

Defne Güntürkün is a textile and fashion designer, an embroidery artist from Istanbul, Turkey. She received her bachelor’s and master of arts degrees at Mimar Sinan University of Fine Arts in Istanbul. She studied at the Accademia Dİ Belle Arti Di Bologna in Bologna, Italy as a part of her MA degree. Her master thesis with the title “Handling fashion case under color trends” was completed in 2010.
         She has been designing fabric patterns as a part of her professional activities for over 15 years and she has been a self-taught embroidery artist since 2011. Her long term experience in fabric designing, dealing with color combinations, working on nature inspired illustrations is reflected in her embroideries.
         She has an art studio in downtown Istanbul, Karaköy, where she spends a big part of her days doing what she loves the most.

Hola! My name is Santiago Celio Cioli, but everyone knows me as Santo Cielo (kind of an anagram with my name).
In my childhood, I remember being surrounded by fabrics, threads, and dressmakers. For many years, my mother owned a haberdashery in the little town where I was born, and I tend to think this had an influence on my later decision to study Industrial Design in Textiles.
I started learning embroidery in 2015 while I was doing a joint degree thesis about hand embroidery and national identity: We created an interview/workshop system where embroiderers, in this case, women of various ages, would tell us stories relating to their craft, teaching us one or two stitches at the same time. Thanks to them, I was able to discover and learn beautiful techniques.
Nowadays, I focus mostly on portraits of animals and humans using the thread painting technique. Many portraits are created in response to customer requests I receive through Instagram and my website; through family photos, I get involved in people’s lives to create a memory they can treasure for years to come.
I love to impart my passion and skills to others because I find beauty in the verbal and mimetic transmission of this knowledge, just as those women did for me.

Hello there! My name is Ciara a.k.a PRETTY STRANGE. I’m an independent artist specializing in lettering, illustration, murals, and hand-embroidery. In 2017, I started Pretty Strange Design with a mission to make eye-popping, beautiful, and offbeat creations that inject imagination into everyday life. 

I’m always seeking to make work that is well-crafted and intriguing, but also deeply thoughtful and socially-conscious. I take my role as an artist, encourager, and truth-teller to heart. 

I’ve been featured by Insider, Better Homes & Gardens, Frankie, and PopSugar and some of my past clients include Cosmopolitan, Verizon, Madewell, Ann Taylor LOFT, and Facebook.

I am a contemporary multimedia artist working in mixed media, embroidery, paint, etc. to produce thought provoking artwork that comments on social and environmental injustice. My Caribbean background has influenced my work in the early stages of my career as I have always been drawn to vibrant colors, people and emotions. 

However, after coming to the United States to pursue an education and career in the arts, I discovered a deeper passion for activism and the ability to use my artwork to evoke positive change and unity in society. 

Since graduating from the University of Tampa in May 2020, some of my most recent achievements include a TIME magazine commission to produce the hand embroidered flag that appears on the cover of the August 31st/ September 7th issue 2020, a commission from the Washington Post to capture the history made by Vice President Kamala Harris and even appearing as a keynote speaker for Adobe MAX; sharing my journey and emphasizing the importance of art as a vehicle for activism.

My unique hand embroidery work has also been featured in Colossal magazine, The Jealous Curator blog, The American Craft Council, Embroidery Mag UK and Domestika. I hope to inspire other young aspiring artists to experiment, pursue their dreams and create art that tells a story.

I'm Cristin Morgan, fiber artist, illustrator, and author of Hoop Dreams: Modern Hand Embroidery. I live and stitch in beautiful Richmond, Virginia. I love what I do, and it is an honor to share it with you!

I'm a lifelong crafter with a deep love for making things. I've been embroidering since elementary school, mostly just for fun, but professionally since 2015. I'm self-taught, which means that over the years I've practiced and practiced some more until I've landed on a style and method that works for me. Embroidery is a traditional medium, but I love that there is plenty of room for exploration and innovation. I still love experimenting and learning and incorporating new methods and materials. The possibilities are truly endless!

My work is influenced by many things, but most often I find inspiration in the colors and textures of the materials I use. I really love using vibrant color palettes in my work, along with bold and clean shapes. I find it so satisfying to bring a simple, stylized shape to life with texture and color! 

When I'm not embroidering, I play roller derby for River City Roller Derby here in Richmond. (My derby name is Needle & Dread!) Other things I love include: animals, nature, adventures, and vegan snacks. I want to live in a tiny house some day.

Hi! My name is Michelle Staub and I'm a self-taught embroidery artist that has been creating custom hand-stitched pet portraits since 2014. I am based out of Cincinnati, Ohio where I craft gorgeous keepsakes using only needle and thread.

My biggest inspiration is the love that people share with their pets. It’s so rewarding to create a personalized piece of artwork to commemorate a pet and celebrate its life. I am unbelievably grateful to make such meaningful and personal art for people.

The technique I use to embroider is called thread painting, or needle painting, which came naturally to me after studying oil painting in college. The stitches you create are so similar to brush strokes and although you can't mix thread colors like you can paint, you can still create beautiful gradients and capture tiny details. I've been enamored with embroidery ever since my first cat portrait where I realized how perfect thread was as a medium to replicate the likeness of fur. Since then, I've spent thousands of hours learning and refining my technique and I can't wait to share what I've learned with you!

You can find more of my work on Instagram @StitchingSabbatical and at StitchingSabbatical.com

teacher.aboutMe:
Domestika is the fastest-growing creative community where the best creative experts share their knowledge and skills through professionally produced online courses.

It all started as an online forum and a small but dynamic showcase of creative professionals, designed to help them connect and learn from each other.

Inspired by their thriving community, Domestika widened its reach by producing online courses for anyone interested in unleashing their creative potential and connecting with like-minded creatives from around the world.

Domestika carefully curates the teacher roster and produces all the courses in-house, to ensure a high-quality online learning experience for everyone. Today, the online community is home to over 6 million people from around the world who are curious and passionate about learning new creative skills.

teachers.aboutMe:
Never did I think that learning how to sew my own clothes would afford me the sort of freedom I have had since I bought my first sewing machine in 2013. Ever since that year, I have gone ahead to win the popular BBC show: Great British Sewing Bee in April 2019.

I am Juliet Uzor. A mum of 1 and an enthusiastic dressmaker who enjoys sewing clothes that fit my style, body type and personality. I trained and worked as a top ranking primary school teacher and recently took on sewing and craft content creation. I have also received training at the London College of Fashion in digital sewing pattern creation. 

I work as a freelance sewing and craft magazine columnist. I also use my YouTube channel, blog and social media platforms to inspire people to create and style their own clothes through easy-to-follow sewing tutorials, tips and tricks content.

My name is Elisalex and I’m the founder of By Hand London sewing patterns. It has been my work and passion for almost a decade to create sewing patterns for people who love to dress up, stand out and become the creators of their own style, and to teach the often daunting art of fitting, encouraging and supporting our customers on their journey to making fabulous clothes that fit like a dream.

I live in London in the UK with my teenage old son and our two cats :) 

At By Hand London our aesthetic philosophy is: more is always more! Our sewing patterns, and all of the supporting tutorials, hacks and sewalongs we post on our blog are a celebration of the limitlessness that learning to sew can have over your style. Even the plainest of days can be a special occasion when you choose to dress up in your handmade finest! 

The beauty of learning to sew is that you will never stop learning, and you never know what tangent you might meander off on at various points in your journey! I won't ever get too comfortable in my skills, or declare myself an "expert" as I am constantly learning and improving, and the best thing about that is that I will never get bored! There will always be a new challenge waiting for me around the corner...

Learning to sew will probably change your life in ways you never expected. I always tell my students (and myself!) that perfection is never the goal, only progress. Be patient with yourself and learn at your own pace, celebrate your mistakes and "fails" for the learning curves that they are, and remember to marvel at all of your creative triumphs!

In my work, I use a sewing machine to create thread drawings and large scale installations. Using my sewing machine, I am able to create a range of designs- from objects in my home like backpacks and shoes to brightly coloured abstract patterns. I often sew into fabric that dissolves in water so  I can build up stitched lines on a temporary surface.  The crossing threads create strength so that when the fabric is dissolved, the thread drawing can hold together without a base. With only the thread remaining, these images appear as though they would be easily unraveled and seemingly on the verge of falling apart, despite the works raveled strength. I am interested in thread's assumed vulnerability,  its ability to unravel, and its strength when it is sewn together.
I show my work in galleries nationally and internationally with recent solo exhibitions in Ottawa (ON), Virginia Beach (VA) and Vancouver (BC) and has completed residencies at Harbourfront Centre’s Textile Studio in Toronto, and the Klondike Institute of Art and Culture in Dawson City, Yukon. I have received awards and scholarships from the Ontario Crafts Council, The Canada Council for the Arts, The Handweavers and Spinners Guild of America, The Young Masters Art Prize, The Ontario Society of Artists, The Surface Design Association and The Embroiderers Guild of America.

I'm Monisola Omotoso, Moni to my friends. In my 30+ years working in fashion design and pattern cutting, I'm still enthusiastic about the subjects. I've designed and pattern cut my own labels and accessories range which were sold throughout London, Europe and Japan. I've freelanced as a flat pattern cutter and draper for fashion companies such as Birdsong London and Alexander McQueen.  

In 2012, I qualified with a PGCE and have since taught at various institutions, including the Royal College of Art, Central Saint Martins, Morley College, Liverpool John Moores and the London College of Fashion. 
I'm passionate about education and use my lecturing skills and extensive pattern cutting knowledge effectively in my company. Having developed a range of learning resources, the Cut & Spread™ pattern making kits, and produced mini, speedy educational videos, Pattern Cutting Deconstructed is recognised by my Instagram followers as the go-to platform for fashion creatives who want to learn pattern cutting skills in an accessible fun way. I'm renowned for my step-by-step teaching approach and ability to make confusing calculations deceptively simple. I also have a keen eye for the finer details that can make or break the look of a student’s designs.

My name is Chinelo Bally, I am a fashion designer, an author, a television personality and an avid lover of all things creative and creating. I specialise in a unique method of garment production called Freehand Cutting. 

Over the past 10 years I have shared my skill with interested students and audiences all over the world. I run workshops all over the UK, regularly participate in craft exhibitions, and take part in loads of fun craft centred series for national television stations in the UK. My first television appearance was as a contestant on BBC2's "The Great British Sewing Bee" (season 2) where I came second. 

Following the success of the show, I have written 2 bestselling books, "Freehand Fashion" (2015) and "Sew Chinelo" (2021), that guides the reader step by step through the projects ensuring that makers of all abilities can participate in this thrilling craft. 

My passion for fashion design and dressmaking takes root in fund memories dotted throughout my life. From nostalgic memories of looking through my mum's wardrobes and trunks as a child, to walking through the narrow lanes of the fabric section of old Alade Market in 90s Lagos, playing with scrap off cuts from my mum's store to describing my desired dress to the very patient local dressmaker. I've always had a special appreciation for clothes and fabric, experimenting with embellishments and up-cycling store bought clothes. In January 2010, I decided that I was tried of ill fitting clothes that didn’t fully represent my style profile; I bought my very first sewing machine the day I decided I would start making my own clothes; and so the story began! I learnt the basics of freehand cutting from my aunty and then went on to develop my own version of the traditional African method of garment construction. 

The allure of this method is how beautifully the clothes fit. There is also the creative freedom you are afforded because the starting point isn't a pre-prescribed design by the commercial pattern company; you may chose to start off with a design in mind and stay guided or you can let it evolve organically into another amazing creation; freehand cutting is truly liberating. 

Freehand cutting help you develop a deeper understanding of how and why clothes fit the body, this understanding is essential for upgrading you dressmaking skills from basic to extraordinary. 

I like to describe my style as a celebration of the many facets of femininity, it’s s a celebration of the female form in all its variations. If you love originality, appreciate a great fit and want to freely explore and experiment with you style, then Freehand cutting is for you.

I'm Luisa Hurtado, but you might know me better as @designerluisa from TikTok, or @imluluisa on Instagram. I'm a passionate upcycler and Fashion Designer.

I grew up in a small town in Mexico, where as a child, fashion always fascinated me. I dreamt of wearing unique clothes, different from what everyone else had. 
I realized I wanted to start making my own garments because I was asking way too much from my grandma and my mom. So I decided to learn!
I was able to attend a university in my own state, in Mexico, where I graduated with honors in Fashion Design & Garment Industry. 
Right after I graduated I was an assistant teacher in my own university teaching sewing & pattern making.. After that I had a few collections come out and Fashion Shows at city events that allowed me to reach a new market.
Not long after that, I met the love of my life, and moved to the United States where I started from scratch, without recognition, which was challenging.
I had fun during this time as well, I even made my own wedding dress and created some fun pieces for friends and family. I sold my designs at small local events, always seeking ways to share my passion for fashion.

This passion to share & teach led me to start my Youtube channel, and later TikTok. 

It was on TikTok where my work, particularly a backpack made from upcycled jeans, caught the eye of many, including major brands like Levi's.

Now, I am focusing on sharing my knowledge with others and helping people around the world get started on their own projects, prioritizing creativity, sustainability, and lots of fun!

-Luisa xx

teacher.aboutMe:
My love for nature and miniature things began early when I first saw bonsai in The Karate Kid movie. This art form captivated me, and I soon learned that it could be created with almost any tree species. My journey began over 15 years ago when my mother gifted me my first bonsai. Unfortunately, I lacked the knowledge to care for it, but a year later, my aunt gifted me another, reigniting my passion.

During the pandemic, as I expanded my collection, I discovered how therapeutic and calming bonsai could be. It provided solace during tough times, helping me find peace and focus. My skills grew as I entered competitions, earning recognition and prizes, including a second-place finish in a bonsai styling competition among the top artists in the state. This accomplishment motivated me and showed that I could potentially pursue bonsai as a career, especially since I had only been taking it seriously for a few months, while most competitors had years of experience. The following year, I won the President’s Award at the state bonsai exhibition for having one of the best trees in the exhibit.

I am self-taught, having primarily learned through reading many books and hands-on practice, later enhancing my skills with educational videos and guidance from masters better than me, most importantly I never stop educating my self & learning more each day. Today, I run a professional bonsai nursery where I teach in-person classes, offer workshops, and lead demonstrations. I sell and ship trees across the United States and travel for bonsai projects. I’m excited to share my passion and help you appreciate the calming art of bonsai.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hi! I'm Hannah Veiga, a multidisciplinary artist and educator primarily practicing in pyrography. You may know me from my online presence on Instagram and TikTok as @hannahveiga.studio.

I work from my home studio creating original works of art, but the primary thing that grew my business as an artist from the very start of my career, is pet portraiture. I love to create realistic portraits while including a bit of whimsy and character through additions of florals, mushrooms, or any nature-related element to build a composition and bring the portrait to life. 

In all of my work, whether it's an original or custom piece, I strive to create designs that work with the wood and compliment the existing beauty within the grain. To create something that doesn't act to cover up the wood, but to merge as though it was meant to be there all along. Each of my original artworks is a sanctuary, offering a moment of peace, wonder, or reflection, inviting you to journey beyond the boundaries of the ordinary.

 I'm excited to share with you how you can bring these themes and techniques into your own works of art!

teacher.aboutMe:
Hello, everyone! I’m Dani, the creative mind and maker behind CJ Design (in English) and Danii’s Ways (en Español). I’m originally from Chile but now call Canada home, where I live with my family—Cale, Luca, and Isabella.

I learned to knit at the age of 8, thanks to my grandmother, who patiently taught me. I picked it up quickly and, over the years, continued to knit here and there. During my university days in Chile, I taught my best friend how to knit, and together we launched a small brand selling knitted hats. That experience sparked my entrepreneurial spirit, and I’ve been chasing creative dreams ever since. Turning my hobby into a full-time career is truly a dream come true!

Fast forward to today—I’m a full-time content creator, pattern designer, and YouTuber. It’s been an incredible journey to do what I love every single day. I started my YouTube channel in Spanish back in 2016, focusing on sewing tutorials. Over time, I discovered crochet and fell head over heels for its endless possibilities. That passion led me to shift from sewing to knitting and crocheting entirely. Once I felt confident enough with my English, I launched CJ Design. Many people ask what it stands for—it means Cozy Journey Designs. It was a spur-of-the-moment decision that stuck, but it perfectly captures my creative journey.

These days, CJ Design is my main focus, although I still share patterns in both English and Spanish. My designs combine modern aesthetics with cozy, approachable vibes. They’re simple yet stylish, and I aim to help you create pieces that you’ll not only love but also feel proud of.

teacher.aboutMe:
Estudié Economía y Periodismo y encontré en el Marketing Digital el equilibrio perfecto entre la comunicación y los números. Trabajé más de 3 años en Google, en las oficinas de Buenos Aires y Ciudad de México. Allí tuve el privilegio de trabajar con más de 60 PyMes de todo Latinoamérica y el desafío de acompañarlos hacia la digitalización y guiarlos en el entendimiento de la medición de sus acciones para tomar decisiones. 

Con más de 10 años trabajando con Google Analytics, me declaro un apasionado de la herramienta. Poder tener información detallada de quién entra a tu sitio y cómo se comporta una vez en él, para poder después tomar decisiones de optimización de pauta digital o de diseño de la página, creo que es fascinante. 

En 2018 ingresé a EnviaFlores.com, el mayor e-Commerce de Flores de todo México, como Director de Marketing. Estuve a cargo de la estrategia de mercadotecnia y comercial liderando a un equipo de más de 25 personas.
Allí estuve a cargo de la estrategia en Google Ads, Facebook Ads, Redes Sociales, Email Marketing y el Calendario Promocional. También lideré el Comité de UX de la compañía durante el Rediseño de su Sitio Web.

En 2020 me sumé como Head of Performance Marketing en Síclo, una cadena de indoor cycling. Lideré los esfuerzos por conseguir suscriptores para su app Síclo+ durante la pandemia, que se enfocaba en personas que quisieran entrenar desde sus casas. Manejé la estrategia de Paid Marketing con foco en adquisición y sus canales para generar retención de clientes existentes.

En 2021 fundé mi propio eCommerce junto a dos socios, en el que vendíamos productos de decoración y construcción para el hogar a través de marketplaces como Mercado Libre y Amazon.

Actualmente me dedico a dar servicios de consultoría de Growth Marketing de manera independiente. Capacitaciones para empresas, tanto en Google Ads, Facebook Ads, TikTok Ads y Google Analytics; Consultorías de Funcionalidad de Sitio Web; Consultoría Estratégicas de Marketing Digital y Auditorías a Agencias y Equipos Internos de Marketing.

Aparte de eso, me apasiona la fotografía (Instagram: @gabiperelman), amo viajar y jugar al hockey sobre césped.

teachers.aboutMe:
Hola, mi nombre es Josefina Allendes y soy artista plástica.

Siempre me han interesado las manualidades, especialmente el arte textil. Tanto que cuando era niña en vez de jugar con las muñecas les hacía ropa.

Además de artista textil, también soy escultora especializada en cerámica gress, un proceso con el que me encanta mancharme las manos y que compagino con el bordado.

Hace algunos años cree Wild Spirit, una marca de ropa y zapatos para niños 100% hecha a mano.

También colaboro con diseñadores y decoradores en la confección de piezas únicas. He trabajado para marcas como Yirko Sivirich, Bito Feris, Donna Cattiva, Nel Blue o Galera.


Me encanta la libertad y creatividad de la técnica del bordado. Dejarme llevar por las líneas que voy trazando y el sonido del hilo al pasar. Es un proceso mágico que te lleva a un lugar de paz.

Mi trabajo parte de la naturaleza.  Todo empieza con el color y las texturas que encuentro tras un paseo por el campo.  Esa tranquilidad te entrega para ponerte creativa y empezar a bordar.

Mi máxima inspiración son los árboles. Me encanta detenerme un momento para apreciar la belleza que los hace diferentes. Sus ramas y sus hojas  son pura vida,  textura y buena energía.  En ellos encuentro todo, volumen, textura, color y movimiento.

Artesana con aguja e hilo.
Desde que tengo uso de razón he tenido una aguja en la mano.
Mi abuela me enseñó a coser, a bordar, a hacer ganchillo, a tejer. Manualidades para tenerme entretenida en los muchos días que pasaba con ellos (mis abuelos).
Despues de muchos años, he encontrado en sus enseñanzas, una forma de vida.
Honrar su legado y adaptarlo, de una forma única y original, a la sociedad actual. 
Tradición y tecnología, unidas, para crear objetos llenos de vida.
Bordados en madera.

Hola! Soy Malena, la persona detrás de la marca Pimienta Joyería. Mi interés y experimentación en distintos oficios me llevó a aprender joyería donde encontré un espacio cómodo para trabajar tanto con el metal como con otros materiales y técnicas, como el hilo, la tela y el bordado, donde siempre puedo jugar y dejar correr la imaginación.

Soy Docente de Artes Visuales con orientación en Escenografía, carrera de la Universidad de La Plata, en donde trabajé en muchas disciplinas que trato de combinar con lo que voy aprendiendo en distintos talleres particulares y algunos saberes conseguidos de forma autodidacta. Es así que dentro de Pimienta hago piezas con cuidado y atención en  los detalles, inspiradas en elementos hogareños, como las plantas de mi patio, recuerdos de la infancia y las mascotas que me acompañan, mezclando técnicas clásicas de la joyería con otras de distintos oficios.

Hello! I'm Sara Pastrana, the brainchild behind Flourishing Fibers but I'm also a full-time designer based in Los Angeles, California. I have a son that I just adore. He is my motivation and my number one fan.

I learned to cross-stitch as a teenager but didn’t start exploring embroidery as an art medium until much later in life. In 2012 I began my embroidery art journey by experimenting with all sorts of materials. I ultimately found my niche working with wood and paper. Over the years, my journey has transformed from experiment, to hobby, to passion.

Embroidering unconventional materials allows me to be both creative and technical. Each piece I create challenges me to find a balance between what I envision and how it’s going to be achieved. The design process is fun, relaxing, and without any restrictions but the execution requires meticulous planning. In the end, it is the thread that really brings the work to life.

My inspiration often comes from opposite ends of the spectrum. Some designs are inspired by nature, while others are inspired by geometry. I find beauty in the symmetry and repetitiveness of patterns just as much as the fluidity of nature.

I'm an artist and educator, originally from New York State, now living and working in Richmond, VA, USA. I have a background in textile design and I run the fiber and textile program at Virginia Commonwealth University.

I believe there is a strong relationship between the land and our interior landscapes. When we are connected to the land, we’re connected to ourselves, and one another.
 
I bring together materials and processes that express the union of humanity and the physical world. Whether stitching, drawing, planting seeds, or harvesting, my hands echo the gestures made by thousands of hands over thousands of years and I feel connected to the lineage of people working with textiles, plants and the land. Stitching, like agriculture, can be functional-- a technical solution to join materials/a means of survival-- or, both can be done purely in service of the soul, lifting the spirit through beauty and wonder.

teachers.aboutMe: Soy Miguel Bustos, llevo 25 años dibujando como obsesión, 15 años como profesión y los últimos 10 años entregado a la tarea de enseñar los que he aprendido, durante los cuales me he centrado en la figura humana como inspiración y  recurso primario de mis imagenes, llegando a entenderla y poder explicarla a todo tipo de público con recursos que he recopilado a lo largo de mi carrera como dibujante. Trabajo como docente en Casatinta desde 2012 realizando talleres de dibujo, anatomía e ilustración. También he trabajado como ilustrador para editoriales como Rey Naranjo (Gabo: memorias de una vida mágica, 2012), Ediciones Vestigio (El Pornógrafo, 2019) y Editorial Planeta (El difícil oficio de perdonar, 2019).

Soy pintor y docente. Licenciado en Bellas Artes por la Universidad Politécnica de Valencia en la especialidad de pintura. Durante muchos años desarrolle mi labor como docente y gestor ligado a la Universidad de la Laguna donde obtuve mi DEA (Diploma estudios avanzados), gracias diferentes becas de investigación.
En los últimos años he desarrollado mi proyecto pictórico entorno al desnudo y el retrato participando en diferentes exposiciones colectivas e individuales tanto en España como en diferentes países Europeos.
Como docente realizo demostraciones e imparto workshops por toda Europa.

Soy Dani Torrent, y nací en Barcelona en 1974. Licenciado en Historia del Arte, y tras cursar estudios en dirección de cine y Bellas artes, finalmente llego a la ilustración donde encuentro mi verdadera vocación. Ahí puedo aplicar los conocimientos de narrativa visual del cine y el bagaje visual de la Historia del Arte. 

Desde 2010 me dedico a la ilustración, sobretodo en el campo de la literatura infantil y juvenil, especializándome en la creación de álbumes ilustrados, de los que a menudo soy autor tanto del texto como de la ilustración. En ellos me gusta tratar temas complejos, tales como el paso del tiempo, la muerte, o la melancolía inherente en la felicidad huyendo de los estereotipos, lo que sitúa a mis libros en un punto inconcreto entre lo infantil y lo adulto.

En estos años he ido pasando de una ilustración con un acabado más pulido a uno más gestual, elíptico  y expresivo, para lo cual he encontrado en las técnicas secas tales como el lápiz o el pastel mi vehículo de expresión ideal. Entre otros premios obtuve el Junceda a mejor ilustración adulta, el Jóvenes creadores de la Fundación Fita, el 2º Manuel António da Mota (Portugal), y finalista en el CJBooks de Corea, el Hiii illustration, o el Compostela, gracias al que publiqué mi primer álbum en 2011.

Como artista plástico he expuesto en España, Italia, Francia, México o Nueva York.

Paralelamente desarrollo una labor como educador y profesor de ilustración, en centros como el MNAC de Barcelona, IED, Visions Centre d'il·lustració, escuela Llotja, CIFO l'hospitalet o Spazio MEC 8Italia). También he realizado talleres y charlas en diferentes lugares de España, Inglaterra, Ucrania o Colombia.

Dibujo desde que tengo uso de razón y es una de las cosas que más disfruto hacer, es mi verdadera pasión y creo que todos deberíamos tener la oportunidad de hacerlo!

 Cada dibujo es una nueva experiencia, un desafío y una oportunidad. El dibujo es la forma de arte más sincera y la base más sólida para trabajar con cualquier otra técnica. Por eso creo que tan sólo con un lápiz y un papel se pueden hacer obras increíbles.

El dibujo nos enseña sobre la frustración, superación, la paciencia, ansiedad y también sobre el disfrute del hoy y del ahora. Esta obsesión por la línea me llevó a trabajar con gente como The Rock (Dwayne Johnson), Josh Brolin, PayPal, MercadoLibre, Canal 13, Marcelo Tinelli, entre muchos otros.

Pueden sumarse a mi Patreon, donde tienen más de 175 videos con tutoriales, procesos completos y donde también van a poder coordinar una reunión virtual conmigo para mostrarme su trabajo y yo poder ayudarlos en vivo!

Los invito a acompañarnos mutuamente en este increíble e infinito viaje lleno de líneas que es el dibujo!

I was born in Cartagena de Indias -Colombia on 1988, graduated from Visual Arts in the Javeriana University of Bogota in 2011, made an online visual essay course in schoolism Canada on 2013, and an MFA. in painting at Savannah College of art and design in Savannah Georgia until 2020.
I started as an illustrator for magazines and companies since 2008 in Colombia and abroad, such as EuroDisney, Der Spiegel, Tv Channel Historia in Quebec, Detroit Business, Reveu Long Course, Semana, El Tiempo, and many others. 
Recently I had the opportunity to work  as a teacher at SCAD where I taught painting and mixed media in 2020. Currently I am working as a painter, preparing for my upcoming solo show in 2023 at the Museum of modern art in Cartagena.
