teachers.aboutMe:
Matt Kenney is a professional furniture maker that has written dozens of articles and two books about woodworking. As a child growing up in Florida, he made tree forts and skate ramps, but for the last 20 years he has been making furniture. His passion for the craft led to an editorial job at Fine Woodworking magazine, where he wrote articles, was feature in how-to videos, and co-hosted the popular Shop Talk Live podcast. Starting in Spring 2015, Matt made 52 boxes in 52 weeks. That project became the basis for his first book, 52 Boxes in 52 Weeks (Taunton Press). He left the magazine in 2018 to spend more time with his tools. He’s been making furniture, traveling the US and world to teach, and writing since. Matt constantly strives to improve his craftsmanship and design. The result of his efforts is furniture that is modern but grounded in the best of classic design, able to sit harmoniously alongside a wide range of furniture styles, and built to survive generations of daily use.

Matt’s passion for the craft led him to learn the Japanese art of kumiko, which he incorporates into his furniture and uses to create beautiful decorative wall hangings. His love for kumiko pushed him to share the art with others, so he began to teach it and eventually wrote a book about it: The Art of Kumiko (Blue Hills Press, 2020).  He has taught kumiko both in the United States and internationally, and believes that its popularity is due to its delicate elegance and stunning geometric patterns. Although kumiko appears complex and difficult to make, Matt’s experience has allowed him to develop techniques that make the art approachable to beginners and seasoned woodworkers, and that produce excellent results even the first time you give it a try.

We are Jack Bibbings and Matthew Hensby. We make contemporary wooden furniture from our workshop in London with a focus on using hand tools to produce practical everyday pieces suited to contemporary homes. 

Much of our work is characterised by the tools we use. We work predominantly with hand tools because of the warmth and individuality they impart and where the judgement and skill required means that things are never predictable and without challenge. This approach contributes significantly to the feel of what we make.

Rather than producing modern furniture using modern processes, or traditional processes to produce traditional designs, we marry traditional craft with contemporary design to make work that feels grounded and relevant.

My name is Alexandre Chappel, I’m an Industrial designer, maker, and Youtuber. 

I’m originally from Switzerland but I’ve spent the past 20 years of my life in Norway. 

This is also where I studied industrial design and learned to become a fine furniture maker. In the past, I’ve done many different things, but all of them with the common theme of creating something. I’ve designed and fabricated furniture for clients built prototypes for products and made all sorts of cool things for myself. 

In Design school, we were lucky enough to have a big workshop with lots of tools. And we got to play around with everything from metal and woodworking to laser cutting and 3d printing. Me already having a background in woodworking I felt right at home and fell in love with the possibilities of combining these technologies with each other. 

I’m lucky enough that I turned my hobby into my job, so for the past 3 years now, I’ve made videos about making things on Youtube. If you want you can check out my channel youtube.com/achappel 

I love doing what I do, being able to inspire people to make something and pursue their passions. 
And I hope I can inspire you to try out something new and start making something.

Urvi Sharma is a furniture and product designer based in Providence RI. She completed her BFA in Furniture Design at the Rhode Island School of Design in 2017 and in 2018, co-founded design studio INDO- with her partner Manan Narang.
Urvi uses a layered design process, incorporating personal narrative, traditional techniques and modern ways of making into her work. Mirroring her experiences growing up in New Delhi, India and working for designers worldwide, her products connect with their audience in an increasingly diasporic world while embodying unique identities with the stories they tell.
In 2021, Urvi made her TV debut as a contestant on Ellen's Next Great Designer, a furniture design and build competition hosted by Ellen DeGeneres and streaming now on HBO Max.

Sandy or Sand to his friends and family is a bespoke furniture designer-maker based in Beckenham, SE London. 

Previous to setting up Sand Buchanan , Sandy had a 10 year career in the Oil & Gas E&P sector working around the world as a Geoscientist. He holds a BSc and MSc in Geoscience.

After several redundancies, a general dislike for big corporate politics and a growing unease about what the sector was doing Sandy turned to making and craft in the pursuit of meaningful work.

His work exclusively uses fallen British grown timber from as local to his workshop as possible. With this emphasis on sustainability Sandy's work celebrates natural imperfections to reconnect clients with the natural properties that make timber so unique.

I am the founder and lead instructor at the London School of Furniture Making. 

38 years in the industry has seen me work in areas as diverse as construction, furniture making and  guitar making. While I have gained formal qualifications in many subjects I am first and foremost a woodworker, lover of tools, tinkerer, life-long learner and avid reader of anything to do with making stuff.

I love passing on what I've learnt and in a teaching career that spans nearly three decades, I've introduced hundreds of students to the joy of woodworking.

When my wife and I were living in Las Vegas, about to get married and move into our first apartment, we wanted good quality furniture made with actual wood. I borrowed some tools, found a youtube video, and took a crack at building a dining table. A dining room set turned into building a bedroom set, then into a building a living room set and eventually pieces for friends and family. 

After a move to southern Indiana we had a chance to reset. Woodworking had turned into a side hustle for local clients ran out of my garage for the first 3 years before transitioning into full-time work and leasing a space. I developed a passion and love for woodworking, content creation, and entrepeneurship that I didn’t know was there. 

Throughout the last few years of full-time furniture building I've shipped pieces throughout the country for various residential/businesses clients, and developed a love for studying and building mid-century modern, Scandanavian, and Danish style furniture. In our shop we build various styles of furniture depending on client' requests but focus on mid-century modern style and plan to shift towards only mid-century style pieces throughout the future.

Dicen que todo lo que empieza, acaba. Por eso queremos comunicaros que nos despedimos de WANNA y comenzamos una nueva etapa, esta vez desde nuestros propios proyectos personales.

Es difícil escribir el punto final de esta historia, cuando nos hemos dedicado a ella en cuerpo, mente y corazón durante una década. Pero las tres estamos de acuerdo en que, por coherencia y respeto hacia nosotras mismas y hacia el proyecto, ha llegado el momento de empezar un viaje por separado. 

Queremos dar las gracias a todos y cada uno de los clientes que nos han confiado sus sueños en estos años. Nos habéis permitido llegar mucho más lejos de lo que jamás imaginamos, cuando creamos aquel blog de decoración. 

Gracias a todas las personas y empresas que han colaborado en los proyectos de WANNA: profesionales freelance, artistas, artesanos, fotógrafos, fabricantes, proveedores… Y en el proyecto de WANNA en sí mismo.

Gracias a todas las instituciones académicas que nos han invitado a compartir nuestro expertise y nos han dado la oportunidad de descubrir nuestra pasión compartida por la docencia. 

Gracias a las organizaciones que han contado con nosotras para impartir conferencias, talleres o participar en mesas redondas.

Gracias a las asociaciones de las que hemos formado parte y que nos han ayudado, inspirado y hecho sentir muy bien acompañadas durante estos años.

Gracias a nuestros churritos, por hacernos mejores. Las manos tiemblan al teclear esta frase. Os queremos y estamos seguras de que nos volveremos a encontrar. 

Y gracias a ti, que estás leyendo esto por formar parte de nuestra pequeña comunidad virtual. 

Podéis seguirnos la pista en nuestros perfiles de instragram:

Esther: @somoscarne.es

Cathy y María: @melonbreakers

Un abrazo y hasta siempre. 

Cathy, Esther y María.

Soy Ana Hernández, directora creativa del estudio de diseño de interiores y producto Masquespacio. Tengo la suerte de haber podido convertir mi pasión en mi profesión. Me encanta todo lo que rodea nuestro mundo creativo y me motiva afrontar nuevos retos, cumpliendo los sueños de nuestros clientes. Otra de mis pasiones es compartir nuestras experiencias adquiridas en nuestro día a día en Masquespacio, tanto a nivel creativo como sobre las barreras que puede significar buscar la innovación en cada proyecto. 

Gracias a nuestra dedicación diaria nos hemos convertido de un estudio de interiorismo convencional en un estudio creativo que en el momento actual se enfoca principalmente en el diseño de interiores y producto que desarrolla estrategias visuales customizadas para cada proyecto.  Hemos recibido un reconocimiento internacional a lo largo de nuestros siete años de existencia que nos ha llevado a hacer proyectos en Alemania, Noruega y Estados Unidos entre otros, además de haber sido galardonados con varios premios por nuestra trayectoria como el 'Massimo Dutti Nuevos Valores' por AD España y el 'Wave of The Future' por Hospitality Design Magazine USA, sumando también premios por los proyectos realizados como el Hospitality Design Award, Red Dot y Wallpaper Award.

Esta es una pequeña ventana que te acercará a mi mundo, en donde la magia reside en la luz y el color, para conseguir espacios alegres, que producen sensaciones y no dejan indiferente. Estos son los dos pilares fundamentales de mis trabajos y sobre los que voy construyendo el resto de los elementos.
Mi carrera es una constante búsqueda por encontrar la belleza, fijándome en los pequeños detalles que juntos consiguen crear una composición única.

Me confieso una apasionada de las antigüedades, de encontrar esas piezas que brillan a través de su historia, y que no dudo al mezclarlas con los muebles más actuales y sencillos. Es curioso descubrir cómo estas piezas más antiguas, lo que hacen es aportar frescura a los espacios y los convierten en lugares únicos.
Es mi mejor forma de transmitir lo que siento y comunicarme, donde no hay reglas, el color, los estampados y los diferentes materiales, nunca sobran ni se pelean.En resumen aquí podrás encontrar “THE COLOR OF MY LIFE” Todo aquello que me apasiona, que refleja lo que siento, por eso lo quiero compartir y que también consiga emocionarte.

Hola! Soy arquitecta fundadora de NeuronaLab e interiorista especializada en proyectos de vivienda y oficina.
Pienso que poner a las personas en el centro del diseño es el principal camino viable para conseguir espacios confortables y saludables. Mediante un análisis exhaustivo del emplazamiento, de su entorno y de las necesidades de los usuarios, diseño edificios en los que aplico criterios de neuroarquitectura y bioconstrucción para conseguir el bienestar de las personas. 
En 2011 cofundé el estudio de arquitectura Nook Architects, en el que he dirigido proyectos durante más de 10 años y he ejercido la docencia y preparación de cursos online.
En 2015 creé los espacios de trabajo compartido Zamness. 
Actualmente soy fundadora de NeuronaLab y directora del Máster de Bienestar, Neuroarquitectura y Bioconstrucción en la Escuela LCI Barcelona.

Estudié Arquitectura y después de conocer qué es un diseñador de iluminación decidí dedicarme a esto. Fundé mi oficina, LumLum en 2014 y desde entonces no he parado.
En LumLum hacemos diseño de iluminación arquitectónica. Acá todos los días experimentamos con nuestro material principal, la luz.

My name is Nasima Alam. I am a primary school teacher, turned self taught cake artist, specialising in bespoke wedding cake designs.  My cake journey was a very unexpected one, which began in 2015 by pure accident. I’ve always been into art and pursued this up to University level. My artistic interests were also evident in my home interior and design, when I dabbled in property developing. It took a different direction when I began to implement this into cake decorating.

 I’ve always enjoyed baking but to be able to take this to an artistic level was very much up my street.  I began teaching myself new skills and techniques through watching lots of YouTube videos and before I knew it, by 2016 Sweet Drops of Heaven was established as a viable registered business. I  teach cake decorating classes, have my own cake stencil designs and also created a cake decorating product called Sweet Flakes of Heaven.  I’ve been fortunate enough to collaborate with large businesses such as Daniel Wellington and have been featured in many industry cake magazines, such as Satin Ice, Cake Masters, Cake Decoration & Sugar Craft.

Hi, I'm Liz Shim of Eat Cake Be Merry! I am a professional cake artist that has been making cakes for over 13 years. I've created cakes for all of life's celebrations ranging from weddings to birthdays and everything in between. 

As much as I love baking and decorating cakes, I also love teaching others how to create special cakes themselves. I've traveled the world sharing my skills and through online courses I've taught thousands of students all over the globe. I'm so glad to have the opportunity to teach you as well and I look forward to seeing what we will create from my class together!

Hi, I'm Kate Kim, a professional baker and cake designer based in London(Kflowercake). I am the proud recipient of the Cake International Bronze award in 2017 - the biggest cake decorating competition in the world. As well as providing private lessons, I currently supply to local cake shops with a selection of my cakes.
I moved from South Korea to London around five years ago and started offering private lessons to individuals interested in cake decoration. This originally started out as a hobby as I enjoyed sharing knowledge and meeting new people. As my classes became more popular, this eventually became my full-time job. However, with the onset of coronavirus I have had to stop offering my lessons and thought it would be a lovely idea to continue my work online and share my knowledge globally to those who have the same interests as me. Through my lessons, I hope individuals around the world will be able to develop a new hobby whilst aiding those who are already bakers looking to expand their skillset. Who knows? A small hobby could turn into an amazing job!

In an effort to bridge the gap between art and science, I've focused on the way people interact with and experience art, using a medium we all love: food. Specifically, cakes! I am the owner and founder of Duchess of Cameron, a New York City-based bespoke cake company specializing in painted cakes. Taking inspiration from the most influential eras of art history, I create one-of-a-kind works of edible art with designs ranging from delicate chinoiserie motifs embellished with hyper-realistic sugar flowers to intricate paintings reminiscent of Rococo frescoes.

I have appeared on multiple Food Network shows including as a judge on Buddy vs Duff, Season 3, and received “New York Wedding Awards Manhattan Cake Designer of the Year,” along with "Best of Weddings" by The Knot and "Couples' Choice Award" by Wedding Wire, and am listed by The St. Regis New York on their exclusive Preferred Vendor List. Among hundreds of wedding clients, I have also worked with Louis Vuitton, Tiffany & Co., STARZ Network, Ferrero Rocher, the Four Seasons Hong Kong, Martha Stewart, and renowned artist Jeff Koons. You can also see my work in past issues of Vanity Fair, House & Garden, amNY, and The World of Interiors.

I am Kwun, a cake artist from Thailand and I teach cake decoration.
You may know me from Butter & Blossoms on social media. 
My specific art is Sculpture Painting Flowers with buttercream and chocolate cream.
Sculpture Painting using pallet knives is my signature technique, since 2017. I have taught overseas in more than 15 Countries. My base studio in Bangkok, Thailand also provides workshops for students overseas.

Hi! I'm Lindsey, a cupcake designer and content creator, also known as Lindsey Baked This on social media. I discovered my passion for cupcake decoration in 2020, transforming what started as a hobby into a thriving career.

I began my artistic journey as a student at Rhode Island School of Design, where I majored in illustration. There, I not only learned the fundamentals of drawing and painting, but also cultivated an eye for detail and a penchant for imaginative expression.

Building on my artistic background, I embarked on a 14-year career in the advertising industry, serving as a creative director. In this dynamic role, I mastered the art of conceptualizing, crafting compelling aesthetics, and bringing concepts to life through graphic design and photography. This experience equipped me with the tools to seamlessly translate my artistic vision onto the canvas of cupcakes.

Fueled by my passion for creativity and a desire to spread joy, I have amassed a dedicated following on social media, captivating audiences with engaging and entertaining decorating videos. For me, buttercream is more than just an ingredient—it's edible paint, a medium through which I brings my imaginative designs to life.

My cupcakes are known for their ingenuity and whimsy, each creation reflecting my playful spirit. Whether it's crafting whimsical characters or creating new decorating techniques, my goal is always to bring a smile to people's faces - and to their taste buds!

When I'm not busy whipping up treats in my New York City kitchen, I enjoy exploring the city's vibrant culinary scene, taking leisurely runs, and spending quality time with my cat, Pepper. 

Join me on my sweet journey of creativity and culinary delight, where every cupcake is a work of art and every bite is a taste of happiness!

teachers.aboutMe: David Peña Toribio, más conocido por su seudónimo artístico, Puño, nació en Madrid en 1978. Dibuja desde que tiene uso de razón y, además de asistir a una escuela de cine, cursó estudios de Técnico Superior en Comunicación Audiovisual. Además de ganarse la vida como escritor infantil e ilustrador, es educador creativo en Holanda, España y Colombia. Ha vivido en Coruña, París, Ámsterdam y Medellín donde también desarrolla sus proyectos fotográficos y editoriales y colabora con plataformas de transformación social a través del dibujo. Ha colaborado en publicidad, prensa (por ejemplo, en los diarios El País, El Mundo o Público), animación y en la ilustración de obras infantiles y de adultos. Durante un tiempo dirigió las editoriales Ediciones Peo y Ultrarradio y ha publicado en varias revistas de cómics, como Argh!, Cretino, Lunático, El Manglar y Garabattage.  Ha cosechado varios premios como el Tercer Premio de Animación Nontzeflash (2006), el Primer Premio de Fotografía Cinemad (2008), el Primer Premio CreaCómic de CAM (2009), el Premio Internacional de Ilustración Fundación SM  (2009) por su libro ¡Ñam! y el Premio Barco de Vapor 2018 por su novela La Niña Invisible. Desde 1997 se dedica a enseñar dibujo, creatividad, ilustración y narrativa a gente de todas las edades y todas partes del mundo, a través de talleres, escuelas de arte y universidades de España, Holanda y Colombia. Ha coordinado y dirigido varios cursos de ilustración, entre otros el Microdoctorado en Mr Marcel School o el Curso One Year de Ilustración en el Istituto Europeo di Design. También ha sido comisario del ciclo de exposiciones La Ciudad En Viñetas en CentroCentro (Palacio de Cibeles) para el Ayuntamiento de Madrid.

Lo único que hago en mi vida es luchar contra el aburrimiento. 

Y la única forma que se me ocurre es jugar a contar historias con dibujos, que es lo que sé hacer. Me dedico a ilustrar cosas complejas y llevarlas a aquel punto tan simple en el que si lo abstraigo un poco más, no se entenderá nada. 

Simplificar las cosas y las historias es como limpiar la paja del grano, sacarle brillo y presentarlas. Esto permite generar imágenes en la cabeza de los demás. 

Yo siempre digo que el éxito de los Playmobils con los que jugábamos de pequeños, es que una cara de playmobil es la cara de cualquiera y te ves reflejado en él: cuando jugabas con ese playmobil, eras tú mismo el protagonista pirata o bandolero. Se podría decir que dibujo playmobils.

Lo mío es escribir con palabras, esquemas y dibujos. La finalidad es contar cosas. “cuéntalas, usando todo lo que tengas alrededor para mostrar eso que quieres.”

En los dibujos me gusta hablar de la muerte, del sexo, del amor, de los amigos, y relaciones humanas. A veces resbalo hacia temas de actualidad, que al final es hablar también de amor y de desamor, de traiciones, venganzas, o relaciones humanas al fin y al cabo.

Me gusta mucho la tecnología, y he tenido mucha suerte de haber vivido este mundo de las redes sociales que te permiten tener una audiencia, conseguir llegar a mucha gente e interactuar con ellos. Soy muy sociable, y esto, unido a la gran hegemonía de la imagen en Instagram me están dando muchas alegrías. Soy alguien feliz, aunque tenga muchos dibujos dramáticos. El humor es lo que tiene, que parte del drama, del drama humano.

He tenido la suerte de aprender y conocer de cerca a algunos de mis maestros que son (o han sido) también amigos, como Forges, Javier Mariscal, Mario Eskenazi o Christoph Niemann. Y he publicado muchos libros, desde los primeros de La Cebolla Asesina por los años 2000, a La Tortilla de Patatas junto al gran David de Jorge o mi último libro Homo Machus, sobre el machismo. 

Licenciado en Bellas Artes por la Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea, soy profesor de ilustración y diseño en la Universitat Oberta de Catalunya, en Eina, en IDEP y BAU. Dirijo un estudio de diseño que se llama Chispum.

Fruto de los libros y de la práctica, cocino la mejor tortilla de patatas del planeta. Y no tengo abuela. 

@javirroyo

--------

Soy ilustrador, diseñador y profesor. Dirijo el estudio de ilustración y diseño Chispum. He ilustrado para publicaciones como Interviú (ilustrando a Juanjo Millás) o El País entre otros. Actualmente colaboro ilustrando y haciendo humor gráfico para El País, El Semanal, Visual, la Maleta de Portbou, Uppers, El Meteorito y El Estafador. Formé parte de la revista satírica “El Virus Mutante” junto a Forges, Gallego y Rey, El Roto, Peridis o Pablo Carbonell entre otros. Creé La Cebolla Asesina. Mis últimos libros publicados son “Martín Berasategui y David de Jorge” (Debate / Penguin Random House y Premio Junceda de Ilustración), "La Tortilla de Patatas” (Debate / Penguin Random House, junto a David de Jorge), "La Escuela” (Foundawtion, Premio a la mejor obra aragonesa en 2018), “Grandes cócteles del mundo" (Casa Camper / Ediciones Malpaso, “Life is Sho” (Chispum), “Homo Machus” y “Laborachismo” (Lumen / Penguin Random House). Soy patrono y encargado de Educación de Foundawtion, fundación sin ánimo de lucro, con proyectos de desarrollo en educación y arquitectura en África. Soy profesor de ilustración y diseño en la Universidad Oberta de Catalunya (UOC), Eina, BAU e IDEP. Premio Graffica 2020.

¡Hola!
Somos Pierina Másquez y José María Denegri, las manos y ojos detrás de Fortuna, un estudio
creativo y experimental de juego, labor y reflexión en torno al dibujo. Trabajamos desde la
ciudad de Lima, al sur de Latinoamérica, desde el 2019.
El proyecto indaga las posibilidades funcionales y sensibles de la línea dentro y fuera de
los formatos convencionales, la relación con la ciudad, las prácticas pedagógicas y las
posibilidades de integrar el dibujo con la vida misma.
En los últimos años hemos podido colaborar con diferentes proyectos locales e internacionales.
Durante el mes de mayo, realizamos una residencia artística en el espacio La Chispita (MX).
A inicios del 2021 lanzamos nuestro primer curso de dibujo online junto a DOMESTIKA.
Hace muy poco fuimos parte del festival Radical Sounds Latinoamerica (AL), donde
presentamos la publicación colectiva de volcanes Latinoamericanos “Desatando nudos,
moviendo montañas”. Nuestro trabajo ha sido publicado en: FARE Magazine (UK) Osmosis.
pe (PE), Hermanas (PE), PROTEA (MX) entre otros. Hemos participado de la Subasta Anual
del Museo de Arte de Lima MALI (PE) y del Museo de Arte Contemporáneo MAC (PE).
Actualmente venimos preparando una serie de podcasts en torno al dibujo y la ciudad,
gracias al fondo de Apoyos Económicos COVID 19 del Ministerio de Cultura del Perú.
Durante la semana, seguimos dibujando desde el sexto piso de un viejo edificio modernista
con vista a la desteñida puesta de sol limeña.

Gusti
Nací en Buenos Aires Argentina en 1963.
Cursé estudios de diseño y promoción publicitaria en la escuela de arte 
Fernando Fader.
Trabajé para revistas infantiles y en estudios de animación
realizando  series para tv.
En el año 1985 me trasladé a Europa 
Comencé a trabajar para diversas editoriales de España y 
a publicar en diferentes países.
He publicado más de 150 libros  en más de 20 idiomas.
Algunos de mis  libros han sido galardonados con varios premios 
como el Premio nacional de ilustración por el libro “Un pirata valiente.
La Pomme Dór de Bratislava por  la obra” Pip y la linea “
El Appeles -Mestres por el libro ”Uña y carne “
El Award ragazzi en Bologna en la categoria discapacidad 
por el libro ” Mallko y papá“ .
El Premio Serra Dór por el libro “El niño gris”
El Premio Junceda en dos oportunidades
que concede la Asociación Profesional de Ilustradores de Catalunya 
Estoy nominado al premio
Hans Christian Andersen en representación de Argentina para el
año 2022.
He sido director artístico de la Casa de Carlota durante dos años,un estudio de 
diseño innovador donde trabajan diseñadores junto a
personas con discapacidad intelectual .
Soy  fundador y presidente de la asociación “Windown ”que trabaja
por el arte como herramienta de inclusión.
Participo activamente en el campo de la inclusión 
ofreciendo laboratorios de arte y conferencias sobre imagen y discapacidad.
Doy clases de dibujo y de Album ilustrado en la escuela de diseño Eina 
Imparto  diversos talleres inclusivos en Colombia,
Nicaragua, Brasil, Chile, Argentina,Alemania,Italia .
Soy padre de dos hijos uno con ojos marrones 
y el otro con ojos claros y un cromosoma de más .
Colaboro con proyectos de conservación como el del Cóndor Andino
 y del Aguila Harpía en Argentina y Ecuador. 
Vivo y trabajo en Barcelona.

teacher.aboutMe:
Domestika is the fastest-growing creative community where the best creative experts share their knowledge and skills through professionally produced online courses.

It all started as an online forum and a small but dynamic showcase of creative professionals, designed to help them connect and learn from each other.

Inspired by their thriving community, Domestika widened its reach by producing online courses for anyone interested in unleashing their creative potential and connecting with like-minded creatives from around the world.

Domestika carefully curates the teacher roster and produces all the courses in-house, to ensure a high-quality online learning experience for everyone. Today, the online community is home to over 6 million people from around the world who are curious and passionate about learning new creative skills.

teachers.aboutMe:
Fábrica de Texturas es un proyecto 100% “Hágalo Usted Mismo” con base en Madrid desde 2012. Detrás de Fábrica estamos Gabriela Rodríguez y Xavier Robledo, con muchas ganas de enseñar y divulgar todo lo que cae en nuestras manos y de diseñar más allá del objeto.

Experimentamos con técnicas artesanales y artes plásticas, recuperamos y transformamos técnicas artesanas tradicionales para hacerlas más accesibles y actuales. Hemos creado unos kits DIY (Do It Yourself) con los que puedes aprender sencillas técnicas con las que desarrollar tu creatividad.

Tipia Lab es una escuela taller de Arte Fotográfico del Siglo XIX y XX, somos Mario Nieto y Katalina Fuentes especializados en la imagen química desde hace más de 20 años, nos apasiona la enseñanza y la investigación de los procesos fotográficos alternativos, también llamados Procesos Antiguos. Nuestro nombre surge del griego «TYPOS» relativo a la imprenta, o al Arte de Copiar. Nuestro objetivo es la preservación del conocimiento para que las nuevas generaciones tengan la oportunidad de conocer y trabajar en el objeto fotográfico desde una perspectiva analógica y tradicional.

Amazink es un estudio de serigrafía manual ubicado en el centro de Madrid. 

A los mandos del estudio esta Noelia Tramullas, ilustradora y maestra de taller, con muchas ganas de contagiar su pasión por la gráfica y más concretamente por la serigrafía en ediciones limitadas. 

Realizo proyectos tanto para artistas e ilustradores como  personales, siempre dejando espacio a la experimentación y tratando de superar los limites de la técnica. 

La finalidad del estudio es hacer llegar la serigrafía manual a mas gente, para ello se imparten cursos a diferentes niveles, monográficos para empresas e incluso eventos con serigrafía en vivo. Además, para facilitar el acercamiento del público a la serigrafía, Amazink es un taller de acceso abierto, donde pueden hacer uso de las instalaciones y adquirir materiales.

Soy artista y editor de obra gráfica. Actualmente dirijo la editora Ogami Press en Madrid.
Mi interés por las técnicas gráficas me lleva a formarme y colaborar en los talleres más destacados de Madrid y Londres. Me especializo en fotograbado y en técnicas de transferencia de imágenes y tras crear mi propio taller, fundo en 2009 la editora Ogami Press.
Como artista he sido finalista del Premio José Hernández (2007), segundo premio en la II Bienal de grabado Provincia de Valladolid (2009), primer premio en Premio Internacional de Grabado Dinatía Vivanco en 2012, primer premio en el VII Certamen Internacional de Grabado Jesús Nuñez 2012 y segundo Premio Internacional Atlante 2014. Tercer premio José Caballero de las Rozas 2014 (Madrid). Beca de residencia Staff Exchange en el Programa Pasword Printmaking en el MGLC de Ljubljana, Eslovenia
Como docente he impartido cursos en el Museo Reina Sofía, la Real Casa de la Moneda, en la Fundación Pilar y Joan Miró de Palma, en BilbaoArte, en el CIEC de Betanzos, en la Fundación Fuendetodos de Zaragoza o en la Universidad de BBAA de Sevilla entre otros. De la misma manera he realizado ponencias en el Instituto del Patrimonio Cultural de España, en la Facultad de Bellas Artes de la Universidad Complutense, en la Facultad de Bellas Artes de Sevilla o en  Bilbaoarte, Bilbao.

teachers.aboutMe:
Artista Visual e Ilustradora Digital-  
Lo mío son los retratos. He trabajado en base al rostro, probando diferentes técnicas y materiales a lo largo de mi carrera como Ilustradora y Artista Visual. 
Recientemente descubrí el mundo del bordado y me sumergí en la inmensidad de posibilidades de éste. 
Me enamoré especial mente del Bordado con Punch Needle, el cual ha sido usado por años para la creación de alfombras, pero decidí darle un giro a esta técnica y probar algo que nadie había hecho hasta este momento.

Lo que más me apasiona en el Arte, es descubrir nuevos usos para materiales/medios y/o técnicas comunes.
La mayoría de mis referentes y artistas favoritos son aquellos que han logrado tomar un medio común y transformarlo en una obra de arte.

Hi! My name is Micah, and I am a fashion designer turned fiber artist who specializes in punch needle rug hooking.

I discovered punch needle in 2018 originally planning to incorporate this technique into my fashion work, but it quickly became an obsession that changed the course of my art (and my life)! I created the first punch needle coat in 2018, and I love exploring ways that punch needle can be incorporated into fashion, accessories, and other non-traditional applications.  

Through my work, I am to take something traditional (like punch needle) and do something new, creating something that blurs the line between art, fashion, design and craft. Because of this, I don’t like to limit myself to one form or style, so my work spans everything from fine art to decorative art. I have made rugs, pillows, artwork, wall hangings, wearables and accessories – and this variation is part of the fun! I am always looking for new ways I can apply my skills across multiple arenas.

In 2019 I trained with renowned punch needle artist Amy Oxford to become a Certified Oxford Punch Needle Instructor, and in 2020 I launched Punch Needle World as a community and educational resource dedicated to teaching and spreading the word about this craft. I am passionate about keeping the history and traditional techniques of punch needle alive as we bring it into the 21st century!

Today, I balance my time between creating custom artwork for clients and developing patterns, content and educational resources for Punch Needle World.  My work has been featured in online blogs, books and publications such as Koel Magazine, MANEQUIM, Mollie Makes, Love Embroidery and Amy Oxford's Guide to Punch Needle Rug Hooking.

I believe there is so much self-confidence, therapy and joy to be found in creating things with your own two hands, and this is what I hope to inspire through my work and teaching!

Rose Pearlman is an artist, teacher, and textile designer.  With a background in fine arts and a love of well designed functional objects, her creations blur the lines between art and craft and pushes the boundaries with non-traditional techniques and materials.  Rose teaches monthly rug hooking workshops in and around her home in NYC, and also welcomes commissions for one of a kind constructions in decor and home furnishings. Her work has been featured in fiber magazines, galleries, and numerous online design sites and her first book, Modern Rug Hooking, '22 Punch Needle Projects For Crafting A Beautiful Home,' was published by Roost Books in 2019. Rose lives in Brooklyn, NY with her husband and two children.

Hi! My name is Adeline and I am a self-taught punch needle artist and designer.

Over the years, I’ve dabbled in different art media and I consider myself lucky to have found punch needle back in 2019. My punch needle journey has been and still is evolving as I learn and grow in my practice. I started with small projects such as pillows, trivets, and crossbody bags. As I tried to perfect my stitches, I quickly moved on to larger projects like rugs and wall hangings. During that time, I advanced from traditional punch needle rug hooking to a broader multi-texture and multi-technique fiber world. I was able to incorporate weaving, embroidery, beading and tufting into my work and now the possibilities are endless!

These days, besides creating my own experimental and “just for fun” projects, I’m also designing digital punch needle patterns and working on commissions and collaborations.

Punch needle is my tool of self expression and my creative outlet. I’ve always enjoyed turning my own designs into functional beauties and it changed my life when I realized my art can also bring joy to someone else. It has lead me to a supportive community of fiber lovers and friends, for which I will be forever grateful.

Youmeng Liu is a designer and embroidery artist.  She graduated from the London College of Fashion (LCF) with a MA in Fashion Artifact.  Upon graduation she was selected as a finalist for International Talent Support (ITS) and was invited to showcase her work in Italy.  She was also a finalist at the prestigious Hand & Lock Embroidery prize in 2019.

Her vision is to produce 301 embroidered art works of common edible food items.  Every piece of artwork has been created using her newly developed 3D punch needle embroidery technique which combines the skill of hand embroidery, scissors sculpting and an artistic eye.  As a result, this gives the work a very realistic look.

teachers.aboutMe: Jimbo is an accomplished hand lettering artist and graphic designer, Jimbo is most known for the powerful colour palettes and clever design techniques he uses to demonstrate mastery of the form. Many of his pieces are accented with floral embellishments, a design motif that has captured the attention of thousands across social media. Today, the Croatia-based designer is the co-founder of BAM! Creative Studio (also known as ShoutBam on Instagram), which specialises in letter crafting, illustration and digital and educational products to help amateur letterers enhance their skills.

Hi, my name's Dan Forster, I’m a lettering artist and designer. I was lucky to grow up with a Dad who was a designer, lettering artist and calligrapher. So from an early age I was exposed to a ton of art and design. I spent a lot of time in his studio watching him work, rummaging through his books, or tracing my comics – so it was almost inevitable I’d end up in a creative career.

I tried my hand a calligraphy and lettering at an early age, but found it so hard that I gave up almost immediately. So initially I worked in design and branding but developed a deep love for type and typography. It wasn’t until after my Dad passed away in 2008 that I discovered the true depth and breadth of his lettering work. I was so blown away by what I found in his studio that it inspired me to pick up a pen and start drawing letters again. This time I stuck at it, slowly got better and eventually switched careers to become a full-time lettering artist. 

These days I’ve been lucky to work with clients from around the world on all kinds of lettering-based projects, from brand-marks, to book covers, to packing projects and everything in between. Letters are now my world and I love to experiment with new ways to create letter shapes, explore three-dimensional forms and I’m particularly obsessed with curves and flourishing.

Hi! I'm a lettering artist, sign painter, and graphic designer based in Toronto. Along with my full-time freelance work, I am also a public speaker, lettering instructor, and published author, and my work has been featured in Spacing Magazine, Uppercase Magazine & Flare Magazine. I recently received a Communication Arts Award of Excellence in Typography.

My brand is an extension of my personal art practice & research, which focusses on the analog techniques of
brush lettering & sign painting, rooted in the pre-digital commercial arts style of the 1940s-1960s. My work
brings this tradition forward into the 21st century, with two main objectives: to share my deep, heartfelt
appreciation of the craft of handmade letterforms & typography, and to inspire (and challenge) people with
text-based art. Christopher (the brand, and the artist) is equal parts innovation & inspiration.

If you make it well, and make it beautiful, it can last forever.

My name is Cyril Vouilloz aka. RYLSEE 
I'm a Berlin based Swiss Artist who has developed a reputation and skills through diverse forms of art. I Grew up with "illegal" passions like skateboard and graffiti that seems to have forged my graphical style.

Letters have always fascinated me, so much that that passion has allowed me to show my work around the world and to collaborate with big brands like: NIKE, Caran d'Ache, Converse, IKEA...
You can discover some of these adventures in my book HOW TO PLAY WITH LETTERS published by Moleskine®.

Ranging from graffiti, graphic design, hand lettering, and an avant-garde approach to typography. 
I am inspired by moments of everyday life, the city and the passion for skateboarding, laced to the desire to make people smile.

What else?...
I am left handed & Too Shy To Rap!

→ instagram: @RYLSEE

Hi there! My name is Nico Ng. I am a multidisciplinary designer, educator, and creative entrepreneur from Manila, Philippines. I have worked with brands and clients such as Tombow, Faber-Castell, Manuscript, WWF, National Library Board (Singapore), and Kiplinger. I have also given talks and conducted lettering workshops around Southeast Asian countries, such as Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore.

After graduating from university in 2012 with an engineering degree, I decided to take a leap and pursue a creative career. I spent most of my waking hours and sleepless nights learning and practicing design and lettering, until sweet opportunities came one by one, and the rest is history!

My goal is to inspire and help lettering artists express themselves creatively and confidently by imparting my lettering techniques and innovating tools to help them create easier and better.

About me: I am a Designer.
In my professional career I’ve gone from simple visual design to complex strategic and tactical design for products and services.
I help companies connect their products and services in a coherent and deferential way with all their stakeholders. I design, develop and integrate the brand strategies with which companies reach their audiences and goals.
I’m currently founder and creative director at Agencia YOU in Madrid
I have spent the past 20 years in digital design and brand strategy. 
In 2015 I developed a methodology aimed at brining brands and users closer together. To do this I pulled on all my experience especially in the fields of Branding and User Experience Design.
Also in 2015 I founded Agencia YOU to bring my Brand User Experience methodology to market.
In 2016 I co-founded "Brand The Gap", a Madrid based Branding community, to bring new Branding trends and ideas by organising monthly events.
And in 2017 I set up KoolBrandSkiool, a high performance centre for advanced Branding.
I've worked for international companies such as IconMedialab, Vogue Magazine, The Marketing Store and Sopra Steria as well as prestigious Spanish agencies like Estudio Oscar Mariné and Tau Diseño.
Most of my recent experience is for the financial retail sector having worked on projects for BBVA, Santander, Bankia and Bankinter. I've taken on projects for clients such as Telefónica, McDonald’s, Ikea, Carrefour and Heinz and have developed assignments in Spain, Portugal, UK, Russia and Singapore.
I’ve given conferences on Brand User Experience for Campus Madrid (Tech-hub/Google), UXERS and Interactive Design case studies for the Pompeu i Fabra University in Barcelona.
I enjoy teaching and have done so for the Carlos III University of Madrid Master's Degree in Advertising Communication . I have also taught at the IED Madrid (Istituto Europeo di Design), the Interactive Advertising Bureau (WholeSocial-IAB, Madrid) and the Madrid School of Marketing.
Awards are great such as the one I received from ID Magazine’s Interactive Design Awards for the Vega Sicilia websites.
I play guitar, compose and sing in a Post-Punk band

About Agencia YOU:
Agencia YOU was born in 2015 in Madrid. It’s aim is to bring the Brand User Experience methodology to market and, thereby, help brands focus their resources on the right strategy.
We close the gap that may exist between your brand and its audience. We do it by developing brand strategies focused on their users.
Agencia YOU helps its clients in 2 ways: firstly by developing strategies for positioning, contents, re-branding and brand tracking and secondly executing the strategy which may include Naming and Visual ID, Apps and Digital Design, Content creation and Channel activation.
Apart from end to end solutions, we also develop workshops, in-house teaching and sectorial studies and reports.
We have helped create better customer experiences and strategies for companies such as APQ, Katia Dental, IGT, Homequity and Activa
At YOU we aim to be innovative and are always looking for ways to improve our methodology by including new aspects like IoT, Service Design, Blockchain and Product Typology to name a few.

Full-stack brand strategist blending psychology, business, and design like it’s a caramel frappuccino. Forever on a mission to craft brands people remember with a smile. 

After graduating with a summa cum laude degree in business from American University, I was fascinated by the possibilities that brand building can unlock. Deeply intrigued by the power of symbols and stories to strengthen these brands, I pursued a Master of Arts in Design Management from SCAD. 

All along, I’ve had the honor to craft content for brands like Canva, Creative Market, Smashing Magazine, Webflow, and many more. From niche local businesses to an entire Caribbean city, I’ve also designed what dozens of brands look and feel like. No strategy is too foreign: if it shapes the brand’s story, I’ve tried it and I’m here to walk you through it.

All in all, I believe brand building is a battle to recover the soul of business. And I’m fully enlisted.

You can always find me crawling down some vintage rabbit hole. If you too are triggered by faux bolds, our friendship is meant to be. Come say hi @laurabusche.

I am the Principal of Los Angeles-based brand consultancy FINIEN and a partner at Chameleon Collective, a business consultancy that in 2022 made the Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies for the second year in a row. 

A Graphic Designer turned Creative Director turned Brand Strategist, I love to create clarity for brand transformations. I do so for startups and Fortune 500s alike, but the thrill is the same since I wholeheartedly believe that any venture can turn into an admired brand if developed in an intrinsic, holistic, and methodological manner. 

I have deep expertise in guiding organizations through their brand transformations and have advised companies such as Marriott International, Warner Brothers, Match Group, Honeywell, Kaplan, and Randstad. My thoughts on branding have appeared in publications like Inc., Forbes, Entrepreneur, and The Washington Post, and my creative direction has won over 50 international awards.

All three of my books became international Amazon best-sellers and turned into go-to resources for entrepreneurs and marketers alike. From my Resonaid brand strategy workshops to the Hitting the Mark podcast, I am in a constant stimulation cycle. In 2022 I received the inaugural Global Startup Mentor Award for being the highest-rated mentor in the U.S. by Founder Institute, the world's largest pre-seed accelerator.

Originally from Vienna, Austria I have been living in Los Angeles for over half my life. I enjoy speaking and traveling the world to hold keynotes and group workshops, where I get to share my actionable brand advice.

Jessie McGuire is first-ever Managing Partner of New York-based brand design agency ThoughtMatter, leading a diverse team of artists, writers and strategists to create daring designs and identities for global brands, local communities, art museums and foundations, institutions and non-profits. She has been instrumental in helping the studio more than double in size, growing its creative and strategic capabilities. Her passionate approach has also informed ThoughtMatter’s work with cultural institutions like Yerba Buena Center for the Arts, and innovators like Web3 diversity pioneers World of Women, as well as companies like Viacom, Procter & Gamble and many others. Jessie has been integral in shaping the purpose and creative vision of ThoughtMatter, spearheading projects and campaigns that reflect the agency’s culture and mission. Those have included a modern redesign of the U.S. Constitution, lauded by everyone from PBS to Fast Company, to protest posters for the Women's March and March for Our Lives. She has raised awareness and support for socially progressive causes such as Girls Write Now and The Joyful Heart Foundation, as well as on community-minded efforts for The New-York Historical Society, Downtown Staten Island and The Center for Arts Education. As one of the few women of color to lead an agency, she acts as a mentor and advocate for anyone eager for brands that reflect their needs and experiences – whether that’s through crafting inclusive messaging, coming up with sustainable packaging solutions, or helping brands to use design to foster stronger communities.

teachers.aboutMe:
Lilly Maetzig is the maker behind Mae Ceramics, a small but prolific business, which started in New Zealand and moved to London in 2016. Lilly is the sole maker of Mae Ceramics, specialising in handmaking functional objects for everyday use.

She is based in London, living and working in South East London, making from a studio on the beautiful Deptford Foreshore.

Lilly first experimented with ceramics in 2011 whilst at art school, where she learned how to slip cast and make sculptural work. After graduating, she worked from a shared studio, which is where she fell in love with the art of functional ceramics. 

Her work is mostly minimal, with sharp lines and a limited colour palette, bringing a stillness to the work. However, sometimes she strays from what is clean and tidy, with the occasional playful glaze or decoration. Lilly mostly makes wheel thrown work, however part of her love of ceramics is the slower pace of handbuilding. Handbuilding has a meditative peace to it, and whilst only a small portion of the Mae Ceramics portfolio is handbuilt, the time spent doing it and the different qualities of the finished products make them some of the most cherished.
Lilly's work explores the contrast between the texture of raw and glazed clay, and often lets the natural qualities of the materials show through on the surface of a finished piece.

Sono una artista italiana e la ceramica è il mio mezzo espressivo da 20 anni.
Sono nata a Torino, ho studiato restauro a Firenze e mi sono specializzata in scultura ceramica in Spagna. 
Oltre a creare sculture e installazioni per gallerie e arredatori internazionali, mi dedico all'insegnamento e alla diffusione del kintsugi e della filosofia wabi-sabi.
Come esperta di kintsugi ho collaborato in pubblicità ed eventi per marche come Netflix, Shiseido, Audi e Roku gin.

Hessa Al Ajmani is an Emirati visual artist born in Abu Dhabi and based in Ajman. Her practice as an artist is heavily influenced by curiosity of the human psychology and the natural world, and the idea of observing things which are not so noticeable, but are often present human interactions and daily commutes. Her current work with ceramics translates her passion for exploration and observation by imprinting native plants and wildflowers onto functional ceramicware as a form of research to understand more about the native flora that is present in the UAE. A key element and driving force of her current research is her deep appreciation of pottery as an ancient craft and experimentation through trial-and-error. 

In 2019, Al Ajmani founded Clay Corner Studio, the first public arts studio in Ajman dedicated to ceramics and painting, which she currently manages and teaches regular ceramics classes in. The studio caters to professional and amateur artists and offers facilities, private spaces, memberships and classes. Since then, the studio has become an integral community space for Ajman's residents.

Al Ajmani graduated from Zayed University in 2016 with a BFA in Visual Arts and Applied Psychology. She currently works in Sharjah Art Foundation’s Community and Outreach Programme, organizing workshops, excursions, photowalks, and events to engage Sharjah’s community with artist exhibitions, location, and contemporary themes. 

Some of Al Ajmani’s notable exhibitions and other art-related public appearances include House of Failure at SIKKA Art Fair (2019),  Made in Tashkeel at Tashkeel (2018), Emirates Fine Arts Society’s  Annual Exhibition at Sharjah Art Museum (2018-2019), Vantage Point 6 at Sharjah Art Foundation (2018), Future Perfect Future exhibition at Al Serkal Avenue (2017), Markers & Makers exhibition in Manarat Al Saadiyat (2017), /4 (Out of Four) pilot round in Dubai Design District, twice runner-up for ADMAF’s Creativity Award (2015-2016), and first place winner of CDA’s Human Rights Short Film Competition (2014).

My name is Nastia Calaca, and I’m an independent ceramic artist from Ukraine, currently living and creating in Haarlem, the Netherlands.
 I have created a successful small ceramic brand, selling my works and putting smiles on people’s faces worldwide since 2016.
I consider my sculptures versatile and understandable, playful, sometimes humorous, and somehow narrative.
While I try to avoid using exact images or book illustrations as a base for my artwork, I come to them through my personal interpretations and childhood memories. 
Despite the fact that I’m focused mainly on the anthropomorphic subject in my art, I do admire people and they have always been a great inspiration to me.
I have happened to develop a style and chose a theme that people around the globe find appealing and worth investing in.
My own works make me chuckle, so maybe this is the answer.
I’m telling jokes and stories in clay.

I am a potter who aims at creating contemporary and playful shapes.
My approach to pottery is fairly intuitive. I enjoy experimenting with forms and glazes hoping that something unique will emerge.

Sarah Pike is a full time ceramic artist who makes functional pottery in her studio on the edge of a small town in the Rocky Mountains of Canada. She specializes in slabbuilt ceramics, which means she makes pottery from soft pieces of clay that she rolls flat by hand, textures, and then forms into functional wares. She is best know for her unique textures which she achieves by carving intricate texture tools out of clay and pressing these tools into the soft slabs clay in a variety of patterns and designs. Her work is pleasure to hold as the glaze surface is satiny smooth contrasting with the tactility of the raised patterns.
Sarah has been making pottery full time for 10 years, but ceramics has been a part of her life since childhood. She has exhibited internationally and sells her work worldwide. Sarah travels the world teaching workshops. Sarah's work is featured in a number of books and magazines. Sarah is a proud member of the Canadian ceramic collective, Make and Do.

Mi nombre es Martin Kano, Soy Productor Musical e Ingeniero de Mezcla y Mastering, llevo mas de 19 años en la industria musical, he producido y mezclado mas del 1300 canciones de diversos géneros (Rock, Pop, Electrónica, Jazz, Hip Hop, Trap, Boom Bap, Reggaeton, Reggae, Cumbia, Bossa Nova, Reggae, Electronica) de 40 países (Argentina, Uruguay, Brasil, Chile, Bolivia, Ecuador, Perú, Venezuela, Mexico, EEUU, Puerto Rico, Canada, Italia, Reino Unido, España, Australia, Corea del Sur, Japón, Mongolia, India, Tailandia, Francia, Finlandia, Estonia, Bélgica, China, Emiratos Arabes Unidos, Nueva Zelanda, Malasia, Rusia, Ucrania, Polonia, Alemania, Suiza, Sudafrica, Cameron, Arabia Saudita, Turquía, Islandia, Estonia, Nepal )


He Ganado de 4 Premios Internacionales: Premio MBN en Ecuador por Mejor Producción Musical, Latino Chicago Awards en EEUU, Monster Music Awards en Mexico y Premio Gardel 2023, también soy miembro votante de Latin Grammy.

En mi portfolio figuran Artistas y Empresas como: Alejandro Lerner, Charly Garcia, Hernan Cattaneo, Ke Personajes, Poncho, Malena Villa, Rescate, Frost, Redimi2, Manny Montes, John Schlitt (Petra), Abraham Laboriel, Michael Landau, Vinnie Colaiuta, Presidencia de la Nación Argentina, Presidencia de la Nacion Ecuador, Coca Cola, Nextel, Mercado Libre, La Campagnola, Budweiser, Fivver.

 Tuve la bendición de ser el único productor musical en Sudamerica que trabajo junto al legendario Geoff Emerick (Ingenieros de los disco mas reconocidos de The Beatles) como asi tambien con ingenieros de audio reconocidos en el mundo como: Chris Lord-Alge, Michael Brauer, Sylvia Massy, Joe Baldrige, Gustavo Borner.
 Fui invitado en dos oportunidades al “Concierto 1×1” organizado por el Gobierno Nacional de Ecuador en la Ciudad de Cuenca y Quito, para poder asesorar a nuevas bandas y artistas de todo el pais.

Actualmente junto a mi empresa de seminarios presenciales llamada MasterClass Premium colaboramos con Dolby impartiendo  sesiones formativas sobre Dolby Atmos Music.

Alejo Stivel es cantante, compositor y productor musical; un artista dentro del escenario y detrás de la mesa del estudio. Fundador de Tequila, la mítica banda de rock.

Se ha consagrado como el productor musical de mayor prestigio de España, habiendo producido más de 200 discos, que vendieron de más de 8 millones de copias. Entre los que destacan "19 días y 500 noches" de Joaquín Sabina, El canto del loco, La oreja de Van Gogh, M Clan, La Cabra Mecánica, Jarabe de Palo, Estopa, Fito Páez, Charly García, Fer del grupo Maná, entre muchos otros.

Dentro de su inmensa trayectoria también ha compuesto miles de jingles para publicidad, ha dirigido obras musicales teatrales, y por su estudio han pasado innumerables estrellas internacionales.

Hola! Soy Nico Astegiano!

Qué bueno conocernos en este momento... me presento! Soy Nicolas Astegiano, Youtuber, Productor, Técnico Superior en Sonido y medios Audiovisuales. Dueño de Audire Studios, llevo mas de 14 años trabajando dentro de la industria musical de manera activa, con más de 60 producciones discográficas y más de 350 producciones musicales individuales. 
Ademas soy músico multi-instrumentista, principalmente desde la guitarra y llevo en paralelo mi proyecto musical llamado "Closbit". 
La música es mi pasión y mi gran amor desde mi infancia, vivo rodeado de ella la mayor parte de mi tiempo y espero que así sea por el resto de mi vida!

Me llamo Luca Petricca y soy técnico de sonido y productor musical desde hace más de veinte años. 
Empecé trabajando como asistente de ingeniero en estudios de grabación cuando tenía 20 años y poco a poco fui ascendiendo a puestos con más responsabilidad gracias a las oportunidades que me dieron técnicos y estudios de Madrid, hasta llegar a un nivel en el que me pude enfrentar yo solo a las demandas y necesidades que tenían mis clientes. Explico esto primero porque es una responsabilidad muy grande tener en tus manos la obra de alguien y que dependa de ti en una cierta medida la huella que va a dejar esa obra en el público que la escuche. Por eso hay que tener paciencia, ir ganando experiencia en la prueba/error que nos enseña la profesión, y ser muy consciente de tu responsabilidad como técnico de grabación, mezcla o productor en un proyecto.
Yo empecé trabajando en cinta analógica y pasé a trabajar en Protools con sus primeras versiones, primero como pistas extras sincronizadas con mi cinta y después ya como mi daw principal. He seguido trabajando en esa plataforma desde entonces hasta ahora, es decir, tengo más de quince años de experiencia con Protools. 
Soy además uno de los dueños de un estudio de grabación en Madrid que se llama Estudios Reno. Tras diez años de freelance trabajando en diferentes estudios en España y ejerciendo labores de mezclador, productor asociado y técnico para diferentes productores, decidí abrir Reno para poder trabajar más con la parte de la industria musical con la que me sentía más vinculado a nivel emocional y personal, la música independiente. Desde el rock y el pop en todas sus vertientes, pasando por electrónica, rap y coqueteos con el jazz o el soul hasta llegar a música instrumental o experimental. Sintiendo siempre que cada uno de esos proyectos formó parte de mi vida en el momento en el que trabajaba en él. Es la única forma en la que puedo trabajar. Siendo durante un tiempo miembro del grupo con el que trabajo.
Ahora además de mantener mi estudio y mi carrera como técnico de FOH en directo, soy también profesor mezcla en una escuela en Madrid, United Pop, con lo que se me ha abierto un camino que nunca pensé y que es también muy satisfactorio, como es el poder ayudar a jóvenes y no tan jóvenes interesados en el sonido a utilizar una serie de herramientas y métodos de trabajo para que sus proyectos tengan un proceso y resultado más profesional y por lo tanto más satisfactorio. 
Al final, lo que queremos con la música es hacer sentir y para eso los mezcladores tenemos que utilizar todos nuestros conocimientos técnicos y casi psicológicos para lograr hacer sentir al público lo que la canción propone con los elementos que hay grabados.
Espero que este curso de Domestika os ayude en alguna medida, ya sea técnica y/o emocional, a sentir que vuestra música llega un poco más lejos de lo que habíais podido imaginar antes.

Soy Productor Musical, ingeniero de Mezcla & Músico
Desde niño sentí una fuerte atracción por el arte, siempre me gustó dibujar, escribir y crear. Así fue como a los 13 años mis papás me regalaron mi primera guitarra eléctrica y desde ese momento no la volví a soltar más. Terminando la etapa del colegio, había que decidir qué hacer con mi futuro, y asi fue, gracias al apoyo de mi familia, que entre a estudiar música en Santiago de Chile, Pero ya estando dentro rápidamente me di cuenta que mi camino no iba por ahí solamente, ahi fue cuando al siguiente año, decidí cambiarme de carrera a Ingeniería en Sonido, aunque para ser honesto, no iba mucho clases, no por que no quisiera, sino porque en ese tiempo ya me encontraba realizando mis primeros trabajos como músico e ingeniero de grabación, primeras experiencias laborales que fueron fundamentales para mi desarrollo profesional mientras estudiaba y así fue como el año 2010 me titulé como Ingeniero en sonido. 

Hoy, después de haber incursionado en varios rubros dentro del área de la música y el sonido, ya tengo 12 años de experiencia… Produciendo, grabando y mezclando música para artistas, publicidad y películas de toda Latinoamérica. 

Entre algunas cosas interesantes que me han pasado a lo largo de mi carrera, te puedo contar que tuve el honor de ganar un premio Altazor por la Producción y Mezcla de el disco "El Vacilón" de Combo Ginebra el año 2013, este fue elegido como el “disco Tropical del año”, después Música que realice fue Ganadora de varios premios Achap de publicidad, lo que me llevó a estar varios años ligado a la música para publicidad y televisión. Es por esto que mezclando mis experiencias pasadas, me llamaron para ser uno de los Productores Musicales para el programa de televisión The Voice Chile en sus dos primeras temporadas, en donde tuve el placer de trabajar con artistas como Luis Fonsi, Ana Torroja, Franco Simone, Nicole y Alvaro Lopez, entre otros. Posteriormente, el año 2018, tuve el honor de haber sido ganador del premio a la Mejor canción internacional del Festival de Viña 2018 en co-composición junto a la artista chilena Gabigar. Lo cual meses después nos llevó a radicarnos en méxico por un par de años. 

Además, he tenido la fortuna de aunque he estado con trabajos bien demandantes, nunca he dejado de tocar en vivo, en donde he tenido la oportunidad de trabajar como músico de sesión para artistas como Mon Laferte, La Garfield, Lucybell, Saiko, Kudai, Cami y Gabigar entre varios otros. 

Actualmente me encuentro viviendo en Santiago de Chile, dedicado a mi carrera como Productor Musical & Mixer, tengo mi estudio en Downbeat Studios y desde algunos meses, creamos junto a 3 colegas, Downbeat Music Lab, donde nos encargamos de trabajar de manera integral producciones musicales a nivel global, desde la composición hasta el producto final.

Hello everyone! 👋

 I'm a published wildlife artist based in the beautiful Worcestershire countryside, painting, writing, and running art retreats both locally and overseas. Since joining Domestika in 2020, I’ve loved watching the community grow and enjoy seeing your projects and feedback, which have inspired my book launched in 2024 📚.

Nature is my biggest inspiration 🌿—the birds and animals around my home and studio fuel my creativity. While I've been creating art since childhood, I became a professional artist just over 7 years ago after advanced training in the UK and USA. Since then, I’ve exhibited my work across the UK and New York, and my art has been showcased on luxury cruise liners by Cunard and P&O 🚢. My work is also available through major retailers like Wayfair, Next, and Amazon. I’m represented by Demontfort Fine Art, with pieces in Whitewall and Clarendon Fine Art Galleries 🎨. Fun fact: I designed the logo for Robert Plant's band, Saving Grace! 🎶

Teaching art is a passion of mine, and I love introducing people to the joy of watercolor. As the Resident Artist at Arley Estates in Bewdley, I hold regular classes at the estate's studios.

For face-to-face classes, retreats, and online content, visit my website and subscribe to my newsletter to stay updated! ✨

Www.sarahstokesartist.co.uk

I have been painting since I was a kid. My mom was an artist too, we were always painting together. I studied Astronomy at the university and after that I started to have an interest in digital arts. My focus was mostly in 3d environment modelling.

I have been working in the digital graphics industry since 2005. Last 12 years, we worked on with clients such as Warner Bros, Paramount, Capcom, Ubisoft, 2K, Square Enix and Bethesda for creating digital marketing content. 

I love watercolors and matte paintings. Those 2 subjects are like passion to me.

I’m an artist-illustrator based in London, UK.

Combining bold, expressive brushstrokes and decisively drawn lines, my paintings of nature feel spontaneous and joyful whilst avoiding the sentimentality often associated with wildlife. I'm interested in the way we romanticise the natural world, how we anthropomorphise or uphold elements as desirable whilst disregarding others as a nuisance.

As a teacher, and an artist, I focus on the mistakes. They are fundamental to making creative discoveries and in trying to avoid them we risk stifling ourselves. My courses invite students to draw and paint in unusual and experimental ways, to let go of being in complete control and become open to the unexpected.

I draw mostly in watercolour, ink and coloured pencil, but also experiment with found materials and tools (bubble wrap, emulsion paint, sticks, teabags, squashed blackberries, paintbrush handles…). I often stand to draw and paint on the floor which injects an energy and playfulness to my drawings - the process for me is very physical, almost like a dance.

My work can been found on books, homeware, fabric and fine art prints, and includes clients such as Waterstones, John Lewis, Laura Ashley, Whistlefish, Woodmansterne and Profile Books.

I am an experienced botanical artist and tutor of over 25 years. I paint realistic plant portraits in watercolour and particularly enjoy painting fading flowers, autumnal leaves and seed heads, often painting them larger than life.

I have been awarded four Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) Gold medals for collections of paintings on a botanical theme, amongst many other awards. I have exhibited and taught worldwide and have work in the Shirley Sherwood Collection, the RHS Linley Library and Hunt Institute for Botanical Documentation as well as private collections. My botanical illustrations have appeared on Royal Mail stamps depicting British Flora.

Hello! My name is Emma Thrussell and I am an illustrator from the United Kingdom. I started out my professional creative journey at Ravensbourne university where I studied Art, Design and Animation. I loved experimenting with various art disciplines and this is where I found the passion for illustration and design. 

I work as a freelancer from my cosy studio in South-East London and mostly work in traditional mediums such as watercolours, coloured pencils, paper craft and gouache. My style can be described as whimsical and child-like with a geometric flare.

Hi! I'm Astrid, also known as Urban Anna. I'm a self-taught artist who started creating illustrations with watercolor and pen in 2020. My work is all about capturing the beauty of worldly architecture, and making the everyday magical!

You might have stumbled upon my coloring books Urban Coloring 1, 2 and 3, From Paris with Love, London Baby or Rome is where my heart is and if you like, check out my online course here on Domestika, where I'll share all my secrets and unique style and techniques. And if you're one of my over 300k Instagram followers, thank you so much! It's incredible to have such a global audience appreciating my work. From charming pubs to vibrant storefronts and other colorful facades, my illustrations aim to give you a fresh perspective on the world around us.

Here you can find me on Instagram and Facebook: @UrbanAnna20

I am not: a graphic designer with 30+ years experience or qualified in fine arts.
I am: a Science graduate, creative, analyst, advocate for humanity, cat lady and feeling awkward writing this.

My mission is to humanize statistics. *Really* personalize findings. And elicit lasting emotional
connections by creating original, empathetic data illustrations. Data collected from people, transformed and presented for people.

Hi I'm Jing. I'm an illustration living in the UK. I have been working in the creative field for over 10 years. My clients range from governments to businesses, including European Parliament, UNICEF, General Electric, IBM, Apple, Samsung, Adobe, Google, Washington Post, Dubai Expo and many others.  I love adding lots and lots details to my illustrations. My approach is always, more is more. Apart from that, I have also been a part of the jury of D&AD Award, which is one of the most prestigious awards in design. In my spare time, I have grown 50+ types of plants in my garden (and yes, I talk to them).

Hi, I am Sonja Kuijpers, running STUDIO TERP, my one-woman data illustration studio based in Eindhoven, Netherlands. I design (data-)visualisations for a diversity of clients such as Scientific American, Philips, Frankfurter Allgemeiner, as well as small institutions, companies, and publishers. Any sort of subject or client is a potential to me, I really like the variety and the interaction with researchers and different disciplines.
I love experimenting with shapes and styles, and I also design my own independent (personal) dataviz and data art projects. In 2019 I received an Information is Beautiful Gold Award for my personal project ‘A View on despair’. Creating data visualisation, to me, is trying to locate myself in the data, making sense of numbers with a human approach, showing insights as well as the aesthetics of information and data. 

You can also find me crawling through the forest with my camera, taking pictures of fungi: the big, but most of all the teeny tiny ones.

I am an independent data visualization designer. I designed data visualizations for Google, UN, Scientific American, BBC Science Focus, Penguin Books and La Lettura. I'm co-author of the infographics children's book “Planet Earth”, published by National Geographic Kids and White Star and co-author of the "Geopolitical Atlas of Water".

Many of my projects have an experimental approach and I'm interested in exploring the relationship between data visualization and people.

Hi! I’m Catalina. I'm an information designer who translates complex ideas into meaningful and understandable visual forms that include –but are not limited to: infographics, illustrated maps, charts, and graphs.
I hold an undergraduate degree in Architecture and a master’s degree in Art History, both areas in which I have explored, practiced, and researched how ideas are represented from technical and artistic standpoints. I've taught several university courses in design theory and visual narratives.
During the last 15 years, I’ve worked at the intersection of illustration, design, and visual information. My work can be found online (Dropbox, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Stamen, Wire) and in print media (RBA, Editorial Planeta). 
I live and work in Seattle, WA crafting infographics at GoodRx.

Hola, I'm a designer, doodler, and CEO at Blush, a tool to unlock people's creativity. I previously worked at companies like InVision, Lyft, and Carbon Health. I give design workshops and share design tutorials online. I also host a design podcast, manage Latinxs Who Design, give talks worldwide, and write silly comics.

Patricia Reiners is a UX/UI designer based in Berlin. As a creative resident at Adobe she explored the city of the future and how new technologies like AI, voice control, and augmented reality will change our interfaces. As a podcast host of the “Future of UX”, she is curious about how immersive technology, experience design and society shape the way we connect and design. Patricia loves to share her knowledge through workshops and talks on conferences and works with companies that share her passions for problem-solving and using immersive technologies to benefit society.

Ciao, I am Chiara Aliotta!
I am an Italian award-winning designer with years of experience as a graphic designer, art director, and brand consultant.

I am the creative brain that powers Until Sunday. 
I created my own brand because my work involves wearing many different ‘hats’.  

I designed for organisations large and small (from Joomla and Smashing Magazine to PAMS Foundation, Action Aid Hellas and Medicins Sans Frontieres), but I have also led and developed the artistic vision of several global companies.
And as if that wasn’t quite enough, I also lead multi-disciplinary creative teams, blog regularly about branding and typography, co-run an art gallery, and speak at global creative events!

When I am not working, you will find me travelling, capturing photographs, or taking a dip in the sun-dappled Aegean Sea.

Hello Domestika students!

I am a passionate Design Lead at Build in Amsterdam since 2015. Originally from Strasbourg, France, I am an alumnus of Gobelins School in PariI where I studied interactive design. My practice has been notable for approaching digital design with an accessible mindset, I regularly shares my findings through conference talks & lectures both in-person and virtually (Awwards, Digital Design Days, FITC). My work encompasses brand identities, digital flagship store design for lifestyle & fashion brands (Adidas, Moooi, as well as online exhibitions & museum platforms (Foam Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam, Frans Hals Museum) I am particularly intrigued by the potential of multi-sensory experiences, and have incorporated Augmented Reality, 3D, and sound design into my projects.

My commitment to helping others leverage web accessibility guidelines to their advantage & create outstanding websites that anyone can use is a mission I hold dear. 

I look forward to sharing my knowledge with you!

teacher.aboutMe:
Tsering Carola is a visionary multidisciplinary researcher, writer, and advocate of meditation and contemplative practices, with over 22 years of dedicated study in human behavior, mindful-healing techniques, and the wellness industry. Deeply rooted in Tibetan Buddhism, she integrates Buddhist philosophy and psychology, Eastern traditions, and biodesprogramming into her work, helping individuals unlock their inner potential, spark creativity, and achieve balance in their personal and professional lives.

Specializing in conscious lifestyle and conscious parenting, Tsering has led meditation retreats, talks, and wellness events worldwide, including in NYC, Scotland, Spain, the UK, Mexico, and Colombia. Her work is a blend of ancient wisdom and modern practices, designed to guide individuals toward living with purpose and authenticity.

As a mentor to leaders, CEOs, artists, and families, Tsering specializes in helping people discover their true calling, or "dharma," guiding them step by step to create lives filled with purpose, abundance, and peace. Through her unique methodology, The Path, she empowers others to align their personal, financial, and professional lives with their deepest values and aspirations.

Through Dharma Parents a community-based project that includes a newsletter and course platform, she shares transformative insights on mindfulness, self-awareness, and conscious living. Her mission is to help parents transform parenting into a path of wisdom and personal growth. Additionally, she created Dharma Kids and Elephant Garden  a space dedicated to teaching permaculture, meditation and mindfulness practices to children and adolescents, equipping them with essential life skills from an early age.

Tsering is also the co-founder of Popcycled, an innovative eco-conscious community art studio that promotes upcycling art and mindfulness practices for kids. Through this initiative, she fosters creativity, sustainability, and mindfulness in younger generations.

Her expertise and research extend to her blog, OM Curated and Podcast Nectar Corazon where she shares insights on well-being, spirituality, and conscious lifestyle, wisdom stories, offering readers practical tools for living with intention and awareness.

I am a fineliner artist from Ontario, Canada interested in the intricate details of interiors, plants, and animals, and the creation of newly imagined places. I love architecture and depicting familiar, comforting objects and furniture.

Growing up on a farm, surrounded by animals and antiques, well-loved furniture and objects have had a huge influences on my drawings. My highly detailed works depict dozens of animals and their surroundings, each drawing absolutely brimming with textures and patterns.

 I began drawing and painting from an early age, and attended the University of Western Ontario for my Bachelors of Fine Art in 2018. Upon graduation, I dove right into making drawing my main focus, further exploring the possibilities of fineliner pen. 

Since 2018, my drawings have been displayed in Toronto, Montreal, Nova Scotia, and New York. I am thrilled that both the Colart Collection and Sifton Properties have acquired my works, and that I've been featured in two issues of Create! Magazine. My drawings are collected internationally.
