Naci en Tijuana, B.C. 1973. Creci en Las Playas de Rosarito. Estudie diseño Gráfico en San Diego City College y ilustración en California College of Arts en San Francisco. En 2005 fui becario del FONCA Jóvenes Creadores y Sistema Nacional de Creadores, categoría Narrativa Gráfica durante el periodo 2013-2016. El resultado del proyecto desarrollado con el apoyo SNCA 2013/16 es la novela gráfica Starseeds (2017), publicada por Fantagraphics, Seattle. Además, el cómic Sigil de Crystal fue reconocido con la distinción The Best American Comics (2012) y el cómic Érase una vez obtuvo el 2do lugar en la Bienal de Miradas y fue seleccionado en Images of American Illustration 36 (2017).

Mis ilustraciones han sido publicadas en revistas como Rolling Stone Magazine, Nickelodeon Magazine, UCLA Magazine, Picnic Magazine, New York Times, Variety, Revista Complot y Gatopardo entre otras. En el ámbito comercial he desarrollado proyectos gráficos para empresas como American Airlines, Tequila Silver 1800, Sony Playstation, Jose Cuervo y Miller Lite. Fui seleccionado para aparecer en la sección Fresh de la Revista Communication Arts Magazine en el año 2002.
 
Mi obra ha sido incluida en galleries en New York, Madrid, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Mexico City, France, Berlin, y en museos como Museo Carrillo Gil, Museum of art Oceanside, Museum Contemporary Arts Ssan Diego, Museo de Arte Zapopan, Museum International Des Arts Modesties de Ssettee. Museo de Arte Tijuan, Cecut.

I love comic books. With more than 20 years experience drawing comic books, fanzines and stories with characters such as Judge Dredd, Power Rangers, Starship Troopers and VR Troopers, the narrative possibilities never cease to amaze me. I have drawn graphic novels with Robin Hood, King Arthur, Joan of Arc, the 16th century pirate Grace O’Malley and the graphic novel The Coldest City, written by Antony Johnston, was adapted to film in 2017 as Atomic Blonde, with oscar-winning Charlize Theron.

I have written and published numerous comic book short stories and creator-owned projects, both in the UK and Brazil, such as Project Mega-Ultra, WAR and 10 Lost Days, and also work with book and magazine illustration, plus storyboards for TV and advertising. I was born in England and now live in sunny São Paulo, with my wife and two daughters.

Jimmy is the creator of the popular comic- They Can Talk.  He's amassed over one million followers and his comic has led to opportunities with leading animation studios, a successful greeting card line, and a published book.

My name is André Lima Araújo and I am a Portuguese architect and comics creator. I have worked for the major comics publishers in the US and with an ever growing body of creator owned projects. 
Soon after graduating with a Masters from University of Minho and briefly working as an architect for a year, I began my professional career in comics with Marvel, working on titles such as Fantastic Four, Avengers AI, Spider-Verse, Inhumans, Spidey and Black Panther, among many others. 
Through the years, I have contributed illustrations to a number of additional publications (like Duncan Jones’ Madi and covers for Millarworld or Giant Generator books). In parallel, I have been creating and developing my own comic projects, having published Man Plus (Titan Comics) and Generation Gone (co-created with Ales Kot, Image Comics).
More recently, I worked at DC Comics, where I begun my partnership with Brian Michael Bendis.
My latest book is the original crime thriller A Righteous Thirst For Vengeance, co-created with Rick Remender.
When I'm not working, I like being with my family, reading history books, driving and playing videogames. I lives in Ponte de Lima, Portugal, with my wife Luísa and our three daughters, Matilde, Inês and Leonor.

Alec Longstreth is an award-winning cartoonist, illustrator, and animator who lives in Santa Fe, New Mexico, USA.  Since 2002 he has drawn twenty-four issues of his minicomic, Phase 7 which have been collected into seven books. Two French translations of Alec's graphic novels have been published by L'employé du Moi. In 2007, Alec graduated from Pratt Institute's illustration program with highest honors. His illustration clients include Little, Brown & Co., Highlights, Nickelodeon Magazine, National Geographic for Kids, Weezer, and many others. Alec has also worked as a digital colorist for graphic novels published by Scholastic, and First Second Books. In 2008, Alec was a fellow at the Center for Cartoon Studies and after eight years as a member of the CCS faculty he now works as the school’s Director of Academic Outreach. In 2016, he launched his Eisner-nominated webcomic, Isle of Elsi.

Fred Van Lente is a six-time New York Times bestselling comics writer, novelist and playwright whose work spans mystery/thrillers to historical fiction to superheroes to comedy.

Van Lente burst onto the scene with his first collaboration with cartoonist Ryan Dunlavey, "Action Philosophers", which became a American Library Association Best Book for Teens and the New York Times called "intensely goofy but intellectually rigorous”.

From there he went on to a long career at Marvel, where he worked on titles like "The Amazing Spider-Man", "Captain America" and "Marvel Zombies". He’s also written for DC, Archie Comics, Dark Horse, Boom! Studios, Dynamite Comics, and Valiant, where his run on "Archer & Armstrong" was nominated for a Harvey Award for Best Continuing Series.

Van Lente has continued writing non-fiction graphic novels, often with his artistic collaborator Ryan Dunlavey, including the bestselling Comic Book History of Comics and the middle grade series "Action Presidents". Two entries in the series were nominated for the Excellence in Graphic Literature Awards. In 2021, the third volume won the Theodore Roosevelt Association's Theodore Roosevelt Children’s Book Prize.

His Platinum Studios graphic novel "Cowboys & Aliens" was adapted into a film in 2011 starring Daniel Craig and Harrison Ford, directed by Jon Favreau. The following year, Helen Cho, a character created with co-writer Greg Pak in their acclaimed "Incredible Hercules" series, made her MCU debut in the blockbuster "Avengers: Age of Ultron". His "MODOK’s 11" and "Scorpion" became Hulu’s "Marvel’s MODOK", which named the elementary school in the show after him.

teacher.aboutMe:
Aprender para compartir y compartir para aprender. Esa es la base de mi trabajo como consultora, formadora y conferenciante en comunicación digital e inteligencia artificial. Acompaño a profesionales y organizaciones en un momento en que la tecnología cambia a gran velocidad y necesitamos encontrar formas auténticas y sostenibles de comunicarnos. Mi objetivo no es solo optimizar procesos o introducir nuevas herramientas, sino ayudar a que la comunicación digital y la IA se conviertan en aliadas para crear, conectar y transformar.

Trabajo desde una visión estratégica y práctica:

- Auditorías y planes de acción que aportan claridad en la toma de decisiones.
- Estrategias de marca y comunicación que combinan creatividad y foco.
- Selección de profesionales, proveedores y aplicaciones digitales y de IA
- Programas formativos que desmitifican la tecnología y la hacen accesible.
- Conferencias y ponencias que acercan la IA y la innovación a todo tipo de públicos.

Mi labor es traducir conceptos complejos para que sean comprensibles y acercar la innovación tecnológica a las personas sin perder la esencia humana. Concibo la IA como un partner y una herramienta de cocreación que nos apoya en el análisis, la ideación, la toma de decisiones e incluso en desbloquear la creatividad en momentos clave. 

Me dedico a la comunicación desde 2002. En 2009 empecé a liderar estrategias en redes sociales en agencia y desde 2011 desarrollo mi actividad como profesional independiente de la comunicación digital. Desde 2022, con la apertura de ChatGPT al mundo y de otras plataformas, me he enfocado en la aplicación de la IA en comunicación y marketing digital y en la innovación y la cultura de empresa.

Trabajo con empresas y profesionales de diferentes sectores e imparto conferencias y clases en eventos y universidades.

He publicado siete cursos en Domestika con más de 170K alumnos en todo el mundo:

- Estrategia de comunicación para redes sociales
- LinkedIn: construye tu marca personal
- Instagram: concursos, sorteos, UGC y otras acciones tácticas
- Creación de contenidos con IA
- Introducción al Community Management con IA
- Creación de marca con IA
- Creación de asistentes de marketing digital con IA

Mi motor es la curiosidad: explorar cómo la tecnología puede ampliar nuestras posibilidades y compartir ese conocimiento para que otros puedan aplicarlo en su propio camino.

Si crees que puedo aportar valor a tu proyecto o te apetece conversar sobre cómo comunicar y crecer en la era de la IA, escríbeme, estaré encantada de escucharte.

teacher.aboutMe:
Aprender para compartir y compartir para aprender. Esa es la base de mi trabajo como consultora, formadora y conferenciante en comunicación digital e inteligencia artificial. Acompaño a profesionales y organizaciones en un momento en que la tecnología cambia a gran velocidad y necesitamos encontrar formas auténticas y sostenibles de comunicarnos. Mi objetivo no es solo optimizar procesos o introducir nuevas herramientas, sino ayudar a que la comunicación digital y la IA se conviertan en aliadas para crear, conectar y transformar.

Trabajo desde una visión estratégica y práctica:

- Auditorías y planes de acción que aportan claridad en la toma de decisiones.
- Estrategias de marca y comunicación que combinan creatividad y foco.
- Selección de profesionales, proveedores y aplicaciones digitales y de IA
- Programas formativos que desmitifican la tecnología y la hacen accesible.
- Conferencias y ponencias que acercan la IA y la innovación a todo tipo de públicos.

Mi labor es traducir conceptos complejos para que sean comprensibles y acercar la innovación tecnológica a las personas sin perder la esencia humana. Concibo la IA como un partner y una herramienta de cocreación que nos apoya en el análisis, la ideación, la toma de decisiones e incluso en desbloquear la creatividad en momentos clave. 

Me dedico a la comunicación desde 2002. En 2009 empecé a liderar estrategias en redes sociales en agencia y desde 2011 desarrollo mi actividad como profesional independiente de la comunicación digital. Desde 2022, con la apertura de ChatGPT al mundo y de otras plataformas, me he enfocado en la aplicación de la IA en comunicación y marketing digital y en la innovación y la cultura de empresa.

Trabajo con empresas y profesionales de diferentes sectores e imparto conferencias y clases en eventos y universidades.

He publicado siete cursos en Domestika con más de 170K alumnos en todo el mundo:

- Estrategia de comunicación para redes sociales
- LinkedIn: construye tu marca personal
- Instagram: concursos, sorteos, UGC y otras acciones tácticas
- Creación de contenidos con IA
- Introducción al Community Management con IA
- Creación de marca con IA
- Creación de asistentes de marketing digital con IA

Mi motor es la curiosidad: explorar cómo la tecnología puede ampliar nuestras posibilidades y compartir ese conocimiento para que otros puedan aplicarlo en su propio camino.

Si crees que puedo aportar valor a tu proyecto o te apetece conversar sobre cómo comunicar y crecer en la era de la IA, escríbeme, estaré encantada de escucharte.

teacher.aboutMe:
Hey! I’m María Araujo, the founder and creative mind behind María Amaría. My love for cakes started in my family’s kitchen, where I grew up baking alongside the incredible women in my life. What began as a fun passion project quickly turned into something much bigger—an internationally recognized cake studio where I get to blend art, flavor, and storytelling into every creation. Inspired by seasonal ingredients, floral designs, and my cultural roots, I love turning desserts into edible works of art that make every celebration extra special.

Over the years, I’ve had the chance to create cakes for destination weddings, luxury events, and all kinds of unforgettable moments. My work has taken me from Mexico City to Madrid, Miami, and New York, collaborating with amazing clients along the way. In this course, I want to share not just the techniques behind cake design but also the creativity and thought process that make each cake unique. Whether you’re just starting or looking to take your skills to the next level, I’m excited to help you bring your cake visions to life!

El Tarro de ideas es una curiosa agencia para los locos del Handmade o el "Hazlo tú mismo" fundada en 2011, y dedicada a dar contenido sobre todo DIY (Do It yourself), de reciclaje y vida sostenible para marcas y empresas y en donde también realizamos  workshops y eventos para agencias, medios de comunicación y marcas.

Hemos trabajado para Bezoya, 3M Scoth, Cointreau, Amazon, Cocacola, Peugeot, Turismo de Canarias, National Nederlanden, Limón y Nada, Skagen, Pinturas ALP, entre otros.

También tenemos un programa de televisión "Decoración Creativa" en Canal DeCasa de AMC Networks, en donde hacemos y fabricamos un montón de proyectos DIY de decoración y bricolaje 

Con un blog, "El sitio donde el tarro se destapa", y casi dos millones de seguidores en las redes sociales, se ha convertido en poderoso influencer en el sector, tratando de inspirar haciendo que los más valientes se atrevan a hacer muchas cosas con sus propias manos.

Hola, somos Marc y Cèlia y juntos creamos Antic&Chic hace más de 7 años, un estudio de interiorismo y taller de transformación de muebles. Nos hemos especializado en crear espacios que generan emociones en las personas que los habitan. De ahí nació la necesidad de incorporar piezas originales o antiguas, pero que se adaptaran a una decoración más actual. Nos gusta pensar que restaurando una casa o un mueble podemos conectar con todos los sentimientos que ha guardado a lo largo de su historia y crear así hogares y espacios con mucho carácter.

Nos apasiona descubrir la belleza escondida en objetos olvidados, sentir cómo el arte nos transforma y se transforma según los ojos que lo observan, y conectar con la magia de la naturaleza. Todo ello se ve reflejado en nuestros proyectos, tanto en la combinación de piezas antiguas y modernas, el uso de obras de arte, plantas y siempre con un toque de color que llena de alegría y frescura el resultado final.

Mi nombre es Lucas Rise, nací en Argentina. Desde muy pequeño a los 12 años tuve la posibilidad de comenzar con el oficio de pintor Letrista en la ciudad de 25 de Mayo, Buenos Aires. A los 18 años ingresé en la Universidad de Buenos Aires a estudiar Diseño Gráfico. Luego inicié un viaje por el mundo, lo que me llevó a descubrir muchas culturas gráficas/visuales y enriquecer mi mundo perceptivo. Años más tarde logre fusionar el manejo de la pintura de alta precisión con la creación de diseños propios sobre un formato interactivo como los muebles, acortando así las distancias entre el arte y el receptor. Hoy vivo en San Miguel de Allende, Mexico., donde desarrollo pintura sobre muebles y murales.

Soy Lucia, Argentina de la ciudad de Rosario, pero vivo en Capital Federal hace 12 años, me vine a estudiar Teatro, pero la vida me llevo siempre a conectar con los trabajos manuales, desde chica me gusta trabajar con telas, pinturas, cintas, hilos, y sobre todo dar nuevas oportunidades a los objetos, Reciclar.
Después de una larga búsqueda profesional encontré mi pasión en la Tapicería y el Reciclado de Muebles viejos. 
Amo poder darles nueva viva, renovarlos, mantener la historia que traen, pero adaptarlos a las nuevas tendencias y a las necesidades de cada uno.
Todo puede recuperarse es cuestión de poner manos a la obra! Y dejar todo nuestro amor en el proceso .
Bienvenidas las nuevas oportunidades!

Hola mi nombre es Neus de Crea Decora Recicla y aquí te hago un resumen de mi trayectoria profesional dedicada a la Chalk Paint. 
Mi profesión me ha despertado muchas pasiones y en especial la de compartir conocimientos con otras personas y crear una fantástica comunidad que me llena de energía e ilusión. 

Hace ya una década que empecé mi andadura con este fantástico material. He trabajado con las marcas más prestigiosas de Chalk Paint del mercado y he sido formada de su mano en España, Reino Unido y Bélgica. Fui pionera en España en la divulgación de este producto, produciendo infinidad de tutoriales y vídeos para expandir las virtudes de un producto que nos ayuda a crear un hogar más bello y sostenible.

Decidí sumergirme en este mundo en el 2012, año en el que abrí mi tienda física, mi tienda online y mi taller dedicado exclusivamente a este material. A lo largo de estos años han pasado miles de personas por mi taller y otras tantas por nuestra tienda. También son miles las que cada día se asoman a nuestro perfil de Instagram a buscar inspiración para mejorar su hogar.

Con mi trabajo siento que pongo mi granito de arena para que entre todos construyamos un mundo más respetuoso con el medio ambiente, más creativo y más bello.

- 𝘌𝘴𝘤𝘳𝘪𝘣𝘪𝘮𝘰𝘴 𝘶𝘯𝘢 𝘯𝘶𝘦𝘷𝘢 𝘩𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘰𝘳𝘪𝘢 𝘤𝘰𝘯 𝘭𝘢𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘪𝘨𝘶𝘢𝘴 𝘮𝘢𝘳𝘤𝘢𝘴 𝘥𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘰𝘴 𝘮𝘶𝘦𝘣𝘭𝘦𝘴 -

Violette nace por nuestra inquietud frente al medio ambiente y reciclaje llevado al diseño de interiores y objetos.
Nos mueve la renovación de muebles, objetos y espacios. Renovar revitaliza tu entorno y convierte un espacio en tu espacio, donde quieres estar, donde perteneces.

Diseñamos cuidadosamente nuestros proyectos para interpretar lo mejor posible a nuestros clientes. Creemos que es fundamental crear espacios y objetos armónicos y acogedores que se sientan vividos y propios.

En todas nuestras áreas, buscamos reflejar la personalidad, gustos y ritmos de cada persona a través de un proceso conversado y meticuloso.

teachers.aboutMe:
Apasionada de las técnicas tradicionales textiles y el diseño de interiores cada año viajo a distintos paises para inspirarme y aprender nuevos métodos para desarrollar mis colecciones de textiles utilizando principalmente Macrame y Telar para su producción.
Mis diseños están enfocados tanto para residencias privadas como instalaciones de hoteles y restaurantes.

¡Hola! Soy Larissa Meléndez, diseñadora textil originaria de Chihuahua, México. 

En 2016 descubrí mi fascinación por moldear fibras y empecé a desarrollar mi marca Raké Boho Decor, proyecto donde he explorado, principalmente, el arte del macramé. 
A través de patrones geométricos y formas orgánicas creo piezas auténticas destinadas a brindar armonía y personalidad a espacios y momentos memorables, casi siempre regida por un estilo bohemio. Me gusta viajar ¡y a mi trabajo también! Mis nudos se encuentran decorando espacios a lo largo de mi bello país, desde Los Cabos hasta la Riviera Maya y fuera de éste en Estados Unidos, Canadá, Colombia e Inglaterra. También ha sido exhibido en medios digitales e impresos como AD México y Design Hunter.
Actualmente vivo en Mérida, Yucatán, ciudad que inspiró mi segunda marca Rama Fiber Art, donde junto con mi hermana Vian me encuentro explorando caminos distintos del arte textil.

Los nudos se han convertido en mi terapia y mi manera de vivir lento, feliz y con agradecimiento comparto con cariño lo que para mí ha sido un regalo.

¡Hola! Soy Mapi Casafranca, artista textil y fundadora de AMARENA, marca sostenible de piezas artesanales.
Soy administradora de profesión, pero desde pequeña los productos hechos a mano han sido parte esencial de mi vida, cada fibra que tejo hoy en día está impregnada de las tardes que pasé tejiendo con mi abuela y mamá.

AMARENA nace hace dos años de mi interés por los materiales naturales y el deseo de mantener viva la tradición de tejido ancestral a través de accesorios. 
Hoy, es una marca comprometida con el comercio justo y la producción sostenible que une las técnicas tradicionales de artesanas peruanas con acabados cuidadosamente diseñados. Con el objetivo de transmitir su cultura al mundo a través de bolsos únicos y modernos hechos de fibras naturales que trascienden el paso del tiempo.

Cuando decidí hacer de mi pasión un negocio propio, tuve la oportunidad de conocer muchas comunidades de artesanos y con ellos muchas historias fascinantes. Y es que cuando trabajamos con las manos, todos podemos transmitir nuestra personalidad, historia y tradiciones a nuestras piezas.

Hola! Soy Sara Moreno,  una burgalesa afincada en Madrid, amante de mi familia, la naturaleza y la artesanía textil.

Llevo mas de 10 años creando y desarrollando mi marca Fruto Samore. Una marca vinculada al interiorismo y decoración del hogar, apostando por una decoración sostenible y artesanal 100%.

Mi especialidad son los tapices de telar y macramé.... pero esto último es lo que mas me apasiona y da mas juego a mi creatividad.

Mi mayor ilusión y misión es mostrar todo el mundo lo que se puede hacer en macramé, técnica que no conoce limites y que tiene grandes beneficios para la salud practicando la nudoterapia. Quiero conseguir que cada día seamos más macramistas practicando mi lema: #MacramakersNonStop. Te unes??

Hola! Mi nombre es Daniela Chiñas, soy diseñadora y artista textil. Soy originaria de San Cristóbal de las casas, Chiapas y de Oaxaca, por lo que desde muy chica estuve sumergida en el mundo textil, ya que estas dos partes de México cuentan con una riqueza cultural textil muy extensa. Considero esto como el precursor por mi interés en proyectos de arte y diseño mediante diferentes técnicas artesanales, ocupando diferentes medios, sobre todo los textiles.

Teniendo como base la carrera de Diseño Textil, empecé a explorar las diferentes posibilidades de este material y comencé con mi proyecto personal Daāch. Proyecto que me ha permitido relacionarme con diferentes técnicas creativas y artesanales para comunicar de diferentes maneras, ideas y emociones a través de los materiales, técnicas, pigmentos y texturas.

El objetivo de Daāch, es revalorizar el trabajo artesanal y de oficios en los tiempos actuales, donde los medios industriales y tecnológicos han cambiado la percepción de los trabajos hechos a mano, dándoles el valor que realmente merecen, tanto de manera histórica, social y económica. Permitiéndome trabajar tanto de manera personal como colectiva.

teachers.aboutMe:
Hello, I'm a calligraphy artist, hand engraver and stationery designer.  

Starting my career as a graphic designer I first fell in love with the slow intentional strokes of calligraphy at a workshop in the beginning of 2014. Seeking out workshops and books from calligraphers all around the world my evenings and weekends were quickly occupied by those perfectly imperfect strokes and my home was filled with beautiful inks, papers and nibs. 

Setting up my own calligraphy studio a few years later I now spend most of my time in my studio in South London, working on commissions from luxury brands and loved up couples in the UK and across the world. But when I’m not there you might see me in a beautiful store personalising gifts or teaching a workshop. My approach to calligraphy is very much seeking the joy in the process and celebrating that charm and expression of calligraphy and lettering crafted by hand. 

I've had the pleasure of working with brands such as Cartier, Estée Lauder, The Diana Award, Paperchase and Tate Britain. My work has been featured in beautiful places like Love My Dress, Rock My Wedding, Green Wedding Shoes, Wedding Chicks and Whimsical Wonderland Weddings.

Born and raised in Hokkaido, Japan, I started practicing Shodo at the age of five under the creative supervision of her grandmother, a distinguished GAYU calligrapher. Later I began to take sessions at a Gayu SHODO calligraphy school. This laid a solid foundation not only for my development of the various layers of calligraphy technique and skills but also for the SUMIE technique in calligraphic design.

I work as a freelance artist and a professional calligrapher in U.K./Europe and Japan Since 2000. Besides creating various media of calligraphy works and Neo-Japonism art, my passion for learning and teaching SHODO and the interest in developing the effective method of teaching this beautiful form of art has always been expanding. 

●Since 2002, I give SHODO the art of traditional Japanese calligraphy” lessons based on "one to one" private sessions as well as workshops and group classes . Through my teaching experiences in Japan and Europe with multiple age groups and backgrounds, I developed an original effective yet creative way of teaching SHODO - the Mindfulness-Based-Method. Which I believe works for everyone. I've been teaching with this method since 15 years now.

●I focus on bringing the balance of mind and body together as well as student's individual mindfulness process by specially designed practices. So students can learn little by little how to concentrate on their own Qi (living-energy) flow, conduct and apply it with brush and ink onto the paper.
My lesson is totally tailor suited to individual level/speed/needs and provides the most suitable text for the student's technical development in every lesson and workshops. 
The calligraphy texts are based on seasonal, classics, haiku, tanka, Zen and being prepared for improving sensitive stages of skills, techniques and calligraphy styles.

●My original method and concept of teaching SHODO calligraphy is focused on: 
- mind and body connection
- discovering individual inner quality and peace
- "hands-on" guidance 
- tailor-suited lesson for each individual and needs 
- the middle balance
- "Here and Now" momentum flow 
- the mindfulness process
- distressing the body tension
- breathing awareness
- rising the Qi(energy)flow and awareness 

More info and details:
My SHODO site: 
My Neo-Japonism site: 
ARIGATO

●My inspiration is classical Japanese literature, Ukiyoe & floating world, poetry& classic calligraphy, Japonisme influenced art, Art Nouveau & Art Déco styles, antique Kimono, art of Taisho Romanticism (1910-20's style) and modern art of Japan. As well as everyday life’s living words and letters, living colours, lines, patterns and shapes .

●My passion is to discover a continuity of time and spiritual existence and develop what I refer to as the ’Neo-Japonism’ — a new form of style depicting and conveying the sense of Japanese aesthetics. Specially I am fascinated by a new quality of a co-exisitng spirit and aesthetic as a result of uniting the essence of traditional Japanese art & craftsmanship and various form of Japonisme influenced modern paintings.
I use the new way of fusing my calligraphy and Sumie skills with those forms of art.
And - I just love doing it!

HAPPY PRCTICE!

I’m an award-winning artist who takes inspiration from the incredibly rich and diverse heritage of Islamic arts. Being a student of both the ancient and modern world, I strive to continue a tradition of art based on nature, geometrical beauty and the Sacred. I combine art forms from the ‘Maghreb’ (Northwest Africa) region, Medieval Fatimids to the Safavid Persians and the Mughal Indians to create work that I believe calls us back to our Beloved and to our essential oneness with nature. 
My career started in 2009 when the Mica Gallery in Knightsbridge, London showcased 20 small pieces of my calligraphy. Since then, I’ve had my art displayed across the UK in public and private exhibition and galleries – including in Battersea Power Station, the Three Faiths Forum, various auction houses, and corporate and private collections including members of the Jordanian Royal Family. I have also successfully collaborated with global brands such as: Christian Dior, Jo Malone, Molton Brown, AERIN, Estée Lauder, HP Latex, Al Jazeera and many more.
My appreciation of the historic traditional practices is combined with a desire for self-expression, a love of watercolour as a medium and an acute sense of colour. The result is a mix of ancient disciplines with vivid colours and a modern expressive technique. This integration of arabic calligraphy, sacred geometry and biomorphic patterns, expressed through watercolours, is unique to me.

Thomas Lam, is a Chinese calligrapher, 'ShuFa' artist based in London. He was born and raised in Hong Kong. Since his elementary school, he has started his artistic journey fascinated by art, Chinese culture and history, began with writing KaiShu(Regular script), and grew to love LiShu(Clerical script), HangShu (Running script) and CaoShu (Cursive scripts) later.

For the last 15 years, he has been sharing his artworks online and through workshops in Hong Kong and UK. He has also developed a learning system for teaching all Chinese cultural and calligraphy lovers to master and to enjoy the writing skill. His calligraphy has as well been proudly graced in many body-art, logo, posters and large brand name designs from all over the world, both commercially and privately.    

His passion range from traditional ink-handwriting to modern graphic designs with oriental culture. He is exceptionally informative about comparing a large variety of calligraphy writing tool from Japan, Taiwan and China, including choices of paper, brush and ink and the relation to the writing effects and outcome. Recently his interest has expanded into writing with watercolour and has blended in different elements of crafts into his art creations.

First woman Hebrew Scribe - Orthodox-Certified Soferet STaM (female Jewish traditionally religious calligrapher) in modern times, trained in Jerusalem.  Have been the subject of TV and film documentaries, newspaper and radio interviews and given numerous talks in Canada, Israel, the USA, Italy, and the UK.  Professional fine artist and illustrator, academic with an MA in Art & Science, designer, accredited gemologist, writer, speaker, & radio personality, initiated as a Bat Qol within the Jewish Renewal Movement.  University Lecturer, having taught at many venues on three continents.  Currently splitting my time between Vancouver and London.

I am Carol Fountain Nix, an award-winning entrepreneur, educator, designer, and calligrapher. My work is a fusion of mixed media and calligraphy. My inspiration originates from the colors and textures in nature, and I seek to create works that have an organic, earthy feel. I grew up in the Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina in the USA, which provides an endless array of visual stimulation: rock formations, tree limbs, vines, mossy beds, and cool creek sides lined with mountain laurel.

I am forever a student of calligraphy and I have studied with some of the world’s bests lettering artists. It is a skill that requires dedication, desire, and an acute attention to detail. My goal is to create and preserve the integrity of each letter – not an easy task when writing over many layers of media. Each piece relates directly and metaphorically with the content with regard to composition, color, tone, placement and style.

I have taught calligraphy, hand lettering and typography for many years and conducted workshops all over the USA as well as internationally. I also taught lettering sessions at Facebook's Analog Research Lab, at the company’s headquarters in Menlo Park, and workshops for Adobe  in San Francisco. It was particularly fun to be a featured instructor at the annual Adobe Max Annual Creativity Conference where I taught calligraphy basics to over 180 students – at a digital conference!

teachers.aboutMe:
Hello, my name is Carlo Stanga. I am an illustrator, an architect and a books author.

My story is my Daimon’s story.
As the ancient Greeks used to believe, everyone of us has a Daimon. The Daimon is our real essence, what makes us unique individuals, the real reason why we are on this Earth, our creative talent, in one world, our destiny. 
Not attending to your Daimon, your deepest passion, means to damage your own life. On the contrary, supporting your Daimon makes you closer to happiness, that, not without reason, in ancient greek is called Eudaimonia.
Actually a happy life means attending a work you would have done in any case, just because you like it, even without being paid!

In my story the Daimon showed up very early, when I was 2.
He was a doodler Daimon, making me sketching flying withces and elicopters on every available surface like sheets of paper, tables, walls, the kitchen’s furniture…
At that age I did not speak yet, I was only drawing, so my parents led me to the doctor . “ No worries”, he said, “ he just communicates through drawing, he will begin to speak soon”.In fact a few months later I began to speak, but I never stopped drawing.

At the elementary school, attended between the age of 6 and 10, I was so lucky to have a teacher who understood me and my Daimon, letting him express himself. She was often asking me to create big drawings about the main subjects of the school lessons. So I was usually face-down on a large sheet of paper, as big as a carpet, sketching whimsical scenes about the ancient Romans, rain forest, the french revolution, the solar system and so on. I was drawing with a black felt tip pen and my schoolmates were instructed to color my creations. So most of the time I was sorrownded by my friends, very committed in fill my b&w drawing with beautiful colors, all lying on their stomach, just like me. 
My Daimon had a lot of fun! Soncino, my small medieval town, in northern Italy, collects all the main carachteristics of a city, just as a child could imagine. The citadel, slightly raised on the plain with the Alps in distance, is embraced by large red brick walls that at one point, like an origami, bend in a thousand sides and creates a crenellated fortress, furrowed by drawbridges. 
Medieval, Renaissance and Baroque architecture is not lacking and there is even a fourteenth-century heptagonal tower, unique in Europe, leaning like the tower of Pisa.
Thus, influenced by my small but multifaceted village, palaces, towers and windows began to appear in my childhood drawings as far as the eye could see. However, it was my first trip to a big city that blew my interest in architecture and the urban landscape. I was 8 years old and, with my uncles Anna and Peppo, I visited Rome. I was spellbound. I was struck by everything, both in beauty and in size. I was experiecing everything as a magical adventure. The immense spaces, the noisy streetlife, the sunlight reading the surfaces of ancient walls, things that I had just studied at school and found there, like different walls textures: opus incertum, opus reticulatum, opus mixtum, walls and arches built with immense blocks of stone, fragments of colossal statues, luxuriant fountains. The thing that struck me most in this merry-go-round of emotions was the Pantheon. The emotional impact that the two-thousand-year-old concrete dome with the 9-meter-wide oculus from which rain and sun rays alternated made me decide to be an Architect.
So 10 years later, after the Liceo Classico,the high school, here I am at the Faculty of Architecture at Milan Polytechnic. It is here that the love for the theme grew stronger, while the drawing begins to fluctuate schizophrenically between cold technical design and soft freehand lines. Meanwhile, my Daimon makes me attend the school of comics in via Savona, where the teacher Coca Frigerio, pushing me to deepen the illustration, introduces me to the work of many great Italian illustrators and artists such as Adelchi Galloni and Emanuele Luzzati and above all to the great Bruno Munari in person.
Bruno Munari was a disruptive example, above all for his originality and the sense of freedom that his method and approach had. A perfect Daimon awakener.
In the meantime, it could not be placed in a specific area. A designer? Of course, but also a great illustrator, indeed a conceptual artist, a sculptor of useless machines, origami, dynamic works, a teacher who used an extraordinary method capable of developing creativity, this unknown then as today, a free spirit that preserved intact the creativity of the child, so much so that he was completely at ease with children not yet corrupted by bad teachers. Seeing Bruno Munari working in the creative workshops I collaborated with during my graduation was an experience that instilled in my mind a new way of seeing, more free and nonconformist.
At this point the Daimon was jumping with enthusiasm. It is not for a coincidence that Enthusismos in ancient Greek means: "Having a god inside".

So I started working in parallel as a freelance architect and as an illustrator. Both worked well. However, I was very disturbed and bored by the various bureaucratic aspects that the profession of architect required, moreover, after a few years, the Daimon of the drawing recalcitrated, asking me for more time and commitment in what was obviously my destiny. Just at that time, La Repubblica, the first Italian newspaper, called me for a long collaboration, while the MTA in New York asked me for a large illustration dedicated to the American city subway and at that point I decided to dedicate myself completely to illustration. I therefore quit the profession of architect, but architecture continues to be the protagonist in my designs.
By now my Daimon could express himself freely and my sense of eudaimonia, of satisfaction and completeness, confirmed to me the right choice.
Since then the years dedicated to drawing began, experimenting with methods, colors, techniques up to shaping a very recognizable style that continues to make my Daimon win many international awards such as the Treccani Web Prize in 2016, the American Illustration Award, the Gold Medal from the American magazine Creative Quarterly as well as various Communication Arts "Awards of Excellence".
This is how it happens when you indulge your Daimon and push him to express himself freely. Something magically positive starts, everyone begins to function well and things happen.
One of these things happened on the day when the director of Moleskine Publishing Roberto di Puma called me asking me to propose them my personal project, "whatever you want"he said. My Daimon immediately suggested his dream to me: a series of illustrated books on the most important cities in the world. Today the series collects 3 titles, I am Milan, I am London and I am New York. We are thinking about the next city to give voice to.
So the I am the City series is the activity at the center of my work as an illustrator. Many other initiatives flourish around my books such as lectures and workshops, like  those recently held in New York and exhibitions such as the one at the Africa Center in Manhattan, organized by the Moleskine Foundation, or the personal exhibition at the Bonvini Gallery in Milan inaugurated in 2018.
Meanwhile, the projects continue for many other realities such as the new Futurium Museum in Berlin, the Piccolo Teatro in Milan, the large installation to be created at Malpensa airport on the initiative of MEET-Fondazione Cariplo and other books on architecture and music for the Berlin publisher Raum Italic and Princeton Architectural Press in New York.
Long live the Daimon!

David Drazil is an architect who loves to sketch. Every day he shares his passion for the visual representation of architecture through drawings and tips on his website SketchLikeAnArchitect.com and on his popular Instagram account @david_drazil.

Through creating educational resources on architectural sketching, David is focused on helping other architects, designers, and hobby sketchers to use sketching as a tool to improve their design process and presentation.

A trained architect with international experience, David holds a BSc in Architecture and Building Engineering from Czech Technical University in Prague and an MSc in Architecture and Design from Aalborg University in Aalborg, Denmark. He also collaborates as a featured artist with the iPad sketching apps Morpholio and ShadowDraw. He lives in Prague, Czech Republic.

Pavel brings over 20 years of architectural and concept design experience in various roles as Senior Architect, Creative Director and Founder of Architect and Design firms.  

He is an excellent design communicator and visual storyteller. With his unique ability to conceptualize and design complex systems, Pavel has become increasingly fascinated by working at the intersection of architecture, user interface and immersive experience design. Recently, he has been working as a Consultant in the video game & entertainment industry.

George and Ewald are the co-founders of Bradley Van Der Straeten, a multi-award winning architecture studio, based in London. 

The practice specialises in residential architecture and interior design, with numerous national and international awards & publications under their belt. Aside from the individual approach to creating new homes and home renovations, the team is also nationally and internationally recognised for it’s creation of the world’s largest purpose-designed music therapy centre Nordoff Robbins and it’s community contribution.

They are also the founders of The Two architects, their online platform launched in 2020 and provides pay per meet architect service.

In the early 00’s, George & Ewald became friends at the University of Liverpool, UK. They taught on the Interior Architecture course at the University of Westminster, London and co-presented on UK national television for the show 'Love Your Home and Garden'.

Prior to founding the company George worked for a number of award-winning architects including Australian based Denton Corker Marshall. Ewald worked for Arcasa Arkitekter in Oslo, Dial Architects in Ghent, Belgium and Interiørverkstedet AS, a high end bespoke carpentry firm in Oslo.

My name is Ehab and I am an architect/designer/digital artist, based in Washington D.C, USA . Graduated in 2007 with a Bachelor degree in Architecture,I started my career as a design architect in Dubai, UAE.
While in Dubai I had the chance to work on a lot of high-end projects from residential and hotels to commercial and high-rise buildings. After relocating to the US I started expanding my experience working on Educational and public safety buildings.
I always try to push the boundaries with my designs, and the passion toward the art of design and unique forms led me to create @archihab page on Instagram where I share my digital hand sketches and designs with more than 117K followers. Also my design the "Futuristic Sustainable Mountain Pod" was featured in several architectural websites like "Architizer" and  "Amazing Architecture" and was talked about in several news outlets around the world.

JJ Zanetta’s passion of art and architecture attracted him to the profession of architectural illustration. A student of the craft, he is continually inspired by the master’s of architectural illustration as well as the new possibilities that technology brings.  Along with his dedication to his craft, he has an understanding and practical knowledge of architectural and urban design principles evident in the foundation of his renderings.

Beyond the technical aspects of a drawing, it is JJ’s goal to help his clients reach their audience on an emotional level.  The composition of the renderings are focused on breathing life into the design.  He aims to collaborate with the design team to gain an understanding of the vision and character of the place, and also help imagine what kind of life that environment will foster within it.  Whether, remotely or on charrette, his ability to quickly conceptualize and visually communicate plays an integral role on the design team.

He has had the good fortune to work with excellent clients on projects that present unique challenges and opportunities.   His project experience is wide-ranging; of all scales, character and project types.  For over 10 years he has served his clients, which consist of architects, urban designers, landscape architects, developers, and municipalities, with reliability and professionalism.

If you are interested in working together, I would love to hear from you!

teachers.aboutMe:
Soy Enrique Silguero, nací en Salamanca en 1976. Como no sabía qué quería ser de mayor, estudié periodismo. Por suerte un día agarré una cámara en las prácticas de televisión, y en seguida tuve claro que eso es a lo que me quería dedicar, así que me vine a Madrid y me puse a estudiar Dirección de Fotografía Cinematográfica en el TAI.

Al acabar los estudios de iluminación tuve la suerte de caer en el equipo de cámara de Unax Mendia y trabajar como video assist y posteriormente auxiliar de cámara de varias de sus películas, como "La luna en botella" de Eduardo Grojo; "Adivina quién soy" de Enrique Urbizu; "Isi Disi" de Chema de la Peña; "Mortadelo y Filemón 2" de Miguel Bardem; "Bosque de sombras" de Koldo Serra; o "No habrá paz para los malvados" de Enrique Urbizu. 

Hace ya unos cuantos años que trabajo como director de fotografía. He tenido la suerte de iluminar 5 películas, entre las que cabe señalar "Bornova Bornova" de Inan Temelkuran, "Todo el mundo lo sabe", de Miguel Laraya. Además he hecho la segunda unidad de "Gernika", de Koldo Serra y de "Qué baje Dios y lo vea", de Curro Velázquez. 

También he trabajado en televisión, donde he iluminado “Capítulo 0" de Ernesto Sevilla y Joaquín Reyes, las segundas unidades de la tercera temporada de "El Ministerio del Tiempo". Además, durante cuatro años, iluminé las ficciones de "Cuarto Milenio". 

Y como no, ¡también he hecho proyectos para internet!. La serie "ReStart Up" de Carlos Ruano (YouTube),  la serie documental "Camino al Mundial" de Eulogio Romero (HBO), y más recientemente  "Cam On" (Playz), donde también soy el realizador, son los proyectos más interesantes en los que he trabajado. 

Aunque lo que más me gusta es la ficción, también he hecho anuncios para clientes como Sony, Iberdrola, Coca Cola, Movistar, Fox, Ikea, El Corte Inglés, Adidas, Sony o Puig. Y videoclips de Miguel Bosé, Malú, La oreja de Van Gogh, El Pesacao o Casey Spooner, entre otros. 

¡Ah! y cortometrajes, muchos, muchísimos cortometrajes. Todos los que he podido hacer cuando el resto de proyectos me lo han permitido.

Aparte, como operador de cámara he trabajado en series como "Gigantes", "Velvet", "El Ministerio del Tiempo",  "Olmos y Robles" o "Mónica Chef", entre otras.

Además, ser periodista me ha valido para trabajar durante varios años en la revista especializada "Cameraman" y a crear mi propio blog: The HUB, donde escribo (siempre que el trabajo me lo permite) sobre los proyectos audiovisuales que me gustan.

Y también he trabajado como profesor en la Escuela de Cine y Televisión de San Antonio de los baños (EICTV), en Cuba, donde he impartido un taller de continuidad de luz.

Mi nombre es Yeray Martin Perdomo, Me licencie en Comunicación audiovisual y en Periodismo para más tarde cursar un Master en Comunicación Social. Actualmente soy Director de fotografía y dirijo mis propios documentales. Llevo unos 12 años trabajando en el mundo audiovisual, empecé en Televisión y en los últimos 6 años me he dedicado también a los drones. 

Actualmente soy Director de Fotografía y tengo mi propia Productora / Empresa Operadora de Drones. Me gusta mucho lo que hago y a lo que me he dedicado. Viajar y contar historias es mi pasión y he conseguido convertirlo en mi profesión. Las nuevas tecnologías están cambiando la forma de contar las historias, ahora nuestra creatividad, tiene menos límites.
​
Por eso veo los drones, no únicamente como una herramienta de planos aéreos, sino como una posible grúa o travelling, que nos permite con una única tecnología conseguir diferentes resultados.

Del 2013 al 2016 estuve trabajando en una serie documental llamada “Pacífico” como Socio, Dop, Operador de cámara y drone. Fue una serie documental que grabamos en 380 días de viaje consecutivos durante el año, viajando desde Japón a Nueva Zelanda, filmando en unos 20  países por donde pasaba la expedición. A partir de entonces no he parado de viajar y de utilizar los drones en mis filmaciones, hoy en día he filmado  en unos 50 países.

He trabajado para plataformas como Netflix, Amazon, National Geographic, TVE, Canal ARTE, Televisa etc. En publicidad he trabajado para Repsol, Real Madrid, Aciona, Alcampo, Grupo Heineken y muchas más. He grabado varios videoclips y un documental que está nominado a varias candidaturas para los Goya 2020 y espero seguir viajando y coleccionando historias en mis tarjetas de memoria por el mundo.


Para saber más de mí y mi trabajo, puedes encontrarme en Instagram como @volandovoy.tv o pasearte por mis páginas webs:

De pequeño quería ser pintor. Luego diseñador gráfico. Nunca quise ser director, pero recuerdo de forma muy viva cuando de niño mi padre me llevaba a sesiones de cine al aire libre. Ahora hago películas, dirijo videos musicales, publicidad y escribo. Me apasiona contar historias emocionantes con un buen armazón conceptual y con margen para la experimentación visual. En este momento me encuentro terminando mi ultimo cortometraje, rodado en Los Angeles, y escribiendo el guión de un largometraje y una serie. 

Mis últimos trabajos personales Tramuntana y Santa Ana, donde exploro la intersección entre el documental y la experimentación visual, fueron seleccionados en festivales como Cíclope, SXSW, Sitges, Cannes, Slamdance o BFI London Film Festival entre otros. Mi trabajo ha sido galardonado con varios premios LAUS, un oro en ADC*E y un segundo premio en YDA Cannes. En 2018 Santa Ana ganó una mención de honor al mejor documental en el festival Salute Your Shorts (Los Angeles).

Soy Cineasta y fotógrafo. El 2009 realizo mi proyecto de tesis “Paseo” (mejor film en SANFIC). En 2010 me inicio en la vida profesional en el cine de ficción y documental dirigiendo el documental musical “Electrodomésticos: El Frío Misterio” (mejor film Inedit); Luego, en el 2015  dirijo mi largometraje de ficción “La Mujer de Barro”, estrenando en en el Festival de Cine de San Sebastián y en el Festival de Cine de Berlín (Berlinale 65º) permitiendo abrirme más al panorama internacional. Soy creador y uno de los directores de la serie para Amazon Prime de la primera y segunda temporada de “La Jauría” junto a Lucía Puenzo como showrunner y Nicolás Puenzo y Marialy Rivas como co-directores y producida por Fábula ("Tony Manero", "No", "Spencer", "Una mujer fantástica"). 
En 2020 estreno mi documental “El Negro” coproducción entre Chile  y Francia en asociación con France Televisions sobre la vida del ex guerrillero chileno Ricardo Palma Salamanca.
Actualmente en el año 2022 co-dirijo junto a mi dupla Pepa San Martín la primera serie chilena para Disney + producida por Fábula titulada "Llévame al cielo"  También desarrollo mis películas de ficción: “El Gol Más Triste” , una película que narra las vivencias de la selección chilena de fútbol del año 1973 en Chile y desarrollo y dirijo mi primera película fuera del territorio nacional llamada “Il Cileno”; una película italiana en coproducción con Chile que se rodará casi íntegramente en la Región de Turín, Italia.
Soy también desde el año 2020 miembro de la Academia de Cine de Chile encargada de elegir las películas representantes para los premios Oscar, Goya y Ariel.
Paralelo a esto mi obra fotográfica se ha expuesto en diversos Centros Culturales y Galerías de Chile.
Soy profesor de Cine  desde el año 2013 en diversas universidades en los ramos de Realización, Título, Montaje y Guión. Actualmente me desempeño como profesor de Taller de realización en el tercer y cuarto año de la carrera de Cine de la Universidad del Desarrollo (UDD)

Nací en Comodoro Rivadavia, una ciudad industrial en la Patagonia Argentina. A los 18 años me mudé a Buenos Aires donde emprendí mi camino autodidacta hacia la realización audiovisual. 
Lo que comenzó como una búsqueda personal, al poco tiempo se volvió profesional. Landia me eligió junto a nuevos talentos para co-dirigir un comercial de Coca-Cola. Desde entonces y con muy pocos años en la industria, trabajé de manera independiente con Smirnoff, Amex, Trivago, Adidas, Nike entre otras marcas de alcance nacional, especializándome en la creación de contenidos comerciales, sin dejar de lado proyectos personales que fomentan en mi, el explorar mi visión de manera creativa y experimental. 
Hoy me encuentro representada por Poster con quien estoy empezando un nuevo camino hacia proyectos más grandes trabajando con marcas de carácter internacional como las bebidas Amstel y Rockstar, y junto a quien realicé una campaña para la ONG MACMA. 

Continúo trabajando de manera independiente en proyectos que me atraen y me llenan estéticamente. Mis próximos planes son incursionar en el mundo de la ficción, donde pueda mostrar limpia y puramente, mi manera de ver las cosas.

teachers.aboutMe:
Me llamo Leire Villar y me dedico profesionalmente al ganchillo, generando contenido desde mi marca personal, Ameskeria, para diferentes clientes del mundo craft y editorial.

Ameskeria es una palabra vasca que significa fantasía, imaginación. Desde esta premisa he ido construyendo mi universo a lo largo de los últimos años, con la intención de aportar inocencia, frescura y originalidad al tradicional mundo del crochet.

Adoro los diseños sencillos y fáciles de tejer. 
Me fascina el color, el amigurumi y el diseño de estampados.

Hola! Soy Nati Dorado, diseñadora en crochet y creadora del concepto y técnica Amigurumis 2D que podrás conocer a través de mi marca, Virreinata.

Aprendí a tejer hace 7 años de manera autodidacta –como aprendí tantas otras cosas en mi vida- pues soy muy curiosa y apasionada, no sólo por el saber sino también por el ser y su desarrollo. Si algo no se me enseña o no lo entiendo, yo salgo al mundo a aprender y buscar respuestas.

A través de los años me formé y desempeñé en diversas disciplinas. Todas ellas devinieron en caminos que enriquecieron mi desarrollo como ser humano y artista. Si tengo que destacar algo de todo el aporte que aquello significó para mi arte, sería las matemáticas (¡pasión por ellas!) y el Canto (¡obvio!...  ¿qué te puedo decir? Vivo cantando porque el canto expresa una parte de mi ser y agradezco haberme formado en ello. Mi género favorito es el Jazz, de la mano de mi amada Billie Holiday y Ella Fiztgerald).

Virreinata nace de una pasión por la vida que es Nata en mí. Siento que la vida es un regalo valioso donde encuentro aventuras y sentimientos, formas y colores inquietos que -si decides observar un momento- notarás que adquieren vida propia. En mi caso, han tomado vida en el Amigurumi 2D.

Ahora que sabes un poco más de mi ¿te animas a seguirme en esta #VirreAventura?

Mi nombre es Lhyla Tirado Tacilla, tengo 26 años y soy quien está detrás de Laraña. Soy contadora de profesión, pero actualmente le dedico todo mi tiempo al tejido, diseño y creación de amigurumis. Laraña nació en un momento difícil de mi vida y me ayudó mucho a poder seguir adelante, tejer sana.
Tejo desde muy pequeña, comencé con algunas prendas, pero desde que descubrí el mundo del amigurumi supe que era lo que quería hacer siempre.
Hoy en día me dedico a diseñar personajes en amigurumi, demostrando así, que cada quien puede interpretar un personaje con su estilo propio a través del tejido.

Mi nombre es Marcelo Javier y soy diseñador de piezas en crochet, principalmente amigurumi. De profesión soy profesor de filosofía y lengua castellana, pero actualmente estoy volcado en tiempo completo a tejer, diseñar, escribir y administrar mis redes sociales. 
Comencé tejiendo en dos agujas, pero como la escritura siempre ha sido una de mis pasiones encontré en el amigurumi una posibilidad de llevar a la realidad a los personajes de mis cuentos y poemas. Es por ello que actualmente mi principal foco es el diseño de personajes con esta técnica y el constante descubrimiento de formas de personalización y procedimientos para darle a mis creaciones un aspecto original y distintivo.

Si tejer es mejor cuando es de a dos, lo qué pasa en Tutitas es magia…
Hola! somos Daniela y Pilar, dedicamos nuestra vida a crear y enseñar amigurumis.
Somos soñadoras, creativas y determinadas en seguir nuestros sueños, la felicidad es un estado que encontramos al permitirnos poder hacer día a día lo que nos apasiona…
Antes de Tutitas nos dedicábamos a cosas muy distintas, Pili de profesión Bióloga y Dani en el área de derecho, sin darnos cuenta y escuchando nuestro corazón quisimos hacer de este arte un estilo de vida, nuestro hogar se llenó de lanas, crochet y amigurumis por todos lados, en casa se vive el tejido!
Nos encanta aplicar en nuestras muñecas toda la técnica que hemos adquirido, plasmando  ternura y los años de aprendizajes para que cada diseño sea muy entretenido de tejer!
En ellas encontrarás tonos pasteles, detalles florales, puntos de fantasía y accesorios muy románticos.
Te invitamos a entrar en nuestro tuti mundo!!!

teacher.aboutMe:
I’m Chelsea, an artist and art historian who transforms paintings into wearable miniature masterpieces. Through my brand, Venus de Chela, I specialize in crafting intricate polymer clay earrings inspired by the works of great masters like Van Gogh, Monet, and Picasso. With my background in art history, I reinterpret iconic artworks into unique, hand-sculpted jewelry, blending traditional artistic techniques with modern craftsmanship.

In my Domestika course, Miniature Masterpieces: Crafting Art History Earrings with Polymer Clay, I guide students through the process of turning famous paintings into miniature, wearable works of art. From selecting colors and textures to sculpting fine details, I share my expertise in creating pieces that honor the beauty and legacy of historical masterpieces. This course is perfect for art lovers and creatives eager to explore the intersection of fine art and jewelry-making, learning to craft their own tiny tributes to the world’s most celebrated artists.

Soy colombiana residente en Argentina, graduada en Diseño Gráfico de la escuela de Bellas Artes de Cali. Trabajé durante 10 años como directora de arte para publicidad en agencias como Young & Rubicam, McCann Erickson, en el 2006 viajé a Buenos Aires (Argentina) a estudiar animación, ahí continué trabajando en dirección de arte hasta que en el año 2010 me dediqué totalmente a la ilustración y empecé a trabajar de manera freelance para Argentina, Brasil, Colombia, España y Estados Unidos.

Desde ese mismo año y hasta la actualidad, desarrollo mi parte artística personal en la que enfoco la creación de personajes provenientes de mundos fantásticos que van y vienen entre su realidad y la mía, en formatos tanto digitales como analógicos que van de la pintura, la escultura, la cerámica y el muralismo. También he participado en muestras colectivas e individuales en galerías y eventos de arte en Argentina y Colombia.

Melissa Galbraith is the fiber artist behind MCreativeJ. She was born and raised in the desert of Washington state, where her mother instilled a love of making things by hand at an early age. Drawing on her love of nature, Melissa creates whimsical and modern embroidery patterns and kits. She loves sharing how anyone can embroider with her embroidery kits, patterns, and virtual workshops.

​Melissa was reintroduced to hand embroidery after finding her desk job monotonous and needing a creative outlet. She loves that embroidery allows her to play with texture and color and is also a portable craft. Along the way, many crafty minded makers also wanted to learn how to embroider too but were daunted by where to start. So Melissa began to share her embroidery knowledge.

Melissa's embroidery kits and patterns make it easy to learn a new craft for makers of all skill levels. She loves seeing makers fall in love with the needle arts and seeing that magical ah-ha moment of learning something new.

teachers.aboutMe:
Hello, I’m Luke and I am very, very passionate about drawing, so much so I decided to base my whole life around it. I have learnt a great deal over the years and hope that through Domestika, I can share this knowledge and my passion for the simplest of all the arts, drawing.

I began my career as a designer before becoming a full-time artist back in 2015. Since then I have specialised in drawing on location, exploring and sharing my fascination with the world around me and how drawing can help us connect with both places and people.

Most recently I have created the Sunday Times Best Seller ‘Together’ my first graphic novel. Together takes a philosophical look at the events of 2020. Using the metaphor of a monumental storm, we follow a man and his dog through the uncertainty and change that it brings to their lives. 

After graduating from University I began my design career in London, the transition from designer to full time artist was gradual but inevitable. Since first sharing my work online I have grown a loyal social media audience of over 300,000 people. 

I look forward to continuing this journey into drawing and hope to inspire others to take their own....

My name is Philip Harris and I am freelance Illustrator, chihuahua owner and vintage blues fan currently based in Exeter, UK.

I became inspired by illustration as a child studying my grandfather’s old sketchbooks around the family home. During university I inherited my granddad’s collection of dip pens and began experimenting with pen and ink, Becoming fascinated by crosshatching, pointillism and line-work.

I still use the same pen nibs today as well as diversifying to use other mediums such as Rotring pens, fine liners, Posca pens, Procreate, Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop.

I love to draw my inspiration from wildlife, the natural world and the folktales that are tied up with the landscapes around us.

I am originally from Ukraine and currently live in Israel. I work in the areas of book illustration and narrative art for for magazines and brands, deeply influenced by myth and fairytales.  

I am self-trained and started out professionally by writing and illustrating my own book, “The Land of Stone Flowers”. Originally published in Russia in 2015, it was nominated for the national bestseller award and later translated into ten languages. 

I do hand drawn art on paper, merging a lot of mythical and traditional motifs from various cultures with contemporary ideas. My favorite medium is pen and ink. 

I have worked with numerous publishing houses to create art for books, including Harper Collins, Penguin Books, Macmillan, Disney-Hyperion, Usborne and Chronicle. I made art for movies, including The True Adventures of Wolfboy, created fancy commercial art for such advertising agencies as JWT New York or D8 studio (Glasgow), and did editorial jobs for magazines like New Yorker and LA times.

Dan is an architect, illustrator, and educator, passionate about the visual exploration of architectural concepts, urban scenes, and historical spaces. His drawings enjoy applicability across a wide range of projects, from architectural high-rise design concepts and hospitality resorts to interior commercials and Hollywood movie sets. Dan's work has been exhibited with the SFMOMA, the AIA, and numerous private galleries.

Dan is a Registered Architect (WA #10221), holds NCARB certification, and is a LEED Accredited Professional. An active member of the American Institute of Architects, Dan serves on the Board of Directors at the California Chapter. Apart from his design practice, he serves as faculty with the Academy of Art San Francisco, teaching drawing studios and drawing classes. Dan holds a Master of Architecture degree from the AAU, San Francisco, and a Master of Arts from Harvard University.

Eva is an artist who depicts drawings that blend realism with fantasy, through movement and detail. She works in multiple media forms like ink on paper, digital mediums, gouache, graphite, and animation. Through her drawings, Eva strives to convey the emotion and narrative around various topics like empowerment, mental illness, superstition, and futurism. Her work is often characterized as detailed, surreal, psychedelic, and colorful. She uses ink and graphite for traditional works, occasionally using watercolor or gouache. Often, she will color her work digitally using Procreate and/or Photoshop. 

Art was a part of her life from a young age, as her mother had a passion for painting and drawing. She studied music in her undergraduate university at Berklee College of Music, and went on to pursue illustration shortly after. Music has a great influence on what she makes - it is a spiritual process for her. 

Born and raised in Connecticut, she now lives and works as both an artist and musician in Brooklyn, NY, USA.

Hi I'm Fuji
I've been working as an artist since 2018 and in 2019 I had the fortune of winning Sky Arts Landscape artist of the Year. Over this time I've been exhibiting in London at art fairs and group shows and am now with a lovely gallery in Mayfair. 
Throughout my career I've always been experimenting with what I can do and trying to fully explore the possibilities of ink and composition. Finding a balance of art and design in my work has always been crucial for me and I wanted to share a slice of that process.

teachers.aboutMe:
I am a self-taught gouache artist, inspired by nature and always looking for that little spark of magic to add to my paintings. I paint mostly landscapes, often with a little sprinkle of fantasy to satisfy my deep love of fairy tales and adventure stories.

My creative journey started with explorations in other mediums, including charcoal, oils and watercolor before discovering and falling in love with gouache. Gouache provides the perfect combination of bold, opaque color with the flexibility of a water-soluble medium; perfect for the modern artist!

When I'm not painting with gouache, I'm busy encouraging others to give it a go. I love to share my work and process videos on social media and support other artists wanting to try out this quirky medium.

Don Kilpatrick III moved to Detroit in 2007 to begin his career at the College for Creative Studies as a faculty member in the Illustration Department of which he has been the department chair since 2010.   

Kilpatrick's work has been featured in publications such as Fortune, the L.A. Times, Nautilus magazine, and the Wall Street Journal. His illustration can be found on the Olympic medal for the XIX Winter Games in Salt Lake City. Most recently his work can be found in the form of a series of large-scale murals on the newly built Little Caesar’s Arena in Detroit.

Additionally, he has exhibited his artwork in Detroit, New York, Los Angeles, Philadelphia, Tokyo, and Miami. He has regularly shown his work in both group and solo gallery shows, and most recently in January 2019 at M Contemporary gallery in Ferndale, Michigan. This recent show included prints, woodcuts, paintings, and a collaboration with renowned bespoke shoemaker and artist Noriyuki Misawa.

Hi! My name is Cécile Berrubé and I’m a french illustrator/painter based in Scotland. When I’m not in my little studio I like going for walks in the woods or the hills and take pictures of birds and plants. I’m deeply inspired by Nature and cosy moments of simple life. I mostly work with gouache but I also enjoy experimenting with pencils and watercolour. I always carry a little sketchbook with me!
My main source of inspiration are animals, I love making character study pages and drawing them with different postures and expressions.

Hi! I’m Mike Thomas, an Artist, Designer and Illustrator living & working in London and the South East of the UK. Currently working as a freelance artist and art tutor, I paint, draw and doodle everywhere I go. So if you'd like to join me for an adventure, grab your sketchbook and favourite brushes! Let's go get lost!! ᕕ( ᐛ )ᕗ

Aloha, my name is Tommy Kim. I am art director in animation industry and plein-air painter living in Hawaii. My passion is to capture everyday life into work of art that we can cherish. I find my peace whenever I am outside studying nature with my gouache paints and I hope you can join my journey as well and find happiness in life. 

In this domestika course, I talk about my journey as an artist and go through step by step process of my gouache paintings. I hope you guys enjoy it!

Hello! My name is Maddy and I am an independent artist based in the Netherlands.

My work explores the beauty of the natural world through light, color and texture. You can often find me in the forest sketching or taking photos and finding inspiration for my next paintings. 

I mainly work in gouache and digital mediums, though I also enjoy watercolor and Ink. As both a traditional and digital painter, I have been exploring ways to bring these mediums together through the creation of custom digital brush sets which use real traditional brushstrokes and textures .

I am passionate about sharing knowledge and have been livestreaming my art process as a partnered Twitch streamer and featured Behance streamer for the past 5 years. 

I’ve also done asset and background painting for Ddraig House Game studio and worked with companies such as Wacom, Adobe Behance, Artstation, and Amazon Games.

I am a self taught artist, specializing in acrylics and gouache. I began expressing myself through art ever since I could pick up a crayon, and have not stopped since! 
I love showing the beauty and gorgeous colors of everyday items that we’re surrounded by…  flowers, fruit, animals and knickknacks.  I love to paint subjects that make the viewer smile, perhaps capturing a pleasant memory from the past, that brings happiness when viewed. I have painted for clients worldwide! My most recent clients include Trader Joes, Serena & Lily, and a collaboration with Winsor Newton and Michaels Craft Stores.

Hola, Soy Juanita Londoño Ilustradora editorial y de cuentos infantiles.

Soy de Medellín, Colombia pero mi pasión por viajar me ha llevado a muchos lugares en el mundo, entre esos, Vancouver donde adquirí mi diploma en Animation Concept Art.

Mi trabajo se caracteriza por retratar personajes y escenarios en colores vibrantes, detalles texturizados y llenos de emociones buscando transportar a las personas a universos llenos de magia. Mi búsqueda es vivir a través del realismo mágico que está tan profundamente conectado con mis raíces latinoamericanas.

He trabajado con clientes como Simon & Schuster, Target, Quarto y Harper Collins.

Hola! Me Llamo Jimena Sánchez Sarquiz y soy ilustradora. De niña, pasaba mucho tiempo en la biblioteca de mi escuela viendo los libros ilustrados y enamorándome de las coloridas imágenes. Siempre me ha gustado el dibujo y la pintura, a los 11 años acompañaba a mi abuela a sus clases de pintura al óleo y hacía is propios cuadros.

Estudié Comunicación Visual en la UNAM y desde entonces con la intención de dedicarme a la ilustración.  Tomé la especialidad de ilustración dentro de mi escuela y después de graduarme seguí complementando mi educación con diferentes cursos y diplomados. 

He trabajado como ilustradora desde hace mas de 10 años, principalmente en el campo de la ilustración infantil y juvenil. Algunos de mis clientes incluyen Editorial Norma, Edebé, Edelvives, Editorial Santillana, Macmillan Education, Cambridge University Press, Capplen Damm y Editorial Televisa.

After graduating with a BFA from the University of Tennessee at Martin and working for a few years as a graphic designer; I decided to shift into the world of my first love—illustration! I work both digitally and traditionally, depending on the project, and I am most comfortable when settling into the beginning “research” phase of projects. The traditional media I use most often are: watercolor, gouache, and colored pencils (I am on a constant search for the perfect, scratchy pencil texture) I am naturally very curious and ask a lot of questions—this quality is a constant fuel for inspiration.

I live in Nashville, TN in a small house with my husband and 2 cats. Most of the time I am working upstairs in my studio, but a few days a week I join a group of friends and fellow illustrators at a co-working space.

My hobbies include playing board games, participating in (almost) any event, learning languages, and planning trips (I loves public transit). Some of my favorite topics are birds, traveling, science, animal fun facts, and history.

Clients include Highlights Magazine, Sleeping Bear Press and Chronicle.

Hi! I’m a children’s book author and illustrator who loves to illustrate fun, ridiculous and spunky characters in meaningful stories. My illustration debut book, Ambitious Girl, released at #1 on the NY Times bestsellers list and at #1 on the Indiebound list and is available in all major retailers, such as Barnes and Noble and Target. I’ve worked with three out of the big five publishers, Hachette, Penguin Random House and Macmillan, and I also do freelance illustration with smaller clients such as libraries and children’s hospitals across the US. I have a background in animation and graphic design and love to bring the skills I learned from my past lives into the illustrations I create today. I’m represented by Kelly Sonnack at the Andrea Brown Literary Agency. 

I’m currently illustrating a young chapter book series, ESME’S BIRTHDAY CONGA LINE (Tundra, 2022) about a plucky girl who is sure she can plan her own birthday party when her Mimi and Pipo forget. 
A couple of fun facts about me: 
- I’m an avid gnome collector! I have 17 garden gnomes at the moment but I’m always on the prowl for more.
- I used to be a preschool teacher! It’s a career that I miss every day and would love to go back to teaching later in my life.
- I had a childhood pet sheep named Sheep. 

Check out my work at:
@marissaarts on Instagram
@marissaillo on Twitter

Hi, my name is Ema Malyauka and I’m a children book illustrator born in Belarus, currently living in cozy town Alkmaar, the Netherlands.  I have a large collection of sketchbooks that is constantly growing. I love experimenting, finding new materials and creating textures. I have drawn for various publishing houses and companies.
 I am a self-taught illustrator who is in love with art! I am excited to be part of Domestika community and I can't wait to share my courses with you!

I'm Lucy Fleming, an illustrator and author living in the north of England. 

As a Children's Picture book illustrator I've had the opportunity to work with some incredible brands and publishers from all around the world. My art style is whimsical and charming with a pinch of playfulness.

My first author/illustrator picture book 'Ella's Night Lights' was published by Walker Books in 2020 and has been published in several languages world-wide. It seems like a dream that I am now making magical books, like those I cherished as a child.

Digital Marketing Manager at Coppel. Former Digital Integration Vicepresident and Regional Leader of Social Media Directors at McCann Worldgroup. I started my career in production, worked as a creative, and as a planner and I have more than 60 awards on festivals like EFFIES, IAB, Circulo de Oro, and El Ojo de Iberoamérica.
