You can find me on Instagram as @AnaMarin and on Twitter and TikTok as Mujerdepocafe.
Spanish spoken.

Hi, I'm Hana, a social media marketing consultant working with small to medium-sized companies and female founders. Some clients I worked with include Amazon, glh Hotels, Olixa, and Children's Salon, to name a few.

My journey in social media marketing started in 2007 – blogging for an Apple magazine and later founding a fashion magazine, for which I wrote over 1,500 blog posts. Then, through a series of workshops on blogging for the general public that I ran in Prague, I got connected to working with people and training them on social media.

After I moved to London in 2014, I became a lecturer at the University of the Arts of London, where I taught social media marketing, Instagram marketing, and blogging for seven years. During this time, I started my consultancy, filmed two marketing courses with an online learning platform Domestika, taught marketing at a recognised international university Istituto Marangoni, and trained teams, staff members and business owners of new and well-established brands from America to Tasmania.

My vision is that brands and companies succeed on social by gaining visibility and reach and training provides them with a complete skillset, effortless strategy and results, and a simple and enjoyable process.

I'm Tiago, a content creator and published author.
I write, illustrate, podcast, and make videos about creativity and content creation through an empathetic lens.

My project is called Tira do papel and I create across 6 different channels, where I speak with over 240k people.

I believe in the healthy balance of taking action (creating) and respecting our mental health ✏️

I build brands with people and for people. I am a seasoned marketing executive with 20+ years of experience in social media engagement, brand marketing and communications, community building strategy & digital content in top global companies like Instagram, the BBC and Booking.com.

I firmly believe that creativity drives growth and I am someone who celebrates and promotes differences integrating content across cultures, time zones, languages and geographies.

I know that if you put your mind to something, you will make it happen. The key is to take the first step and unleash your creativity.

Soy Alejandra Gonzalez y me dedico a la industria de los creadores de contenido digitales. Soy CEO de TNG Management, una agencia de representación de talento digital. TNG Management es parte del grupo DW Group, así que es agencia hermana de la tan posicionada DW Entertainment and Media.  Desde los inicios de mi carrera me he dedicado a la industria del entretenimiento y medios. Empecé mi carrera como editora de la sección de vida nocturna en Chilango, un título que en ese entonces era parte Grupo Editorial llamado Grupo Editorial Expansión. Después me lancé a desarrollar el área comercial y operativa de un start up llamado Kiwilimon logo y previo a independizarme, culminé mi carrera corporativa trabajando siete años en YouTube como líder de Socios Estratégicos en el Ecosistema de Creadores en Hispanoamérica.

He sido embajadora de diversidad, equidad e inclusión y he dado conferencias motivacionales a emprendedores y jóvenes. Soy fan de la estrategia creativa. Es decir, me encanta resolver problemas o construir un camino de formas creativas para poder lograr objetivos. Y esto lo aplico en mi día a día con mis clientes y socios comerciales. Me apasiona ver cómo la democratización de la información a través de las redes sociales ha logrado crear a increíbles contadores de historias. Creo que las marcas hoy tienen ese reto, saber como contar historias y creo que muchas lo están haciendo, porque eso es lo fascinante, saber cómo conectar con las audiencias a través del lenguaje correcto.

With over 12 years in industry, I know how to lead teams to collaborate effectively, helping brands to deliver campaigns across social that resonate. I have a wealth of experience building teams and nurturing talent, from 3D artists, Designers, Copywriters, Art Directors & Motion Designers, to create slick, well oiled campaigns. A conceptual creative, I love working on a new brief and working with clients. I'm a safe pair of hands, able to pick up and lead as well as ideate and deliver. 

At Cult, I've been pushing the boundaries of briefs, focusing on social first campaigns and launching a virtual world for a major global beauty brand. Prior to this, I spent 3 years at We Are Social with my finger on the pulse across TikTok, Instagram & Youtube. We launched Westfields TikTok and created excitement on Lidl's social accounts making their shoes sell like gold dust. All whilst managing and growing a large team of designers and creatives.

From TikTok to the Metaverse, I love looking at briefs with a fresh approach and leading creative teams to deliver campaigns that don’t just look good, but deliver on results. When I’m not collaborating or directing on set, you’ll often find me speaking at events, leading workshops, mentoring or judging awards.

I am a business coach currently residing in Ramsgate, right by the sea. I am the founder of flower studio The Flower Arranger, worldwide membership platform The Coven Girl Gang and independent bookshop Book Bodega. I have been self-employed and running businesses for nearly a decade and I'm here to help you run yours!

teachers.aboutMe: My professional experience in film production spans over 20 years in drama, documentaries, music videos, news, programming and branded content. 6 years ago my life, and that of my family was turned upside down due to the birth of my second daughter with severe cardiac and other medical conditions. She spent a long time fighting for her life and we were with her night and day in hospital for months. During this time I began to explore my iPhone video capabilities and began to wonder how good was it - could I shoot professional content with it. After time we left the hospital and my daughter survived but the experience left me questioning many things, including my career, and so I decided to commit fully to exploring the potential of mobile filmmaking and its future. The film industry and filmmaking colleagues thought I was crazy and there was no future in it. I spent many years gaining my experience and knowledge of how to shoot with a mobile and its been a difficult but very rewarding journey. In the last 3 years I have been a guest speaker and lecturer at some of the most important film schools and industry organisations teaching and demonstrating the possibilities of mobile filmmaking. I have travelled the world filming documentaries, music videos and drama using a mobile phone and have been incredibly fortunate winning over 12 international film awards. It's now my time to pass my knowledge and experience to others, to learn from my mistakes and adventures to engage, motivate and inspire the next generation of mobile filmmakers in a world that it is now recognised and respected and continues to grow and develop.
Hi, I create videos for the internet, oh I also love TikTok. :) And I'm from Iceland, not sure if I need to say that lol but I guess I just did.

I am Jose Prada, a Spanish filmmaker who has worked in the commercial and documentary field for brands such as Ford, L’Oréal, Red Bull, Zara, NHS, etc. When I moved to London, I co-founded JRVISUALS, a video production company based in London, with my friend and partner Rene Strgar. We are two award-winning filmmakers who merged their creative minds to produce video, photography, and social media content.
 
We love our job. We love making films. We are creative (and a bit crazy) minds, with years of experience in the filmmaking industry. We are also cool guys to work with (at least, people say that).

I'm an artist, and I enjoy sharing my creative process with people around me. I make videos of every step of my artistic life and I'm always happy to know when people find additional inspiration in my aesthetics! Don't forget to follow me on Instagram @fornstudio to find more inspiration!

Hi! We're Charlene Tassinari and Carly Potock, the co-founders of Canvas+Co. Our company builds video marketing strategies that put the brain science of human attention at the core of the approach, so that our client's creative can create pause, be unskippable, and stop-the-scroll.

We met in 2015 when we founded YouTube's first digital video brand strategy team for small-to-medium businesses. Our insights-driven methodology was delivered to 500+ brands globally through client workshops and industry events, including Google’s annual CMO Academy, hosted in partnership with Columbia Business School. 

After working closely with marketers around the world, we saw a common challenge emerge for brands large and small in achieving success on YouTube. They needed access to nimble, affordable and high-quality video creative in order to truly unlock the power of digital video. With this new problem to solve, we pivoted the team in 2018 to building first-of-kind video production solutions for Google’s customers. We developed creative tools like Video Builder in partnership with the YouTube Product team and formed industry relationships to launch Google's first video production partnership program called the YouTube Creative Directory.

In 2020,  we founded Canvas+Co to help more brands succeed in a video-first world. Our clients learn to master the art and science of building effective cross-platform video marketing strategies that earn consumer attention, translate seamlessly across formats, and drive performance.

Pete Majarich is a Designer and Filmmaker based in Sydney, Australia.

In his advertising career, he’s collaborated with brands like Apple, Netflix, Slack, Microsoft, Google, Nike, Uber, The NRL, Coca-Cola, McDonald’s, Harley Davidson, Domino’s, Toyota, and Volkswagen. He has personally been commissioned for work by Twentieth Century Fox, Warner Music Group, The Australian Open and U2.

His self-initiated work has been featured by Wired Magazine, Mashable, Shortlist, Adobe, Fast Company, VICE, The Academy of Motion Pictures®, Bored Panda, Lost at E Minor, My Modern Met, Design Taxi, Booooooooooooom, Comedy Central, We and the Color, DeMilked, Archillect and This Isn’t Happiness™. He’s also reached the front page of Reddit, Buzzfeed, and recieved a coveted Vimeo Staff Pick.

Majarich’s advertising work has been recognised by The One Show, Cannes Lions, Clios, and featured in-book at D&AD. He was selected as one of 34 from over 7,000 creatives worldwide for Weiden and Kennedy’s SEEKING program and is a former runner-up Sydney Morning Herald Designer of the Year.

Interests include Art Direction, Code, Motion Design, Typography, Minimalism, Branding, Sustainability, Start-ups, Strategy, Photography, Gradients, Cinematography, Drones, Sneakers, Space, Sci-fi, Gaming, Illustration, Basketball, VR, AR, AI, Advertising, AI-based Advertising, Digital Media, Directing, Film, 3D Printing, Remixes and animated GIFs.

I’m blue I’m pink es un estudio de dirección de arte, set design, fotografía y vídeo, creado por dos mentes curiosas, apasionadas por el arte y el diseño dispuestas a ayudar a las marcas a crear una identidad propia. Nuestro estudio está localizado en Sant Feliu de Guíxols, un pueblo costero en el Empordá tocado por la tramontana, como Dalí.
Definimos nuestro estilo como sofisticado, elegante y surrealista. Nos gusta jugar con diferentes tipos de materiales, texturas y colores. Nuestro proceso empieza desde la creación del concepto, la dirección de arte, el set design hasta la fotografía o vídeo final. Trabajamos la composición al milímetro buscando la perfección/imperfección.
Nos entusiasma trabajar con clientes que aman el diseño y quieren desarrollar su mensaje de una manera muy personal.
Como a Amelie, nos gustan los detalles que nadie más ve.

Hello, I´m Paloma Rincón! I´m a  Madrid based photographer working worldwide, from commercial assignments for big companies to more experimental and personal projects.

I create photographic images where different languages and techniques get mixed up. The result showcases interesting worlds where shapes, textures, materials, lights and typography blend together living in harmony inside fine, rich, and detailed graphic compositions. The virtual and the real worlds integrate in a totally natural fashion erasing the boundaries of tactile and digital.  My dynamic still life photographies combine an accurate use of technique and the creativity of a craftsman.

Products, props, and sometimes people are approached with a unique point of view. A very meticulous process where elements change meaning building completely new compositions. Playing with reality, the beauty of handcraft recovers its value and magic.
 
Clients: Ikea, Sonos, Samsung, Oreo, Playstation, Powerade, Kleenex, Vodafone, Toyota U.S.A., Schweppes, Swatch, Yoigo, Renfe, Ono, Estrella Damm, Voll Damm, Aquarius, Architectural Digest, Universal Music, DCODE Festival, Serial Cut, y agencias como Saatchi & Saatchi L.A., JWT NY, TBWA, 72 & Sunny L.A., Ogilvy Madrid, Leo Burnett Budapest, Herezie Paris, Publicis, 72 and Sunny L.A., Sra. Rushmore, China Madrid o S.C.P.F. among many others.
 _______________________________________________________________________________________________

¡Hola! Soy Paloma Rincón, soy fotógrafa y trabajo internacionalmente en un amplio espectro de proyectos: desde campañas comerciales para grandes marcas hasta imágenes más experimentales y trabajos personales. 

Mi trabajo se centra principalmente en el mundo del bodegón. Creo imágenes fotográficas donde se mezclan diferentes lenguajes y técnicas: fotografía, escultura y diseño se funden mediante un meticuloso proceso donde los elementos son compuestos fuera de su contexto habitual redefiniendo su significado. Con un estilo muy gráfico, trabajo la composición y el color de forma dinámica y alegre, combinando un preciso uso de la técnica y la creatividad de un artesano.

Algunos de mis clientes: Ikea, Sonos, Samsung, Oreo, Playstation, Powerade, Kleenex, Vodafone, Toyota U.S.A., Schweppes, Swatch, Yoigo, Renfe, Ono, Estrella Damm, Voll Damm, Aquarius, Architectural Digest, Universal Music, DCODE Festival, Serial Cut, y agencias como Saatchi & Saatchi L.A., JWT NY, TBWA, 72 & Sunny L.A., Ogilvy Madrid, Leo Burnett Budapest,  Herezie Paris, Publicis, 72 and Sunny L.A., Sra. Rushmore, China Madrid o S.C.P.F. por mencionar algunas.
Fotógrafo especializado en fotografía de producto. Realiza instantáneas para publicidad, así como talleres presenciales y online relacionados con la fotografía de bodegón y gastronómica.

Hola! Soy Josefina Mogrovejo, Diseñadora de Imagen y Sonido; Fotógrafa y Directora de Arte. 

Mi trabajo se enfoca en Set Design, lo que también llamamos bodegón y naturaleza muertas. Recorrer mercadillos y casas de amigos en busca del prop ideal se ha vuelto mi especialidad! ;)

Exploro y resignifico objetos, busco combinaciones impensadas y soy una convencida de que podemos trasmitir el mensaje que queremos cuando todos los elementos de una fotografía están cuidadosamente seleccionados.

He trabajado en proyectos de pequeña y gran escala para clientes nacionales e internacionales como Disney, Nesquik, Beefeater, Mc Donalds, Tastemade, Brother, Monoblock, Kasadesign y Filgo, entre otros. 

Soy una fanática de generar mundos a través de distintos elementos, jugar con los colores y también combinar texturas y formas diversas.

Dicto talleres desde hace más de 10 años. Enseñar y transmitir lo que fui aprendiendo en estos años de trabajo es una de mis grandes pasiones.

Seguime en @josefinamvejo ;)

Mireia Ruiz, 1983, Barcelona. Plastic artist who lives and works in her studio in Barcelona. She completed her graphic design studies at the BAU design school in Barcelona (2001-2005). After being part of several design studios, she joined Cocolia Studio (2009- 2019), where she took charge of its art direction and developed creative photography and set design projects.

Today, she devotes herself to her artistic passion, by dealing with the use of color as a communicative tool.

In 2019 she was a member of the jury at the AdgFad Laus student awards, and also at the 080 Fashion Week Barcelona fashion contest.
She also works as a teacher at the IDEP Barcelona design school, teaching “Experimental projects and creativity”, in the Postgraduate courses in Fashion, Graphic and Photography.

#mireiaysuscosas

Estoy viviendo un sueño y todo fue porque empecé buscando la luz. Eso suena algo espiritual, y sí, pero me refiero a que un día fui estudiante de Comunicación Social en la Pontificia Universidad Javeriana y mi énfasis en lo audiovisual me llevó a la búsqueda de la luz. Ahí comenzo un camino de continuo aprendizaje que me ha permitido representar la luz en diferentes formas, también de esa constante busqueda es que viene mi empresa y su nombre: White Studios, que a día de hoy tiene operación en mi Colombia y en Canadá, donde actualmente vivo.

Me gusta mucho saber que empresas como Falabella, MNG o Dafiti, aparecen dentro de mi portafolio, pero mi verdadera alegría está en cada ocasión que logro componer con imágenes una historia exitosa que logra llevar un producto hasta su público. Eso es lo que quiero compartir contigo, las enseñanzas que la experiencia en fotografía de moda y de producto, a lo largo de estos siete años, me ha dejado.

¿Por qué le gusta mi trabajo a mis clientes? Porque siempre estoy pensando en cómo algo se puede ver mejor. Lo hago con sus marcas, con sus productos y con sus e-commerce. Después de compartir este curso juntos, vas a estar en capacidad de entregar a tus clientes una mejor imagen de cara al mercado que les espera.

Hay mucho camino por delante y todavía la historia se está construyendo. Por ahora, vamos a aprender a sacar lo mejor de tus habilidades y lo mejor de los productos frente a la luz.

teachers.aboutMe:
Hola, soy Carla Marin, artista textil y creadora de la marca Fibra Bohemia que se especializa en la técnica de macramé.
Soy administradora de profesión, trabajé muchos años en el sector hidrocarburos, pero siempre tuve una gran afición por las manualidades, ya que mi mamá pintaba y siempre estaba sumergida en algún tipo de manualidad desde que tengo uso de razón.

Fibra Bohemia nació en el año 2017, en un momento difícil de mi vida donde los nudos se volvieron mi refugio, ayudándome a desconectar de todo lo que estábamos pasando como familia, para luego convertirse en mi terapia creativa.
 A través de Fibra Bohemia busco revivir el arte de los nudos de una forma contemporánea utilizando fibras naturales como el cordón de algodón. Me dedico a crear piezas de macramé decorativas que dan calidez a cualquier espacio así como también joyería y accesorios que le pueden dar vida a tu día a día.

Una de las cosas que más me apasiona es dictar talleres, con estos he logrado conectar con cada uno mis alumnas/os, y no hay nada mas lindo y satisfactorio que poder compartir mi pasión por los nudos con otras personas. A través de ellos puedes lograr desconectar del mundo exterior y conectar contigo mismo, sin que importe el tiempo, lugar y espacio.

Mi nombre es Constanza Bielsa, nací en Córdoba, Argentina, actualmente vivo en Santiago de Chile.
Estudié Arquitectura, al terminar la carrera realicé un Diplomado en Arquitectura sustentable.
En 2008, comencé con mis estudios relacionados a la orfebrería, profundizando y especializándome en la joyería textil. Desde entonces he tomado algunos cursos específicos, y el resto de mis aprendizajes han sido de manera autónoma.
Estoy dedicada a la docencia, enseñando en las carreras de arquitectura, diseño vestuario y textil, también en escuela de joyería. Tengo mi marca de joyería de autor homónima CB y trabajo como colaboradora en una oficina de arquitectura.
Mi trabajo se ha destacado por el cruce del uso de tecnologías digitales (técnica) y los textiles en desuso (materia prima).
He ganado varios concursos y premios, lo cual impulsaron el desarrollo de mi carrera “autodidacta”, dándome la posibilidad de mostrar mi trabajo en ferias internacionales en países como España, Italia, Alemania, Argentina, Brasil entre otros.
Algunos de los premios que he ganado son Premio Chile Diseño-2022, y Bienal Iberoamericana de diseño 2022, ambos con el proyecto “Imaginarios Orgánicos”.

¡Hola! Somos Elsa Amigo y Daniela Le Feuvre, mamá e hija y juntas conformamos Fatto, el mejor espacio para aprender a confeccionar accesorios.

Decidimos emprender juntas en un momento de búsqueda vocacional de Dani después de haber ejercido como profesora y de haberse dado cuenta de lo entretenido que era el oficio de orfebre de Elsa, que llevaba 10 años haciendo accesorios y dando clases de manera informal a amigas en su casa. Juntas le dijimos a que si a darle un nuevo sentido a Fatto. 

Fatto se funda de nuestro reencuentro entre mamá e hija, pero tiene que ver mucho con nuestra pasión por las cosas hechas a mano que arrastramos desde nuestra familias formadas por mujeres que solucionaban los problemas domésticos con creatividad y con el poder de sus manos. 

Enseñamos a hacer accesorios porque marcan personalidad y para nosotras significan darse cariño, la sanación qué hay detrás de crear con las manos cobra más sentido cuando las alumnas se hacen algo para sí mismas y que eleva su auto cuidado.

Los diseños que luego enseñamos en nuestro espacio son creación diseñadas por nosotras, en donde el color y las texturas juegan un rol fundamental, por esto nuestros materiales favoritos son mostacillas, cristales, hilos, piedras y textiles.

Me dedico al diseño y confección de joyería fina, bajo mi marca homónima que creé el año 2019. Mi especialidad son las joyas de diseño de autor, producidas de forma manual y a baja escala, con metales preciosos, piedras naturales y la técnica italiana del micro mosaico. 

La magia detrás de las joyas ocurre en mi estudio en Santiago de Chile, donde confecciono las piezas y también recibo a clientes que quieren visitar mi taller y conocer más sobre mi trabajo. En mi cuenta de instagram comparto mi trabajo, el proceso detrás de las joyas y las cosas que me inspiran. Este medio me ha permitido relacionarme y llegar a gente a lo largo de Chile y el mundo. 

He tenido la oportunidad de vivir y recorrer distintos lugares, como Barcelona, Madrid, Mallorca, Italia y Chile por supuesto, lo cual me permitió formarme con diferentes maestros, aprender sus técnicas y el ‘saber hacer’ de cada uno de ellos.

Para mí, crear joyas es un proceso en el cual puedo expresar mis emociones, una forma de comunicarme a través de la naturaleza de los materiales y los símbolos, que se transforman en pequeñas obras de arte que acompañan en el tiempo. Me inspira profundamente trabajar con materiales tan nobles y maravillosos como los metales, el vidrio y las piedras naturales. Mi búsqueda personal es intentar acercar lo sublime a nuestro mundo cotidiano.

Hola somos Laura y Ana, hermanas creadoras de la marca VATTEA, nuestra pasión por la artesania y el diseño nos llevo a estudiar nuestras carreras,  producción de joyería y diseño industrial respectivamente. En el año 2016 consolidamos nuestra marca de joyas en la ciudad de Medellín (Colombia).

Creamos cada pieza con gran cuidado en los detalles y procesos manuales, el trabajo con los hilos cocidos a mano y almidonados es el resultado de un proceso de investigación con féculas naturales. La exploración de materiales es parte del proceso creativo en nuestro taller, nos encanta descubrir todo lo que se puede lograr inteviniendolos... cortar, soldar, enrollar... ¡infinidad de posibilidades!

Nos inspiramos en diversas culturas ancestrales y sus representaciones a través de objetos y símbolos, tomamos los colores como referentes del folclor colombiano evocando la calidez y fuerza de las mujeres latinas.
 
El material base de VATTEA es el bronce. A cada pieza le damos una textura o pulido para dar este efecto de rusticidad que se ve en nuestras joyas, posteriormente cada pieza es bañada en oro de 24 quilates. El hilo de algodón es otro de los materiales que caracteriza a la marca, este pasa por procesos como la costura a mano y luego un almidonado con féculas naturales. El resultado son piezas con gran valor artesanal.

Nuestras joyas han sido publicadas en revistas como Vogue Latinoamerica, Caras Colombia, Carrusel, Aló entre otras.

Soy una diseñadora autodidacta nacida en Lima, Perú. 

Aunque fui amante de las manualidades desde muy pequeña, después de crear el tocado de boda de mi hermana, descubrí la pasión por el diseño y la joyería fundando así mi marca homónima en 1997.

Mi maravilloso equipo de expertas artesanas y yo desarrollamos nuestra creatividad creando piezas únicas a mano usando diversas técnicas. Cada colección refleja los 24 años de conocimientos y búsqueda conceptual. Nuestro arte va más allá de trenzar el alambre. Trenzamos vínculos y creamos objetos que dan valor y significado a la historia de otras mujeres distinguiéndolas y empoderándolas.


Roxana Pardo is a self-taught designer born in Lima, Peru.

From a very young age she was a lover of crafts, after creating the wedding headdress for her sister, she discovered her passion for design and jewelry, founding her eponymous brand in 1997.

Her wonderful team of expert craftswomen and her develop their creativity by making unique pieces by hand using various techniques.

Each collection reflects 24 years of knowledge and conceptual research. Roxana Pardo's art goes beyond braiding the wire. They braid links and create objects that give value and meaning to the history of other women, distinguishing and empowering them.

Her innovative spirit and her commitment to the highest quality materials and production techniques, in each piece that she bears her signature, continue to be the hallmark of Roxana Pardo today.

Me llamo Maria Rosúa, nací en Rosario, Argentina, en una familia de mujeres artistas y emprendedoras, ellas me enseñaron el arte desde el juego y observándolas aprendi que dentro mio tenía todas las herramientas a disposición para poder crear y ser independiente. Desde pequeña los materiales, los colores, las formas y el hacer eran parte de lo cotidiano. A los 18 años comencé a viajar por el mundo, en esos viajes descubrí el metal y la artesanía, y desde ese momento la joyería se transformo en uno de los propósitos de mi vida. Estudié con artesanos, que me enseñaron técnicas y me abrieron la puerta al mundo de la creación. Esto me llevo a estudiar la carrera de Diseño Industrial, donde adquirí herramientas y le di sentido a mi producción. Tuve la oportunidad de conocer el mundo gracias a mi oficio, estudiar y trabajar en países como Argentina, España, Estados Unidos, Colombia, India, lugares que inspiran mis colecciones y las llenan de experiencias y sentimientos. En el 2015 llegue a Barcelona gracias a una beca que me otorgó mi universidad en la Escola Massana. Dos años mas tarde me mudé a Formentera, la mas pequeña de las Islas Baleares, donde hoy vivo con mi familia y tengo mi taller. 

A lo largo de los años el juego en el taller me permito crear y expresarme. En cada etapa y momento de mi vida voy encontrando distintos materiales con los que diseño, desde el metal como base combinado, con maderas, impresión 3D, pátinas, pintura, plásticos reciclados. 
Busco que mis piezas muestren el contacto con la materia, la imperfección que nos da el ser humanos, cada joya lleva tiempo y dedicación, cargan energía y cuentan historias.
Creo que la producción de artesanías es una postura ante un mundo complejo, por eso busco un diseño consciente, que cuente el momento que vivimos, a través de la forma o la materialidad.

En los últimos años me he dedicado a buscar la manera de dar color al metal, desde la experimentación, pruebas y errores, cursos y talleres que he ido tomando encontré varias técnicas que me permiten llenar de color,  vida y sensaciones mis joyas en metal, intento con el color volver cálido al material, transmitir experiencias, valores, recuerdos, el uso de pátinas, oxidaciones, pigmentos, acuarelas, esmaltes, terminan volviendo a mis diseños en metal pequeñas ilustraciones para decorar nuestros cuerpos.

teachers.aboutMe:
Instagram · @jileecious
Twitter · @PleaseEnjoy
Linkedin · @Ji Lee

I was born in Korea, raised in Brazil, and now I live and work in New York. I'm an independent artist and designer, but I also have a full time job as a creative director at Facebook and Instagram.

My parents were high-school teachers in Korea. To seek better economic opportunities, our family immigrated to São Paulo, Brazil when I was 10. Growing up, my dream was to become an artist like Picasso. With this dream, I went to New York to study at an art school. My parents used their savings to help pay my tuition. But I had to wait table at restaurants for many years to pay for my living. I realized I would have a very hard time making money as an artist. This is when I changed my major to graphic design. After graduating, I worked at graphic design firms, but I was doing very dry and boring corporate work. So I ended up switching to advertising with the hopes of doing more creative work. But the work was still very safe and uncreative. This is when I started to make personal projects like the Bubble Project and Word as Image. These projects became famous and ended up helping me professionally. But most importantly, I was able to find my passion of making things again through personal project. Since then, I continue to always dedicate my time and energy to work on personal projects. Today, I'm a passionate advocate of the message that anyone can benefit from working on personal projects and transform their lives.

teachers.aboutMe:
Welcome! My name is Neberra, and I'm a self-taught surrealist painter located in Lisboa, Portugal. My passion for Art started a long time ago, and I draw and paint since I can remember.
After my degree in Graphic Design, I was fortunate to illustrate a small children's magazine. In the following years, between 2006 and 2007, I worked in a small advertising agency, and after that, I found a teaching post at a Lisbon training school, dedicating the next 5 years to teaching graphic software, 
During this time, I mainly created digital illustrations leaving the conventional, more traditional process aside.
After 2013 I decided to devote myself entirely to pursue an artistic career, participating in many group shows and a few individual exhibitions. I started with acrylic paint to get more confident, and after some months, I got back to oils, which are actually my favorite medium since I was fourteen.
My work was featured in various art magazines, including Catapult, Blopop, Hey, Artit, just to mention a few.
In 2018 my painting "The Great Fetishist" was published on the B cover of "Heavy Metal" magazine, and in 2020 I received an honourable mention with my picture "Saint Rose of Pop" in the Beautiful Bizarre Art Prize.

My work reflects a lot of my unconscious! Especially in the way I see the world and solve my fears and anguish. The images I create work as mediators between my issues and my surrounding reality, a profound interpretation of various aspects of my mind.
What I have understood over time is that not all the process of creation and interpretation is successful. And in this way, I am in part condemned to a constant process of evolution and learning.
I am not devoid of opinions and concerns about the world around me, even because it is this point that undoubtedly creates the instability that I need to solve the best I can by painting. Throughout this process that began at a young age, I identified myself with Surrealism and later with Pop Surrealism, and in these artistic movements, I frame my work.
The fantasy and influence of Pop culture are just as important as sensitivity to environmental and social issues. I often try to revive an Era in which nature had a significant prominence in people's lives. Consequently, a universe emerges, which is a kind of symbiosis that relates the human being to his surroundings and nature itself.
I feel that the paintings I create work as parallel reality windows. In these images, we have subtle references to past historical events, but different realities arise from ours.

Emma Friedlander-Collins is an upcycling and remaking champion, finding positive ways to use her craft powers for good and sharing them with anyone that wants them ;)

She started designing and selling crochet patterns in 2011. With her unique approach and unusual designs, she has established herself as an innovative designer and online success.

Her books 'Crochet Dress-Up', 'Big Hook Crochet' and '35 Crochet Bags' can be found online and in all good book stores.  Although she still sells individual patterns at the place where it all began - her little corner of Etsy and more recently at LoveCrochet.

She is passionate about sustainability and continually works to discover ways to use craft and making to create communities and inspire others.  She also wrangles this into her other work as a content creator for LoveCrafts presenting their sewing channel on Youtube, and lecturer in Visual Promotion where she teaches students the fine art of creating visual stories as part of a BA in Fashion Communication.

Emma has been featured in 'Mollie Makes', 'Simply Crochet, 'Inside Crochet', 'Love Crochet' and 'Crochet Now' magazines, and has contributed to a number of other online and paper publications. She has also collaborated with the lovely people at HobbyCraft, Hoooked Zpagetti, DMC, Crochyay Boxes and other scrummy yarn companies, and has had her yarn photography featured in a variety of publications from The Guardian to LoveCrochet.

She has just signed a contract to write her first upcycling book so watch this space!

You can contact her at  or hop on over to her instagram account and send a message.

teachers.aboutMe:
Oh, hello!

I'm Camille Labarre, a freelance fabricator and designer from NYC. I specialize in puppets, props, and sets for film, animation, and theater. I'm basically a professional crafter - my job is to figure out how to make anything!

Whether on commission or between jobs, I also create punch needle embroidery portraits in my studio. It's the perfect way to combine my love of portraiture with my lifelong obsession with craft. Punch needle is a unique approach to painting with embroidery that's fun and exciting (and easier than you think!) and I hope you'll think so too.

Being a fabricator is an absolute dream - a career that makes sense of what once seemed like a scattered creative background. After graduating with a degree in art from Yale university, I was awarded a year-long fellowship to study basketmaking in Europe. I then joined a guild of traveling craftsmen in France as a leatherworking apprentice. While working at a shoe factory making luxury belts and wallets, I decided to apply to graduate school. I earned my Master of Philosophy in Arts Education from the University of Cambridge the following year, focusing on what craft can teach us about the importance of embodied learning - of learning by doing. 

Soon after, I moved back to my hometown of NYC and got a fabrication internship at an animation company making miniatures for stop-motion animated TV commercials. I couldn't believe that I had found a job that actually rewarded being a jack of all trades. Suddenly, my unspecialized skill set was an asset. It was heaven.

I am now freelancing, which means that between gigs I can find time to make personal work like my punch needle portraits.

The only thing I love to do as much as craft is to teach - and that's where you come in! I'm so honored to have the chance to share a little piece of my world with you. I'll give you the tools you need to approach your work fearlessly and make it your own. You can do this!

Check out my YouTube channel for more crafty madness :)

teacher.aboutMe:
Soy ilustrador y artista visual de la Ciudad de México. En 2013 empecé un proyecto llamado Rimiyoho donde experimento con ilustración digital y animación en vivo, proyectando y pintando graffitis de luz que activan la arquitectura interviniendo edificios o espacios públicos, colaborando también con músicos en vivo para convertir el escenario en un lienzo para el arte digital.
En este proyecto, el dibujo y el mapping se combinan para llevar la ilustración a las calles y compartir con la gente el proceso de creación de una pieza digital animada en vivo usando la aplicación Tagtool para iPad y un proyector.

He tenido la oportunidad de llevar mi trabajo a eventos culturales y comerciales y pintar en escenarios o sobre fachadas de iglesias y edificios históricos, uno de mis proyectos favoritos fue mapear el interior del Teatro Nacional de Taichung en Taiwán, realicé un viaje audiovisual que se proyectó durante un mes en este increíble teatro que fue diseñado por el arquitecto japonés Toyo Ito. He sido invitado a festivales como Mutek Montreal 2019, Mutek Mx 2018, en el ZKM Center for Art and Media en Alemania, en el Museo de Arte Mexicano en Chicago y en Tianjin, China. También he participado en festivales como León Light Fest, Vitae Fest en el Zócalo de la CDMX, FICH 2023, FILUX Mérida 2018, Los Dos Uno 2023, Festival de Cultura y Tecnología de Oaxaca 2017 entre otros.

También he trabajado para marcas como BMW, Porsche, Uber, Pepsi, Stella Artois, Nissan, Huawei, Benetton, entre otros colaborando con Dj´s o músicos para crear nuevas experiencias audiovisuales.

teachers.aboutMe: Gerard + Belevender is a photography and creative direction studio for brands that know who they are - or at least know what they’re not. The majority of our work focuses on food and beverage products,  and the scenes we create are often inspired by pop culture, movies, history, or nostalgia, but are always rooted in worldbuilding.

Hello! I’m Victoria Jane - a photographer, florist and stylist based in Brooklyn, New York. 
I received my first camera at the age of 9 and since then, I’ve barely ever spent a day without one!
After high school, I attended the International Center of Photography. It was there where I really discovered, and was able to nurture my love of photography.
After graduating I accepted any photography job I could, so that I could keep developing my craft. Weddings, events, retail and portraits - you name it, I shot it!
It wasn’t, however, until 2018, that I decided to merge my two passions - photography and florals - which resulted in what I would say was my area of specialty; still-life photography featuring botanicals. 

I would describe my style as ‘Colorful Punchy.’ My work uses florals, bold colors, textures and light, all hopefully coming together to create a distinctive still life scene. 
My creative purpose is to try and reflect the joy of the natural world in a cool, contemporary way while showcasing it’s wonder, beauty and quiet quirkiness.
To date, I have been fortunate enough to bring my style to different retail, health and wellness, food and beverage and lifestyle brands.

Still Life Photographer and Director Amy Currell was born in East London, where she lives and works. Her photography and moving image is shot through a distinctively female lens, and each frame is composed with thoughtfulness and grace – artfully juxtaposing colour, texture, and shape. 

Amy’s lighting draws narratives from shadow and finds warmth in her subjects. Amy is also currently experimenting with blending CGI techniques with traditional stills photography for a perfected reality. 

Expanding in her role as a Director, Amy works with the newest motion control cameras to give any moving image elements of the work an edge, giving the same poise and polish to her film that you’ll find in her photography. 

Amy is highly sought after in the commercial world by global clients who value beauty, and the context of their products in carefully choreographed composition, and these have included - Ikea, British Vogue, Selfridges, Liberty London, Tatler, Bvlgari, Van Cleef & Arpels and London Art Fair.

My name is Daniela Constantini. I am a Mexican photographer living in Bern, Switzerland. I graduated from the Visual Journalism and Documentary Practice program at the International Center of Photography in New York. My long-term project Days of Silence won Rita K. Hillman Excellence Award. 

Since graduation, I have been working as a freelance photographer focusing on Portraiture, Still Life, and Lifestyle. I have been as an Art Director, Stylist, and Photographer on projects with brands like Villars Maître Chocolatier, L'Occitane, Mövenpick, Ojo de Café, in Switzerland, and for Pyne & Smith Clothiers based in California, USA, among others.

My portraiture and still life work won 1st place and the Swiss Photo Award on the 2nd Edition of the International Photo Festival in Olten, 2023, and exhibited at the Photography Festival in Switzerland in Olten, Switzerland. I won Feature Shoot Emerging Photography Awards, Series Winner, 2021. My work was exhibited in Paris and Berlin. I am a 2022 finalist for The Independent Photographer People Awards and the 2021 Open Call Award. I am a 2019 Dior Photography Award Laureate, my work was exhibited at Rencontres de la photographie d'Arles, France.  

I have exhibited work in New York, Mexico City, Olten (Switzerland) Paris, Arles, Berlin, and Amsterdam.

Before moving to New York, I worked as a freelance journalist in Mexico City, my hometown, and collaborated with different companies on video, photo, and journalistic productions.

In 2015 Errr-Magazine, a Mexican magazine devoted to art and literature published my first novel, El gato me da igual. I hold a Bachelor's degree in Communication and a major in Journalism from Universidad Ibero in Mexico City.

Established in 2014, littledrill is a creative studio owned and operated by Shelby Edwards and James Lee Whitney. Together, they bring products, people and places to life through creative photography, video and art direction. West coast raised and east coast based, littledrill explores objects and moods through vibrant colors and graphic presentation. Inspired by pop art, modern design and coastal cities, littledrill creates scroll-stopping concepts that are distinct, varying from clean compositions to quirky and unconventional. They have had the pleasure of working with brands such as Adidas, ESPN, Interscope Records, and more.

Nicolas Polli was born in Brusino Arsizio, Switzerland in 1989, he studied Art Direction at ECAL Lausanne for his Master degree. His photographic work has been exhibited nationally and internationally, notably at l’appartement – Espace Images Vevey, Photoforum Pasquart, Espace Arlaud in Lausanne, Museum Brot in Ulm, Verzasca Foto Festival, Gibellina Photoroad, Coal Mine Winthertur. He published two monographs: "Ferox the Forgotten Archives 1976–2010” and “When Strawberries Will Grow on Trees, I Will Kiss U”. In 2018 and 2020, he won the Swiss Design Award and he is currently the resident at Atelier Robert in Biel. He worked for clients such as Swiss air, Athletic Green, Prada, Ferragamo, Freitag, Ovomaltine, Wallpaper Magazine, Rimadesio, MDF Italia,...

teachers.aboutMe:
Hi! I’m Yulia and I’m a self-taught hand embroidery artist based in Cleveland, Ohio. You can find me on Instagram @mossandfeather. I’ve been embroidering for three years now. I’ve always liked art, like painting and drawing, but it wasn’t until I discovered embroidery that creating art became one of the most important aspects of my life. 

I specialize in thread painting, which is a technique used to create realistic embroidery. It’s a lot like painting on a canvas but using thread instead of paint. Using this technique, you can achieve fine artistic detail, including shading, highlights and smooth color gradients. 

I’ve always been inspired by nature and animals and I love how well thread mimics the look of fur and feathers. It’s really the perfect medium for the type of art I like to create.

Susan is a floral designer, artist and instructor who creates unusual, boundary-pushing floral art including elaborate headpieces, floral wearables, floral installations, and her signature succulent jewelry. Her soulful, seasonally- inspired creations have been described as exquisite living artwork.
A passionate teacher, Susan offers instruction for new and professional florists through her online classes, “Virtual Studio” membership, and through destination workshops. 
 
Susan’s work has been featured in leading industry publications and websites including Fusion Flowers Magazine, Martha Stewart Weddings, Flower magazine, Florist’s Review, My Modern Met, Refinery 29, SELF, Buzzfeed, Good Housekeeping, Belle Armoire, and Modern Wedding Flowers. Susan is a member of Chapel Designers and Slow Flowers. Her first book, “The Art of Wearable Flowers” was released spring 2020, with Chronicle Books.

I'm Freya and I spend my days merrily making jewellery from my wee studio in Glasgow, Scotland!

I work in mostly brass and make simple identifiable yet naive forms that are then made into earrings, necklaces and pins.

I am always doodling. I find it so pleasing how just with the placing of a nose, eyes and mouth one can create a sort of character and in the same way a few wiggly lines can quickly represent the human form. I work mostly with sheet material and use a piercing saw to cut out the details of each face, bum and boob without a stencil making each is unique. Piercing sheet metal is a brilliantly limiting medium of positive and negative space. It forces me to distill my ideas and drawings to their most essential parts.

Why brass? Lots of the materials found in the jewellery industry are a bit problematic. Precious stones and metals, especially higher value ones, can have cloudy origins. Brass is a wonderful material, it’s an alloy typically made from recycled metals and its cost allows for an expressive approach to making. 
Keeping my work somewhat accessible in price is really important to me and using brass also happens to mean I can charge a bit less for my pieces so its a win win win! :)

Gabriela is a Brazilian born, Scottish based photographer. She works across editorial, lifestyle and still life photography, working primarily with independent companies and makers to create striking and effective content that elevate brand and business.
Through her personal bodies of work, flowers and flesh are used as symbolic starting points to explore ideas and ideals of love, sex, beauty and death.

Hi yall! My name is Alicia and I'm a full time Chicago based jeweler who specializes in adding unique textures to my sculptural jewelry. With a background in Cultural Anthropology as well as a degree in Jewelry Design from New York’s Fashion Institute of Technology, I apply my knowledge of ancient techniques like reticulation and acid etching to my more contemporary designs. 
My love of complex looking ceremonial jewelry created with minimal tools such as fire, sand and beeswax have led me to truly admire the work throughout the Mesoamericas and the African diaspora. I've honed my unique style while working for dozens of major jewelry companies in the fashion industry in New York City, learning the business ins and outs during the day, while creating at night. 
I truly love the creation of jewelry and just love to share what I know and what I'm still trying to figure out. I love that you can really hone in one one concept, like wax carving, beading or metal work and just keep making things in that aspect. If you want to explore more, you can and if you don't , it's fine too.
With almost two decades of experience under my belt, and a decade of being an independent jeweler in my own right with my eponymous brand, Lingua Nigra, I continue to fabricate new ways to explore bygone approaches to creating wearable art.

I'm a Japanese Brazilian paper jeweller based in Leipzig, Germany and since 2013, I'm behind Mayumi Origami, a jewellery brand designed with high quality Japanese Chiyogami silkscreened paper. It's currently available in different museums shops in Europe such as the British Museum in UK, Orient Museum in Portugal and CODA Museum in the Netherlands.
At the Centro de Joalharia de Lisboa, I studied Jewellery Design and attended several jewellery and paper making courses in Japan, UK and Germany.
In 2018 and 2019, I was invited to tutor workshops exploring the Origami jewellery field at the West Dean College, UK and at the Papierwerk Glockenbach in Germany.

teachers.aboutMe:
I'm born in 1982 in Tortona (AL), I live and work in Voghera (Italy).
In 2007 i achieved my degree in painting at the Art Academy of Brera (Milan).

i work exclusively with colored pencils, I often represent the flora, fauna and female mystics of Sardinia from the 16th to the 18th centuries
Combining organic shapes and textures with chiaroscuro contrasts of light and shadow, my drawings portray isolated female faces framed by plants and animals. 
My imagery refers to the herbalist traditions and Sardinian folklore of the mystical seductresses who enchant, curse and cure. My body of work is a tribute to the legacy of healing women throughout history. 

my works appeared in books, newspapers and magazines such as The New Yorker, Juxtapoz Magazine, Hi Fructose Magazine, Les Arts Dessines, Arte Mondadori.
With Albin Michel I published the illustrated book "Poucette" (distributed in Spain for Edelvives with the title "Pulgarcita"). I'm preparing an illustrated book in collaboration with Sébastien Perez.

I collaborate with Jonathan LeVine Projects (New Jersey) and Thinkspace Projects (Los Angeles) for America, Gallery Benoni (Copenhagen), Galleria Patricia Armocida (Milan), Galleria Giovanni Bonelli (Milan) for Europe.
I took part in the 54th International Art Exhibition, Biennale di Venezia, Italian Pavilion, curated by Vittorio Sgarbi, Lombardy Regional Pavilion, Palazzo Te, Mantova, "Turn The Page: the first ten years of hi-fructose" at the Virginia Museum of Contemporary Art (Moca) (US), POW! WOW! Hawai'i at the Honolulu Museum of Art School (US), THE NATURE SQUISITE: BEYOND THE BOUNDARIES OF POP at the Stelline Foundation (Milan), The New Vanguard - at The Lancaster Museum of Art and History (MOAH) and IMAGO at the Much Museum in Munich (Germany).
Among my solo shows: “Dear Collapse” Thinkspace Project (Los Angeles), “Monism” Galleri Benoni (Copenhagen), “Il Ricordo è un Consolatore Molesto” Galleria Patricia Armocida (Milan), “Home” Galleria Giovanni Bonelli (Milan), “ Animanera ”Jonathan LeVine Gallery (NY).

Hello! My name is Michele Bajona and I'm a contemporary figurative artist born in 1971 in Vicenza, Italy. 
I learned the art of painting from my hometown maestro Otello de Maria and I focused on watercolors with Frederic Wong at the Art Student League of New York.
I love to share my knowledge with the art community and keep learning and experimenting on different supports and with different techniques in order to capture the essence of light and movement.
I like to play with water and to measure myself with the magic of nature, the figurative approach of my art has within it a level of abstraction that allows me to transmit emotions at a deeper level. 
Art has the power to show different worlds generated from a blank canvas, I want to share this process through my work.

I am an artist and fashion illustrator producing works based on form, colour and texture. I have worked with large European fashion houses and featured internationally in fashion magazines and wider press.

In 2020 I was chosen by illustrious fashion magazine VOGUE, to be one of seven artists picked to draw my favourite couture looks from Vogue's Runway archive pages.

I am ever-curious of what different tools can achieve and my work is an evolving exploration of what is possible through them.

My work featured as the cover image of the biography of Italian Baroque Artist Artemisia Gentileschi. Written by art critic and writer Johnathan Jones, the book accompanied the first complete retrospective of Gentileschi’s work at the National Gallery in 2019.

I am from upstate New York, but have been living in San Diego, California for 15 years. I come from a family of six and have a twin brother, who is an artist as well. Like many artists growing up, I have been creating art for as long as I can remember. From drawing dinosaurs very early on to my favorite cartoon and video game characters, I was always creating.

I have my degree in art as well as extensive academic training. I love to teach and have been teaching drawing and painting for 10 years. I have had the privilege to create art in multiple industries, from gaming and movies to the fashion industry. I have worked with some spectacular clients such as TIME Magazine, BLT Communications, Remetee Clothing, to name a few. I have been published in multiple books and magazines, such as Spectrum, Infected By Art, ARC Salon, etc and have won awards for my art.

My name is Bo Feng Lin. I am an illustrator and artist and work as the founder for Gagiland.

My aim is to create captivating portraits with eye-catching shapes and vibrant colors. Whenever I can, I incorporate beautiful beaches, palm trees, and blue skies to create a dreamy, tropical vibe.

I'm passionate about representing minorities in my art but I also live for minimalistic art with a tropical touch!

My client work include book covers, children book illustrations, collectibles, and illustrations in fashion and cosmetics.

I’m Dr. Anita Johnston a depth psychologist, author, and storyteller. My book, Eating in the Light of the Moon, using myth, metaphor and storytelling to transform struggles with food, has been published in seven languages.  Currently I’m the Founder and Executive Clinical Director of Ai Pono Hawaii and Founder of the online platform, Light of the Moon Café. 
My life’s work has been to weave together archetypal psychological principles, indigenous wisdom, and modern neuroscience to help illuminate the deeper meaning of our internal struggles. I use the language of symbolism and story to move beyond the confines of logical, linear thought and enter the intuitive landscape of the psyche--where insight, transformation and healing await. I believe that by reconnecting with the depth and breadth of multiple aspects of who we are, we can find balance, freedom and ease in our creative endeavors.

teachers.aboutMe:
My name is Connie Lim and I am a freelance illustrator and educator from Los Angeles, USA. From an early age art has been my passion, from drawing every day as a young child through to enrolling to study illustration at the prestigious Art Centre College of Design in Pasadena, California. It was there that I fell in love with drawing, learning about the human form, experimenting with media and just discovering myself as a creative. 
 
It was the first year here that I laid the foundations for my obsession with drawing characters. I was always drawn to emotions, expressions, and theatrical energy. I discovered fashion embodied all these aspects and was the perfect outlet. My passion then brought me to London in 2010 to study at Central Saint Martins and the UK has been a creative base for me on and off since during the past ten years. It was these years in the UK that has given me the opportunities and experiences to hone in on my own creative voice.
 
Following my graduation I set about developing my love of illustration and fashion to forge striking images of my characters in couture, reflecting the artisanal approach and application with a determination to create a truly unique aesthetic. This has driven me through a strong period of creative growth and as my reputation as a freelance artist has grown, I have had my work published, both on the web and in print, featured in magazines, been involved in gallery shows, installations, and collaborated and consulted in my field both in the UK and overseas. I am now also privileged to be invited to impart my knowledge and demonstrate my techniques at a number of educational art institutions, which is a great honour. In terms of immediate upcoming projects for early 2020, I will be participating in a group exhibition in Portland, Oregon from February 15, 2020 to March 4, 2020 at the well known Nucleus Gallery. I have also been invited to Central Saint Martins in February as a guest to teach drawing techniques and oversee their Balenciaga portfolio project to undergraduates on their prestigious BA Fashion course. My past exhibitions and clients include: ShowStudio, La Perla, Louboutin, Bulgari, Guerlain, Revlon, Gallery Nucleus, Oxo Gallery and my current publication of ‘The Illustrator’ by Taschen published 2019.

Hey Everyone! Welcome to my little art corner in the big universe we know as the internet! To introduce myself I should start out by saying that I am the owner, designer, and creative force behind Mountain Maiden Co. A personal collective of wearable art made by yours truly. 
Graduating with a BFA in Photography and a minor in Studio Art from Black Hills State, I  have always felt a strong draw to the artistic realm.
Growing up with an artistic parent, I have been on a somewhat eccentric path for most of this crazy walk we call life, it is in this path I have come to realize that my sole purpose is simply "to create".  
 
I was first  introduced to bead weaving and bead looming at the age of 6. It came to be a core thread (pun intended) throughout my childhood, however I was reintroduced to the concept of combing metal and beadwork while on vacation in South Africa in 2019. It was in the majestic Dutch wine lands that I stumbled upon several antiquities in a small antique shop north of Cape Town utilizing the method. This changed my life. Inspired by a technique that had been around for centuries, I added a dabble of contemporary design and modern artistry, bringing it into the 21 century. 
From that point on Mountain Maiden Co was established and from there I have continued to mix mediums as well as test the limits of the foundations of old forms of adornment mixed with modern ideas to create a space inspired by the natural world!

teacher.aboutMe:
I have used art as a catalyst for mental and emotional growth ever since I was a little kid. While growing up in the D.C. metro area of Northern Virginia, I never wavered in my pursuit to be an artist. I graduated cum laude in 2007 with a Bachelor of Fine Arts from the Maryland Institute College of Art in Baltimore. 
.
After graduation I moved to Panama City, Florida, where months later I became the owner of an art gallery and cultural venue space called Gallery Above.  Hosting monthly art exhibits, weekly swing dances and film nights, and countless music performances of local and touring bands, Gallery Above served as the hub for the sub-culture of Bay County.  2 years later I worked as exhibitions manager at the local arts museum for a short while before deciding to leave and concentrate on my main love: creating art.
.
For 15 years I have been working as a professional artist and art instructor.  My work has focused consistently on humans and our connection with nature.  Often combining playful abstractions with realistic portraits, my drawings, oil paintings, cut-paper, and watercolors have exhibited in galleries and museums all across the United States.  I have had several solo exhibitions and won many awards for my work including several Best-in-Shows.  Recently I have created many murals across Northwest Florida, and as far as New York City. 
.
In 2018 climate change hit my life and my entire area directly in the form of Hurricane Michael, which formed unusually and extremely quickly into a category 5.  The hurricane not only destroyed my home leaving me displaced to temporary less-than-ideal living situations for almost 3 years, but it ripped away so much of the natural environment that I loved.  Over millions of acres, the hurricane destroyed 75-90% off all the trees, and 95% of the tree canopy.  In the months following the hurricane, I also suffered multiple personal losses and challenges, all leaving me in a deep depression.  
.
After a year without creating any art, drowning in trauma and loss, I decided to take a drastic step toward self-healing.  I booked a tiny off-grid treehouse in the woods of the mountains of North Georgia for a week.  Unplugged and isolated, I set out to heal through nature and art.  I feared I might just cry for a week, but every morning I hiked and every day I created art until the sun set.  I created works about loss that healed me.  Inexplicably it worked far better than I could have ever hoped for.  That week I clawed out of the depths of my depression, and I have never been back.
.
In 2023 I relocated to Asheville, North Carolina, after falling in love with the mountains, endless forest trails, and thriving arts community.  Asheville promised to be a haven in the changing climate, and yet recently Hurricane Helene ravaged my life yet again, this time sparing my home, but destroying the gallery and teaching space I belonged to in the River Arts District.  Through nature and art, and the arts community, I am healing again.
.
My recent work has focused on interactivity: my new book, “Pull Me Apart” is full of pull tabs, spin wheels, and more, for people to manipulate and play.  I have also expanded into creating interactive murals, where visitors can spin a giant wooden wheel, revealing different images behind cut-out areas of the design.  I am embracing my inner-most weirdo, and creating the art that most wants to come screaming out of me.  Paradoxically, when we create something truly for ourselves, it’s what others connect with most.  Exploring that beautiful interconnectivity of us all motivates my continued creative pursuits.

Hola! Soy Paz, vivo en Buenos Aires y tengo un perro enorme que se llama Apolo.
Me formé en Artes Visuales y en Ilustración.
Me gusta tanto la creación como la teoría que rodea a los libros, decidí hacer un Máster en libros y literatura infantil en la UAB (Universidad Autónoma de Barcelona). En ese marco me centré en estudiar la materialidad del libro como elemento narrativo. El interés en explorar las maneras de involucrar al soporte me llevaron a aprender las técnicas de paper cut e Ingeniería en papel.
Doy clases en la Universidad y en el Profesorado de Bellas Artes.  He tenido la suerte de llevar mis talleres de creación de libros extraordinarios a ferias del libro y museos en Argentina, Uruguay y España.
Mis ilustraciones han sido incluidas en el 10 Catálogo Iberoamérica ilustra 2019, Guadalajara, México y fueron seleccionadas en el CICLA Original Illustrators Exhibition - Chen Bochui International award en 2019 -2020 y 2021, y forman parte de la colección del Shanghai Baoshan International Folk Art Museum en China.
He publicado libros en: Edelvives, Fondo de Cultura Económica, La brujita de Papel, Milrazones, Gerbera Ediciones, AZ Editora, Biblos. Colaboro con algunas marcas y compañías de teatro creando instalaciones de papel,  juguetes y videos de stopmotion con piezas de papel. Algunos de mis clientes son: Maped, LabCO, Cést Moi, Pizzini, Ohra Pampa, Semillita, entre otras.

Soy Noe Arata, vivo en Buenos Aires, estudie diseño en la Universidad de Buenos Aires y  hace casi 10 años trabajo con papel.

Siempre me gusto trabajar con las manos y algo que me resulta muy atractivo del papel es su disponibilidad: un ticket de compra, un boleto de colectivo, una caja de algún perfume, donde sea que uno mire encuentra montones de texturas, colores y gramajes.

Cuando era chica hacia origami y plegaba cajas.
En la universidad, el papel me servía para construir moldes y maquetas.
Desde hace muchos años tengo una pastelería con mi pareja. Haciendo eventos surgió la necesidad de tener decoraciones y volví a encontrar en el papel un medio amable y lleno de posibilidades.

Una vez que empecé a trabajar en serio con papel, ya no pude detenerme.

Desarrolle proyectos para empresas como Brother, Loreal, Pesqueira y Enamorada del Muro entre otras.

Participe en la Feria Puro Diseño 2015 y gane el premio revelación.

Actualmente trabajo en Dobleufa, mi pequeña marca y allí ofrezco guirnaldas y objetos varios de papel calado que vendo en ferias, construyo instalaciones para eventos corporativos y producciones fotográficas y, la parte que mas me gusta, corto a mano pequeñas obras que convierto en escenas plegables o que enmarco. 
También dicto clases de papercut desde mi taller en Palermo.

Nunca me sentí cómoda con los medios expresivos tradicionales y en el papercut encontré una forma amable de materializar mis ideas. La variedad de gramajes y texturas hacen infinitas las posibilidades de la técnica.

Hola, soy Ale Rambar. Soy artista costarricense dedicado a crear obras de arte creadas por medio de capas de papel. Las piezas se crean analizando los cuerpos humanos topográficamente, tal como un topógrafo analizaría montañas, valles o ríos.

Cada pieza se corta por separado, capa por capa y luego se ensambla a mano para crear "topografías humanas". Esta técnica fue desarrollada a lo largo de mi carrera como arquitecto. Mientras estudiaba encontré una fascinación por los mapas topográficos, su sinuosidad y su capacidad para transformarse en elementos tridimensionales.

Esta técnica artística la utilizo para hablar de tolerancia, respeto entre nosotros y respeto por el planeta. Estas piezas de arte buscan abrir espacios para el diálogo a favor de la inclusión.

Manuela Maya Rendón (La Fleuristerie)

Hola, hola Soy Manu, creadora de La Fleuristerie (@lafleuristeriedesign).
Soy orgullosamente colombiana, Diseñadora Industrial de profesión, emprendedora apasionada y una loca amante de llenar el mundo de flores y color. 

La Fleuristerie es un taller de diseño botánico en donde desarrollamos flores de papel pintadas a mano. Nace de mi pasión por la botánica, por el diseño y una estrecha relación con el arte. Con mi trabajo busco enaltecer a la naturaleza otorgando a mis creaciones un toque realista que me exige estudiar cada parte de las flores, entenderla y conocerla, para posteriormente convertirlas en pequeñas obras de arte que llegan día a día a las manos de muchos enamorados y clientes también son amantes de las flores. 

Mi profesión me ha permitido profundizar en diversos materiales y encontrar en el papel el elemento perfecto para materializar mis ideas. También me ha dado las herramientas para la búsqueda e investigación de técnicas y estilos que luego maravillosamente se convierten en mis cómplices a la hora  de dar forma, color y textura a mis creaciones.

Hola soy Cristian, soy ilustrador y me dedico al desarrollo de ilustraciones con volumen ocupando distintos tipos de materiales, muchos de los cuales son reciclados, e colaborado con diarios, revistas y editoriales. Hoy en día trabajo en la creación de libros ilustrados y encargos personalizados en formato de obra de arte.

teachers.aboutMe:
Soy Alex Molina diseñador floral y director de Savia Bruta Flower School.
Desde siempre me han gustado las flores y las bellas artes, amo la naturaleza y la vida en el campo. Desde bien pequeño estuve  en contacto con la naturaleza y mi mayor afición era plantar cosas y verlas crecer. 

Cuando comencé a estudiar jardinería encontré mi verdadera vocación; el diseño floral. El diseño floral engloba mis dos grandes pasiones el arte y la naturaleza.

En 2014 abrí junto a mi socia nuestra empresa de decoración floral y unos años después inaugure la primera escuela de diseño floral de Madrid. Durante los últimos años hemos formado a cientos de nuevos floristas y tenemos alumnos en cualquier parte del mundo gracias a nuestra escuela online. 

Desde hace más de 15 años me he dedicado al mundo de las flores y espero seguir trabajando y creando con ellas durante toda mi vida para mi es un verdadero lujo poder trabajar y vivir de ellas.

Estilista Floral afincada en Barcelona, hace uso de las flores y plantas como medio artístico para contar narrativas.

Su trabajo con las flores es muy gráfico y contemporáneo, destaca su función como profesora de diseño floral, el diseño de instalaciones efímeras, decoración de eventos y ferias, estilismo floral para editoriales y anuncios y un trabajo de investigación continuo a nivel artístico.

Le gusta la naturaleza, las contradicciones del ser humano y observar como funcionan las cosas.

Ora comenzó en mi casa hace 2 años, todo inició con una intención y unas ganas inmensas de redefinir el diseño floral en mi ciudad. Al principio no sabía casi nada de las flores, no me sabía ni el nombre del clavel! Pero creo fielmente que cuando uno está encaminado en un propósito las cosas van funcionando mágicamente. La práctica y el trabajar con las flores me ha llevado a explorar ideas de negocio que nunca me imaginé desde la dirección de arte a dictar talleres. Hemos transformado la manera en que las personas perciben e interactúan con el mundo floral, un mundo más arriesgado donde no hay reglas. Dentro de poco tiempo, nos hemos distinguido por diseñar experiencias sensoriales que dan de qué hablar y hemos tenido el placer de trabajar con marcas como Google, Chanel, Versace, Carolina Herrera, Cartier, Mont Blanc y H&M. También hemos incursionado en el mundo de los matrimonios en todo Colombia,  diseñando mundos mágicos para parejas a punta de detalles de fina coquetería. Si algo hemos aprendido en este negocio es que Its all about the picture. El éxito de un evento para nosotros está en que todos los invitados no puedan irse sin tomar mucha fotos.

¡Hola, soy Dani! Vivo en la CDMX, soy fotógrafo y también soy el Artista Floral detrás de Xochipilli Estudio, en donde creamos ambientaciones florales para eventos, bodas y talleres de floristería en donde busco que cada alumno pueda encender su chispa creativa (que estoy seguro que vive en cada persona en esta tierra) y compartirles los conocimientos y herramientas que me han ayudado a desarrollar mi estilo. 

En mi trabajo como diseñador floral el color es mi estilo, me gusta poder trabajar con muchos colores que formen una paleta de color rica y alegre, no solo en los arreglos, también haciendo estilismo, lo mío es crear propuestas con mucho color y dinamismo.

Me inspiro 100% en la naturaleza y eso me hace sentir responsable con mi impacto ambiental, por eso todo lo que hago y enseño son técnicas sostenibles, libres de espuma floral y basadas en mecánicas reusables y desechos compostables.

teachers.aboutMe:
¡Hola! Soy Marta y desde muy pequeña me paso el dia inventando.

Mi pasión son las lanas, los algodones, los hilos, los botones, las telas, las cintas y en definitiva ¡todo lo que se venda en una mercería!. Doy rienda suelta a mi creatividad en mi página y tienda de patrones online , donde desde hace más de 12 años, enseño paso a paso cómo tejer y confeccionar ropa y complementos.

La ropa de bebé es mi debilidad por muchas razones, obtienes resultados muy pronto y con muy poco material, además una prenda hecha a mano ¡siempre es el regalo perfecto!. Las prendas de niños y bebés son la base de una prenda de mayor envergadura ya que todo empieza con una version mini ❤️.

Soy Psicologa de formación y Marketiniana de profesion. Desde el nacimeinto de Creativa Atelier, compaginé mi trabajo en marketing con el compartir mis conocimeintos de knitting, crochet y costura en mi blog, hasta que en 2016, decidí decicarme en exclusiva a lo que me hacia más feliz: enseñar a tejer y demostrar que todo es mas fácil de lo que parece y que podemos hacerlo con nuestras propias manitas 🙌🏻.

Estoy orgullosa de haber colaborado con las marcas de hilaturas más prestigiosas y reconocidas del sector: Katia Yarns and Fabrics, Anchor Crafts, We Are Knitters, DMC, Knitive. Y revistas y publicaciones como The Sewing Box Magazine, Labores del Hogar, Molly Makes, Fair Cotton Crochet y Ser Padres.

Soy tejedora en cuerpo y alma desde que aprendí, como a muchas, también me enseñó mi abuela mientras estudiaba Ingeniaria Técnica en diseño industrial. Cuando termié la carrera estaba deseando pasar mi vida tejiendo. Decidí entonces estudiar un master de un año en diseño de punto.

Desde 2005 trabajo como diseñadora y profesora de punto. Vivo entusiasmada entre estas dos facetas. Soy profesora de proyectos de punto industrial en la Universidad en la carrera de Diseño de moda en Barcelona desde 2015, asesora en la fabricación de punto industrial, diseñadora de prendas y colecciones de punto manual, así como profesora en cada taller ó rincón del mundo en el que aparece la posibilidad.

He diseñado cientos de prendas desde bebe hasta adulto. Y poco tiempo atrás, hace unos dos años, he empezado a comercializar mis nuevos diseños a través de ravlery y a comparitrlos en las redes sociales a través de ig.

Espero inspiraros y contagiaros mi amor el punto, el diseño y las prendas tejidas a mano.

Me encanta crear con las manos: bordar, dibujar, crochetear, pero sobre todo, tejer.  Me relaja, me permite desconectar, me hace soñar.  Los colores me llenan de energía y me ayudan a expresar mis emociones.  Enseñar y que otros aprendan conmigo me hace inmensamente feliz.  En estos últimos años, me he especializado en la técnica jacquard.  Espero que te guste mi trabajo.

Hola!!!, me presento Soy Joice, creadora de mi amada SiempreOveja.  Una apasionada por los colores, texturas y formas esféricas. Creo profundamente en el aprendizaje de forma autodidacta, donde cada uno crea sus formas, sin limites ni restricciones. 

Durante mi existencia he buscado el porque de las cosas, desde observar los arboles y sentir que eran nuestras almas, hasta que las estrellas se creaban porque había una gran luz afuera y era filtrada por un colador.

Para mi la imaginación, explorar y experimentar han sido mis cimientos. Aprendi desde el haciendo y descubrí que era la mejor manera para entender mis errores logrando encontrar así la forma para confeccionar lo que tenia en mi mente. nunca creí en las reglas especificas para hacer algo, al final todo esta bien, solo hay que ajustarlo a lo que quieres, sin embargo, las técnicas básicas nos van ayudar entender las formas y desde ahi podemos jugar y trasformar. Aprendi a tejer a los 7 años con palillos de sushi, así que realmente creo que podemos crear a partir de lo que tengamos en casa.

Me gusta contar historias y eso es lo que hago con todas mis creaciones, primero parti con mis gordos quienes tenían nombre, fecha de nacimiento, personalidad y una historia. Para luego llegar a los chalecos y crear así mi primera colección llamada armadura. La confección de chalecos llego de forma instintiva como un salvavidas, fueron mis herramientas, mis abrazos,  mi contención. Con ellos aprendi a entender mis emociones y como ir guiando mi sentir, deje que simplemente cada forma se fuera dando de manera natural sin resistencia, casi como un grito de mi alma aclamando escucha. Este conocimiento y experimentación me ayudo a entender mis procesos y como ir plasmo todo esto en mis prendas de punto. Esto es lo que quiero compartir contigo, te animas?

¡Hola mi nombre es Josefina Vergara!, pero más conocida como Pope.
Mi mamá es diseñadora de moda, por lo que nací entre telas e hilados, transformándome en una apasionada por la moda y siempre bocetando ideas desde los 10 años, aunque le puse fin cuando entre a estudiar diseño digital, sin saber que más adelante me reencontraría con la moda, pero de otra manera.
Mi historia con las agujas comenzó cuando me quede embarazada de mi primera hija, donde tuve que reposar durante 3 meses en cama, por lo que me dedique aprender a tejer. Cuando ya tenía el tejido dominado empecé hacer mis propios diseños, siempre trabajando con diferentes texturas, materiales, técnicas sin tener miedo de probar cosas nuevas y de no seguir las reglas.
El año 2020 saqué mi primer patrón llamado Scrap Cardigan, donde tuvo una aceptación tan grande que me llamaron para escribir un patrón en la revista "EL ARTE DE TEJER". Seguí tejiendo, creando sin parar y saqué muchos patrones nuevos. El año 2021 decidí postular para la revista POMPOM mag, donde hice un patrón llamado LEONORA CARDIGAN, donde era realmente una pintura en un chaleco. Posteriormente me llamaron de University Club, para que hiciera mi primera colección de chalecos.
Hoy en día estoy trabajando proyectos para diferentes editoriales de distintas partes del mundo, y escribiendo mis patrones donde los vendo por Ravelry.

Hi, I am Pope vergara, a Chilean knitwear designer; I have two kids and a husband I love so much. He pushes me to work on my passion which is designing clothing.

My mom is a fashion designer, so I was born among fabrics and yarns. Fashion was 
always my passion.

When I got pregnant with my first child, I had to be on bed rest. At that time, I started knitting, but what caught my attention the most was designing and creating my clothes. I constantly tested materials and new techniques, innovating and challenging the unusual.

I have a unique style because I always like mixing different fibers, materials, and trends with my stamp, from rocker to more feminine ones. I want to make people feel good and shine with my designs. Nature, the human body, music, science, biology, and artwork inspire me. 
I hope you love my designs, and if you have any questions or comments, tell me!!
