teachers.aboutMe:
Hola, soy Estefa González y soy diseñadora de crochet y la creadora de la marca Santa Pazienzia. 

Santa Pazienzia es una web dedicada a enseñar a tejer a crochet. En ella publico mis patrones, mis cursos, escribo el blog y tengo también mi tienda online de productos para tejedores y tejedoras. 

Comencé a tejer en el año 2014 y desde entonces no he podido parar. Soy autodidacta y aprendí los primeros puntos buscando vídeos por internet. 

Los accesorios fueron los proyectos que me dieron a conocer, sobretodo bolsos y Clutchs con un estilo moderno.

Al principio, el blog y el redactar patrones era un simple hobby y fue evolucionado de forma muy natural hasta lo que es hoy. Una empresa dedicada al crochet con alumnos en más de 50 países. 

Mi primer ebook lo saqué al año de tener el blog y se llama “Trapillo para principiantes”. Hasta 2020 he publicado 9 ebooks, 4 cursos online y más de un centenar de patrones además de haber hecho colaboraciones para grandes marcas como Katia, Casasol o We are knitters.
He participado en dos libros publicados por la editorial The Sewing Box y he aparecido en las principales revistas del sector Handmade como The Sewing Box, Labores del hogar, Bebé moderno,  Manos Maravillosas, Bellota-Yedra, siendo portada de algunas de ellas. 

Una vez que me di a conocer de modo online, me lancé a dar talleres presenciales en diferentes ciudades y países. Sólo en el año 2018 impartí más de 40 workshops en ciudades diferentes como Barcelona, Madrid, Sevilla, Valencia. Esta es una de las partes de mi trabajo que más me gusta ya que me permite conocer gente maravillosa que comparte esta afición. El crochet engancha porque más allá del tejido se crea COMUNIDAD. 

El siguiente paso en mi carrera fue abrir mi tienda de productos para tejer y lo último que he hecho ha sido crear mi propia línea de accesorios SP para tejedoras y tejedores.

Me presento! Soy Alicia y cuando tejo flipan las abuelas. Crochetera insaciable y madre de #ConiDarko, un conejo con mucha personalidad. Soy una persona que cree en el aprendizaje a lo largo de la vida y el constructivismo. De ahí que siempre tenga ganas de aprender nuevas técnicas que más tarde extrapolo a mi trabajo como maestra infantil. 
Soy una apasionada de las tendencias LifeStyle y mi perdición es diseñar todo tipo de productos en crochet. Me encanta pasarme el día creando y dejarme sorprender por lo que mis manos pueden llegar a hacer. Mis diseños tienen un estilo muy fresco, inspirados en la simpleza del movimiento nórdico. Aunque, últimamente lo que más está fascinando al mundo crochetero es que me gusta crear piezas inspiradas en las texturas que se consiguen con las dos agujas y por mucho que no te lo creas yo te aseguro que todo lo que hago  #EsCrochet

En la actualidad trabajo como directora de una preciosa Escuela Infantil en la serranía de Huelva. Un paraje precioso dónde perderse y comprobar que aprender es jugar y jugar es aprender. Me hace muy feliz compaginar mi amada profesión con mi segunda pasión, el crochet. Desde la tranquilidad de mi casa y al compás de bellas canciones o acompañada de series que me enamoren, creo unos patrones de infarto que podrás encontrar en mi tienda o en forma de colaboración con las marcas más importantes del sector.

Amo las casas de playa, más que las playas. Me pirra aprender una y mil cosas. Las matemáticas siempre han sido mi devoción. Y desde que tengo en mi vida a #ConiDarko, mi fiel compañero de orejas grandes, soy más feliz que una perdiz. Tiene un shutato precioso llamado #LucasElRegalito o #Lanksy para los followers.

¡Ahhhhh! Soy una yarnbomber de mucho cuidado. A veces, te cuento mis peripecias en instagram. Pero otras veces me guardo mis aventuras para mí y el sombrerero loco. 

Todo esto y mucho más suelo contártelo en @alimaravillas o en el blog de mi web  ¿Te apuntas a pasarlo bien y disfrutar de los pequeños detalles?

Soy Estefanía, más conocida en redes sociales como Alelí. Soy diseñadora y profesora de crochet. Desde pequeña y en la actualidad me la he pasado haciendo manualidades; me encanta pintar con acuarelas, reciclar muebles, bordar y tejer. Siempre estuve muy involucrada en el mundo del DIY e imaginando una vida creativa que estuviera relacionada con crear con mis manos. 

En lo personal soy muy romántica, fanática del estilo vintage, las flores y los colores pasteles. En mis diseños vas a ver una fusión el romanticismo y lo vintage que te va a enloquecer! Pero a la vez cada diseño sigue las tendencias de moda, eso los hace únicos y muy modernos. Me encanta crear diseños con texturas llamativas, únicas y originales, texturas que se logran a partir de puntas sencillas.

Estudie Profesora de Nivel Inicial, durante algunos años trabaje en jardines de infantes y escuelas rurales, en mis tiempos libres tejía como hobby , como descubrimiento total de la técnica de crochet, aprendí de manera autodidacta y por curiosidad. Un día empecé a tejer y vender lo que tejía. Después de un tiempo me di cuenta de que lo que a mi me gustaba era enseñar todo lo que sabia sobre crear con una aguja y un ovillos. Comencé a dar clases de crochet en mi taller. 

Mi taller, mi lugar de trabajo donde paso muchas horas creando y dónde sucede la magia de Alelí, era el garaje de la casa de mis papás, yo lo transformé en mi estudio, aún es mi lugar de trabajo cada día, en él me inspiro y pongo a tope mi creatividad.

Despertar la creatividad e inspiración a personas de cualquier parte del mundo es mi aspiración y mi gran objetivo! Por eso en mis redes sociales además de encontrar tejido e hilados, me encanta compartir mis momentos de trabajo, mi música, el día a día de mi vida como emprendedora, pintar con acuarelas, mis series preferidas y recetas que preparo en la comodidad de mi casa.

Comparto gran parte de mi vida como tejedora-emprendedora en @aleli.decocrochet y en mi blog
Te espero para descubrir juntos el mundo mágico de crear a crochet.

¡Hola! Mi nombre es Laura , y soy la persona que está detrás de Susimiu.
Mi historia con el ganchillo comenzó hace ya algunos años.
Durante toda mi vida mi casa ha estado llena de mantas hechas por mi abuela, de todas las formas, tamaños y colores. Siempre me han encantado, así que un día como otro cualquiera me propuse aprender a hacerlas yo misma( cosa que por aquel entonces me parecía imposible)
Así, poco a poco, con la ayuda de Google ,y haciendo y deshaciendo cientos de veces, fui aprendiendo todos los puntos y trucos. Fue todo un aprendizaje.
Pocos meses más tarde, ya tenía acabada mi primera manta, y yo, muy orgullosa de ella, quise compartirla en un blog con el resto del mundo, con todos los patrones necesarios para hacerla.
Y así, y de esta forma tan sencilla, fue como empecé en esta maravillosa aventura.
Podéis ver todos mis trabajos en mi web , Susimiu, diseñada y elaborada por mi misma; donde comencé enseñando recetas de dulces , para terminar especializándome en el gran mundo del ganchillo.
Espero que os guste lo que hago, pero sobre todo, que lo disfrutéis tanto como disfruto yo haciéndolo.
¡Gracias por estar aquí!

Hola! Soy Maria Jesus Labbe, creadora de Relmu Tejidos, Soy Amante de los colores, los textiles y de crear  con ellos lo que me salga del corazón .. Todo comenzó con mi amor por los viajes y las culturas, el destino me hizo viajar desde muy joven y me quedo grabado en el cuerpo. Estudie diseño textil lo cual me hizo profundizar en el amor por los colores y los tejidos,  fueron mi herramienta de autonomía para ahorrar y poder viajar durante mis estudios con amigas a distintas partes de America latina como mochilera y recolectora de tesoros. Me enamore de la libertad que me generaba el poder viajar y al mismo tiempo trabajar, comencé a admirar mucho ese estilo de vida..Fue en un viaje al sur de chile en una feria local que me encontré con un puesto de lanas naturales muy coloridas y algo en mi corazón exploto! había encontrado un tesoro que no iba a soltar... Decidí formalizar mi hobbie y crear RELMU quise enfocarme en la producción responsable siguiendo el recorrido desde a oveja al chaleco, y así mantener la producción a baja escala.. Con mi primer y ultimo amor me toco continuar con los viajes y mientras mis compañeras se decidieron por trabajar en empresas a mi me ahogaba la idea de estar frente a un computador diseñando cosas que me pedían otros, por lo tanto  entre romance y aventura me lance con el tejido como aliado, empece a hacer a pedido lo  que luego se volvió en un trabajo sin parar de tejer y tejer donde fuera que estaba... Mi técnica era el crochet y algunas piezas a palillo pero mi fuerte siempre fue el crochet... Tenia lista de pedidos y así me pasaba día tras día, hasta que me quede embarazada y decidí buscar ayuda, comencé con 4 tejedoras de una fundación local, luego fueron 10... Se abrió un nuevo mundo para mi, ya no estaba tejiendo todo yo, estaba delegando el tejido lo cual me llevo a poder crear mas volumen,hacer diseños mas innovadores, y dedicarme a los detalles de mi marca. Fue un gran salto para mi ya que juntando el talento de distintas tejedoras mas mi creatividad e ideas pudimos lograr diseños únicos con una historia hermosa detrás de cada uno... Ha sido un proyecto personal de un sueño que ha ido creciendo y transformando. He visto lo que  significa para las tejedoras este trabajo. Pasar de ser dueñas de hogar, algunas jubiladas, y que ahora pueden generar ingresos de sus hogares y tener independencia, las a hecho soñar y manifestar ideas nuevas. 
En la pandemia todo cambio, los pedidos eran muchos, decidí no tomar mas pedidos y solo crear y vender a travez de las redes sociales, lo cual cambio el ritmo nos dio tiempo para armar colecciones, para proyectarnos como marca, enfocarnos en nuestros valores de Slow Fashion , de moda consciente,   armamos nuestra pagina web y terminar vendiendo a travez de ella... Esto genero un nuevo mundo para Relmu nos abrimos a muchas posibilidades y cada vez armamos una red mas bonita de mujeres y personas rescatando el bello oficio de el tejido y del diseño..

Animation is definetely my passion and with hard work and lot of studying I turned my dream in my job. For last 6 years I worked on several animation features/TV shows for Dreamworks TV, Double Negative, Magic Hill Animation. And now I work as a full-time freelancer in Netflix Animation.

Hello! My name is Sammy Khalid but I am mostly known on the internet as 'Chigg'. I am an award-winning Concept designer, illustrator, and digital artist from Dublin, Ireland.  I primarily work in the entertainment industry, specifically film/TV and animation where I design characters, sets, vehicles, and props. In addition to this, I create artwork for different brands, games, publications and personal art.

I studied traditional and 3D animation at BCFE, Ireland, earning a BA in Animation from the University of Dundee. This foundational education has led to a broad 2D and 3D skillset tempered by a keen knowledge of traditional art techniques. I have been trained
in, and have proficiency in the fundamentals of design, figure drawing, colour theory, perspective, lighting, anatomy and
composition.

Throughout my career, I’ve worked on amazing projects like Black Mirror, His Dark Materials, League of Legends and Aquaman 2 with clients such as Disney, Netflix, Marvel Studios and Warner Bros. Working in design and illustration have been my life’s passion and I am thankful every day for the chance to do what I love and share my skills with the next generation.

I am an Art director, concept artist and a matte painter in the film & games industry, specializing in conceptual and visual development of environments, creatures and FX. 

Throughout my career, I had the privilege of working on Films and series projects such as Ad Astra, American Gods, The Boys, The Alienist, Vikings, Cowboy Bebop and many more. Among some of the companies i have worked for are Mr.X, HASBRO, Wizards of the Coast, and I currently work as an Art Director at Pixomondo.

I like to play. That is the best reason I know for drawing anything at all; to play. I've been quite serious about it since I was shouting at the other kids for not playing properly as we ran around in kindergarten, and nothing much has changed since then, except the tools have become fancier and the rules have become a lot more intricate.

I play by making worlds, and stories, and characters and things, and my toys are pens and stylus, procreate and imagination. My game consists of weaving worlds that work, like our own, but different, and letting the characters and creatures make magic by bringing the world to life, making little stories of their own. It is the most fun I know how to have, and I would love to share it if you want to play along.

I am a concept artist and illustrator with 12+ years experience in the entertainment and TTRGP industry. But what I really love doing is solving problems, specifically those about worldbuilding and architecture. As such I've worked for big studios, from AAA gaming to Bollywood film and a bunch of stuff in between, such as one of my all time favorites: Dungeons & Dragons!
It's a long way of saying I come up with, and paint, buildings for all sorts of projects. Besides that I love teaching art, playing video games, relaxing in my nook when it rains, walking my dog when it's dry and tasting the many different chocolates this world has to offer.

teachers.aboutMe:
¡Hola! Soy Verónica de Arriba, ilustradora y diseñadora y creadora de la marca Depeapa.

Mi trabajo se desarrolla alrededor de mis ilustraciones y las aplico a todo tipo de objetos. Creé Depeapa en 2008 y he diseñado durante estos años numerosas colecciones de productos ilustrados que vendo en tiendas de todo el mundo y en mi propia tienda online.

He creado tanto artículos de decoración como láminas, bandejas, cojines, móviles, tea towels y accesorios como tote bags, mochilas, camisetas, sudaderas, broches o collares. Dando rienda suelta a la imaginación y aprendiendo diferentes técnicas y medios.

Mis diseños han aparecido en revistas como Harper’s Baazar, Elle Decor, Frankie magazine, Boston Globe, Milk magazine, House and Garden, Kireei, Flow magazine, Mollie makes, Yen o Viva y se ha publicado en libros como "Freestyle – Ilustrando la moda urbana", "Koala", "Pequeña empresa creativa" y "The New Artisans".

En 2011 unos años después de crear Depeapa abrí mi tienda en Etsy y fue uno de los grandes aciertos de mi trayectoria porque me ha permitido dar a conocer más mi trabajo y que mis productos lleguen a clientes de todo el mundo, desde Japón a EE. UU.

En 2017 Etsy me eligió mentora de su campaña Etsy Resolution España, un curso online en el que asesoré sobre fotografía de producto a pequeñas marcas que querían abrir su propia tienda en Etsy.

Me gusta mucho el diseño, la ilustración y la artesanía. Siempre trabajo con proveedores cercanos porque creo que saber dónde, cómo y quién fabrica un producto es muy importante. Intento cuidar cada pequeño detalle y ofrecer una marcada diferencia con respecto a los artículos producidos en masa.

Ayudando a negocios digitales desde 2006. 
Soy orgulloso cofundador de Marketing Paradise, agencia digital especializada en diseñar estrategias para Ecommerce.
Trabajo como consultor de marketing digital para tiendas online de todo tipo de tamaños y sectores. 

Me dedico a conseguir que mis clientes consigan negocios rentables, escalables y sostenibles, diseñando planes ambiciosos de adquisición, conversión y retención de cliente.
Cuento con amplia experiencia en canales como posicionamiento SEO, gestor de campañas CPC o planes de contenido para marcas con alta presencia digital.

¡Hola! Soy Alisa, artista y diseñadora. Nací en Ucrania, ahora vivo en España y es aquí donde hace 6 años empecé mi aventura creativa.

Soy autodidacta, me encanta probar y experimentar con diferentes medios y texturas para crear ilustraciones, estampados y collages. Encuentro mucha fuente de inspiración en la naturaleza, viajes, diseño de interiores, arquitectura y simplemente en los pequeños detalles de la vida cotidiana.

Distribuyo mis diseños a través de la venta online y licencias. Ahora mis ilustraciones se pueden encontrar en Urban Outfitters, H&M, World Market, Fy! y Minted. También se venden varios artículos para el hogar con mis estampados en Target, Wayfair y Society6.

Soy especialista en Comercio Electrónico, egresada de la Esden Business School, Madrid, con un Máster en Dirección de Marketing Digital e eBusiness, cuento con 15 años de experiencia ayudando a startups y empresas internacionales a tener éxito en canales digitales. Soy una de las pioneras del comercio electrónico en México, lancé mi primera tienda online en el año 2010. Experta en la creación, desarrollo, implementación y evolución de negocios digitales generadores de ROI. He colaborado para marcas internacionales como BBVA Bancomer, Grupo Diltex, The Coca Cola Company, entre otras.
 
Cuento con estudios certificados por empresas de nivel internacional como Adobe (Diplomado de certificación como Web Developer Adobe), Google (Google Advertising Expert, Search Engine Marketing) IAB (Diplomado de Marketing Interactivo) y Universidad Iberoamericana (Diplomado de Diseño de Sitios Web). 

Soy además fundadora de ECAB (ECommerce Advisors Bureau) consultoría de comercio electrónico, desde 2016. Para mí, una de las mejores maneras de empujar la economía digital del país es compartir conocimientos. Imparto cursos y talleres especializados en Comercio Electrónico con el fin de empoderar empresas y nuevos negocios a migrar a la transformación digital.
 
Actualmente soy además, creadora y coordinadora del diplomado de Comercio Electrónico y Negocios Digitales de la Universidad Iberoamericana campus Ciudad de México y en la Universidad del Valle de México

Soy Ingeniero Informático, trabajo que ejercí durante un par de años en una de las empresas de telecomunicaciones más grandes del mundo. Posteriormente decidí que quería probar suerte y, a los 25 años, fundé junto a otros dos socios Lanzanos, la primera plataforma de Crowdfunding española. Esta empresa la vendimos en 2012. 

A continuación, junto a mis dos socios, fundé Acumbamail, una plataforma de email marketing orientada a pequeñas y medianas empresas, líder en su segmento en España y con presencia en varios países de Latinoamérica. Enviamos los emails de más de 3500 empresas, con un volumen mensual de más de 300 millones de correos.

Llevo más de 6 años dedicado al marketing digital, especialmente con un fuerte enfoque a resultados (venta, generación de leads, consecución de objetivos, etc.). Actualmente trabajo en Accenture Interactive como Digital Marketing Consultant en Madrid. Estoy especializado en proyectos de CRO (conversion rate optimization) y he trabajado en prácticamente todas las industrias en varios países llevando a cabo la planificación y ejecución de experimentos de optimización como test A/B, personalizaciones, estrategia de landing pages para canales de paid media, etc. 

Me encanta la analítica web y todo lo relacionado con datos. En mi día a día los uso para reconocer posibles puntos de fricción en la experiencia de cliente, y para poder plantear en base a ellos todas las hipótesis que testamos en CRO. He trabajado con muchas herramientas del mercado como Adobe Target, Adobe Anlytics, Google Optimize, Google Analytics, Optimizely, Oracle Maxymiser, AB Tasty, etc.

Hola!
Somos Héctor y Gerardo, fundadores de Algoritmo Consultores , ambos con experiencia laboral en empresas como Amazon y Mercado Libre liderando unidades de negocio para desarrollar clientes al siguiente nivel. Algoritmo es una empresa enfocada 100% en ayudar a desarrollar marcas en el ámbito digital , como : ventas en marketplaces ( Mx y US ), desarrollo de sitios web, manejo de redes sociales, estrategias de trafico ( marketing ) y desarrollo de producto. Hemos trabajado con clientes de practicamente todas las categorías como son: Decoración, Deportes, Vitaminas y Suplementos, Cocina, Ropa y Accesorios, Juguetes y Bebés, entre otras. Una de nuestras virtudes es poder crear programas a la medida de todos nuestros clientes, para poder entregar resultados en el corto plazo.

Mascha Davis MPH, RDN is a nationally recognized registered dietitian nutritionist, humanitarian and founder of Nomadista Nutrition, a private nutrition practice based in Los Angeles. Her writing and expertise have been featured in numerous publications and media outlets including TIME, CNN, Newsweek, the Washington Post, ABC news, Men’s Health Magazine, Women’s Health, Mind Body Green, Bustle, Refinery29, PopSugar Fitness, Reader’s Digest, and many more.

In her private practice, she uses an evidence-based approach and Nutrigenomics to help her clients optimize their health, manage chronic conditions and achieve a healthy weight. In addition, Davis provides nutrition consulting services to start-ups and corporations.

Before launching her private practice, she spent five years working on programs for the treatment and prevention of malnutrition in women and children in Africa, which she discusses in her TEDx talk.

Her nutrition tips, health advice and recipes can be found on her Instagram account @nomadista_nutrition and her blog on nomadistanutrition.com. Her book with publisher Simon & Schuster, Eat Your Vitamins, is available online and in bookstores nationwide.

Hello! We are Arabela and Elle, the women behind Weekend Creative. We are a photographer and art director team based in the San Francisco Bay Area. We specialize in creative brand photography and stop motion with a focus on unique and playful concepts. In addition to photography, we have well-rounded backgrounds in advertising, graphic design, art direction, and media which helps us to approach our projects with a unique perspective. 

We believe that strong images are essential to capturing an audience and building a strong relationship with your customers. From sunglasses, to packaging, to beverages, we work with clients from every industry and we don’t shy away from a good challenge. We love working with companies who know how to have fun, and trust us to elevate their brand to the next level. 

Is it the weekend yet?

FOR BEHIND THE SCENES FOLLOW MY INSTAGRAM @TIBOR_GALAMB

Tibor Galamb is an advertising photographer and director based in Budapest, Hungary, working with clients across the European Union and worldwide. He specializes in creative advertising photography, bringing a bold and distinctive visual style to every project. With a strong focus on storytelling and brand identity, Tibor is available for commissioned work globally.

Originally trained in civil engineering at the Budapest University of Technology, Tibor later pursued his passion for photography, earning a Bachelor’s degree in Professional Photography from Edinburgh College in 2013. His background in engineering continues to shape his creative process, he approaches each composition with an eye for geometry, structure, and light, transforming technical precision into striking visual narratives.

His portfolio reflects not only technical excellence but also a creative curiosity that pushes him to experiment with new perspectives and visual solutions, making his work stand out in the world of commercial photography.

Over the years, Tibor has collaborated with a wide range of international brands, including Meta, Volkswagen, Waterman Paris, Lidl, Redbull, Adidas, Pepsi, Jägermaister, Camper, Dr Oerker, Reebok, Swedbank, Saudi Telecommunication Company, Ergo, MobilFox, Al Marai, Mondelez

Gabriela is a Brazilian born, Scottish based photographer. She works across editorial, lifestyle and still life photography, working primarily with independent companies and makers to create striking and effective content that elevate brand and business.
Through her personal bodies of work, flowers and flesh are used as symbolic starting points to explore ideas and ideals of love, sex, beauty and death.

Still Life Photographer and Director Amy Currell was born in East London, where she lives and works. Her photography and moving image is shot through a distinctively female lens, and each frame is composed with thoughtfulness and grace – artfully juxtaposing colour, texture, and shape. 

Amy’s lighting draws narratives from shadow and finds warmth in her subjects. Amy is also currently experimenting with blending CGI techniques with traditional stills photography for a perfected reality. 

Expanding in her role as a Director, Amy works with the newest motion control cameras to give any moving image elements of the work an edge, giving the same poise and polish to her film that you’ll find in her photography. 

Amy is highly sought after in the commercial world by global clients who value beauty, and the context of their products in carefully choreographed composition, and these have included - Ikea, British Vogue, Selfridges, Liberty London, Tatler, Bvlgari, Van Cleef & Arpels and London Art Fair.

Hi, I'm Lizzie! I'm a creative director, photographer, prop-maker, and major pun enthusiast. I work with a wide variety of brands from beauty to ice cream to create playful, eye-catching content that lives on their social media and beyond. Vivid colors, bold patterns, and overall maximalism are cornerstones of my creations and I love to craft elaborate scenes with miniatures, varying textures, and props that I hand-make.

teachers.aboutMe:
Julieta Álvarez es una firma que este 2021 celebra su noveno aniversario. Siempre con la cerámica como protagonista, sus creaciones pasan de la joyería a la decoración, pasando también por el mundo del arte y la escultura.

La firma ha cosechado grandes éxitos desde sus comienzos, entre los que cabe destacar su llegada a más de 20 países de los cinco continentes. Forma parte de las propuestas de museos destacados como el Pompidou de París, el Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Luxemburgo o el Reina Sofía en Madrid, entre muchos otros.

Después de varias colaboraciones con grandes firmas de moda del panorama nacional e internacional, es bueno mencionar la última. Siendo Julieta Álvarez la diseñadora de las últimas colecciones de joyería de Lladró, sin duda una de las casas de cerámica más consagradas en todo el mundo.  

Sus diseños han desfilado en pasarelas de moda acompañando las colecciones de Ángel Schlesser o Ión Fiz entre otros, se han expuesto en muestras y exposiciones y están en manos de actrices e influencers.

Hola soy Maria Romero Laspiur, y soy la creadora de MRLASPIUR. Mi pasión por el arte, la moda y el diseño me llevó a estudiar Bellas Artes y después enfocar mi carrera en el diseño de textil y de moda. En el año 2017, creé mi proyecto en el diseño de joyas mediante impresión en 3D, junto al entonces también fundador del proyecto Jaime Arteche Limousin en Madrid. Dos años después, nos mudamos a San Sebastián (España), donde consolidé mi proyecto en solitario e inauguré mi propio estudio-tienda. 

Creo cada pieza con gran cuidado en los detalles y mezclando procesos artesanales con tecnológicos. También le doy mucha importancia a la sostenibilidad, buscando e investigando en materias primas ecológicas y de cercanía.
Mi inspiración parte del mundo pictórico, de la cultura textil y de la naturaleza que me rodea. Trato de que todas las colecciones tengan como punto de partida un imaginario vegetal de formas orgánicas y vivos colores, que creo yo misma desde mis ilustraciones y pinceladas.

El material base de los diseños, es el PLA, un polímero vegetal que se produce a partir del almidón de la yuca y del maíz. Materia prima que es muy ligera, resistente y además biodegradable!
Nuestras joyas han sido publicadas en revistas como Vogue España, Vanidad, Neo 2, Telva entre otras.

Me llamo Mercedes, nací en Bogotá.

Desde siempre me ha gustado la capacidad que tienen los humanos de transformar los materiales para materializar sus ideas.

Me gustan las flores, el arcoíris, los pájaros, el mar y las montañas, amo cocinar para mi familia y lo que más me gusta hacer en la vida es inspirar a la gente contando las historias de los objetos que diseño.  

Estudie joyería en Mexico en la escuela de artesanías en el Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes, cree mi marca de joyería y accesorios hace 20 años. Hoy nuestra empresa tiene un equipo de cincuenta personas y le da trabajo a más de 200 artesanos alrededor de Colombia. Me gusta soñar, trabajar y viajar.

Hola somos Laura y Ana, hermanas creadoras de la marca VATTEA, nuestra pasión por la artesania y el diseño nos llevo a estudiar nuestras carreras,  producción de joyería y diseño industrial respectivamente. En el año 2016 consolidamos nuestra marca de joyas en la ciudad de Medellín (Colombia).

Creamos cada pieza con gran cuidado en los detalles y procesos manuales, el trabajo con los hilos cocidos a mano y almidonados es el resultado de un proceso de investigación con féculas naturales. La exploración de materiales es parte del proceso creativo en nuestro taller, nos encanta descubrir todo lo que se puede lograr inteviniendolos... cortar, soldar, enrollar... ¡infinidad de posibilidades!

Nos inspiramos en diversas culturas ancestrales y sus representaciones a través de objetos y símbolos, tomamos los colores como referentes del folclor colombiano evocando la calidez y fuerza de las mujeres latinas.
 
El material base de VATTEA es el bronce. A cada pieza le damos una textura o pulido para dar este efecto de rusticidad que se ve en nuestras joyas, posteriormente cada pieza es bañada en oro de 24 quilates. El hilo de algodón es otro de los materiales que caracteriza a la marca, este pasa por procesos como la costura a mano y luego un almidonado con féculas naturales. El resultado son piezas con gran valor artesanal.

Nuestras joyas han sido publicadas en revistas como Vogue Latinoamerica, Caras Colombia, Carrusel, Aló entre otras.

Hola! Soy Malena, la persona detrás de la marca Pimienta Joyería. Mi interés y experimentación en distintos oficios me llevó a aprender joyería donde encontré un espacio cómodo para trabajar tanto con el metal como con otros materiales y técnicas, como el hilo, la tela y el bordado, donde siempre puedo jugar y dejar correr la imaginación.

Soy Docente de Artes Visuales con orientación en Escenografía, carrera de la Universidad de La Plata, en donde trabajé en muchas disciplinas que trato de combinar con lo que voy aprendiendo en distintos talleres particulares y algunos saberes conseguidos de forma autodidacta. Es así que dentro de Pimienta hago piezas con cuidado y atención en  los detalles, inspiradas en elementos hogareños, como las plantas de mi patio, recuerdos de la infancia y las mascotas que me acompañan, mezclando técnicas clásicas de la joyería con otras de distintos oficios.

teachers.aboutMe:
I am an artist, designer, writer and illustrator. I studied fashion design with printing at Central Saint Martin's College of Art and Design in London. After that, I got my Masters in Fine Arts from Goldsmiths University in Design Futures. Since then, I have worked as a fashion designer, have published several books and have participated in collective and solo exhibitions. 
I teach creative workshops to children, teachers and illustrators at my moveable school L'École de Papier. At the school, I research and reproduce many ancient narrative formats such as shadow theatres, theatre books, leperellos and story boxes.
Though my work varies from one project to another, what fascinates me is storytelling. This fascinations transmits itself in my illustrated books,  my window displays and my paper cuttings. 
I have collaborated as an illustrator in the french magazine Marketing and was invited among 3 other female artist to collaborate in a special edition of Le Chocolat des Français x Instagram (2018) which was launched to celebrate International Women's Day. 
My illustrated works include the anthology Los artistas del hambre. Narraciones de la bohemia madrileña (2011); Raconte-Moi Chqara et la musique andalouse (2011), by Mohamed Benlamlih; the 2013 of Leyendas del Rin, written by Victor Hugo; and Este cuerpo es humano · This Body is Human (2015), written by Grassa Toro and translated to English by Claudio Cambon. I am the author of the theatre book To Night and Back · Mece la noche (2015) and the artist book Songs of the jungle (2019), inspired by scenes from The Jungle Book by Rudyard Kipling.

I love making things and I love using my hands. I always have, and no doubt I always will. My fidgeting fingers just can't stop. I am a happy maker who's happy making.

Born and raised in London, UK.  Working and living as a craft artist and maker in Madrid, Spain since 2001.
After studying a Foundation course at Central Saint Martin's College of Art & Design in London, I went on to study a degree in Ceramics at UWE in Bristol. It was there where I discovered my passion for texture and form, taking inspiration from nature and flora to develop sculptural pieces in porcelain paper-clay and with wicker.

Since then, my fascination with vegetation and plants mixed with my curiosity for experimenting with different materials has led me to create botanical art in paper, wicker and wire.
I want to bring the freshness and life of the outdoors inside!

Hi! I’m Sarah Louise Matthews and I’m a freelance paper engineer, paper cut designer and published author based in Yorkshire, England. I work with a variety of brands and clients to design and create diverse, bespoke layered papercuts and 3D paper sculptures for a broad range of commissions - from small, detailed paper sets and props to be used for styling product photography, to oversized, tactile papercrafted window displays, the scope of my work ranges hugely but I always keep paper craftsmanship and a sense of fun at the heart of what I do.

My playful paper pieces have been commissioned by brands including Bentley, Ted Baker, Clive Christian, Sipsmith and Olivia Burton, to name a few, and my work has adorned the windows of stores including Selfridges and Pandora on Oxford Street, London. On top of creating bespoke commissions for brands, I have also run papercraft workshops, written a book ‘Paper Craft Home’, published by Search Press, and contributed many papercraft projects to craft magazine Mollie Makes.

‘Paper Engineer’ would probably have been my dream job as a child, had I known of its existence, as I have vivid childhood memories of hours spent folding origami penguins and making handmade pop up books. I graduated from my Textile Surface Design Degree in 2011 with a range of folded paper jewellery and have been building on my skills through endless experimentation ever since. I am now a full time freelance Paper Engineer, spending my days buried under paper working on commissions in my studio in Yorkshire. You can keep an eye on my latest creations on my instagram @_sarah_matthews

I am a paper engineer, illustrator and author with twelve years of experience art directing and creating paper artwork for editorial and advertising clients. I also design and illustrate interactive and immersive books for children and adults, including the first pop-up book sent into space.

I graduated from Central Saint Martins in 2009 with a degree in Graphic Design. My studio was based in South London until 2021 when I relocated to Bristol (UK).

As a paper engineer, I have worked with clients that include Vanity Fair, Vogue, Fanta and TIME magazine. As an author and illustrator, I have published books with Laurence King and Michael O'Mara Books. I currently split my time between books, paper engineering, and teaching for MA Illustration (online) for Falmouth University.

We are Adrian & Gidi, a multidisciplinary creative studio specialised in the fields of crafts, photography, design and animation based in Amsterdam. We favour a playful and refined approach toward our work. 

One of our favourite material we work with is paper. It's so versatile, relatively cheap and it comes in many colours. It's just a magical process to see how a flat piece of paper can become anything you want. 

For the past ten years we have worked for clients all over the world. Every project is different and unique and that fact continues to challenge us in a positive way. We are grateful that our small paper worlds can have a large reach and hopefully leave a positive impression on the viewers.

Bio - LA native, and world premiere paper sculptor Jeff Nishinaka is able to shape, bend, and pinch the delicate material to craft hyper-detailed murals. Nishinaka’s 40 years of paper sculpting has led him to thousands of projects including Bloomingdales, Cartier, Johnnie Walker Blue Label, Penn State University, Paramount Pictures, HBO, and Moncler to only name a few. Nishinaka is able to focus on and execute very small details in a larger image, something seemingly impossible to craft with paper.

Mi nombre es Gonzalo Ibáñez, soy arquitecto (2017) con diplomado en Estética y Filosofía (2018). Enfoco mi producción artística en el trabajo de la acuarela y el paisaje. 

La dificultad y espontaneidad de esta técnica me cautivó totalmente, siendo hoy mi principal recurso de expresión. Dedico mi día a día a estudiar y conocer más de este mundo, intento siempre ampliar la frontera de mi técnica y trato, por medio de mi trabajo y enseñanza, comunicar a los demás esta enriquecedora pasión.

He participado en festivales y exposiciones colectivas a nivel internacional, como la bienal de Kosovo o el festival Fabriano Acquarello en Italia. Además, he recibido premios de primer lugar en concursos como el Mini Castra 2020 de Eslovenia y el concurso nacional IWS Chile Viña del Mar 2020. Actualmente imparto talleres de acuarela para distintas edades a nivel nacional e internacional.

I am a portrait artist based in the United Kingdom. I have taught workshops on portraiture, figure drawing and anatomy. 

I am known for my distinctive style of drawing, and enjoy creating dynamic portraits, with a focus on strong shadows and lighting. I believe learning the fundamentals of drawing and portraiture is important to unlock your creative potential and allow your individual style to come through.

Dibujo desde que tengo uso de razón y es una de las cosas que más disfruto hacer, es mi verdadera pasión y creo que todos deberíamos tener la oportunidad de hacerlo!

 Cada dibujo es una nueva experiencia, un desafío y una oportunidad. El dibujo es la forma de arte más sincera y la base más sólida para trabajar con cualquier otra técnica. Por eso creo que tan sólo con un lápiz y un papel se pueden hacer obras increíbles.

El dibujo nos enseña sobre la frustración, superación, la paciencia, ansiedad y también sobre el disfrute del hoy y del ahora. Esta obsesión por la línea me llevó a trabajar con gente como The Rock (Dwayne Johnson), Josh Brolin, PayPal, MercadoLibre, Canal 13, Marcelo Tinelli, entre muchos otros.

Pueden sumarse a mi Patreon, donde tienen más de 175 videos con tutoriales, procesos completos y donde también van a poder coordinar una reunión virtual conmigo para mostrarme su trabajo y yo poder ayudarlos en vivo!

Los invito a acompañarnos mutuamente en este increíble e infinito viaje lleno de líneas que es el dibujo!

Je m’appelle SIM SIM, et je suis actuellement artiste portraitiste spécialisé dans le dessin au fusain
Je suis d’origine vietnamienne et je vis actuellement à Montauban, au Sud de la France ! 

Je n’ai malheureusement pas eu la chance d’être né dans une famille issue du milieu artistique. Mes parents sont issus de l’immigration vietnamienne, de ce fait je n’ai pas eu d’opportunités financières et culturelles pour pouvoir accéder à des cours artistiques, faire des sorties culturelles..
J’ai donc appris en autodidacte, grâce aux bouquins, mais surtout grâce aux vidéos qui circulaient sur les réseaux sociaux, YouTube… Ensuite, j’ai eu l’opportunité d’intégrer une MANAA (mise à niveau en art appliqués) , c’est une formation d’une seule année où l'on n’apprend les bases du dessin, la couleur, le design,. On touche un peu à tout ! Ensuite j’ai réalisé une première année en 3D animation, une formation plus numérique (utilisation de logiciel 3D, de rendu, photoshop, cours de scénographie) mais au final celà ne m’a pas plu, et j’ai décidé d’arrêter cette formation et de me lancer en autodidacte !
J’ai commencé à prendre des cours en ligne sur différentes plateformes d’enseignement (schoolism, east oak studio, new masters academy) sur le dessin, l’anatomie, la peinture

J’étais vraiment mauvais élève à l’école, et le dessin est la seule chose que je maitrisais plus au moins ! C’était le dessin ou le néant ahah
Plus sérieusement, en apprenant le dessin, je suis tombé sur une chaîne YouTube d’un portraitiste (ThePortraitArt) qui réalise ses œuvres au fusain et je suis tombé amoureux de ce médium; le fait de retranscrire les émotions en dessinant des personnes. Je me suis alors imposé un objectif d’atteindre ce niveau en une année.

J’ai commencé à poster mon travail sur les réseaux sociaux. Au début sur Facebook, pour avoir la réaction de mes proches. 
J’ai ensuite élargi mon cercle et je me suis concentré sur Instagram : là-bas, on pouvait partager son travail avec un public totalement nouveau ! J’ai découvert de très nombreux artistes, j’ai alors commencé à interagir avec leurs communautés, et petit à petit, ma petite communauté s’est formée. 
Puis je suis arrivé sur Twitter, où j'ai intégré une petite communauté artistique. 
Les réseaux sociaux m’ont permis de me connecter avec d’incroyables personnes, que ce soit en France ou à l'international. Grâce à cette petite notoriété engendrée, j’ai commencé à avoir mes premiers clients, mes premières commandes ! 

Maintenant, j'ai la chance d’avoir des contacts avec des galeries pour des expositions, pour la vente d'œuvres  à des collectionneurs d’arts.  j'ai pu exposer à Paris, Madrid, et à la foire internationnale d'art contemporains de Vienne ! Je prépare ma nouvelle exposition qui devrait se dérouler au Japon prochainement.

Jono Dry is a self-taught artist from South Africa, born in 1989 in Pretoria and currently residing in Cape Town. Known for his large-scale graphite drawings, Dry blends hyperrealism with surrealism to create visually and emotionally engaging pieces.

Inspired by his efforts to make sense of his relationships, Dry works intuitively, often discovering deeper meanings and coincidences in his art years after their creation. His work serves as a form of therapy, profoundly influenced by his experiences with anxiety and loneliness. The meticulous technique and attention to detail in his drawings allow him to produce photorealistic images that often feature dark, empty backgrounds, isolating his subjects and highlighting their emotional depth.

Recurring motifs such as kudu horns, flowers and plants, hummingbirds, and bandages weave through his pieces, each symbolizing different facets of his journey. The kudu horns represent resilience and strength, flowers and plants signify growth and healing, hummingbirds evoke a sense of fleeting beauty and joy, and bandages hint at the ongoing process of emotional recovery. These elements intertwine, creating a visual narrative that reflects both the fragility and the resilience of the human spirit.

Jono has exhibited his work both locally and internationally, including shows at the Zeitz MOCAA in Cape Town, the Vienna Contemporary Art Fair, and the Di Carta Papermade exhibition in Italy. His dedication to his craft is evident in each piece, often taking months to complete, reflecting his commitment to perfection and intricate planning.
Dry also shares his creative process and techniques through social media and educational videos, fostering a community of artists and art enthusiasts who learn from and engage with his work. Through his art, Jono Dry aims to bridge the personal and the universal, connecting with audiences on a deeply emotional level and shedding light on the hidden aspects of the human experience.

teachers.aboutMe:
Soy Marta Grau, Estudié joyería y más tarde diseño de producto, especializándome en calzado. Trabajé durante años para una importante firma de calzado en la que tuve la oportunidad de aprender casi todo sobre el sector. Llegó un momento en el que no podía retener más el sueño de mi infancia, que comenzó cuando tomaba prestados los zapatos de mi tía Mode aquellos fines de semana que pasábamos en la casa de los abuelos. Corría y bailaba con sus zapatos de tacón. Me gustaba su ruido al andar, la elegancia que transmitían, lo mayor que me sentía. Era mágico… Deseaba diseñar y crear mis propios zapatos.

Decidí formarme en aquello que me faltaba para lanzarme a crear Lilday: aprender el oficio de zapatera. Lo hice de la mano de un maestro zapatero, un personaje muy auténtico al que le tengo mucho cariño. A día de hoy sigue siendo mi mentor!

Mi taller está en Aiguafreda, un pueblo en la montaña a unos 40 minutos en coche de Barcelona. Aquí diseño y fabrico cada par de zapatos siguiendo una filosofía slow. Creo en trabajar desde el corazón, porque así es como se dota de alma a las cosas que creamos. Utilizo pieles de curtición vegetal, libres de tóxicos que nos hacen daño a nosotras y al Planeta, y tintes vegetales como corteza de árbol (castaño, mimosa... todos ellos tiñen). Fabrico cada par bajo pedido, de esta forma no tengo excedente innecesario de material ni de stock. Por ejemplo, los zuecos están tallados en un bloque sólido de madera de pino: la madera sobrante la aprovechamos en casa para otros usos. Tardó aproximadamente 5 días en hacer cada par.

Suelo hacer colecciones pequeñas, pero el verano tiene algo que me hace diseñar sandalias sin parar. De hecho, este verano incorporé un nuevo modelo a mitad de temporada (las sandalias Marta). Es lo bueno que tiene no depender de los demás: ser capaz de crear mis propios prototipos, mis propias suelas, trabajar la piel... me permite una flexibilidad con la que jamás habría soñado.

Actualmente me he decantado por hacer pequeñas producciones y zapatos personalizados.

I'm a bright and bold knitwear designer who loves colour and who teams playful aesthetics with a love for craft and community! I launched my self named brand in 2014 and have since won Selfridges Bright New Things Award in 2016 and been stocked in luxury stores worldwide. My work now brings its designs out of the Luxury stores and into your homes by transforming the brand to Make- it-Yourself, transforming our designs into patterns and kits, championing craftmanship and Slow Fashion. My work has featured in Craft and Fashion Magazines as well as being displayed in the V&A's Fashioned from Nature exhibition and the Ferragamo Museums Sustainable Thinking Exhibition.  More than just creating beautiful garments, I love to creates playful experiences that encourage and champion social and environmental change. My passion is in running a wide range of workshops, events and classes that let you interact and engage with my love of textile crafts by recreating my designs in your own unique style!

Hello, My name is Lydia I am a seamstress and I only wear clothes I have made. I have not bought a single item of clothing from a shop in over six years! I called the project Made My Wardrobe. It started as personal journey to reconnect with my body and has turned into a full time business sharing my clothes making skills with anyone who wants to make their dream wardrobe. We now have a team of six who design patterns, kits and courses to make sewing accessible and creative. We have a beautiful sewing studio in Bristol, England. Do pop by to check out our fabrics if you are ever near by!

My mum taught me to sew when I was a little girl. When I finished school I started an apprenticeship to learn how to design and make garments. My background is in costume for theatre, dance and live performance. I am fortunate to have worked with some of the most prestigious theatres in the UK such as Sadler's Wells and The Royal Opera House. 

Some of my favourite projects have come from working with my closest friends and I am lucky enough to be surrounded by a community of makers who inspire me constantly. My favourite thing about sewing is that there is always more to learn.

See you at the sewing machine!

I'm Monisola Omotoso, Moni to my friends. In my 30+ years working in fashion design and pattern cutting, I'm still enthusiastic about the subjects. I've designed and pattern cut my own labels and accessories range which were sold throughout London, Europe and Japan. I've freelanced as a flat pattern cutter and draper for fashion companies such as Birdsong London and Alexander McQueen.  

In 2012, I qualified with a PGCE and have since taught at various institutions, including the Royal College of Art, Central Saint Martins, Morley College, Liverpool John Moores and the London College of Fashion. 
I'm passionate about education and use my lecturing skills and extensive pattern cutting knowledge effectively in my company. Having developed a range of learning resources, the Cut & Spread™ pattern making kits, and produced mini, speedy educational videos, Pattern Cutting Deconstructed is recognised by my Instagram followers as the go-to platform for fashion creatives who want to learn pattern cutting skills in an accessible fun way. I'm renowned for my step-by-step teaching approach and ability to make confusing calculations deceptively simple. I also have a keen eye for the finer details that can make or break the look of a student’s designs.

My name is Beth Dow, and I live in Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA, where I’m a visual artist and leatherworker. 

My leather business is Fieldwork Goods, and I use traditional processes to make useful and durable leather bags by hand. I taught myself how to sew leather because I couldn’t find the kinds of bags and cases that I wanted to buy. These skills give me the freedom to make what I need, and I love the dimensional problem-solving of designing new patterns. I teach several leather workshops a year, and the most recent schools were the Penland School of Craft and North House Folk School. In my course you will learn to make a small tote bag, picking up skills that will enable you to make all kinds of other leather goods, from wallets to handbags. 

I’m also a visual artist working with digital and film photography. My photographs have been exhibited around the world, and I teach photography at a local university. My studio is split right down the middle, with visual art occupying half, and leatherwork in the other half. Some days I make images, and other days I make useful objects, and the slow, meditative process of sewing leather by hand offers a restoring break from spending hours at the computer editing photographs. My motto is: Make it like you mean it. 

Education: MFA (Photography), University of Minnesota

Follow me on Instagram!
Leatherwork: @fieldworkgoods
Photography: @bethdow

The Hat - In history a part of everyday life that has long since faded away.
We are a husband and wife duo and create HATS that hold true to their heritage, yet reflect the spirit of the Modern Nomad travelling the world. Every Hat is handmade in our studio in Vienna, Austria using traditional millinery techniques mixed with a vision for the future of hat making.

I'm Luisa Hurtado, but you might know me better as @designerluisa from TikTok, or @imluluisa on Instagram. I'm a passionate upcycler and Fashion Designer.

I grew up in a small town in Mexico, where as a child, fashion always fascinated me. I dreamt of wearing unique clothes, different from what everyone else had. 
I realized I wanted to start making my own garments because I was asking way too much from my grandma and my mom. So I decided to learn!
I was able to attend a university in my own state, in Mexico, where I graduated with honors in Fashion Design & Garment Industry. 
Right after I graduated I was an assistant teacher in my own university teaching sewing & pattern making.. After that I had a few collections come out and Fashion Shows at city events that allowed me to reach a new market.
Not long after that, I met the love of my life, and moved to the United States where I started from scratch, without recognition, which was challenging.
I had fun during this time as well, I even made my own wedding dress and created some fun pieces for friends and family. I sold my designs at small local events, always seeking ways to share my passion for fashion.

This passion to share & teach led me to start my Youtube channel, and later TikTok. 

It was on TikTok where my work, particularly a backpack made from upcycled jeans, caught the eye of many, including major brands like Levi's.

Now, I am focusing on sharing my knowledge with others and helping people around the world get started on their own projects, prioritizing creativity, sustainability, and lots of fun!

-Luisa xx

teachers.aboutMe:
I'm Chelsea, a Maker, Miniaturist, and prop designer. Although I spent nearly a decade as a licensed Landscape Architect, my love of creating models and miniatures led to a career in creating scale replicas. I now offer custom made miniature replicas as well as a line of DIY modern dollhouse kits.

I love miniatures and the opportunity to share the skills and techniques I use at home. To view more of my work check out Season 3 of NBC Making It, my website Chelseamakes.com, or my instagram @ChelseaMakes.

Hello! I’m Jessica, I’m an artist and Interior designer. I specialise in creating tactile, handcrafted models and I design luxury interiors that have craftsmanship at the heart.

My niche style and unusual approach to design has allowed me to work on a broad range of commissions, spanning across the worlds of advertising, interiors, art, editorial and installation. I have created playful models and designs for the likes of  Vogue, Volkswagen, BBC, Mulberry, BMW, Stylist, Liberty, Selfridges, ITV and Christian Louboutin. 

I set up my own business after graduating in 2010 and have been working on commissions ever since. Through self teaching I have learned a lot about the design industry and model making, mostly through self teaching, and lots of trial and error!

I make all of my creations from my studio in the Southdowns (UK).

Hi! I’m Yulia and I’m a self-taught hand embroidery artist based in Cleveland, Ohio. You can find me on Instagram @mossandfeather. I’ve been embroidering for three years now. I’ve always liked art, like painting and drawing, but it wasn’t until I discovered embroidery that creating art became one of the most important aspects of my life. 

I specialize in thread painting, which is a technique used to create realistic embroidery. It’s a lot like painting on a canvas but using thread instead of paint. Using this technique, you can achieve fine artistic detail, including shading, highlights and smooth color gradients. 

I’ve always been inspired by nature and animals and I love how well thread mimics the look of fur and feathers. It’s really the perfect medium for the type of art I like to create.

Evan Lorenzen (Art and Such Evan) is a multi-disciplinary artist that resides in Denver, Colorado. He currently spends most of his time working on miniature illustrations, woodworking, and animation. To test his natural limits, Evan does not use any magnifying instruments during the miniature drawing process.  Additionally, Evan considers it very awkward and unsettling to write biographies in the third person as he found out in the construction of this traditionally-styled artist’s bio. 

Focusing on the relationships between painting and animation, he graduated in 2013 from Marlboro College with a Bachelor of the Arts. Evan worked as a designer at a screen printing shop in Denver before becoming a full-time artist and tattooer.  He started exploring the realm of micro, handmade books, which led to his current interest in miniature illustrations- most of which are around 1 inch tall. Primarily working in pen and ink as well as watercolor, Evan currently finds himself influenced by mythology, medieval woodblock prints, cartoons, and the natural world.

Hi! I'm an artist from Toronto, Canada and I create miniatures for most of my waking hours :)

While I've always dabbled with creating tiny crafts as a child, I officially started making miniatures a few years ago, largely inspired by all the beautiful stop-motion animation movies and tv shows from various studios around the world. It is my goal to be able to create an ambiance and tell a story through my miniatures.

Since then, I have had the fortune to work with clients such as Madewell, Hunker Home, and Walmart in realizing their visions in miniature. You can also find me blabbering on about miniatures in publications such as CBC Arts and Chatelaine Magazine.

Thanks so much for checking out my profile, and please feel free to check out my projects below. I hope they'll bring you joy and perhaps encourage you to dip a toe into the world of miniature if you're not fully immersed already ;)

teacher.aboutMe:
Comunicadora, terapeuta nutricional certificada, biohacker y educadora en salud ancestral

Soy Ximena de la Serna, licenciada en Comunicación, terapeuta nutricional certificada y creadora del método “5 Pilares Ancestrales”, una filosofía de vida que integra descanso, movimiento, nutrición, relaciones conscientes y conexión con los ciclos naturales de luz y oscuridad.

Desde hace más de 14 años comparto contenidos en YouTube, cursos y formaciones online donde investigo, divulgo y enseño cómo recuperar la salud, la belleza y la vitalidad que nos pertenecen por derecho natural.

Mi trabajo es una invitación a dejar de delegar nuestro bienestar en sistemas externos, y volver a lo esencial: a cuidarnos con nuestras propias manos, a confiar en la sabiduría de nuestro cuerpo y a reconectar con el alma.

Creo firmemente que la salud no es un privilegio, sino una forma de soberanía personal, y que a través del conocimiento ancestral, la ciencia verdadera y la simplicidad de lo hecho en casa podemos transformarlo todo.

My name is Charlotte Stone and I am the creator and designer behind Stone Knits. I am internationally known for designing knitting patterns, in particular my speciality, socks with whimsical colorwork designs using the stranded knitting technique. I am originally from London in the UK but I have been living now for many years in Zürich, Switzerland. 

I have been knitting since I was a small child having learnt with my grandma and have been designing colourwork sock patterns since 2016. I now have a large collection of patterns available to purchase on Ravelry and Etsy and have had some featured in publications by Laine Magazine and Wool It magazine. I have also been teaching workshops on how to knit colourwork socks in Zürich since 2019.  I released my first ever book; Charming Colourwork socks in 2022, which featured 25 new colourworks sock designs of mine. The book was an international best seller for knitting and has since been translated into German, Korean and soon in French too. 

I currently live in the hills above Zürich, Switzerland with my family and my demanding cat, Ivy and I always have a sock knitting project at hand to work on!

teacher.aboutMe:
Barbie Williams es cantante, compositora y productora musical con más de 15 años de experiencia en la industria. Vivió en Berlín, donde trabajó como compositora para Sony BMG Alemania y colaboró con destacados productores de música electrónica.
Fué cantante y compositora de SIAMES, su banda de indie pop, que ha acumulado más de 200 millones de reproducciones solo en YouTube y cuenta con una audiencia global. 
Desde el 2023, lleva su proyecto solista en el que fusiona el folklore latinoamericano con la electrónica y el pop, utilizando su voz como elemento central en la composición.

Barbie ha realizado giras por Europa, Latinoamérica y EEUU, presentándose en emblemáticos lugares como el Gran Rex (ARG), el Gramercy Theatre (NY), y en festivales destacados como Vive Latino (MX), Tecate Pa'l Norte (MX) Fusion Festival (GER),entre otros.

Su enfoque se ha centrado principalmente en la creación y composición musical, explorando su voz como herramienta principal. Mediante el uso de loops, armonías y ritmos, da vida a sus composiciones, introduciendo conceptos innovadores y creativos en cada sesión de songwriting.

Lizzie Snow is the creative & brand director behind 'fortyonehundred'.

Since having built the brand from scratch over the last decade, Lizzie has collaborated with brands including Apple, Whittaker’s, Blunt Umbrellas, Lululemon, Converse, Peugeot, AllBirds, and more.

The business sits at the intersection of brand, creativity, academia, and contemporary commerce. Spanning internationally commissioned murals, online courses, product lines, collaborations, events, and an upcoming published book deal.

With a Master of Fine Arts, Bachelor of Design, and over 150,000 people following her across social media accounts - Lizzie Snow is a New Zealand creative and business person with a diverse portfolio of successes.

I am the founder of The Financial Wellness Forum, author of Real Life Money and The Real Life Money Journal and woman behind the @myfrugalyear Instagram account.

I work to encourage and educate on financial wellbeing, discussing how mindset, privilege and circumstances contribute to our financial wellness, with a particular emphasis on the unique challenges faced by people with unconventional financial circumstances.

I offer one to one coaching, group workshops and consultancy for businesses wanting to offer financial wellbeing support to their employees.

I am the Money Matters columnist for Glamour UK, and have bylines in The I Paper, Grazia, Refinery29 and others.

Hi everyone, my name is Abigail! I am a former professional ballerina and now the owner and creator behind The Creative Bix! If you love digital art, lettering, typography, illustrating, colors, & texture, you’re in the right place! I create and sell digital products, and specialize in designing digital tools for fellow creatives, like you! I do my best to create fun & unique products that inspire your workflow and bring your designs to life! 

I started learning about digital art in 2020 during lockdown, and I became obsessed! I started practicing everyday and trying out as many different techniques as I could. Then, in late January 2021, I began posting my art on Instagram. In February, I made my first TikTok, and in March I opened an Etsy store on a whim. Since then, I’ve continued to work hard to grow my business, and it’s been a whirlwind of many new, exciting opportunities that I couldn’t be more grateful for.

From the beginning, and still to this day, my goal is to spread joy and positivity through my art. Art comes in so many different forms, whether it’s music, dancing, photography, painting, digital art, or more. But no matter what form in which art is consumed, it is such a vital part of society, and I believe it should be accessible to everyone. I love using my small business to show that art can be done by anyone and is available to everyone, whether it’s digital or traditional! Thank you for stopping by, and have fun creating!

I am a business coach currently residing in Ramsgate, right by the sea. I am the founder of flower studio The Flower Arranger, worldwide membership platform The Coven Girl Gang and independent bookshop Book Bodega. I have been self-employed and running businesses for nearly a decade and I'm here to help you run yours!

Hey there, art lovers!

I'm Hannah Stelter, but you can call me your multidisciplinary art cheerleader. I specialize in watercolor and acrylic but dabble in wire sculpture, dance, and more! Beyond creating, I'm also an entrepreneur and, most importantly, a self-love champion.

Being a full-time artist was just a dream, until... well, it wasn't!  I started sharing my work online in 2020, inspired by other amazing artists. My relatable art and empowering message resonated quickly, and I built a fantastic community.

Within a year, my art was bringing in a whopping $100,000, and I was living my dream job!

People often ask how I did it. The answer? Learning tons, creating even more, and ditching perfectionism. (I even gave a TED Talk about it - "The Middle Finger Method", check it out!)

Now, I love sharing tips and tricks for other aspiring artists, teaching classes on embracing the creative mess, and of course, creating art that makes you smile!

Want to know more? Head over to hannahstelter.com and let's connect!

teacher.aboutMe:
Hey there! My name is Aynsley, known under my shop name Knotted Neon. I am a crochet and pattern designer based out of Toronto, Canada. I began crocheting in the Spring of 2020, and since then I have been pushing the boundaries of crochet and walking others through the process of how I achieve that. When I first started crocheting, my first ‘popular’ design was a cardigan depicting a cow being abducted by aliens. I haven’t made one in years, but it really catapulted my creative career and encouraged me to keep exploring the amazing medium of crochet and fiber arts.

Since then, I have found myself really drawn to creating food-inspired bags! I love the creativity that comes with it and how each person can have a connection to the food depicted. Since the beginning of my crochet journey, I have always focused on making whimsical and humorous accessories that add a touch of joy to fashion. From a crochet pizza rat bag to a sardine bag, I love to create a diverse range of crochet pieces that have you covered for any silly event or even a whimsical trip to the grocery store! Even more than making these pieces, my favourite thing is to teach others how to explore crochet and create adorable and goofy food bags. All of my patterns are written in English, along with any work on here. :)

teachers.aboutMe:
Hello! I am a fiber artist specializing in frame loom weaving, macrame, and punch needle art. I began creating with fiber just over six years ago and I’ve never looked back! I am endlessly inspired by colour and texture, and love to create art pieces that bring joy and happiness to my clients spaces. My signature pieces are usually big and bold, packed full of jewel-toned fibers that add interest to any space. 

I also love to share my love of weaving with others, and I regularly teach weaving workshops, both in person and online. I created my own beginners ecourse in 2021 as well. Teaching is my favourite as it allows me to connect with folk’s from all walks of life as we share our love of fiber craft together. 

I currently live in Montreal, Canada with my partner, two kids, and dog Luba.

I am a wool-based fibre artist from the South Coast of England with a love of playful colours and textures. Born without a sense of smell, I believes my sense of complementary colours has been heightened to compensate. I have been lucky enough to have written 2 books, '40 Knots and How to Tie Them' and my next book 'Punch Needle Embroidery for Beginners' which is out in November 2020.

A bit about my weaving practice:
In 2013 I saw a small wooden lap loom on Ebay and not really having a clue what it was, I bought it anyway. I didn’t realise that this would be the start of my love for weaving. Teaching myself with books from the library and anything I could find on the internet I managed to find my own style and am well and truly addicted. Trying to create as much texture in my work and exploring the use of colour I look forward to where this weaving journey will take me.

I'm Marion, a self-taught tapestry weaver and artist based in Dublin, Ireland.

I started weaving as a hobby and immediately fell in love with it. I have always enjoyed making things with my hands, and experimented with knitting, embroidery and macramé before discovering weaving. I also love interior design and statement art pieces, and woven tapestries bring a unique depth and texture to spaces.

The repetitive nature of weaving is therapeutic and calming for me, and I love that it involves no computers, screens, technology or plugs. It can be picked up and put back down again with minimal set up and or clean up and requires very little specialist tools. When I weave I listen to music, podcasts or audiobooks. My smaller looms are transportable, and I weave indoors, outdoors, watching movies or chatting with friends, whenever I can fit in time for weaving.

Every piece I make is an experiment and opportunity for learning for me. I take inspiration from nature, interior design, photography, and many other forms of visual art, and love trying out new styles and techniques.

Weaving is something that is slowly migrating from a hobby to a vocation. I work full-time for a consultancy that specialises in culture, sustainability and wellbeing so finding time to weave can be challenge, but I hope to weave myself out of the day job sometime soon.

Hi! I'm Cass, a textile designer, hand-weaver, educator and all round lover of textiles based in Oxford, UK. I love to weave richly-textured pieces that explore and combine unusual materials and fibre arts techniques to create sustainable art, textiles and lighting, working with private clients and design professionals worldwide.

Although I have been living in England for almost 20 years, I was born and raised in Montreal, Canada where I studied building engineering. But in my mid 20s I found myself on a journey, traveling the world, exploring the arts and searching for my passion in life. This ultimately led me to London and Central Saint Martins where I completed a degree in textile design, specialising in weaving in my 30s.

Alongside my design practice, I am a passionate educator. Working with both adults and children at my community weaving studio, The Oxford Weaving Studio, I share my love and knowledge of weaving and the broader fibre arts. It is here where I also researched, designed and developed The Oxford Frame Loom, a new type of frame loom that aims to bridge the gap between hand-weaving and tapestry weaving, enabling weavers of all levels to discover and explore this craft in new ways.

Today my goal is to share my love of weaving with the wider community and to inspire others to learn, grow and discover their weaving style.

Happy weaving!
Cass

I’m Allyson, a fibre artist based in Pictou, Nova Scotia, Canada. 


My weaving journey began seven years ago when I was studying Studio Art at the University of Guelph in Ontario, Canada. I was taking a variety of studio courses, and focussing much of my time studying painting, drawing, and sculpture, which included welding and woodworking. 
There were no textile or tapestry weaving courses in the Fine Arts department at the time, so I took to the internet to try and find anything I could to teach myself how to weave. There wasn’t much in the way of online resources at the time, which lead to me developing a practice that was completely self-taught. 


Three years later in 2016, I took a giant leap by quitting my job in retail and began weaving full-time. 
Since then I have exhibited my work in Canada, the US, and Europe, made hundreds of custom pieces for homes and commercial spaces all over the world, developed and created five online video weaving courses, and been featured in numerous publications including two books on contemporary weavers. 


A little bit about my process and philosophy: 

I make mostly small-scale work using fibres and other materials that I find second-hand as much as possible, and I weave with simple tools that I make myself or source from my local craft and hardware stores. 

It has always been really important to me that I do as much as I can with as little as I can, and that includes creating as little waste as possible by re-using all of my yarn scraps.

There are almost an endless amount of techniques that you can use to weave different patterns and designs, many different types of looms and tools, and more yarns in existence than you can imagine. All of this can make weaving seem really intimidating, which is why the goal of my artistic practice and as a teacher is to simplify the process as much as possible while maximizing the visual potential by using bold colour palettes and three-dimensionality. 

My hope is that this will help to make weaving more of an accessible art form and inspire others to explore their interest in the craft.

Hi! My name is Rachel Snack, and I am a weaver, educator and textile artist living in Philadelphia. 

I grew up knowing I wanted to be an artist, and started making paintings and ceramics from a young age. When it came time to decide on college I chose to attend a prestigious art school, The School of the Art Institute of Chicago. It was there that I learned to weave and really fell in love with the practice. I graduated with a Bachelor of Fine Art in Fiber & Material Studies and later went on to receive my Master of Science in Textile Design from Philadelphia University.

After college I worked in textile conservation and then accepted an artist residency for a non-profit called Awamaki in Peru. Peru was a life changing experience for me, and challenged me to grow as an individual and an artist. The culture, people and textiles of Peru were so inspiring to me. It’s an extremely resilient and wise culture, with a rich textile history. 

When I came home from Peru I attended graduate school, and then I went to work for another yarn company as their Creative Director. During that time it became clear to me how important it was to foster a weaving community and share my passion, and so I founded my own business, Weaver House. 

Weaver House is a textile studio, yarn shop and weaving school dedicated to preserving craft tradition through hand-making and weaving education. We teach all levels of weaving in our studio, sell looms, tools and yarn and I also create commission-based woven artworks. 

I have exhibited my work internationally, been published in numerous books and magazines, and taught courses on weaving, fiber dyeing and textile conservation throughout the United States. Weaving is my true passion and I’ve been lucky enough to practice the art for over twelve years.
